entries.definition: (high or holy ground), a mountainous district of Asia mentioned in the Bible in connection with the following events:— (1) As the resting-place of the ark after the deluge. (Genesis 8:4) (2) As the asylum of the sons of Sennacherib. (2 Kings 19:37; Isaiah 37:38) Authorized Version has “the land of Armenia.” (3) As the ally, and probably the neighbor, of Minni and Ashchenaz. (Jeremiah 51:27) [Armenia] The name Ararat was unknown to the geographers of Greece and Rome, as it still is to the Armenians of the present day; but it was an ancient name for a portion of Armenia. In its biblical sense it is descriptive generally of the Armenian highlands—the lofty plateau which over looks the plain of the Araxes on the north and of Mesopotomia on the south. Various opinions have been put forth as to the spot where the ark rested, as described in (Genesis 8:4) (but it is probable that it rested on some of the lower portions of the range than on the lofty peak to which exclusively) Europeans have given the name Ararat, the mountain which is called Massis by the Armenians, AgriDagh, i.e. Steep Mountain, by the Turks, and Kuh-i-Nuh, i.e. Noah’s Mountain, by the Persians. It rises immediately out of the plain of the Araxes, and terminates in two conical peaks, named the Great and Less Ararat, about seven miles distant from each other; the former of which attain an elevation of 17,260 feet above the level of the sea and about 14,000 above the plain of the Araxes, while the latter is lower by 4000 feet. The summit of the higher is covered with eternal snow for about 3000 feet. Arguri, the only village known to have been built on its slopes, was the spot where, according to tradition, Noah planted his vineyard. “The mountains of Ararat ” are co-extensive with the Armenian plateau from the base of Ararat in the north to the range of Kurdistan in the south, we notice the following characteristics of that region as illustrating the Bible narrative; (1) its elevation. It rises to a height of from 6000 to 7000 feet above the level of the sea. (2) Its geographical position . Viewed with reference to the dispersion of the nations, Armenia is the true centre of the world; and at the present day Ararat is the great boundary-stone between the empires of Russia, Turkey and Persia. (3) Its physical character . The plains as well as the mountains supply evidence of volcanic agency. (4) The climate . Winter lasts from October to May, and is succeeded by a brief spring and a summer of intense heat. (5) The vegetation . Grass grows luxuriantly on the plateau, and furnishes abundant pasture during the summer months to the flocks of the nomad Kurds. Wheat, barley and vines ripen at far higher altitudes than on the Alps and the Pyrenees.
entries.definition_ko:
('높고 거룩한 땅') 아시아의 산악 지대로, 성경에서 다음 사건들과 관련하여 언급된다. (1) 홍수 후 방주가 머문 곳(창세기 8:4). (2) 산헤립의 아들들이 피신한 곳(열왕기하 19:37; 이사야 37:38). 흠정역은 이를 '아르메니아 땅'으로 옮겼다. (3) 민니와 아스그나스의 동맹이자 아마도 그 이웃(예레미야 51:27).

아라랏이라는 이름은 헬라와 로마의 지리학자들에게 알려지지 않았고 오늘날 아르메니아 사람들에게도 그러하나, 아르메니아의 한 지역을 가리키는 옛 이름이었다. 성경적 의미에서 이 말은 대체로 아르메니아 고원 전체를 가리키니, 북으로 아락세스 평원을 굽어보고 남으로 메소보다미아를 굽어보는 높은 고원이다.

창세기 8:4이 말하는 방주가 머문 자리에 대해서는 여러 견해가 나왔다. 다만 유럽 사람들이 오직 그 높은 봉우리 하나에만 아라랏이라는 이름을 붙였는데, 방주는 그 봉우리보다 산줄기의 더 낮은 부분에 머물렀을 개연성이 크다. 그 산은 아르메니아 사람들이 마시스라 부르고, 튀르크 사람들이 '가파른 산'이라는 뜻의 아그리다그라 부르며, 바사 사람들이 '노아의 산'이라는 뜻의 쿠히누흐라 부른다.

이 산은 아락세스 평원에서 곧바로 솟아올라 두 개의 원뿔 봉우리로 끝맺으니, 대아라랏과 소아라랏이라 불리며 서로 칠 마일쯤 떨어져 있다. 앞의 것은 해발 17,260자에 이르고 아락세스 평원에서는 14,000자쯤 되며, 뒤의 것은 그보다 4,000자 낮다. 높은 쪽 봉우리의 꼭대기는 3,000자 남짓이 만년설로 덮여 있다. 그 비탈에 세워진 것으로 알려진 유일한 마을 아르구리는 전승에 따르면 노아가 포도나무를 심은 자리였다.

'아라랏의 산들'은 북쪽 아라랏 기슭에서 남쪽 쿠르디스탄 산줄기까지 아르메니아 고원 전체에 걸쳐 있다. 성경의 서술을 밝혀 주는 그 지역의 특징으로 다음을 짚을 수 있다. (1) 높이. 해발 6,000자에서 7,000자까지 솟아 있다. (2) 지리적 위치. 민족들의 흩어짐에 비추어 볼 때 아르메니아는 참으로 세계의 중심이며, 오늘날 아라랏은 러시아와 튀르크와 바사 세 제국 사이의 큰 경계석이다. (3) 물리적 성격. 산지뿐 아니라 평원도 화산 활동의 증거를 보여 준다. (4) 기후. 겨울이 시월부터 오월까지 이어지고, 그 뒤에 짧은 봄과 몹시 무더운 여름이 따른다. (5) 초목. 고원에는 풀이 무성하게 자라 여름철 동안 유목하는 쿠르드 사람의 가축에게 넉넉한 목초를 대어 준다. 밀과 보리와 포도는 알프스나 피레네보다 훨씬 높은 고도에서도 익는다.

entries.definition: (a teacher, or lofty), the son of Amram and Jochebed, and the older brother of Moses and Miriam. (Numbers 26:59; 33:39) (B.C. 1573.) He was a Levite, and is first mentioned in (Exodus 4:14) He was appointed by Jehovah to be the interpreter, (Exodus 4:16) of his brother Moses, who was “slow of speech;” and accordingly he was not only the organ of communication with the Israelites and with Pharaoh, (Exodus 4:30; 7:2) but also the actual instrument of working most of the miracles of the Exodus. (Exodus 7:19) etc. On the way to Mount Sinai, during the battle with Amalek, Aaron with Hur stayed up the weary hands of Moses when they were lifted up for the victory of Israel. (Exodus 17:9) He is mentioned as dependent upon his brother and deriving all his authority from him. Left, on Moses’ departure into Sinai, to guide the people, Aaron is tried for a moment on his own responsibility, and he fails from a weak inability to withstand the demand of the people for visible “gods to go before them,” by making an image of Jehovah, in the well-known form of Egyptian idolatry (Apis or Mnevis). He repented of his sin, and Moses gained forgiveness for him. (9:20) Aaron was not consecrated by Moses to the new office of the high priesthood. (Exodus 29:9) From this time the history of Aaron is almost entirely that of the priesthood, and its chief feature is the great rebellion of Korah and the Levites. Leaning, as he seems to have done, wholly on Moses, it is not strange that he should have shared his sin at Meribah and its punishment. See Moses. (Numbers 20:10-12) Aaron’s death seems to have followed very speedily. It took place on Mount Hor, after the transference of his robes and office to Eleazar. (Numbers 20:28) This mount is still called the “Mountain of Aaron.” See Hor. The wife of Aaron was Elisheba, (Exodus 6:23) and the two sons who survived him, Eleazar and Ithamar. The high priesthood descended to the former, and to his descendants until the time of Eli, who, although of the house of Ithamar, received the high priesthood and transmitted it to his children; with them it continued till the accession of Solomon, who took it from Abiathar and restored it to Zadok (of the house of Eleazar). See Abiathar.
entries.definition_ko: '교사' 또는 '높은 자'라는 뜻으로 아므람과 요게벳의 아들이며 모세와 미리암의 형이다(민수기 26:59). 말이 어눌한 모세를 대신해 하나님의 통역자 역할을 했으며(출애굽기 4:16) 출애굽의 기적들을 수행하는 도구가 되었다. 모세가 시내산에 오른 사이 금송아지를 만드는 죄를 지었으나 회개했고, 이후 대제사장으로 세워졌다. 호르산에서 죽어 아들 엘르아살이 뒤를 이었다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 12:27) priests of the family of Aaron.
entries.definition_ko: 아론 가문의 제사장들을 가리킨다(역대상 12:27).

entries.definition: See Month. (father), an element in the composition of many proper names, of which Abba is a Chaldaic form, having the sense of “endowed with,” “possessed of.”
entries.definition_ko: 월(MONTH) 항목 참조. 또한 '아버지'라는 뜻으로 여러 고유명사의 구성 요소로 쓰이는 갈대아어 형태(압바)의 어원이기도 하다.

entries.definition: See Apollyon.
entries.definition_ko: 아볼루온(APOLLYON) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (God-given), one of the seven eunuchs in the Persian court of Ahasuerus. (Esther 1:10)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 주신'이라는 뜻으로 아하수에로 왕의 바사 궁정 일곱 내시 중 하나이다(에스더 1:10).

entries.definition: (perennial, stony), one of the “rivers of Damascus.” (2 Kings 5:12) The Barada and the Awaj are now the chief streams of Damascus, the former representing the Abana and the latter the Pharpar of the text. The Barada (Abana) rises in the Antilibanus, at about 23 miles from the city, after flowing through which it runs across the plain, of whose fertility it is the chief source, till it loses itself in the lake or marsh Bahret-elKibliyeh.
entries.definition_ko: '끊임없이 흐르는, 돌이 많은'이라는 뜻으로 다메섹의 '강들' 중 하나이다(열왕기하 5:12). 오늘날의 바라다강이 아바나에 해당하는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (regions beyond), a mountain or range of highlands on the east of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and forming the eastern wall of the Jordan valley at that part. Its most elevated spot was “the Mount Nebo, head of the Pisgah,” from which Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death. These mountains are mentioned in (Numbers 27:12; 33:47,48) and Deuteronomy 32:49
entries.definition_ko: '저편의 땅들'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 동쪽, 모압 땅의 산악 지대로 여리고 맞은편에 위치한다. 모세가 약속의 땅을 바라본 느보산, 곧 비스가산 정상이 이곳에서 가장 높은 지점이다(민수기 27:12).

entries.definition: See Ab.
entries.definition_ko: 압(AB) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: • Father of Adoniram. (1 Kings 4:6) • Son of Shammua, (Nehemiah 11:17) called Obadiah in (1 Chronicles 9:16)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 아도니람의 아버지(열왕기상 4:6). (2) 삼무아의 아들로 역대상 9:16에서는 오바댜라고도 불린다(느헤미야 11:17).

entries.definition: father of Shelemiah. (Jeremiah 36:26)
entries.definition_ko: 셀레먀의 아버지이다(예레미야 36:26).

entries.definition: (my servant). • A Merarite, and ancestor of Ethan the singer. (1 Chronicles 6:44) (B.C. before 1015.) • The father of Kish, a Merarite, in the reign of Hezekiah. (2 Chronicles 29:12) (B.C. before 736.) • One of the Bene-Elam in the time of Ezra, who had married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:26) (B.C. 659.)
entries.definition_ko: '나의 종'이라는 뜻. (1) 므라리 가문 사람으로 찬양자 에단의 조상(역대상 6:44). (2) 히스기야 시대 므라리 가문 기스의 아버지(역대하 29:12). (3) 에스라 시대 이방 여인과 결혼한 벤엘람 자손 중 하나(에스라 10:26).

entries.definition: (the servant of God), son of Guni and father of Ahi, one of the Gadites who were settled in the land of Bashan, (1 Chronicles 5:15), in the days of Jotham king of Judah. (B.C. 758.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 종'이라는 뜻으로 구니의 아들이자 아히의 아버지이며 바산 땅에 정착한 갓 지파 사람이다(역대상 5:15).

entries.definition: (servile). • A judge of Israel, (Judges 12:13,(15) perhaps the same person as Bedan, in (1 Samuel 12:11) (B.C. 1233-1225). • Son of Shashak. (1 Chronicles 8:23) • First-born son of Jehiel, son of Gideon. (1 Chronicles 8:30; 9:35,36). • Son of Micah, a contemporary of Josiah, (2 Chronicles 34:20) called Achbor in (2 Kings 22:12) (B.C. 628.) • A city in the tribe if Asher, given to the Gershonites, (Joshua 21:30; 1 Chronicles 6:74) the modern Abdeh, 10 miles northeast of Accho.
entries.definition_ko: '종의'라는 뜻. (1) 이스라엘의 사사로 사무엘상 12:11의 브단과 동일 인물로 추정된다(사사기 12:13). (2) 사삭의 아들(역대상 8:23). (3) 기브온의 아들 여히엘의 맏아들(역대상 8:30). (4) 요시야 시대 미가의 아들로 열왕기하 22:12에서는 악볼이라 불린다(역대하 34:20). (5) 아셀 지파의 성읍으로 게르손 자손에게 주어졌다(여호수아 21:30).

entries.definition: (i.e. servant of Nego, perhaps the same as Nebo), the Chaldean name given to Azariah, one of the three friends of Daniel, miraculously save from the fiery furnace. Dan. 3. (B.C. about 600.)
entries.definition_ko: '느고(느보)의 종'이라는 뜻으로 느부갓네살이 다니엘의 세 친구 중 하나인 아사랴에게 붙인 갈대아 이름이며, 풀무불에서 기적적으로 구원받았다(다니엘 3장).

entries.definition: the name of several places in Palestine, probably signifies a meadow . (i.e., breath, vapor, transitoriness, probably so called from the shortness of his life), the second son of Adam, murdered by his brother Cain, (Genesis 4:1-16) he was a keeper or feeder of sheep. Our Lord spoke of Abel as the first martyr, (Matthew 23:35) so did the early Church subsequently. The traditional site of his murder and his grave are pointed out near Damascus.
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인의 여러 지명에 쓰이는 '초원'이라는 뜻이며, 또한 아담과 하와의 둘째 아들로 형 가인에게 죽임을 당했다(창세기 4:1-16). 양 치는 자였으며, 주님은 그를 첫 순교자로 언급하셨다(마태복음 23:35).

entries.definition: (the great abel), the place where the ark rested in the field of Joshua at Bethshemesh. (1 Samuel 6:18)
entries.definition_ko: '큰 아벨'이라는 뜻으로 벧세메스의 여호수아의 밭에서 언약궤가 머문 곳이다(사무엘상 6:18).

entries.definition: (meadow of the house of oppression), a town of some importance, (2 Samuel 20:15) in the extreme north of Palestine, which fell an early prey to the invading kings of Syria, (1 Kings 15:20) and Assyria. (2 Kings 15:29)
entries.definition_ko: '억압의 집의 초원'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 최북단의 중요한 성읍이며(사무엘하 20:15) 일찍부터 수리아와 앗수르 침략군의 표적이 되었다.

entries.definition: (Abel on the waters), also called simply Abel, (2 Samuel 20:14,18) another name for Abel-bethmaachah. (2 Chronicles 16:4)
entries.definition_ko: '물가의 아벨'이라는 뜻으로 아벨벧마아가의 다른 이름이며 단순히 '아벨'로도 불린다(사무엘하 20:14,18).

entries.definition: (meadow of the dance), in the northern pat of the Jordan valley, (1 Kings 4:12) to which the routed Bedouin host fled from Gideon, (Judges 7:22) Here Elisha was found at his plough by Elijah returning up the valley from Horeb. (1 Kings 19:16-19)
entries.definition_ko: '춤의 초원'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 계곡 북부에 위치하며(열왕기상 4:12) 기드온에게 패한 미디안 무리가 도망친 곳이다. 엘리사가 밭을 갈다가 엘리야에게 부름받은 곳이기도 하다(열왕기상 19:16-19).

entries.definition: (meadow of Egypt), the name given by the Canaanites to the floor of Atad, at which Joseph, his brothers and the Egyptians made their mourning for Jacob. (Genesis 50:11) It was beyond (on the east of) Jordan. See Atad. (Schaff and others say it was on the west bank, for the writer was on the east of Jordan. It was near Jericho, or perhaps Hebron.)
entries.definition_ko: '애굽의 초원'이라는 뜻으로 요셉과 그 형제들, 애굽 사람들이 야곱을 위해 애곡한 아닷의 타작마당에 가나안 사람들이 붙인 이름이다(창세기 50:11).

entries.definition: (the meadow of the acacias), in the “plains” of Moab, on the low level of the Jordan valley, opposite Jericho. The last resting-place of Israel before crossing the Jordan. (Numbers 33:49) The place is most frequently mentioned by its shorter name of Shittim. See Shittah Tree, Shittim, Shittim.
entries.definition_ko: '아카시아의 초원'이라는 뜻으로 모압 평지, 요단강 저지대에 위치하며 이스라엘이 요단강을 건너기 전 마지막으로 머문 곳이다(민수기 33:49). 더 짧은 이름 '싯딤'으로 더 자주 언급된다.

entries.definition: (lofty), a town in the possession of Issachar, named between Kishion and Remeth in (Joshua 19:20) only.
entries.definition_ko: '높은'이라는 뜻으로 잇사갈 지파의 한 성읍이며 기시온과 레멧 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 19:20).

entries.definition: mother of King Hezekiah, (2 Kings 18:2) written Abia, Abiah, Or Abijah, Abijah Or Abijamin (2 Chronicles 29:1)
entries.definition_ko: 히스기야 왕의 어머니로(열왕기하 18:2) 아비야로도 표기된다(역대하 29:1).

entries.definition: • Son of Becher, the son of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:8) • Wife of Hezron. (1 Chronicles 2:24) • Second son of Samuel. (1 Samuel 8:2; 1 Chronicles 7:28) • The son of Rehoboam. (1 Chronicles 3:10; Matthew 1:7) See Abijah Or Abijam, 1. • Mother of King Hezekiah. [Abi] • Same as Abijah Or Abijam, 4.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 베냐민의 아들 베겔의 아들(역대상 7:8). (2) 헤스론의 아내(역대상 2:24). (3) 사무엘의 둘째 아들(사무엘상 8:2). (4) 르호보암의 아들(역대상 3:10; 마태복음 1:7). (5) 히스기야 왕의 어머니. (6) 아비야 또는 아비얌과 동일 인물.

entries.definition: the eighth of the 24 courses or classes into which the priests were divided for serving at the altar. (1 Chronicles 24; Luke 1:5) See Abia, Abiah, Or Abijah, Abijah Or Abijam, 4.
entries.definition_ko: 제사장들이 성전 봉사를 위해 나뉜 24반차 중 여덟째 반차이다(역대상 24장; 누가복음 1:5).

entries.definition: (father of strength). See Abiel Or Abiel.
entries.definition_ko: '힘의 아버지'라는 뜻. 아비엘(ABIEL) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (father of gathering, i.e. gathered), (Exodus 6:24) otherwise written Ebi/asaph. (1 Chronicles 6:23,37; 9:19) one of the descendants of Korah, and head of the Korhites. Among the remarkable descendants of Abiasaph were Samuel the prophet, (1 Samuel 1:11) and Heman the singer.
entries.definition_ko: '모음의 아버지, 곧 모아진'이라는 뜻으로(출애굽기 6:24) 에비아삽으로도 표기되며(역대상 6:23) 고라의 후손이자 고라 자손의 우두머리이다. 그 후손 중에는 선지자 사무엘과 찬양자 헤만이 있다.

entries.definition: (father of abundance, i.e. liberal), High priest and fourth in descent from Eli. (B.C. 1060-1012.) Abiathar was the only one of the all the sons of Ahimelech the high priest who escaped the slaughter inflicted upon his father’s house by Saul, in revenge for his father’s house by Saul, in revenge of his having inquired of the Lord for David and given him the shew-bread to eat. (1 Samuel 22:1) ... Abiathar having become high priest fled to David, and was thus enabled to inquire of the Lord for him. (1 Samuel 23:9; 30:7; 2 Samuel 2:1; 5:19) etc. He adhered to David in his wanderings while pursued by Saul; he was with him while he reigned in Hebron, and afterwards in Jerusalem. (2 Samuel 2:1-3) He continued faithful to him in Absalom’s rebellion. (2 Samuel 15:24,29,35,36; 17:15-17; 19:11) When, however, Adonijah set himself up fro David’s successor on the throne, in opposition to Solomon, Abiathar sided with him, while Zadok was on Solomon’s side. For this Abiathar was deprived of the high priesthood. Zadok had joined David at Hebron, (1 Chronicles 12:28) so that there was henceforth who high priests in the reign of David, and till the deposition of Abiathar by Solomon, when Zadok became the sole high priest.
entries.definition_ko: '풍요의 아버지, 곧 관대한'이라는 뜻으로 엘리로부터 4대손인 대제사장이다. 아버지 아히멜렉의 집안이 사울에게 학살당할 때 유일하게 살아남아 다윗에게 피신했으며, 다윗의 방랑과 통치 기간 내내 그와 함께했다. 압살롬의 반역에도 신실했으나, 아도니야의 왕위 계승을 지지한 일로 솔로몬에게 대제사장직을 박탈당하고 사독이 유일한 대제사장이 되었다.

entries.definition: (green fruits). [Month]
entries.definition_ko: '푸른 열매'라는 뜻. 월(MONTH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (father of knowledge), a son of Midian. (Genesis 25:4; 1 Chronicles 1:33)
entries.definition_ko: '지식의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 미디안의 아들이다(창세기 25:4).

entries.definition: (father of the judge), chief of the tribe of Benjamin at the time of the Exodus. (B.C. 1491.) (Numbers 1:11; 2:22; 7:60,65; 10:24)
entries.definition_ko: '재판자의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 출애굽 당시 베냐민 지파의 지도자였다(민수기 1:11).

entries.definition: (father of strength, i.e. strong). • Father of Kish, and consequently grandfather of Saul, (1 Samuel 9:1) as well as of Abner, Saul’s commander-in-chief. (1 Samuel 14:51) (B.C. 1093-1055.) • One of David’s mighty men. (1 Chronicles 11:32) In (2 Samuel 23:31) he is called ABI-ALBON. (B.C. 1053.)
entries.definition_ko: '힘의 아버지, 곧 강한'이라는 뜻. (1) 기스의 아버지로 사울과 아브넬의 조부(사무엘상 9:1). (2) 다윗의 용사 중 하나로 사무엘하 23:31에서는 아비알본이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (father of help, helpful). • Eldest son of Gilead, and descendant of Manasseh. (Joshua 17:2; 1 Chronicles 7:18) (B.C. 1450.) He was the ancestor of the great judge Gideon. [Gideon] • One of David’s mighty men. (2 Samuel 23:27; 1 Chronicles 11:28; 27:12) (B.C. 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '도움의 아버지, 곧 도움이 되는'이라는 뜻. (1) 길르앗의 맏아들로 므낫세의 후손이며 사사 기드온의 조상(여호수아 17:2). (2) 다윗의 용사 중 하나(사무엘하 23:27).

entries.definition: (father, i.e. source, of joy). • The beautiful wife of Nabal, a wealthy owner of goats and sheep in Carmel. (B.C. 1060.) When David’s messengers were slighted by Nabal, Abigail supplies David and his followers with provisions, and succeeded in appeasing his anger. The days after this Nabal died, and David sent for Abigail and made her his wife. (1 Samuel 25:14) etc. By her he had a son, called Chileab in (2 Samuel 3:3) but Daniel in (1 Chronicles 3:1) • A sister of David, married to Jether the Ishmaelite, and mother, by him, of Amasa. (1 Chronicles 2:17) In (2 Samuel 17:25) for Israelite read Ishmaelite. (B.C. 1068.)
entries.definition_ko: '기쁨의 근원'이라는 뜻. (1) 나발의 아름다운 아내로 다윗의 사자들이 나발에게 멸시당했을 때 다윗과 그 부하들에게 양식을 공급하고 그의 분노를 가라앉혔으며, 나발이 죽은 뒤 다윗의 아내가 되었다(사무엘상 25:14). (2) 다윗의 누이로 이스마엘 사람 예델과 결혼해 아마사를 낳았다(역대상 2:17).

entries.definition: (father of, i.e. possessing, strength). • Father of Zuriel, chief of the Levitical father of Merari, a contemporary of Moses. (Numbers 3:35) (B.C. 1490.) • Wife of Abishur. (1 Chronicles 2:29) • Son of Huri, of the tribe of Gad. (1 Chronicles 5:14) • Wife of Rehoboam. She is called the daughter, i.e. descendant, of Eliab, the elder brother of David. (2 Chronicles 11:18) (B.C. 972.) • Father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai. (Esther 2:15; 9:29)
entries.definition_ko: '힘을 가진 아버지'라는 뜻. (1) 모세 시대 레위 므라리 가문의 지도자 수리엘의 아버지(민수기 3:35). (2) 아비술의 아내(역대상 2:29). (3) 갓 지파 후리의 아들(역대상 5:14). (4) 르호보암의 아내로 다윗의 형 엘리압의 후손(역대하 11:18). (5) 에스더의 아버지이자 모르드개의 삼촌(에스더 2:15).

entries.definition: (he (God) is my father), the second son, (Numbers 3:2) of Aaron by Elisheba. (Exodus 6:23) Being, together with his elder brother Nadab, guilty of offering strange fire to the lord, he was consumed by fire from heaven. (Leviticus 10:1,2)
entries.definition_ko: '그(하나님)는 나의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 아론과 엘리세바의 둘째 아들이다(민수기 3:2). 형 나답과 함께 여호와께 다른 불을 드려 하늘에서 내린 불에 죽임을 당했다(레위기 10:1,2).

entries.definition: (father of renown, famous), son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 8:3)
entries.definition_ko: '명성의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 벨라의 아들이자 베냐민의 손자이다(역대상 8:3).

entries.definition: (my father is Jehovah). • Son and successor of Rehoboam on the throne of Judah. (1 Kings 4:21; 2 Chronicles 12:16) He is called Abia, Abiah, Or Abijahin Chronicles, Abijamin Kings. He began to reign B.C. 959, and reigned three years. He endeavored to recover the kingdom of the Ten Tribes, and made war on Jeroboam. He was successful in battle, and took several of the cities of Israel. We are told that he walked in all the sins of Rehoboam. (1 Kings 14:23,24) • The second son of Samuel, called Abia, Abiah, Or Abijah, Abia, Course OfH in our version. [Abia, Course Of, Abia, Abiah, Or Abijah, Abia, Course OfH, No. 3] • Son of Jeroboam I., king of Israel; died in his childhood. (1 Kings 14:1) ... • A descendant of Eleazar, who gave his name to the eighth of the 24 courses into which the priests were divided by David. (1 Chronicles 24:10; 2 Chronicles 8:14; Nehemiah 12:4,17) • One of the priests who entered into a covenant with Nehemiah to walk in God’s law, (Nehemiah 10:7) unless the name is rather that of a family, and the same with the preceding.
entries.definition_ko: '나의 아버지는 여호와이시다'라는 뜻. (1) 르호보암의 아들이자 유다 왕위 계승자로 여로보암과 전쟁을 벌여 승리했으나 르호보암의 죄를 그대로 따랐다(열왕기상 14:31). (2) 사무엘의 둘째 아들. (3) 여로보암 1세의 아들로 어려서 죽음. (4) 엘르아살의 후손으로 다윗이 정한 24반차 중 여덟째 반차의 이름이 됨. (5) 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 제사장 중 하나.

entries.definition: [Abia, Abiah, Or Abijah, Abijah Or Abijam, 1]
entries.definition_ko: 아비야(ABIJAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Abilene]
entries.definition_ko: 아빌레네(ABILENE) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (land of meadows), (Luke 3:1) a city situated on the eastern slope of Antilibanus, in a district fertilized by the river Barada (Abana). The city was 18 miles from Damascus, and stood in a remarkable gorge called Suk Wady Barada .
entries.definition_ko: '초원의 땅'이라는 뜻으로(누가복음 3:1) 안티레바논 동쪽 경사면, 바라다(아바나)강이 흐르는 지역에 위치한 도시이다. 다메섹에서 18마일 떨어져 있었다.

entries.definition: (father of Mael), a descendant of Joktan, (Genesis 10:28; 1 Chronicles 1:22) and probably the progenitor of an Arab tribe (Mali).
entries.definition_ko: '마엘의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 욕단의 후손이며(창세기 10:28) 아라비아 부족의 조상으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (father of the king), the name of several Philistine kings, was probably a common title of these kings, like that of Pharaoh among the Egyptians and that of Caesar and Augustus among the Romans. Hence in the title of (Psalms 34:1) ... the name of Abimelech is given to the king, who is called Achish in (1 Samuel 21:11) • A Philistine, king of Gerar, Genesis 20,21, who, exercising the right claimed by Eastern princes of collecting all the beautiful women of their dominions into their harem, (Genesis 12:15; Esther 2:3) sent for and took Sarah. A similar account is given of Abraham’s conduct of this occasion to that of his behavior towards Pharaoh. [Abraham] (B.C. 1920.) • Another king of Gerar int he time of Isaac, of whom a similar narrative is recorded in relation to Rebekah. (Genesis 26:1) etc. (B.C. 1817.) • Son of the judge Gideon by his Shechemite concubine. (Judges 8:31) (B.C. 13221319.) After his father’s death he murdered all his brethren, 70 in number, with the exception of Jotham, the youngest, who concealed himself; and he then persuaded the Shechemites to elect him king. Shechem now became an independent state. After Abimelech had reigned three years, the citizens of Shechem rebelled. He was absent at the time, but he returned and quelled the insurrection. Shortly after he stormed and took Thebez, but was struck on the head by a woman with the fragment of a millstone, comp. (2 Samuel 11:21) and lest he should be said to have died by a woman, he bade his armor-bearer slay him. • A son of Abiathar. (1 Chronicles 18:16)
entries.definition_ko: '왕의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 블레셋 왕들의 공통 칭호였던 것으로 보인다(애굽의 '바로', 로마의 '가이사'와 유사). (1) 그랄 왕으로 아브라함에게서 사라를 데려갔다가 돌려준 인물(창세기 20-21장). (2) 이삭 시대 그랄 왕으로 리브가에 관해 비슷한 사건을 겪음(창세기 26:1). (3) 사사 기드온의 아들로 형제 70명을 죽이고 세겜 왕이 되었으나 훗날 여인이 던진 맷돌에 맞아 죽었다(사사기 8:31). (4) 아비아달의 아들(역대상 18:16).

entries.definition: • A Levite, a native of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark remained 20 years. (1 Samuel 7:1,2; 1 Chronicles 13:7) (B.C. 1124.) • Second son of Jesse, who followed Saul to his war against the Philistines, (1 Samuel 16:8; 17:13) (B.C. 1063.) • A son of Saul, who was slain with his brothers at the fatal battle on Mount Gilboa. (1 Samuel 31:2) (B.C. 1053.) • Father of one of the twelve chief officers of Solomon. (1 Kings 4:11) (B.C. before 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 기럇여아림의 레위인으로 그 집에 언약궤가 20년간 머물렀다(사무엘상 7:1). (2) 이새의 둘째 아들(사무엘상 16:8). (3) 사울의 아들로 길보아 전투에서 전사(사무엘상 31:2). (4) 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 하나의 아버지(열왕기상 4:11).

entries.definition: (father of light). Same as Abner. (1 Samuel 14:50) margin.
entries.definition_ko: '빛의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 아브넬과 같은 인물이다(사무엘상 14:50 난외).

entries.definition: the father of Barak. (Judges 4:6,12; 5:1,12) (B.C. 1300.)
entries.definition_ko: 바락의 아버지이다(사사기 4:6).

entries.definition: • A Reubenite, son of Eliab, who with Korah, a Levite, organized a conspiracy against Moses and Aaron. (Numbers 16:1) ... [For details, see Korah] (B.C. 1490.) • Eldest son of Hiel the bethelite, who died when his father laid the foundations of Jericho, (1 Kings 16:34) and thus accomplished the first part of the curse of Joshua. (Joshua 6:26) (B.C. after 905.)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 르우벤 사람 엘리압의 아들로 레위인 고라와 함께 모세와 아론에 대한 반역을 조직했다(민수기 16:1). (2) 벧엘 사람 히엘의 맏아들로 아버지가 여리고 성 기초를 놓을 때 죽어 여호수아의 저주를 성취시켰다(열왕기상 16:34).

entries.definition: a beautiful Shunammite (from Shunem, in the tribe of Issachar), taken into David’s harem to comfort him in his extreme old age. (1 Kings 1:1-4)
entries.definition_ko: 잇사갈 지파 수넴 출신의 아름다운 여인으로 다윗의 노년을 위로하기 위해 후궁으로 들어왔다(열왕기상 1:1-4).

entries.definition: (father of a gift), The eldest of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and brother to Joab and Asahel. (1 Chronicles 2:16) Like his two brothers he was the devoted follower of David. He was his companion in the desperate night expedition to the camp of Saul. (1 Samuel 26:6-9) (B.C. 1055.) On the outbreak of Absalom’s rebellion he remained true to the king, and commanded a third part of the army in the decisive battle against Absalom. He rescued David from the hands of the gigantic Philistine, Ishbi-benob. (2 Samuel 21:17) His personal prowess on this, as on another occasion, when he fought singlehanded against three hundred, won for him a place as captain of the second three of David’s mighty men. (2 Samuel 23:18; 1 Chronicles 11:20)
entries.definition_ko: '선물의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 누이 스루야의 세 아들 중 맏이이며 요압과 아사헬의 형제이다(역대상 2:16). 다윗을 충성스럽게 따랐고 사울의 진영으로 함께 야습을 갔으며, 압살롬 반역 때는 군대의 삼분의 일을 지휘했다. 거인 블레셋 사람 이스비브놉으로부터 다윗을 구했다(사무엘하 21:17).

entries.definition: (father of peace), father or grandfather of Maachah, who was the wife of Rehoboam and mother of Abijah. (1 Kings 15:2,10) He is called Absalom in (2 Chronicles 11:20,21) This person must be David’s son. See LXX.; (2 Samuel 14:27)
entries.definition_ko: '평화의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 르호보암의 아내이자 아비야의 어머니인 마아가의 아버지 또는 조부이며(열왕기상 15:2) 역대하 11:20에서는 압살롬이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (father of deliverance). • Son of Bela, of the tribe of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 8:4) • Son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, and father of Bukki, in the genealogy of the high priests. (1 Chronicles 6:4,5,50,51; Ezra 7:4,5)
entries.definition_ko: '구원의 아버지'라는 뜻. (1) 베냐민 지파 벨라의 아들(역대상 8:4). (2) 비느하스의 아들이자 대제사장 족보에서 북기의 아버지(역대상 6:4).

entries.definition: (father of the wall), son of Shammai. (1 Chronicles 2:28)
entries.definition_ko: '벽의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 삼매의 아들이다(역대상 2:28).

entries.definition: (father of the dew), one of David’s wives. (2 Samuel 3:4; 1 Chronicles 3:3)
entries.definition_ko: '이슬의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 아내 중 하나이다(사무엘하 3:4).

entries.definition: (father of goodness), son of Shaharaim by Hushim. (1 Chronicles 8:11)
entries.definition_ko: '선함의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 사하라임이 후심을 통해 낳은 아들이다(역대상 8:11).

entries.definition: (father of praise), descendant of Zorobabel in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. (Matthew 1:13)
entries.definition_ko: '찬양의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 예수 그리스도의 족보에서 스룹바벨의 후손이다(마태복음 1:13).

entries.definition: [Purification]
entries.definition_ko: 정결례(PURIFICATION) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (father of light). • Son of Ner, who was the brother of Kish, (1 Chronicles 9:36) the father of Saul. (B.C. 1063.) Abner, therefore, was Saul’s first cousin, and was made by him commanderin-chief of his army. (1 Samuel 14:51; 17:57; 26:5-14) After the death of Saul David was proclaimed king of Judah; and some time subsequently Abner proclaimed Ishbosheth, Saul’s son, king of Israel. War soon broke out between the two rival kings, and a “very sore battle” was fought at Gibeon between the men of Israel under Abner and the men of Judah under Joab. (1 Chronicles 2:16) Abner had married Rizpah, Saul’s concubine, and this, according to the views of Oriental courts, might be so interpreted as to imply a design upon the throne. Rightly or wrongly, Ish-bosheth so understood it, and he even ventured to reproach Abner with it. Abner, incensed at his ingratitude, opened negotiations with David, by whom he was most favorably received at Hebron. He then undertook to procure his recognition throughout Israel; but after leaving his presence for the purpose was enticed back by Joab, and treacherously murdered by him and his brother Abishai, at the gate of the city, partly, no doubt, from fear lest so distinguished a convert to their cause should gain too high a place in David’s favor, but ostensibly in retaliation for the death of Asahel. David in sorrow and indignation, poured forth a simple dirge over the slain hero. (2 Samuel 3:33,34) • The father of Jaasiel, chief of the Benjamites in David’s reign, (1 Chronicles 27:21) probably the same as the preceding.
entries.definition_ko: '빛의 아버지'라는 뜻. 넬의 아들로 사울의 아버지 기스의 형제이며(역대상 9:36) 사울에 의해 군대 총사령관이 되었다. 사울 사후 사울의 아들 이스보셋을 이스라엘 왕으로 세웠으나 다윗과 협상하다가 요압에게 배신당해 살해되었다(사무엘하 3:33,34).

entries.definition: Mentioned by our Saviour, (Matthew 24:15) as a sign of the approaching destruction of Jerusalem, with reference to (Daniel 9:27; 11:31; 12:11) The prophecy referred ultimately to the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans, and consequently the “abomination” must describe some occurrence connected with that event. It appears most probable that the profanities of the Zealots constituted the abomination, which was the sign of the impending ruin; but most people refer it to the standards or banners of the Roman army. They were abomination because there were idolatrous images upon them.
entries.definition_ko: 주님이 예루살렘 멸망의 징조로 언급하신 표현으로(마태복음 24:15) 다니엘서를 인용한 것이다. 궁극적으로 로마에 의한 예루살렘 파괴를 가리키며, 열심당의 신성모독 행위 또는 로마 군대의 우상이 새겨진 깃발을 가리키는 것으로 해석된다.

entries.definition: (father of a multitude) was the son of Terah, and founder of the great Hebrew nation. (B.C. 1996-1822.) His family, a branch of the descendants of Shem, was settled in Ur of the Chaldees, beyond the Euphrates, where Abraham was born. Terah had two other sons, Nahor and Haran. Haran died before his father in Ur of the Chaldees, leaving a son, Lot; and Terah, taking with him Abram, with Sarai his wife and his grandson Lot, emigrated to Haran in Mesopotamia, where he died. On the death of his father, Abram, then in the 75th year of his age, with Sarai and Lot, pursued his course to the land of Canaan, whither he was directed by divine command, (Genesis 12:5) when he received the general promise that he should become the founder of a great nation, and that all the families of the earth should be blessed in him. He passed through the heart of the country by the great highway to Shechem, and pitched his tent beneath the terebinth of Moreh. (Genesis 12:6) Here he received in vision from Jehovah the further revelation that this was the land which his descendants should inherit. (Genesis 12:7) The next halting-place of the wanderer was on a mountain between Bethel and Ai, (Genesis 12:8) but the country was suffering from famine, and Abram journeyed still southward to the rich cornlands of Egypt. There, fearing that the great beauty of Sarai might tempt the powerful monarch of Egypt and expose his own life to peril, he arranged that Sarai should represent herself as his sister, which her actual relationship to him, as probably the daughter of his brother Haran, allowed her to do with some semblance of truth. But her beauty was reported to the king, and she was taken into the royal harem. The deception was discovered, and Pharaoh with some indignation dismissed Abram from the country. (Genesis 12:10-20) He left Egypt with great possessions, and, accompanied by Lot, returned by the south of Palestine to his former encampment between Bethel and Ai. The increased wealth of the two kinsmen was the ultimate cause of their separation. Lot chose the fertile plain of the Jordan near Sodom, while Abram pitched his tent among the groves of Mamre, close to Hebron. (Genesis 13:1) ... Lot with his family and possessions having been carried away captive by Chedorlaomer king of Elam, who had invaded Sodom, Abram pursued the conquerors and utterly routed them not far from Damascus. The captives and plunder were all recovered, and Abram was greeted on his return by the king of Sodom, and by Melchizedek king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who mysteriously appears upon the scene to bless the patriarch and receive from him a tenth of the spoil. (Genesis 14:1) ... After this the thrice-repeated promise that his descendants should become a mighty nation and possess the land in which he was a stranger was confirmed with all the solemnity of a religious ceremony. (Genesis 15:1) ... Ten years had passed since he had left his father’s house, and the fulfillment of the promise was apparently more distant than at first. At the suggestion of Sarai, who despaired of having children of her own, he took as his concubine Hagar, her Egyptian main, who bore him Ishmael in the 86th year of his age. (Genesis 16:1) ... [Hagar; Ishmael] But this was not the accomplishment of the promise. Thirteen years elapsed, during which Abram still dwelt in Hebron, when the covenant was renewed, and the rite of circumcision established as its sign. This most important crisis in Abram’s life, when he was 99 years old, is marked by the significant change of his name to Abraham, “father of a multitude;” while his wife’s from Sarai became Sarah. The promise that Sarah should have a son was repeated in the remarkable scene described in ch. 18. Three men stood before Abraham as he sat in his tent door in the heat of the day. The patriarch, with true Eastern hospitality, welcomed the strangers, and bade them rest and refresh themselves. The meal ended, they foretold the birth of Isaac, and went on their way to Sodom. Abraham accompanied them, and is represented as an interlocutor in a dialogue with Jehovah, in which he pleaded in vain to avert the vengeance threatened to the devoted cities of the plain. (Genesis 18:17-33) In remarkable contrast with Abraham’s firm faith with regard to the magnificent fortunes of his posterity stand the incident which occurred during his temporary residence among the Philistines in Gerar, whither he had for some cause removed after the destruction of Sodom. It was almost a repetition of what took place in Egypt a few years before. At length Isaac, the long-looked for child, was born. Sarah’s jealousy aroused by the mockery of Ishmael at the “great banquet” which Abram made to celebrate the weaning of her son, (Genesis 21:9) demanded that, with his mother Hagar, he should be driven out. (Genesis 21:10) But the severest trial of his faith was yet to come. For a long period the history is almost silent. At length he receives the strange command to take Isaac, his only son, and offer him for a burnt offering at an appointed place Abraham hesitated not to obey. His faith, hitherto unshaken, supported him in this final trial, “accounting that God was able to raise up his son, even from the dead, from whence also he received him in a figure.” (Hebrews 11:19) The sacrifice was stayed by the angel of Jehovah, the promise of spiritual blessing made for the first time, and Abraham with his son returned to Beersheba, and for a time dwelt there. (Genesis 22:1) ... But we find him after a few years in his original residence at Hebron, for there Sarah died, (Genesis 23:2) and was buried in the cave of Machpelah. The remaining years of Abraham’s life are marked by but few incidents. After Isaac’s marriage with Rebekah and his removal to Lahairoi, Abraham took to wife Keturah, by whom he had six children, Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbok and Shuah, who became the ancestors of nomadic tribes inhabiting the countries south and southeast of Palestine. Abraham lived to see the gradual accomplishment of the promise in the birth of his grandchildren Jacob and Esau, and witnessed their growth to manhood. (Genesis 25:26) At the goodly age of 175 he was “gathered to his people,” and laid beside Sarah in the tomb of Machpelah by his sons Isaac and Ishmael. (Genesis 25:7-10)
entries.definition_ko:
('무리의 아버지'라는 뜻) 데라의 아들이며 큰 히브리 민족의 조상이다(주전 1996-1822년). 셈의 자손에서 갈라져 나온 그 집안은 유브라데 저편 갈대아 우르에 자리 잡고 있었고 아브라함이 거기서 났다. 데라에게는 나홀과 하란이라는 두 아들이 더 있었는데, 하란은 아버지보다 먼저 갈대아 우르에서 죽으며 아들 롯을 남겼다. 데라는 아브람과 그 아내 사래와 손자 롯을 데리고 메소보다미아 하란으로 옮겨 가 거기서 죽었다. 아버지가 죽자 일흔다섯 살이던 아브람은 사래와 롯과 함께 하나님의 명령을 따라 가나안 땅으로 나아갔고(창세기 12:5), 자기가 큰 민족의 조상이 되며 땅의 모든 족속이 그로 말미암아 복을 얻으리라는 두루뭉술한 약속을 받았다. 그는 큰길을 따라 나라 한복판을 지나 세겜에 이르러 모레 상수리나무 아래 장막을 쳤다(창세기 12:6). 여기서 이 땅을 그 자손이 차지하리라는 더 나아간 계시를 여호와께 환상으로 받았다(12:7). 다음으로 머문 곳은 벧엘과 아이 사이 산이었으나(12:8), 그 땅에 기근이 들어 아브람은 더 남쪽으로 곡식이 풍성한 애굽으로 내려갔다. 거기서 그는 사래의 빼어난 아름다움이 애굽의 강력한 군주를 끌어 자기 목숨이 위태로울까 두려워하여, 사래로 자기 누이라 하게 하였다. 아마도 그 형 하란의 딸이었을 터이므로 실제 관계상 얼마쯤 그럴듯하게 그리 말할 수 있었다. 그러나 그 아름다움이 왕에게 알려져 사래가 왕궁으로 불려 들어갔다. 속임이 드러나자 바로가 얼마쯤 분노하며 아브람을 그 나라에서 내보냈다(12:10-20). 그는 큰 재물을 지니고 애굽을 떠나 롯과 함께 팔레스타인 남쪽을 지나 벧엘과 아이 사이 옛 진 친 곳으로 돌아왔다. 두 친족의 재산이 늘어난 것이 마침내 그들이 갈라지는 까닭이 되었다. 롯은 소돔 가까운 요단의 기름진 들을 골랐고 아브람은 헤브론 가까운 마므레 상수리 수풀에 장막을 쳤다(창세기 13장).
소돔을 침공한 엘람 왕 그돌라오멜에게 롯이 가족과 재산과 함께 사로잡혀 가자 아브람이 정복자들을 뒤쫓아 다메섹에서 멀지 않은 곳에서 그들을 온전히 무찔렀다. 포로와 노략물을 다 되찾았고, 돌아오는 그를 소돔 왕과, 지극히 높으신 하나님의 제사장인 살렘 왕 멜기세덱이 맞았다. 멜기세덱은 신비롭게 나타나 족장을 축복하고 그에게서 노략물의 십분의 일을 받는다(창세기 14장). 이 뒤에 그 자손이 큰 민족이 되어 그가 나그네로 있는 땅을 차지하리라는 세 번 거듭된 약속이 종교 예식의 온 엄숙함으로 확인되었다(창세기 15장). 아버지 집을 떠난 지 열 해가 지났으나 약속의 이룸은 처음보다 도리어 멀어 보였다. 자기 자식을 낳기를 단념한 사래의 제안으로 그는 그 애굽 여종 하갈을 첩으로 삼았고, 그가 여든여섯 살에 이스마엘을 낳았다(창세기 16장). 그러나 이것이 약속의 이룸은 아니었다. 열세 해가 더 흘러 아브람이 여전히 헤브론에 살 때 언약이 새로워지고 할례가 그 표징으로 세워졌다. 아흔아홉 살에 있었던 이 더없이 중요한 고비는 그 이름이 '무리의 아버지'라는 뜻의 아브라함으로, 아내의 이름이 사래에서 사라로 뜻깊게 바뀐 것으로 표시된다. 사라가 아들을 낳으리라는 약속이 18장에 서술된 놀라운 장면에서 거듭되었다. 날이 뜨거울 때 장막 문에 앉아 있는 아브라함 앞에 세 사람이 섰다. 족장은 참된 동방의 후대로 나그네들을 맞아 쉬며 기운을 차리게 하였다. 식사가 끝나자 그들은 이삭이 날 것을 예고하고 소돔으로 향하였다. 아브라함이 따라가며 여호와와 나눈 대화에서, 그 평지의 성읍들에 선고된 진노를 돌이키려고 간구하였으나 뜻을 이루지 못하였다(창세기 18:17-33).
자기 자손의 웅대한 앞날에 대한 아브라함의 굳은 믿음과 뚜렷이 대비되는 일이, 소돔이 멸망한 뒤 어떤 까닭으로 옮겨 가 블레셋 그랄에 잠시 머무는 동안 일어났으니, 몇 해 전 애굽에서 있었던 일의 되풀이나 다름없었다. 마침내 오래 기다린 아이 이삭이 났다. 아들의 젖 떼는 것을 기려 아브라함이 베푼 '큰 잔치'에서 이스마엘이 조롱하매 사라의 질투가 일어(창세기 21:9) 그 어미 하갈과 함께 내쫓으라고 요구하였다(21:10). 그러나 그 믿음의 가장 혹독한 시련은 아직 오지 않았다. 오랫동안 역사는 거의 침묵한다. 마침내 그는 외아들 이삭을 데려다 정한 곳에서 번제로 드리라는 이상한 명령을 받았고 곧 순종하였다. 지금까지 흔들리지 않은 그 믿음이 이 마지막 시련에서도 그를 붙들었으니, '그가 하나님이 능히 이삭을 죽은 자 가운데서 다시 살리실 줄로 생각한지라 비유컨대 그를 죽은 자 가운데서 도로 받은 것이니라'(히브리서 11:19). 여호와의 사자가 그 제사를 그치게 하였고 영적 복의 약속이 처음으로 주어졌으며, 아브라함은 아들과 함께 브엘세바로 돌아와 한동안 거기 살았다(창세기 22장). 그러나 몇 해 뒤 본래 살던 헤브론에 있었으니 거기서 사라가 죽어(23:2) 막벨라 굴에 장사되었다. 아브라함의 남은 생애에는 사건이 별로 없다. 이삭이 리브가와 혼인하여 라해로이로 옮겨 간 뒤 아브라함은 그두라를 아내로 맞아 시므란과 욕산과 므단과 미디안과 이스박과 수아 여섯 자녀를 얻었으니, 그들이 팔레스타인 남쪽과 남동쪽 여러 나라에 사는 유목 족속의 조상이 되었다. 아브라함은 손자 야곱과 에서가 나서 장성하는 것을 보아 약속이 차츰 이루어지는 것을 보았고(창세기 25:26), 백칠십오 세의 좋은 나이에 '자기 백성에게로 돌아가' 두 아들 이삭과 이스마엘의 손으로 사라 곁 막벨라 무덤에 뉘였다(25:7-10).

entries.definition: (a high father), the earlier name of Abraham.
entries.definition_ko: '높은 아버지'라는 뜻으로 아브라함의 이전 이름이다.

entries.definition: (father of peace), third son of David by Maachah, daughter of Tamai king of Geshur, a Syrian district adjoining the northeast frontier of the Holy Land. (Born B.C. 1050.) Absalom had a sister, Tamar, who was violated by her half-brother Amnon. The natural avenger of such an outrage would be Tamar’s full brother Absalom. He brooded over the wrong for two years, and then invited all the princes to a sheepshearing feast at his estate in Baalhazor, on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin. Here he ordered his servants to murder Amnon, and then fled for safety to his grandfather’s court at Geshur, where he remained for three years. At the end of that time he was brought back by an artifice of Joab. David, however, would not see Absalom for two more years; but at length Joab brought about a reconciliation. Absalom now began at once to prepare for rebellion. He tried to supplant his father by courting popularity, standing in the gate, conversing with every suitor, and lamenting the difficulty which he would find in getting a hearing. He also maintained a splendid retinue, (2 Samuel 15:1) and was admired for his personal beauty. It is probable too that the great tribe of Judah had taken some offence at David’s government. Absalom raised the standard of revolt at Hebron, the old capital of Judah, now supplanted by Jerusalem. The revolt was at first completely successful; David fled from his capital over the Jordan to Mahanaim in Gilead, and Absalom occupied Jerusalem. At last, after being solemnly anointed king at Jerusalem, (2 Samuel 19:10) Absalom crossed the Jordan to attack his father, who by this time had rallied round him a considerable force. A decisive battle was fought in Gilead, in the wood of Ephraim. Here Absalom’s forces were totally defeated, and as he himself was escaping his long hair was entangled in the branches of a terebinth, where he was left hanging while the mule on which he was riding ran away from under him. He was dispatched by Joab in spite of the prohibition of David, who, loving him to the last, had desired that his life might be spared. He was buried in a great pit in the forest, and the conquerors threw stones over his grave, an old proof of bitter hostility. (Joshua 7:26)
entries.definition_ko: '평화의 아버지'라는 뜻으로 다윗과 그술 왕 달매의 딸 마아가 사이의 셋째 아들이다. 누이 다말이 이복형 암논에게 욕을 당하자 2년 뒤 그를 살해하고 그술로 피신했다가 요압의 중재로 돌아왔다. 이후 반역을 일으켜 헤브론에서 왕위에 올랐으나 에브라임 숲 전투에서 패해 도망치던 중 머리카락이 상수리나무에 걸려 요압에게 죽임을 당했다.

entries.definition: A monument of tomb which Absalom had built during his lifetime in the king’s dale, i.e. the valley of the Kedron, at the foot of Mount Olivet, near Jerusalem, (2 Samuel 18:18) comp. with 2Sam 14:27For his three sons, and where he probably expected to be buried. The tomb there now, and called by Absalom’s name was probably built at a later date.
entries.definition_ko: 압살롬이 생전에 왕의 골짜기(기드론 골짜기)에 세운 기념 무덤으로(사무엘하 18:18) 자신의 세 아들을 위해서라도 남기려 했던 것으로 추정되나, 오늘날 그의 이름으로 불리는 무덤은 후대에 지어진 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: one of the cities in the land of Shinar. (Genesis 10:10) Its position is quite uncertain.
entries.definition_ko: 시날 땅의 도시 중 하나이다(창세기 10:10). 정확한 위치는 알려져 있지 않다.

entries.definition: [Ekron]
entries.definition_ko: 에그론(EKRON) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (the Ptolemaisof the Maccabees and New Testament), Now called Acca, or more usually by Europeans St. Jean d’Acre, the most important seaport town on the Syrian coast, about 30 miles south of Tyre. It was situated on a slightly projecting headland, at the northern extremity of that spacious bay which is formed by the bold promontory of Carmel on the opposite side. Later it was named Ptolemais, after one of the Ptolemies, probably Soter. The only notice of it in the New Testament is in (Acts 21:7) where it is called Ptolemais .
entries.definition_ko: 마카베오서와 신약의 '돌레마이'로, 오늘날 아카 또는 유럽인들이 부르는 생장다크르라 불리며 두로 남쪽 약 30마일의 수리아 해안 최대 항구 도시였다. 신약에는 사도행전 21:7에서 돌레마이로 한 번 언급된다.

entries.definition: (the field of blood) (Akeldama in the Revised Version), the name given by the Jews of Jerusalem to a field near Jerusalem purchased by Judas with the money which he received for the betrayal of Christ, and so called from his violent death therein. (Acts 1:19) The “field of blood” is now shown on the steep southern face of the valley or ravine of Hinnom, “southwest of the supposed pool of Siloam.”
entries.definition_ko: '피의 밭'이라는 뜻으로(개정역에는 아겔다마) 유다가 그리스도를 배반하고 받은 돈으로 산 예루살렘 근처의 밭이며 그의 처참한 죽음으로 인해 이 이름이 붙었다(사도행전 1:19). 오늘날 힌놈 골짜기 남쪽 가파른 경사면에 그 위치가 전해진다.

entries.definition: (trouble) signifies in the New Testament a Roman province which included the whole of the Peloponnesus and the greater part of Hellas proper, with the adjacent islands. This province, with that of Macedonia, comprehended the while of Greece; hence Achaia and Macedonia are frequently mentioned together in the New Testament to indicate all Greece. (Acts 18:12; 19:21; Romans 15:26; 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:15; 2 Corinthians 7:5; 9:2; 11:10; 1 Thessalonians 1:7,8) In the time of the emperor Claudius it was governed by a proconsul, translated in the Authorized Version “deputy,” of Achaia. (Acts 18:12)
entries.definition_ko: '고난'이라는 뜻으로 신약에서 펠로폰네소스 반도 전체와 헬라스 본토 대부분을 포함한 로마 속주를 가리킨다. 마케도니아와 함께 언급되어 헬라 전체를 가리키는 데 쓰였다(사도행전 18:12).

entries.definition: (belonging to Achaia), a name of a Christian. (1 Corinthians 16:17)
entries.definition_ko: '아가야에 속한'이라는 뜻으로 그리스도인의 이름이다(고린도전서 16:17).

entries.definition: (troubler), an Israelite of the tribe of Judah, who, when Jericho and all that it contained were accursed and devoted to destruction, secreted a portion of the spoil in his tent. For this sin he was stoned to death with his whole family by the people, in a valley situated between Ai and Jericho, and their remains, together with his property, were burnt. (Joshua 7:19-26) From this event the valley received the name of Achor (i.e. trouble). [Achor, Valley Of] (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '훼방하는 자'라는 뜻으로 유다 지파 이스라엘 사람이며, 여리고 함락 때 온전히 바쳐야 할 전리품 일부를 자신의 장막에 숨겼다가 발각되어 온 가족과 함께 돌에 맞아 죽고 재산도 불태워졌다(여호수아 7:19-26). 이 사건으로 그 골짜기는 아골(곧 '고난')이라 불리게 되었다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 2:7)
entries.definition_ko: 아간과 동일 인물이다(역대상 2:7).

entries.definition: king of Judah, (Matthew 1:9)
entries.definition_ko: 아하스 왕을 가리키는 헬라어식 표기이다(마태복음 1:9).

entries.definition: (mouse). • Father of Baalhanan king of Edom. (Genesis 36:38,39; 1 Chronicles 1:49) • Son of Michaiah, a contemporary of Josiah, (2 Kings 22:12,14; Jeremiah 26:22; 36:12) called Abdonin (2 Chronicles 34:20) (B.C. 623.)
entries.definition_ko: '쥐'라는 뜻. (1) 에돔 왕 바알하난의 아버지(창세기 36:38). (2) 요시야 시대 미가야의 아들로 역대하 34:20에서는 압돈이라 불린다(열왕기하 22:12).

entries.definition: son of Sadoc and father of Eliud in our Lord’s genealogy. (Matthew 1:14) The Hebrew form of the name would be Jachin, which is a short form of Jehoiachin, the Lord will establish.
entries.definition_ko: 사독의 아들이자 주님의 족보에서 엘리웃의 아버지이다(마태복음 1:14). 히브리어 형태는 여호야긴('여호와께서 세우시리라')의 축약형 야긴으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (angry), a Philistine king of Gath, who in the title of the 34th Psalm is called Abimelech. David twice found a refuge with him when he fled from Saul. (B.C. 1061.) On the first occasion he was alarmed for his safety, feigned madness, and was sent away.
entries.definition_ko: '성난'이라는 뜻으로 가드의 블레셋 왕이며 시편 34편 표제에서는 아비멜렉이라 불린다. 다윗이 사울을 피해 두 번 그에게 피신했으며 첫 번째는 미친 척하여 위기를 모면했다.

entries.definition: [Ecbatana]
entries.definition_ko: 악메다(ECBATANA) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (valley of trouble), the spot at which Achan was stoned. (Joshua 7:24,26) On the northern boundary of Judah, (Joshua 15:7) near Jericho.
entries.definition_ko: '고난의 골짜기'라는 뜻으로 아간이 돌에 맞아 죽은 장소이다(여호수아 7:24). 유다 북쪽 경계, 여리고 근처에 위치한다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 2:49) [Achsah]
entries.definition_ko: 악사(ACHSAH) 항목 참조(역대상 2:49).

entries.definition: (ankle-chain, anklet), daughter of Caleb. Her father promised her in marriage to whoever should take Debir. Othniel, her father’s younger brother, took that city, and accordingly received the hand of Achsah as his reward. Caleb added to her dowry the upper and lower springs. (B.C. 1450-1426.) (Joshua 15:15-19; Judges 1:11-15)
entries.definition_ko: '발목 사슬, 발찌'라는 뜻으로 갈렙의 딸이다. 아버지가 드빌을 정복하는 자에게 그녀를 아내로 주겠다고 약속했고, 갈렙의 조카 옷니엘이 그 성을 정복해 악사를 아내로 얻었다. 갈렙은 그녀에게 윗샘과 아랫샘을 더해 주었다(여호수아 15:15-19).

entries.definition: (fascination), a city within the territory of Asher, named between Beten and Alammelech, (Joshua 19:25) originally the seat of a Canaanite king. (Joshua 11:1; 12:20)
entries.definition_ko: '매혹'이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파 영토 안의 성읍이며 베덴과 알람멜렉 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 19:25). 본래 가나안 왕의 거처였다.

entries.definition: (lying, false). • A city in the lowlands of Judah, named with Keilah and Mareshah. (Joshua 15:44; Micah 1:14) It is probably the same with Cheziband Chozeba, which see. • A town belonging to Asher, (Joshua 19:29) from which the Canaanites were not expelled, (Judges 1:31) afterwards Ecdippa. It is now es-Zib, on the seashore, 2h. 20m. north of Acre.
entries.definition_ko: '거짓의'라는 뜻. (1) 유다 저지대의 성읍으로 그일라, 마레사와 함께 언급됨(여호수아 15:44); 그십, 고세바와 동일시된다. (2) 아셀 지파에 속한 성읍으로 가나안 사람들이 쫓겨나지 않았으며(사사기 1:31) 후에 엑딥바로 불렸다.

entries.definition: See MAALEH-ACRABBIM, (Joshua 15:3) in the margin.
entries.definition_ko: 마알레아그랍빔(MAALEH-ACRABBIM) 항목 참조이다(여호수아 15:3 난외주).

entries.definition: the fifth book in the New testament and the second treatise by the author of the third Gospel, traditionally known as Luke. The book commences with an inscription to one Theophilus, who was probably a man of birth and station. The readers were evidently intended to be the members of the Christian Church, whether Jews or Gentiles; for its contents are such as are of the utmost consequence to the whole Church. They are the fulfillment of the promise of the Father by the descent of the Holy Spirit, and the results of that outpouring by the dispersion of the gospel among the Jews and Gentiles. Under these leading heads all the personal and subordinate details may be arranged. First St. Peter becomes the prime actor under God int he founding of the Church. He is the centre of the first group of sayings and doings. The opening of the door to Jews, ch. 2, and Gentiles, ch. 10, is his office, and by him, in good time, is accomplished. Then the preparation of Saul of Tarsus for the work to be done, the progress, in his hand, of that work, his journeyings, preachings and perils, his stripes and imprisonments, his testifying in Jerusalem and being brought to testify in Rome,—these are the subjects of the latter half of the book, of which the great central figure is the apostle Paul. The history given in the Acts occupies about 33 years, and the reigns of the Roman emperors Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius and Nero. It seems most probable that the place of writing was Roma, and the time about two years from the date of St. Paul’s arrival there, as related in (Acts 28:30) This would give us fro the publication about 63 A.D.
entries.definition_ko: 신약의 다섯 번째 책으로 누가복음 저자(전승상 누가)의 두 번째 저작이다. 데오빌로에게 헌정되었으며 성령 강림과 복음의 유대인·이방인 전파를 다룬다. 전반부는 베드로가, 후반부는 바울이 중심인물이며, 대략 33년의 역사를 다루고 로마에서 주후 63년경 기록된 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (festival or boundary), one of the cities in the extreme south of Judah, named with Dimonah and Kedesh. (Joshua 15:22)
entries.definition_ko: '축제 또는 경계'라는 뜻으로 유다 남단의 성읍이며 디모나, 게데스와 함께 언급된다(여호수아 15:22).

entries.definition: (ornament, beauty). • The first of the two wives of Lamech, by whom were borne to him Jabal and Jubal. (Genesis 4:19) (B.C. 3600). • A Hittitess, one of the three wives of Esau, mother of Eliphaz. (Genesis 36:2,10,12,16) In (Genesis 26:34) she is called Bashemath. (B.C. 1797.)
entries.definition_ko: '장식, 아름다움'이라는 뜻. (1) 라멕의 두 아내 중 첫째로 야발과 유발을 낳았다(창세기 4:19). (2) 헷 사람으로 에서의 세 아내 중 하나이며 엘리바스의 어머니(창세기 36:2); 창세기 26:34에서는 바스맛이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (adorned by Jehovah). • Maternal grandfather of King Josiah, and native of Boscath in the lowlands of Judah. (2 Kings 22:1) (B.C. 648.) • A Levite of the Gershonite branch, and ancestor of Asaph. (1 Chronicles 6:41) In v. (1 Chronicles 6:21) Heb Isa called Iddo. • A Benjamite, son of Shimhi, (1 Chronicles 8:21) who is apparently the same as Shema in v. (1 Chronicles 8:13) • A priest, son of Jehoram. (1 Chronicles 9:12; Nehemiah 11:12) • Ancestor of Maaseiah, one of the captains who supported Jehoiada. (2 Chronicles 23:1) • One of the descendants of Bani, who had married a foreign wife after the return from Babylon. (Ezra 10:29) (B.C. 459). • The descendant of another Bani, who had also taken a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:39) • A man of Judah, of the line of Pharez. (Nehemiah 11:5)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 꾸미신'이라는 뜻. (1) 요시야 왕의 외조부(열왕기하 22:1). (2) 게르손 가문 레위인으로 아삽의 조상(역대상 6:41). (3) 베냐민 사람 시므이의 아들(역대상 8:21). (4) 여호람의 아들인 제사장(역대상 9:12). (5) 여호야다를 지지한 마아세야의 조상(역대하 23:1). (6)(7) 포로 후 이방 여인과 결혼한 바니 자손들(에스라 10:29,39). (8) 베레스 계열 유다 사람(느헤미야 11:5).

entries.definition: (a fire-god), the fifth son of Haman. (Esther 9:8)
entries.definition_ko: '불의 신'이라는 뜻으로 하만의 다섯째 아들이다(에스더 9:8).

entries.definition: a city on the Jordan, “beside Zaretan,” in the time of Joshua. (Joshua 3:16) Man, generically, for the name Adam was not confined to the father of the human race, but like homo was applicable to woman as well as to man . (Genesis 5:2) (red earth), the name given in Scripture to the first man. It apparently has reference to the ground from which he was formed, which is called in Hebrew Adamah . The idea of redness of color seems to be inherent in either word. The creation of man was the work of the sixth day—the last and crowning act of creation. Adam was created (not born) a perfect man in body and spirit, but as innocent and completely inexperienced as a child. The man Adam was placed in a garden which the Lord God had planted “eastward in Eden,” for the purpose of dressing it and keeping it. [Eden] Adam was permitted to eat of the fruit of every tree in the garden but one, which was called (“the tree of the knowledge of good and evil,” because it was the test of Adam’s obedience. By it Adam could know good and evil int he divine way, through obedience; thus knowing good by experience in resisting temptation and forming a strong and holy character, while he knew evil only by observation and inference. Or he could “know good and evil,” in Satan’s way, be experiencing the evil and knowing good only by contrast. -ED.) The prohibition to taste the fruit of this tree was enforced by the menace of death. There was also another tree which was called “the tree of life.” While Adam was in the garden of Eden, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air were brought to him to be named. After this the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and took one of his ribs from him, which he fashioned into a woman and brought her to the man. At this time they were both described as being naked without the consciousness of shame. By the subtlety of the serpent the woman who was given to be with Adam was beguiled into a violation of the one command which had been imposed upon them. She took of the fruit of the forbidden tree and gave it to her husband. The propriety of its name was immediately shown in the results which followed; selfconsciousness was the first-fruits of sin their eyes were opened and they knew that they were naked. Though the curse of Adam’s rebellion of necessity fell upon him, yet the very prohibition to eat of the tree of life after his transgression was probably a manifestation of divine mercy, because the greatest malediction of all would have been to have the gift of indestructible life super-added to a state of wretchedness and sin. The divine mercy was also shown in the promise of a deliverer given at the very promise of a deliverer given at the very time the curse was imposed, (Genesis 3:15) and opening a door of hope to Paradise, regained for him and his descendants. Adam is stated to have lived 930 years. His sons mentioned in Scripture are Cain, Abel and Seth; it is implied, however, that he had others.
entries.definition_ko: 요단강가의 사르단 곁 성읍(여호수아 3:16)이자, 성경에서 최초의 사람에게 붙여진 이름이다. 흙(아다마)에서 지어졌다는 데서 유래한 이름으로 추정된다. 하나님이 엿새째 창조하신 완전한 사람이었으며 에덴동산에 두어 지키게 하셨다. 선악을 알게 하는 나무의 열매를 먹지 말라는 명을 받았으나 뱀의 유혹을 받은 아내 하와에게서 열매를 받아먹어 범죄했다. 930세를 살았으며 가인, 아벨, 셋 등의 아들을 두었다.

entries.definition: (red earth), one of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali, named between Chinnereth and Ramah. (Joshua 19:36)
entries.definition_ko: '붉은 흙'이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 요새화된 성읍 중 하나이며 긴네렛과 라마 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 19:36).

entries.definition: the translation of the Hebrew word Shamir in (Ezekiel 3:9) and Zech 7:12In (Jeremiah 17:1) it is translated “diamond.” In these three passages the word is the representative of some stone of excessive hardness, and is used metaphorically. It is very probable that by Shamir is intended emery, a variety of corundum, a mineral inferior, only to the diamond in hardness.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 샤미르의 번역어로(에스겔 3:9) 예레미야 17:1에서는 '금강석'으로 번역된다. 매우 단단한 돌을 상징적으로 가리키며 다이아몬드 다음으로 단단한 강옥(코런덤)의 일종인 에머리일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (my man, earth), a place on the border of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:33)
entries.definition_ko: '나의 사람, 흙'이라는 뜻으로 납달리 경계의 한 장소이다(여호수아 19:33).

entries.definition: [Month] (high), a place on the south boundary of Judah. (Joshua 15:3)
entries.definition_ko: 월(MONTH) 항목 참조; 또한 '높은'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 경계의 한 장소이다(여호수아 15:3).

entries.definition: (new), a place in Judea, about four miles from Beth-horon. 1Ma 7:40,45[Hadashah]
entries.definition_ko: '새로운'이라는 뜻으로 벧호론에서 약 4마일 떨어진 유대의 한 장소이며 하다사(HADASHAH)와 관련된다.

entries.definition: (offspring of God), a son of Ishmael, (Genesis 25:13; 1 Chronicles 1:29) and probably the progenitor of an Arab tribe. (B.C. about 1850.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 자손'이라는 뜻으로 이스마엘의 아들이며(창세기 25:13) 아라비아 부족의 조상으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (strong or stony), one of the places from which some of the captivity returned with Zerubbabel to Judea who could not show their pedigree as Israelites. (Ezra 2:59) Called Addon(Nehemiah 7:61)
entries.definition_ko: '강한 또는 돌의'라는 뜻으로 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 포로 중 이스라엘 혈통을 증명하지 못한 자들이 나온 곳이며(에스라 2:59) 느헤미야 7:61에서는 앗돈이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (mighty one), son of Bela, (1 Chronicles 8:3) called Ardin (Numbers 26:40)
entries.definition_ko: '강한 자'라는 뜻으로 벨라의 아들이며(역대상 8:3) 민수기 26:40에서는 아릇이라 불린다.

entries.definition: This word is used for any poisonous snake, and is applied in this general sense by the translators of the Authorized Version. The word adder occurs five times in the text of the Authorized Version (see below), and three times int he margin as synonymous with cockatrice, viz., (Isaiah 11:8; 14:29; 59:5) It represents four Hebrew words: • Acshub is found only in (Psalms 140:3) and may be represented by the Toxicoa of Egypt and North Africa. • Pethen. [Asp] • Tsepha, or Tsiphoni, occurs five times in the Hebrew Bible. In (Proverbs 23:32) it is it is translated adder, and in (Isaiah 11:8; 14:29; 59:5; Jeremiah 8:17) it is rendered cockatrice . From Jeremiah we learn that it was of a hostile nature, and from the parallelism of (Isaiah 11:8) it appears that the Tsiphoni was considered even more dreadful than the Pethen . • Shephipon occurs only in (Genesis 49:17) where it is used to characterize the tribe of Dan. The habit of lurking int he sand and biting at the horse’s heels here alluded to suits the character of a well-known species of venomous snake, and helps to identify it with the celebrated horned viper, the asp of Cleopatra (Cerastes), which is found abundantly in the dry sandy deserts of Egypt, Syria and Arabia. The cerastes is extremely venomous. Bruce compelled a specimen to scratch eighteen pigeons upon the thigh as quickly as possible, and they all died in nearly the same interval of time.
entries.definition_ko: 독사를 통칭하는 말로 흠정역에서 이 뜻으로 다섯 차례 쓰이며 히브리어로는 네 가지 다른 단어(악슙, 베덴, 체파/치포니, 스피폰)를 나타낸다. 특히 스피폰은 창세기 49:17에서 단 지파를 상징하는 데 쓰이며 애굽·수리아·아라비아의 뿔살모사(케라스테스)와 동일시된다.

entries.definition: (ornament). (Luke 3:28) Son of Cosam, and father of Melchi in our Lord’s genealogy; the third above Salathiel.
entries.definition_ko: '장식'이라는 뜻으로(누가복음 3:28) 고삼의 아들이자 멜기의 아버지로 주님의 족보에 나오며 스알디엘보다 세 대 위이다.

entries.definition: (lord). [Addan]
entries.definition_ko: '주인'이라는 뜻. 앗단(ADDAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (flock), a Benjamites, son of Beriah, chief of the inhabitants of Aijalon. (1 Chronicles 8:15) The name is more correctly Eder.
entries.definition_ko: '무리'라는 뜻으로 브리아의 아들인 베냐민 사람이며 아얄론 주민의 지도자였다(역대상 8:15); 더 정확한 이름은 에델이다.

entries.definition: a fortified town near Jerusalem, probably the Hadidof (Ezra 2:33) and referred to in 1Ma 12:38
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘 근처의 요새화된 도시로 하딧(에스라 2:33)과 동일시된다.

entries.definition: (ornament of God). • A prince of the tribe of Simeon, descended from the prosperous family of Shimei. (1 Chronicles 4:36) He took part in the murderous raid made by his tribe upon the peaceable Hamite shepherds of the valley of Gedor in the reign of Hezekiah. (B.C. about 711.) • A priest, ancestor of Maasiai. (1 Chronicles 9:12) • Ancestor of Azmaveth, David’s treasurer. (1 Chronicles 27:25) (B.C. 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 장식'이라는 뜻. (1) 시므온 지파 방백으로 시므이 가문 출신(역대상 4:36); 히스기야 시대 게돌 골짜기의 함 족속 목자들을 공격한 원정에 참여했다. (2) 마아새의 조상인 제사장(역대상 9:12). (3) 다윗의 재무관 아스마웻의 조상(역대상 27:25).

entries.definition: (dainty, delicate), ancestor of a family who returned form Babylon with Zerubbabel, to the number of 454, (Ezra 2:15) or 655 according to the parallel list in (Nehemiah 7:20) (B.C. 536.) They joined with Nehemiah in a covenant to separate themselves from the heathen. (Nehemiah 10:16) (B.C. 410.)
entries.definition_ko: '우아한, 섬세한'이라는 뜻으로 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 돌아온 454명(혹은 느헤미야서 목록에 따르면 655명)의 조상이다(에스라 2:15). 느헤미야와 함께 이방인과 분리하는 언약을 맺었다(느헤미야 10:16).

entries.definition: (slender), one of David’s captains beyond the Jordan, and a chief of the Reubenites. (1 Chronicles 11:42)
entries.definition_ko: '가는'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 건너편 다윗의 지휘관 중 하나이자 르우벤 지파의 지도자였다(역대상 11:42).

entries.definition: (2 Samuel 23:8) See Jashobeam.
entries.definition_ko: 야소브암(JASHOBEAM) 항목 참조이다(사무엘하 23:8).

entries.definition: (double ornament), a town belonging to Judah, lying in the low country, and named, between Sharaim and hag-Gederah, in (Joshua 15:36) only.
entries.definition_ko: '이중 장식'이라는 뜻으로 유다에 속한 저지대 성읍이며 사아라임과 학게데라 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 15:36).

entries.definition: (justice of Jehovah), Ancestor of Shaphat, the overseer of David’s herds that fed in the broad valleys. (1 Chronicles 27:29) (B.C. before 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 정의'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 가축 떼를 관리한 감독 사밧의 조상이다(역대상 27:29).

entries.definition: (earthy, fortress), one of the “cities of the plain,” always coupled with Zeboim. (Genesis 10:19; 14:2,8; 29:23; Hosea 11:8)
entries.definition_ko: '흙의, 요새'라는 뜻으로 소돔 평지의 '성읍들' 중 하나이며 늘 스보임과 함께 언급된다(창세기 10:19).

entries.definition: (given by the highest), one of the seven princes of Persia. (Esther 1:14)
entries.definition_ko: '지극히 높은 이가 주신'이라는 뜻으로 바사의 일곱 방백 중 하나이다(에스더 1:14).

entries.definition: (rest, pleasure). • One of the family of Pahath-moab, who returned with Ezra and married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:30) (B.C. 459.) • A priest, descendant of Harim in the days of Joiakim, the son of Jeshua. (Nehemiah 12:15) (B.C. 500.)
entries.definition_ko: '안식, 즐거움'이라는 뜻. (1) 바핫모압 가문 사람으로 에스라와 함께 돌아와 이방 여인과 결혼함(에스라 10:30). (2) 여호야김 시대 하림 가문의 제사장(느헤미야 12:15).

entries.definition: (pleasure). • A Manassite who deserted from Saul and joined the fortunes of David on his road to Ziklag from the camp of the Philistines. He was captain of a thousand of his tribe, and fought at David’s side in the pursuit of the Amalekites. (1 Chronicles 12:20) (B.C. 1054.) • The captain of over 300,000 men of Judah who were in Jehoshaphat’s army. (2 Chronicles 17:14) (B.C. 908.)
entries.definition_ko: '즐거움'이라는 뜻. (1) 므낫세 사람으로 사울을 떠나 다윗에게 합류했으며 천부장이었다(역대상 12:20). (2) 여호사밧의 군대에서 30만 명을 거느린 유다 지휘관(역대하 17:14).

entries.definition: (lord of Bezek), king of Bezek, a city of the Canaanites. [Bezek] This chieftain was vanquished by the tribe of Judah, (Judges 1:3-7) who cut off his thumbs and great toes, and brought him prisoner to Jerusalem, where he died. He confessed that he had inflicted the same cruelty upon 70 petty kings whom he had conquered. (B.C. 1425).
entries.definition_ko: '베섹의 주'라는 뜻으로 가나안 성읍 베섹의 왕이며 유다 지파에게 패해 엄지손가락과 엄지발가락이 잘린 채 예루살렘으로 끌려와 죽었다. 자신도 정복한 70명의 왕에게 같은 잔혹행위를 했다고 고백했다(사사기 1:3-7).

entries.definition: (my Lord is Jehovah). • The fourth son of David by Haggith, born at Hebron while his father was king of Judah. (2 Samuel 3:4) (B.C. about 1050.) After the death of his three brothers, Amnon, Chileab and Absalom, he became eldest son; and when his father’s strength was visibly declining, put forward his pretensions to the crown. Adonijah’s cause was espoused by Abiathar and by Joab the famous commander of David’s army. [Joab] His name and influence secured a large number of followers among the captains of the royal army belonging to the tribe of Judah, comp. (1 Kings 1:5) and these, together with all the princes except Solomon, were entertained by Adonijah at the great sacrificial feast held “by the stone Zoheleth, which is by En-rogel.” [ENROGEL] Apprised of these proceedings, David immediately caused Solomon to be proclaimed king, (1 Kings 1:33,34) at Gihon. [Gihon] This decisive measure struck terror into the opposite party, and Adonijah fled to the sanctuary, but was pardoned by Solomon on condition that he should “show himself a worthy man.” (1 Kings 1:52) The death of David quickly followed on these events; and Adonijah begged Bath-sheba to procure Solomon’s consent to his marriage with Abishag, who had been the wife of David in his old age. (1 Kings 1:3) This was regarded as equivalent to a fresh attempt on the throne [Absalom; Abner]; and therefore Solomon ordered him to be put to death by Benaiah. (1 Kings 2:25) • A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat. (2 Chronicles 17:8) • The same as Adonikam. (Nehemiah 10:16) [Adonikam, Or Adonikam]
entries.definition_ko: '나의 주는 여호와이시다'라는 뜻. (1) 다윗과 학깃 사이의 넷째 아들로 형들이 죽은 뒤 왕위를 노려 아비아달과 요압의 지지를 얻어 스스로 왕이 되려 했으나, 다윗이 급히 솔로몬을 왕으로 세우자 성소로 도망쳤다가 용서받았다. 훗날 다윗의 첩 아비삭과의 결혼을 요청한 일로 반역 의도로 간주되어 브나야에게 처형되었다(열왕기상 1-2장). (2) 여호사밧 시대의 레위인(역대하 17:8). (3) 아도니감과 동일 인물(느헤미야 10:16).

entries.definition: The sons of Adonikam, 666 in number, were among those who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:13; Nehemiah 7:18); 1Esd 5:14(B.C. 506-410.) The name is given as Adonijahin (Nehemiah 10:16)
entries.definition_ko: 그의 자손 666명이 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 돌아온 인물이다(에스라 2:13). 느헤미야 10:16에서는 아도니야로 불린다.

entries.definition: (lord of heights), (1 Kings 4:6) by an unusual contraction Adoram, (2 Samuel 20:24) and 1Kin 12:18Also Hadoram, (2 Chronicles 10:18) chief receiver of the tribute during the reigns of David, (2 Samuel 20:24) Solomon, (1 Kings 4:6) and Rehoboam. (1 Kings 12:18) This last monarch sent him to collect the tribute from the rebellious Israelites, by whom he was stoned to death, (B.C. 1014-973.)
entries.definition_ko: '높음의 주'라는 뜻으로 아도람(사무엘하 20:24), 하도람(역대하 10:18)이라고도 불리며 다윗, 솔로몬, 르호보암 시대에 조공 징수를 담당했다. 르호보암이 반란을 일으킨 이스라엘 백성에게서 조공을 걷도록 보냈으나 돌에 맞아 죽었다.

entries.definition: (lord of justice), the Amorite king of Jerusalem who organized a league with four other Amorite princes against Joshua. The confederate kings having laid siege to Gibeon, Joshua marched to the relief of his new allies and put the besiegers to flight. The five kings took refuge in a cave at Makkedah, whence they were taken and slain, their bodies hung on trees, and then buried in the place of their concealment. (Joshua 10:1-27) (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '의의 주'라는 뜻으로 예루살렘의 아모리 왕이며 다른 네 아모리 왕과 동맹해 기브온을 공격했으나 여호수아에게 패해 막게다 동굴에서 잡혀 죽고 나무에 매달렸다(여호수아 10:1-27).

entries.definition: an expression used by St. Paul in reference to the present and prospective privileges of Christians. (Romans 8:15,23; Galatians 4:5; Ephesians 1:5) He probably alludes to the Roman custom by which a person not having children of his own might adopt as his son one born of other parents. The relationship was to all intents and purposes the same as existed between a natural father and son. The term is used figuratively to show the close relationship to God of the Christian. (Galatians 4:4,5; Romans 8:14-17) He is received into God’s family from the world, and becomes a child and heir of God.
entries.definition_ko: 바울이 그리스도인의 현재와 장래 특권을 가리켜 쓴 표현으로(로마서 8:15) 로마의 입양 관습에서 유래한 것으로 보이며, 하나님과 그리스도인의 친밀한 관계를 나타내는 비유로 쓰인다.

entries.definition: [Adoraim]
entries.definition_ko: 아도라임(ADORAIM) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (double mound), a fortified city built by Rehoboam, (2 Chronicles 11:9) in Judah. Adoraim is probably the same place with Adora, 1Ma 13:20Unless that be Dor, on the seacoast below Carmel. Robinson identifies it with Dura, a “large village” on a rising ground west of Hebron.
entries.definition_ko: '이중 언덕'이라는 뜻으로 르호보암이 유다에 건설한 요새 도시이다(역대하 11:9).

entries.definition: [Adoniram; Hadoram]
entries.definition_ko: 아도니람(ADONIRAM), 하도람(HADORAM) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The acts and postures by which the Hebrews expressed adoration bear a great similarity to those still in use among Oriental nations. To rise up and suddenly prostrate the body was the most simple method; but, generally speaking, the prostration was conducted in a more formal manner, the person falling upon the knee and then gradually inclining the body until the forehead touched the ground. Such prostration was usual in the worship of Jehovah, (Genesis 17:3; Psalms 95:6) it was the formal mode of receiving visitors, (Genesis 18:2) of doing obeisance to one of superior station, (2 Samuel 14:4) and of showing respect to equals. (1 Kings 2:19) It was accompanied by such acts as a kiss, (Exodus 18:7) laying hold of the knees or feet of the person to whom the adoration was paid, (Matthew 28:9) and kissing the ground on which he stood. (Psalms 72:9; Micah 7:17) Similar adoration was paid to idols, (1 Kings 19:18) sometimes, however, the act consisted simply in kissing the hand to the object of reverence, (Job 31:27) and in kissing the statue itself. (Hosea 13:2)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인들이 경배를 표현하던 몸짓과 자세는 동방 여러 민족과 유사했다. 몸을 갑자기 굽히거나 무릎을 꿇고 이마가 땅에 닿도록 절하는 것이 일반적이었으며(창세기 17:3), 손님을 맞이하거나 윗사람과 동등한 사람에게 존경을 표할 때도 쓰였다. 입맞춤이나 무릎/발을 붙잡는 행위가 동반되기도 했으며 우상에게도 유사한 방식으로 경배했다.

entries.definition: (splendor of the king). • The name of an idol introduced into Samaria by the colonists from Sepharvaim. (2 Kings 17:31) He was worshipped with rites resembling those of Molech, children being burnt in his honor. Adrammelech was probably the male power of the sun, and Anammelech, who is mentioned with Adrammelech as a companion god, the female power of the sun. • Son of the Assyrian king Sennacherib, who, with his brother Sharezer, murdered their father in the temple of Nisroch at Nineveh, after the failure of the Assyrian attack on Jerusalem. The parricides escaped into Armenia. (2 Kings 19:37; 2 Chronicles 32:21; Isaiah 37:38)
entries.definition_ko: '왕의 광채'라는 뜻. (1) 사마리아에 스발와임 이주민들이 들여온 우상으로 몰렉과 비슷한 방식으로 아이들을 불태워 섬겼다(열왕기하 17:31); 태양의 남성적 힘을 상징한 것으로 추정된다. (2) 앗수르 왕 산헤립의 아들로 형제 사레셀과 함께 니느웨의 니스록 신전에서 아버지를 암살하고 아르메니아로 도망쳤다(열왕기하 19:37).

entries.definition: named form Adramys, brother of Croesus king of Lydia, a seaport in the province of Asia [Asia], situated on a bay of the Aegean Sea, about 70 miles north of Smyrna, in the district anciently called Aeolis, and also Mysia. See (Acts 16:7) [Mitylene] (Acts 27:2) The modern Adramyti is a poor village.
entries.definition_ko: 리디아 왕 크로이소스의 형제 아드라미스의 이름을 딴 곳으로, 소아시아 속주의 항구 도시이며 서머나 북쪽 약 70마일 지점 에게해 연안, 옛 아이올리스(또는 미시아) 지역에 위치한다(사도행전 27:2).

entries.definition: more properly A’drias, the Adriatic Sea. (Acts 27:27) The word seems to have been derived from the town of Adria, near the Po. In Paul’s time it included the whole sea between Greece and Italy, reaching south from Crete to Sicily. [Melita]
entries.definition_ko: '아드리아 해'를 가리키며(사도행전 27:27) 포강 근처 아드리아 마을에서 이름이 유래했다. 바울 시대에는 헬라와 이탈리아 사이, 그레데에서 시칠리아까지 이르는 바다 전체를 포함했다.

entries.definition: (flock of God), son of Barzillai, to whom Saul gave his daughter Merab, although he had previously promised her to David. (1 Samuel 18:19) (B.C. about 1062.) His five sons were amongst the seven descendants of Saul whom David surrendered to the Gibeonites. (2 Samuel 21:8)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 무리'라는 뜻으로 바르실래의 아들이며, 사울이 원래 다윗에게 약속했던 딸 메랍을 그에게 주었다(사무엘상 18:19). 그의 다섯 아들은 다윗이 기브온 사람들에게 넘긴 사울의 후손 일곱 명에 포함되었다(사무엘하 21:8).

entries.definition: (justice of the people), Apocr. Odollam, a city of Judah int he lowland of the Shefelah, (Joshua 15:35) the seat of a Canaanite king, (Joshua 12:15) and evidently a place of great antiquity. (Genesis 38:1,12,20) Fortified by Rehoboam, (2 Chronicles 11:7) it was one of the towns reoccupied by the Jews after their return from Babylon, (Nehemiah 11:30) and still a city in the time of the Macabees. 2Ma 12:38Adullam was probably near Deir Dubban, five or six miles north of Eleutheropolis. The limestone cliffs of the whole of that locality are pierced with extensive excavations, some one of which is doubtless the “cave of Adullam,” the refuge of David. (1 Samuel 22:1; 2 Samuel 23:13; 1 Chronicles 11:15)
entries.definition_ko: '백성의 정의'라는 뜻으로 유다 저지대(세벨라)의 도시이며(여호수아 15:35) 본래 가나안 왕의 거처였다. 르호보암이 요새화했고(역대하 11:7) 포로 후 유대인들이 재정착한 곳이다. 다윗이 사울을 피해 숨은 '아둘람 굴'로 유명하다(사무엘상 22:1).

entries.definition: (Exodus 20:14) The parties to this crime, according to Jewish law, were a married woman and a man who was not her husband. The Mosaic penalty was that both the guilty parties should be stoned, and it applied as well to the betrothed as to the married woman, provided she were free. (22:22-24) A bondwoman so offending was to be scourged, and the man was to make a trespass offering. (Leviticus 19:20-22) At a later time, and when owing, to Gentile example, the marriage tie became a looser bond of union, public feeling in regard to adultery changed, and the penalty of death was seldom or never inflicted. The famous trial by the waters of jealousy, (Numbers 5:11-29) was probably an ancient custom, which Moses found deeply seated—(But this ordeal was wholly in favor of the innocent, and exactly opposite to most ordeals. For the water which the accused drank was perfectly harmless, and only by a miracle could it produce a bad effect; while in most ordeals the accused must suffer what naturally produces death, and be proved innocent only by a miracle. Symbolically adultery is used to express unfaithfulness to covenant vows to God, who is represented as the husband of his people.)
entries.definition_ko: 출애굽기 20:14에 금지된 죄로, 유대 율법상 결혼한 여인과 그 남편이 아닌 남자 사이의 관계를 가리킨다. 모세 율법의 형벌은 두 죄인 모두를 돌로 치는 것이었다(레위기 22:22-24). '투기의 물' 시련(민수기 5:11-29)은 오히려 무죄한 자에게 유리하게 설계된 고대 관습이었다. 상징적으로 간음은 하나님과의 언약을 저버리는 불신실함을 나타내는 데도 쓰인다.

entries.definition: (the going up to), a rising ground or pass over against Gilgal,” and “on the south side of the ’torrent’” (Joshua 15:7; 18:17) which is the position still occupied by the road leading up from Jericho and the Jordan valley to Jerusalem, on the south face of the gorge of the Wady Kelt. (Luke 10:30-36)
entries.definition_ko: '오르막'이라는 뜻으로 길갈 맞은편, 시내 남쪽의 고갯길이며(여호수아 15:7) 오늘날에도 여리고에서 예루살렘으로 오르는 길이 지나는 와디 켈트 협곡 남쪽 사면에 해당한다.

entries.definition: or Paraclete, one that pleads the cause of another. (1 John 2:1) Used by Christ, (John 14:16; 15:26; 16:7) to describe the office and work of the Holy Spirit, and translated Comforter, i.e. (see margin of Revised Version) Advocate, Helper, Intercessor. This use of the word is derived from the fact that the Jews, being largely ignorant of the Roman law and the Roman language, had to employ Roman advocates in their trials before Roman courts. Applied to Christ, (1 John 2:1)
entries.definition_ko: '파라클레토스', 곧 남을 위해 변호하는 자를 뜻하며(요한일서 2:1) 주님이 성령의 직무를 가리켜 쓰신 표현으로(요한복음 14:16) '보혜사'로도 번역된다. 유대인들이 로마 법정에서 로마 변호인을 고용해야 했던 관습에서 유래한 용어이다.

entries.definition: [Egypt]

entries.definition: (a locust), a Christian prophet in the apostolic age, mentioned in (Acts 11:28) and Acts 21:10He predicted, (Acts 11:28) that a famine would take place in the reign of Claudius. Josephus mentions a famine which prevailed in Judea in the reign of Claudius, and swept away many of the inhabitants. (In (Acts 21:10) we learn that Agabus and Paul met at Caesarea some time after this.)

entries.definition: (flame), possibly the title of the kings of Amalek, like Pharaoh of Egypt. One king of this name is mentioned in (Numbers 24:7) and another in 1Sam 15:8,9,20,32The latter was the king of the Amalekites, whom Saul spared contrary to Jehovah’s wellknown will. (Exodus 17:14; 25:17) For this act of disobedience Samuel was commissioned to declare to Saul his rejection, and he himself sent for Agag and cut him in pieces. (B.C. about 1070.) [Samuel]. Haman is called the Agagitein (Esther 3:1,10; 8:3,5) The Jews consider him a descendant of Agag the Amalekite.
entries.definition_ko: '불꽃'이라는 뜻으로 애굽의 '바로'처럼 아말렉 왕들의 칭호로 추정된다. 사울이 여호와의 뜻을 어기고 살려준 아말렉 왕 아각은 사무엘에게 처형되었다(사무엘상 15장). 하만은 '아각 사람'이라 불린다(에스더 3:1).

entries.definition: a beautifully-veined semi-transparent precious stone, a variety of quartz. Its colors are delicately arranged in stripes or bands or blended in clouds. It is mentioned four times in the text of the Authorized Version, viz., in (Exodus 28:19; 39:12; Isaiah 54:12; Ezekiel 27:16) In the two former passages; where it is represented by the Hebrew word shebo it is spoken of as forming the second stone in the third row of the high priest’s breastplate; in each of the two latter places the original word is cadced, by which, no doubt, is intended a different stone. [RUBY] Our English agate derives its name from the Achates, on the banks of which it was first found.

entries.definition: The aged occupied a prominent place in the social and political system of the Jews. In private life they were looked up to as the depositaries of knowledge, (Job 15:10) the young were ordered to rise up in their presence, (Leviticus 19:32) they allowed them to give their opinion first, (Job 32:4) they were taught to regard gray hair as a “crown of glory,” (Proverbs 16:31; 20:29) The attainment of old age was regarded as a special blessing. (Job 5:26) In pubic main qualification of those who acted as the representatives of the people in all matter of difficulty and deliberation. [ELDERS]
entries.definition_ko: 유대 사회에서 노인은 지식의 보고로 여겨져 존경받았으며(욥기 15:10) 젊은이들은 그 앞에서 일어서야 했다(레위기 19:32). 장수는 특별한 복으로 여겨졌으며(욥기 5:26) 백성의 대표로 장로가 세워지는 근거가 되었다.
