entries.definition: This was little cared for by the patriarchs. The pastoral life, however, was the means of keeping the sacred race, whilst yet a family, distinct from mixture and locally unattached, especially whilst in Egypt. When grown into a nation it supplied a similar check on the foreign intercourse, and became the basis of the Mosaic commonwealth. “The land is mine,” (Leviticus 25:23) was a dictum which made agriculture likewise the basis of the theocratic relation. Thus every family felt its own life with intense keenness, and had its divine tenure which it was to guard from alienation. The prohibition of culture in the sabbatical year formed a kind of rent reserved by the divine Owner. Landmarks were deemed sacred, (19:14) and the inalienability of the heritage was insured by its reversion to the owner in the year of jubilee; so that only so many years of occupancy could be sold. (Leviticus 25:8-16; 23-35) Rain.—Water was abundant in Palestine from natural sources. (8:7; 11:8-12) Rain was commonly expected soon after the autumnal equinox. The period denoted by the common scriptural expressions of the “early” and the “latter rain,” (11:1; Jeremiah 5:24; Hosea 6:3; Zechariah 10:1; James 5:7) generally reaching from November to April, constituted the “rainy season,” and the remainder of the year the “dry season.” Crops.—The cereal crops of constant mention are wheat and barley, and more rarely rye and millet(?). Of the two former, together with the vine, olive and fig, the use of irrigation, the plough and the harrow, mention is made ln the book of (Job 31:40; 15:33; 24:6; 29:19; 39:10) Two kinds of cumin (the black variety called fitches), (Isaiah 28:27) and such podded plants as beans and lentils may be named among the staple produce. Ploughing and Sowing.—The plough was probably very light, one yoke of oxen usually sufficing to draw it. Mountains and steep places were hoed. (Isaiah 7:25) New ground and fallows, (Jeremiah 4:3; Hosea 10:12) were cleared of stones and of thorns, (Isaiah 5:2) early in the year, sowing or gathering from “among thorns” being a proverb for slovenly husbandry. (Job 5:5; Proverbs 24:30,31) Sowing also took place without previous ploughing, the seed being scattered broad cast and ploughed in afterwards. The soil was then brushed over with a light harrow, often of thorn bushes. In highly-irrigated spots the seed was trampled by cattle. (Isaiah 32:20) Seventy days before the passover was the time prescribed for sowing. The oxen were urged on by a goad like a spear. (Judges 3:31) The proportion of harvest gathered to seed sown was often vast; a hundred fold is mentioned, but in such a way as to signify that it was a limit rarely attained. (Genesis 26:12; Matthew 13:8) Sowing a field with divers seed was forbidden. (22:9) Reaping and Threshing.—The wheat etc., was reaped by the sickle or pulled by the roots. It was bound in sheaves. The sheaves or heaps were carted, (Amos 2:13) to the floor—a circular spot of hard ground, probably, as now, from 50 to 80 or 100 feet in diameter. (Genesis 1:10,11; 2 Samuel 24:16,18) On these the oxen, etc., forbidden to be muzzled, (25:4) trampled out the grain. At a later time the Jews used a threshing sledge called morag, (Isaiah 41:15; 2 Samuel 24:22; 1 Chronicles 21:23) probably resembling the noreg, still employed in Egypt—a stage with three rollers ridged with iron, which, aided by the driver’s weight crushed out, often injuring, the grain, as well as cut or tore the straw, which thus became fit for fodder. Lighter grains were beaten out with a stick. (Isaiah 28:27) The use of animal manure was frequent. (Psalms 83:10; 2 Kings 9:37; Jeremiah 8:2) etc. Winnowing.—The shovel and fan, (Isaiah 30:24) indicate the process of winnowing—a conspicuous part of ancient husbandry. (Psalms 35:5; Job 21:18; Isaiah 17:13) Evening was the favorite time, (Ruth 3:2) when there was mostly a breeze. The fan, (Matthew 3:12) was perhaps a broad shovel which threw the grain up against the wind. The last process was the shaking in a sieve to separate dirt and refuse. (Amos 9:9) Fields and floors were not commonly enclosed; vineyard mostly were, with a tower and other buildings. (Numbers 22:24; Psalms 80:13; Isaiah 5:5; Matthew 21:33) comp. Judg 6:11The gardens also and orchards were enclosed, frequently by banks of mud from ditches. With regard to occupancy, a tenant might pay a fixed money rent, (Song of Solomon 8:11) or a stipulated share of the fruits. (2 Samuel 9:10; Matthew 21:34) A passer by might eat any quantity of corn or grapes, but not reap or carry off fruit. (23:24,25; Matthew 12:1) The rights of the corner to be left, and of gleaning [Corner; Gleaning], formed the poor man’s claim on the soil for support. For his benefit, too, a sheaf forgotten in carrying to the floor was to be left; so also with regard to the vineyard’ and the olive grove. (Leviticus 19:9,10; 24:19)
entries.definition_ko:
족장들은 농업을 크게 돌보지 않았다. 그러나 목축 생활은 거룩한 족속이 아직 한 가문이던 때에 다른 민족과 섞이지 않고 한곳에 매이지 않게 지키는 수단이었으니, 특히 애굽에 있을 때 그러했다. 한 민족으로 자란 뒤에는 농업이 이방과의 교류를 비슷하게 억제하며 모세 율법 공동체의 기초가 되었다. '토지는 다 내 것임이니라'(레위기 25:23) 하신 선언은 농업을 또한 신정적 관계의 기초로 삼았다. 그리하여 각 가정은 자기 삶을 절실하게 느꼈고, 남에게 넘기지 않도록 지켜야 할 하나님이 주신 소유권을 지녔다. 안식년의 경작 금지는 신적 소유주께 남겨 드리는 일종의 소작료였다. 지계표는 거룩히 여겨졌고(신명기 19:14), 기업이 희년에 임자에게 돌아감으로써 그 양도 불가능성이 보장되었으니, 팔 수 있는 것은 다만 몇 해의 사용권뿐이었다(레위기 25:8-16,23-35).

비 — 팔레스타인은 자연 수원이 풍부했다(신명기 8:7; 11:8-12). 비는 대개 추분 직후에 기대되었다. 성경이 흔히 말하는 '이른 비'와 '늦은 비'(신명기 11:14; 예레미야 5:24; 호세아 6:3; 스가랴 10:1; 야고보서 5:7)가 가리키는 대략 십일월부터 사월까지가 우기였고 나머지는 건기였다.

작물 — 늘 언급되는 곡식은 밀과 보리이며 드물게 호밀과 기장이 나온다. 앞의 두 가지와 더불어 포도나무와 감람나무와 무화과나무, 그리고 관개와 쟁기와 써레의 사용이 욥기에 언급된다(욥기 31:40; 15:33; 24:6; 29:19; 39:10). 두 종류의 소회향(검은 것은 대회향이라 옮겼다, 이사야 28:27)과 콩이나 팥 같은 꼬투리 작물도 주요 산물에 든다.

쟁기질과 파종 — 쟁기는 매우 가벼워 보통 소 한 겨리로 끌 수 있었다. 산지와 가파른 곳은 괭이로 팠다(이사야 7:25). 새 땅과 묵정밭(예레미야 4:3; 호세아 10:12)은 해 초에 돌과 가시를 골라냈으며(이사야 5:2), '가시떨기 가운데' 뿌리거나 거두는 것은 게으른 농사를 이르는 속담이었다(욥기 5:5; 잠언 24:30,31). 쟁기질 없이 씨를 널리 흩어 뿌린 뒤 갈아엎기도 했다. 그런 다음 흔히 가시나무로 만든 가벼운 써레로 흙을 골랐다. 물을 잘 댄 곳에서는 가축이 씨를 밟아 묻었다(이사야 32:20). 파종은 유월절 칠십 일 전으로 정해져 있었다. 소는 창 같은 막대기로 몰았다(사사기 3:31). 뿌린 씨에 대한 수확의 비율은 흔히 매우 컸으니 백 배가 언급되나, 좀처럼 이르지 못하는 한계를 뜻하는 방식으로 쓰였다(창세기 26:12; 마태복음 13:8). 한 밭에 두 종자를 섞어 뿌리는 것은 금지되었다(신명기 22:9).

추수와 타작 — 밀 따위는 낫으로 베거나 뿌리째 뽑았고 단으로 묶었다. 단이나 낟가리는 수레로 타작마당에 옮겼는데(아모스 2:13), 마당은 지금처럼 지름 오십에서 팔십 내지 백 자쯤 되는 단단한 원형의 땅이었다(사무엘하 24:16,18). 그 위에서 부리망을 씌우지 않은 소들이(신명기 25:4) 곡식을 밟아 떨었다. 후대에 유대인은 '모라그'라는 타작 썰매를 썼는데(이사야 41:15; 사무엘하 24:22; 역대상 21:23), 오늘날 애굽에서 쓰는 '노레그'와 비슷했을 것이다. 쇠를 두른 세 개의 굴대가 달린 이 기구는 모는 자의 무게를 더해 곡식을 으깨어 냈는데 낟알을 상하게 하는 일이 잦았고, 짚을 자르고 찢어 꼴로 쓸 만하게 만들었다. 가벼운 곡식은 막대기로 두들겼다(이사야 28:27). 거름은 자주 쓰였다(시편 83:10; 열왕기하 9:37; 예레미야 8:2).

키질 — 넉가래와 키(이사야 30:24)는 키질의 과정을 보여 주는데, 이는 고대 농사의 두드러진 부분이었다(시편 35:5; 욥기 21:18; 이사야 17:13). 대개 바람이 이는 저녁이 선호되었다(룻기 3:2). 마태복음 3:12의 키는 곡식을 바람에 맞서 퍼올리는 넓은 넉가래였을 것이다. 마지막 과정은 체로 쳐서 흙과 검불을 걸러 내는 일이었다(아모스 9:9).

밭과 점유 — 밭과 타작마당은 대개 울을 두르지 않았으나 포도원은 대부분 망대와 부속 건물을 갖추어 울을 둘렀다(민수기 22:24; 시편 80:13; 이사야 5:5; 마태복음 21:33; 사사기 6:11 비교). 동산과 과수원도 흔히 도랑에서 파낸 흙으로 둑을 쌓아 둘렀다. 점유와 관련해 소작인은 정해진 돈을 삯으로 내거나(아가 8:11) 소출의 정해진 몫을 바쳤다(사무엘하 9:10; 마태복음 21:34). 지나가는 자는 곡식이나 포도를 얼마든지 먹을 수 있었으나 베거나 담아 가지는 못했다(신명기 23:24,25; 마태복음 12:1). 밭모퉁이를 남기는 권리와 이삭줍기의 권리는 가난한 자가 그 땅에 대해 지니는 부양의 몫이었다. 그를 위하여 타작마당으로 옮기다 잊은 곡식단도 남겨 두어야 했고 포도원과 감람원에서도 그러했다(레위기 19:9,10; 신명기 24:19).

entries.definition: (uncle). • Son of Omri, seventh king of Israel, reigned B.C. 919-896. He married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of Tyre; and in obedience to her wishes, caused temple to be built to Baal in Samaria itself; and an oracular grove to be consecrated to Astarte. See (1 Kings 18:19) One of Ahab’s chief tastes was for splendid architecture which he showed by building an ivory house and several cities. Desiring to add to his pleasure-grounds at Jezreel the vineyard of his neighbor Naboth, he proposed to buy it or give land in exchange for it; and when this was refused by Naboth in accordance with the Levitical law, (Leviticus 25:23) a false accusation of blasphemy was brought against him, and he was murdered, and Ahab took possession of the coveted fields. (2 Kings 9:26) Thereupon Elijah declared that the entire extirpation of Ahab’s house was the penalty appointed for his long course of wickedness. [Elijah] The execution, however, of the sentence was delayed in consequence of Ahab’s deep repentance. (1 Kings 21:1) ... Ahab undertook three campaigns against Ben-hadad II. king of Damascus, two defensive and one offensive. In the first Ben-hadad laid siege to Samaria, but was repulsed with great loss. (1 Kings 20:1-21) Next year Benhadad again invaded Israel by way of Aphek, on the east of Jordan; yet Ahab’s victory was so complete that Ben-hadad himself fell into his hands, but was released contrary to God’s will, (1 Kings 20:22-34) on condition of restoring the cities of Israel, and admitting Hebrew commissioners into Damascus. After this great success Ahab enjoyed peace for three years, when he attacked Ramoth in Gilead, on the east of Jordan, in conjunction with Jehoshaphat king of Judah, which town he claimed as belonging to Israel. Being told by the prophet Micaiah that he would fall, he disguised himself, but was slain by “a certain man who drew a bow at a venture.” When buried in Samaria, the dogs licked up his blood as a servant was washing his chariot; a partial fulfillment of Elijah’s prediction, (1 Kings 21:19) which was more literally accomplished in the case of his son. (2 Kings 9:26) • A lying prophet, who deceived the captive Israelites in Babylon, and was burnt to death by Nebuchadnezzar. (Jeremiah 29:21)
entries.definition_ko: '삼촌'이라는 뜻. (1) 오므리의 아들로 이스라엘 일곱째 왕이며(주전 919-896년) 두로 왕 엣바알의 딸 이세벨과 결혼해 바알 신전을 세우게 했다. 나봇의 포도원을 탐내 거짓 고발로 그를 죽이고 빼앗았으며, 엘리야는 그의 집안 전체가 멸망할 것을 선언했다. 벤하닷과 세 차례 전쟁을 치렀고, 마지막에 길르앗 라못 전투에서 변장했음에도 화살에 맞아 죽었다. (2) 바벨론 포로 이스라엘 백성을 속인 거짓 선지자로 느부갓네살에게 화형당했다(예레미야 29:21).

entries.definition: (after the brother), third son of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 8:1) [Aher; Ahiram]
entries.definition_ko: '형제 뒤의'라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 셋째 아들이다(역대상 8:1).

entries.definition: (behind the breastwork), a name occurring in an obscure fragment of the genealogies of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:8)
entries.definition_ko: '흉벽 뒤의'라는 뜻으로 유다 족보의 불분명한 단편에 나오는 이름이다(역대상 4:8).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah holds), a priest, ancestor of Maasiai, (Nehemiah 11:13) called Jahzerahin (1 Chronicles 9:12)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 붙드시는 자'라는 뜻으로 마아새의 조상인 제사장이며(느헤미야 11:13) 역대상 9:12에서는 야흐세라라 불린다.

entries.definition: (blooming), father of Eli-phelet, one of David’s thirty-seven captains. (2 Samuel 23:34) In the corrupt list in (1 Chronicles 11:35) Eliphelet appears as “Eliphal the son of Ur.” (B.C. about 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: '꽃 피는'이라는 뜻으로 다윗의 서른일곱 지휘관 중 하나인 엘리블렛의 아버지이다(사무엘하 23:34).

entries.definition: Another (the Hebrew) form of AHASUERIUS. (Ezra 4:6) in margin.
entries.definition_ko: 아하수에로의 히브리어 형태이다(에스라 4:6 난외주).

entries.definition: (lion-king), the name of one Median and two Persian kings mentioned in the Old Testament. • In (Daniel 9:1) Ahasuerus is said to be the father of Darius the Mede. [Darius] This first Ahasuerus is Cyaxares, the conqueror of Nineveh. (Began to reign B.C. 634.) • The Ahasuerus king of Persia, referred to in (Ezra 4:6) must be Cambyses, thought to be Cyrus’ successor, and perhaps his son. (B.C. 529.) • The third is the Ahasuerus of the book of Esther. This Ahasuerus is probably Xerxes of history, (Esther 1:1) (B.C. 485), and this conclusion is fortified by the resemblance of character and by certain chronological indications, the account of his life and character agreeing with the book of Esther In the third year of Ahaseuerus was held a great feast and assembly in Shushan the palace, (Esther 1:3) following a council held to consider the invasion of Greece. He divorced his queen Vashti for refusing to appear in public at this banquet, and married, four years afterwards, the Jewess Esther, cousin and ward of Mordecai. Five years after this, Haman, one of his counsellors, having been slighted by Mordecai, prevailed upon the king to order the destruction of all the Jews in the empire. But before the day appointed for the massacre, Esther and Mordecai influenced the king to put Haman to death and to give the Jews the right of self-Defence.
entries.definition_ko: '사자 왕'이라는 뜻으로 구약에 언급된 메대와 바사의 세 왕을 가리키는 이름이다. (1) 다니엘 9:1의 다리오의 아버지로 니느웨를 정복한 키악사레스로 추정된다. (2) 에스라 4:6의 아하수에로는 캄비세스로 추정된다. (3) 에스더서의 아하수에로는 역사상의 크세르크세스로 추정되며, 와스디 왕후를 폐하고 에스더를 왕후로 삼았으며 하만의 계략으로 유대인 말살을 명했으나 에스더와 모르드개의 중재로 무산되었다.

entries.definition: (water), a place, (Ezra 8:15) or a river, Ezra 8:21On the banks of which Ezra collected the second expedition which returned with him from Babylon to Jerusalem. Perhaps it is the modern Hit, on the Euphrates due east of Damascus.
entries.definition_ko: '물'이라는 뜻으로 에스라가 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아올 두 번째 무리를 모은 장소 또는 강이다(에스라 8:15).

entries.definition: (possessor), eleventh king of Judah, son of Jotham, reigned 741-726, about sixteen years. At the time of his accession, Rezin king of Damascus and Pekah king of Israel had recently formed a league against Judah, and they proceeded to lay siege to Jerusalem. Upon this Isaiah hastened to give advice and encouragement to Ahaz, and the allies failed in their attack on Jerusalem. Isai 7,8,9. But, the allies inflicted a most severe injury on Judah by the capture of Elath, a flourishing port on the Red Sea, while the Philistines invaded the west and south. 2Kin 16; 2Chr 28. Ahaz, having forfeited God’s favor by his wickedness, sought deliverance from these numerous troubles by appealing to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, who forced him from his most formidable enemies. But Ahaz had to purchase this help at a costly price; he became tributary to Tiglathpileser. He was weak, a gross idolater, and sought safety in heathen ceremonies, making his son pass through the fire to Molech, consulting wizards and necromancers. (Isaiah 8:19) and other idolatrous practices. (2 Kings 23:12) His only service of permanent value was the introduction of the sun-dial. He died at the age of 36, but was refused a burial with the kings his ancestors. (2 Chronicles 28:27) • Son of Micah. (1 Chronicles 8:35,36; 9:42)
entries.definition_ko: '소유자'라는 뜻. (1) 유다의 열한 번째 왕으로 요담의 아들이며 약 16년간 다스렸다(주전 741-726년). 즉위 초 수리아와 이스라엘 연합군의 침공을 받았으나 이사야의 격려로 예루살렘 공략은 실패했다. 앗수르 왕 디글랏빌레셀에게 도움을 청해 조공을 바치는 신세가 되었으며, 우상숭배에 깊이 빠져 자기 아들을 몰렉에게 불로 지나가게 했다. (2) 미가의 아들(역대상 8:35).

entries.definition: (sustained by the Lord). • Son of Ahab and Jezebel eighth king of Israel, reigned B.C. 896-895. After the battle of Ramoth in Gilead, in which Ahab perished [Ahab], the vassal king of Moab refused his yearly tribute; comp. (Isaiah 16:1) Before Ahaziah could take measures for enforcing his claim, he was seriously injured by a fall through a lattice in his palace at Samaria. Being an idolater, he sent to inquire of the oracle of Baalzebub in the Philistine city of Ekron whether he should recover his health. But Elijah, who now for the last time exercised the prophetic office, rebuked him for this impiety, and announced to him his approaching death. The only other recorded transaction of his reign, his endeavor to join the king of Judah in trading to Ophir, is related under Jehoshaphat. (1 Kings 22:49-53; 2 Kings 1:1; 2 Chronicles 20:35-37) • Fifth king of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah (daughter of Ahab), and therefore nephew of the preceding Ahaziah, reigned one year, B.C. 884. He is Galled Azariah, (2 Chronicles 22:2) probably by a copyist’s error, and Jehoahaz. (2 Chronicles 21:17) He was 22 years old at his accession. (2 Kings 8:26) (his age 42, in (2 Chronicles 22:2) Isa a copyist’s error). Ahaziah was an idolater, and he allied himself with his uncle Jehoram king of Israel against Hazael, the new king of Syria. the two kings were, however defeated at Ramoth, where Jehoram was severely wounded. The revolution carried out in Israel by Jehu under the guidance of Elisha broke out while Ahaziah was visiting his uncle at Jezreel. As Jehu approached the town, Jehoram and Ahaziah went out to meet him; the former was shot through the heart by Jehu, and Ahaziah was pursued and mortally wounded. He died when he reached Megiddo.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 붙드심'이라는 뜻. (1) 아합과 이세벨의 아들로 이스라엘 여덟째 왕(주전 896-895년). 궁전 다락 난간에서 떨어져 다친 뒤 블레셋의 신 바알세붑에게 병이 나을지 물으려 하다가 엘리야의 책망을 받고 죽음을 선고받았다. (2) 유다의 다섯째 왕으로 여호람과 아달랴의 아들이며 1년간 다스렸다(주전 884년). 삼촌 여호람과 함께 수리아의 하사엘과 싸우다가 예후의 반역 때 함께 죽임을 당했다.

entries.definition: (brother of the wise, discreet), son of Abishur by his wife Abihail. (1 Chronicles 2:29) He was of the tribe of Judah.
entries.definition_ko: '지혜로운 자의 형제'라는 뜻으로 아비술과 그 아내 아비하일의 아들이며 유다 지파이다(역대상 2:29).

entries.definition: (following), ancestor of Hushim a Benjamite. The name occurs in the genealogy of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:12) It is not improbable that Aher and Ahiram, (Numbers 26:38) are the same.
entries.definition_ko: '뒤따르는'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 사람 후심의 조상이며(역대상 7:12) 민수기 26:38의 아히람과 동일 인물일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (a brother). • A Gadite, chief of a family who lived in Gilead in Bashan, (1 Chronicles 5:15) in the days of Jotham and of Judah. (B.C. 758.) • A descendant of Shamer, of the tribe of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:34)
entries.definition_ko: '형제'라는 뜻. (1) 바산 길르앗에 거주한 갓 지파 가문의 우두머리(역대상 5:15). (2) 아셀 지파 사멜의 후손(역대상 7:34).

entries.definition: (friend of Jehovah). • Son of Ahitub, grandson of Phinehas and great-grandson of Eli, succeeded his father as high priest in the reign of Saul. (1 Samuel 14:3,18) Ahiah is probably the same person as Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. (B.C. 980.) • One of Solomon’s princes. (1 Kings 4:3) • A prophet of Shiloh, (1 Kings 14:2) hence called the Shilonite, (1 Kings 11:29) of whom we have two remarkable prophecies extant, the one in (1 Kings 11:30-39) addressed to Jeroboam, announcing the rending of the ten tribes from Solomon; the other in (1 Kings 14:6-16) in which he foretold the death of Abijah, the king’s son, who was sick, and the destruction of Jeroboam’s house on account of the images which he had set up. (1 Kings 14:2,3) (B.C. about 956.) • Father of Baasha king of Israel. (1 Kings 15:27,33) • Son of Jerahmeel. (1 Chronicles 2:25) • Son of Bela. (1 Chronicles 8:7) • One of David’s mighty men. (1 Chronicles 11:36) • A Levite in David’s reign. (1 Chronicles 26:20) • One of the “heads of the people” who joined in the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:26)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 친구'라는 뜻. (1) 아히둡의 아들로 엘리의 증손자이며 사울 시대 대제사장이었고 아히멜렉과 동일 인물로 추정됨(사무엘상 14:3). (2) 솔로몬의 방백 중 하나(열왕기상 4:3). (3) 실로의 선지자로 여로보암에게 열 지파가 솔로몬에게서 찢겨나갈 것을 예언했고, 훗날 여로보암의 아들의 죽음과 그 집안의 멸망을 예언했다(열왕기상 11:29). (4) 이스라엘 왕 바아사의 아버지. (5)~(9) 그 외 여러 인물.

entries.definition: son of Sharar the Hararite (or of Sacar,) (1 Chronicles 11:35) one of David’s thirty mighty men. (2 Samuel 23:33) (B.C. 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: 사랄(또는 사갈)의 아들 하랄 사람으로 다윗의 서른 용사 중 하나이다(사무엘하 23:33).

entries.definition: a Manassite of the family of Shemidah. (1 Chronicles 7:19)
entries.definition_ko: 므낫세 지파 스미다 가문 사람이다(역대상 7:19).

entries.definition: (brother of help). • Son of Ammishaddai, hereditary chieftain of the tribe of Dan. (Numbers 1:12; 2:25; 7:66) (B.C. 1490). • The Benjamite chief of a body of archers in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 12:3) (B.C. 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: '도움의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 암미삿대의 아들로 단 지파의 세습 지도자(민수기 1:12). (2) 다윗 시대 궁수 부대를 이끈 베냐민 지파 지휘관(역대상 12:3).

entries.definition: (brother of renown). • The son of Shelomi and prince of the tribe of Asher. (Numbers 34:27) • Chieftain of the tribe of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 8:7)
entries.definition_ko: '명성의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 셀로미의 아들로 아셀 지파의 방백(민수기 34:27). (2) 베냐민 지파 지도자(역대상 8:7).

entries.definition: [Ahiah, Or Ahijah]
entries.definition_ko: 아히야(AHIAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (a brother who raises up), son of Shaphan the scribe, an influential officer at the court of Josiah, was one of the delegates sent by Hilkaih to consult Huldah. (2 Kings 22:12-14) In the reign of Jehoiakim he successfully used his influence to protect the prophet Jeremiah. (Jeremiah 26:24) He was the father of Gedaliah. [Gedaliah] (B.C. 641).
entries.definition_ko: '일으키는 형제'라는 뜻으로 서기관 사반의 아들이며 요시야 왕궁의 영향력 있는 관리였다. 힐기야가 훌다에게 파견한 사절 중 하나였으며(열왕기하 22:12), 여호야김 시대에는 예레미야를 보호했다(예레미야 26:24). 그다랴의 아버지이다.

entries.definition: (a brother of one born, i.e. before him). • Father of Jehoshaphat, the recorder or chronicler of the kingdom in the reigns of David and Solomon. (2 Samuel 8:16; 20:24; 1 Kings 4:3; 1 Chronicles 18:15) (B.C. before 1015.) • The father of Baana, one of Solomon’s twelve commissariat officers. (1 Kings 4:12) It is uncertain whether he is the same with the foregoing.
entries.definition_ko: '먼저 태어난 자의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 다윗과 솔로몬 시대 사관 여호사밧의 아버지(사무엘하 8:16). (2) 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 하나인 바아나의 아버지(열왕기상 4:12).

entries.definition: (brother of anger). • Son of Zadok the high priest in David’s reign, and celebrated for his swiftness of foot. During Absalom’s rebellion he carried to David the important intelligence that Ahithophel had counselled an immediate attack upon David and his followers. (2 Samuel 15:24-37; 17:15-22) Shortly afterwards he was the first to bring to the king the good news of Absalom’s defeat. (2 Samuel 18:19-33) (B.C. 972-956.) • Saul’s wife’s father. (1 Samuel 14:50) (B.C. before 1093.) • Solomon’s son-in-law. (1 Kings 4:15) (B.C. after 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '분노의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 다윗 시대 대제사장 사독의 아들로 발이 빠른 것으로 유명했다. 압살롬의 반역 때 다윗에게 중요한 정보를 전했고 압살롬의 패배 소식도 처음 알렸다(사무엘하 18:19-33). (2) 사울의 장인(사무엘상 14:50). (3) 솔로몬의 사위(열왕기상 4:15).

entries.definition: (brother of the right hand). • One of the three giant Anakim who inhabited Mount Hebron, (Numbers 13:22,23) seen by Caleb and the spies. (B.C. 1490.) The whole race was cut off by Joshua, (Joshua 11:21) and the three brothers were slain by the tribe of Judah. (Judges 1:10) • A Levite porter. (1 Chronicles 9:17)
entries.definition_ko: '오른손의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 헤브론산에 거주한 아낙 자손 거인 세 형제 중 하나로 갈렙과 정탐꾼들에게 목격되었으며(민수기 13:22) 결국 유다 지파에게 죽임을 당했다(사사기 1:10). (2) 레위인 문지기(역대상 9:17).

entries.definition: (brother of the king). • Son of Ahitub, (1 Samuel 22:11,12) and high priest of Nob in the days of Saul. He gave David the shew bread to eat, and the sword of Goliath; and for so doing was put to death, with his whole house, by Saul’s order. Abiathar alone escaped. [Abiathar] (B.C. 1085-1060.) • A Hittite. (1 Samuel 26:6)
entries.definition_ko: '왕의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 아히둡의 아들로 사울 시대 놉의 대제사장이며 다윗에게 진설병과 골리앗의 칼을 주었다가 사울의 명으로 온 집안이 몰살당했다. 아비아달만 살아남았다(사무엘상 22:11). (2) 헷 사람(사무엘상 26:6).

entries.definition: (brother of death), a Levite apparently in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 6:25) In v. (1 Chronicles 6:35) for Ahimoth we find Mahath, as in (Luke 3:26)
entries.definition_ko: '죽음의 형제'라는 뜻으로 다윗 시대의 레위인으로 보이며(역대상 6:25) 6:35에서는 마핫이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (brother the noble, i.e. a noble brother), Son of Iddo, one of Solomon’s twelve commissaries who supplied provisions for the royal household. (1 Kings 4:14) (B.C. 1014-975.)
entries.definition_ko: '고귀한 형제'라는 뜻으로 잇도의 아들이며 솔로몬의 열두 지방관 중 하나로 왕실에 식량을 공급했다(열왕기상 4:14).

entries.definition: (brother of grace, i.e. gracious). • The daughter of Ahimaaz and wife of Saul. (1 Samuel 14:50) (B.C. about 1090.) • A native of Jezreel who was married to David during his wandering life. (1 Samuel 25:43) (B.C. 1060.) She lived with him and his other wife Abigail at the court of Achish, (1 Samuel 27:3) was taken prisoner with her by the Amalekites when they plundered Ziklag, (1 Samuel 30:5) but was rescued by David. (1 Samuel 30:18)
entries.definition_ko: '은혜로운 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 아히마아스의 딸이자 사울의 아내(사무엘상 14:50). (2) 이스르엘 출신으로 다윗이 방랑 중 아내로 맞았으며(사무엘상 25:43) 아말렉 사람들에게 시글락에서 포로로 잡혔다가 다윗에게 구출되었다(사무엘상 30:5,18).

entries.definition: (brotherly). • Son of Abinadab, who accompanied the ark when it was brought out of his father’s house. (2 Samuel 6:3,4; 1 Chronicles 13:7) (B.C.1043.) • A Benjamite, one of the sons of Beriah. (1 Chronicles 8:14) • A Benjamite, Son of Jehiel. (1 Chronicles 8:31; 9:37)
entries.definition_ko: '형제 같은'이라는 뜻. (1) 아비나답의 아들로 언약궤를 옮길 때 동행했다(사무엘하 6:3,4). (2) 브리아의 아들인 베냐민 사람(역대상 8:14). (3) 여히엘의 아들인 베냐민 사람(역대상 8:31).

entries.definition: (brother of evil, i.e. unlucky), Chief of the tribe of Naphtali. (Numbers 1:15; 2:29; 7:78,83; 10:27)
entries.definition_ko: '불운의 형제'라는 뜻으로 납달리 지파의 지도자이다(민수기 1:15).

entries.definition: (brother of height, lofty), one of the sons of Benjamin, and ancestor of the AHIRAMITES (Numbers 26:38) In (Genesis 46:21) the name appears as “Ehi and Rosh.” It is uncertain whether Ahiram is the same as Aher, (1 Chronicles 7:12) or Aharah, (1 Chronicles 8:1)
entries.definition_ko: '높음의 형제'라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 아들 중 하나이며 아히람 족속의 조상이다(민수기 26:38); 창세기 46:21에서는 '에히와 로스'로 나온다. 역대상 7:12의 아헬 또는 8:1의 아하라와 동일 인물일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (brother of help), a Danite, father of Aholiab one of the architects of the tabernacle. (Exodus 31:6; 35:34; 38:23) (B.C. 1490)
entries.definition_ko: '도움의 형제'라는 뜻으로 단 지파 사람이며 성막 건축가 중 하나인 오홀리압의 아버지이다(출애굽기 31:6).

entries.definition: (brother of the dawn), one of the sons of Bilhan, the grandson of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:10)
entries.definition_ko: '새벽의 형제'라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 손자 빌한의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 7:10).

entries.definition: the controller of Solomon’s household. (1 Kings 4:6)
entries.definition_ko: 솔로몬 왕궁의 관리 책임자였다(열왕기상 4:6).

entries.definition: (brother of foolishness), a native of Giloh, was a privy councillor of David, whose wisdom was highly esteemed, though his name had an exactly opposite signification. (2 Samuel 16:23) (B.C. 1055-1023.) He was the grandfather of Bathsheba. Comp. (2 Samuel 11:3) with 2Sam 23:34Ahithophel joined the conspiracy of Absalom against David, and persuaded him to take possession of the royal harem, (2 Samuel 16:21) and recommended an immediate pursuit of David. His advice was wise; but Hushai advised otherwise. When Ahithophel saw that Hushai’s advice prevailed, he despaired of success, and returning to his own home “put his household in order and hanged himself.” (2 Samuel 17:1-23)
entries.definition_ko: '어리석음의 형제'라는 뜻으로 이름과는 반대로 다윗의 지혜로운 참모였던 길로 출신 인물이며(사무엘하 16:23) 밧세바의 조부였다. 압살롬의 반역에 가담해 조언했으나 후새의 조언이 채택되자 실패를 예감하고 집에 돌아가 목매어 죽었다(사무엘하 17:1-23).

entries.definition: (brother of goodness). • The son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, and therefore of the family of Ithamar. (1 Samuel 14:3; 22:9,11) (B.C. 1125.) He was succeeded by his son Ahijah (Ahimelech). (B.C. 1085.) • Son of Amariah, and father of Zadok the high priest, (1 Chronicles 6:7,8; 2 Samuel 8:17) of the house of Eleazar. (B.C. before 1045.)
entries.definition_ko: '선함의 형제'라는 뜻. (1) 비느하스의 아들이자 엘리의 손자로 이다말 가문 소속이며 아들 아히야(아히멜렉)가 뒤를 이었다(사무엘상 14:3). (2) 아마랴의 아들이자 대제사장 사독의 아버지, 엘르아살 가문(역대상 6:7).

entries.definition: (fertile), a city of Asher from which the Canaanites were not driven out. (Judges 1:31)
entries.definition_ko: '비옥한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파의 성읍이며 가나안 사람들이 쫓겨나지 않았다(사사기 1:31).

entries.definition: (ornamental) daughter of Sheshan, whom, having no issue, he gave in marriage to his Egyptian slave Jarha. (1 Chronicles 2:31,35) From her were descended Zabad, one of David’s mighty men, (1 Chronicles 11:41) and Aza-riah, one of the captains of hundreds in the reign of Joash. (2 Chronicles 23:1)
entries.definition_ko: '장식의'라는 뜻으로 세산의 딸이며 아들이 없어 애굽 사람 종 야르하에게 시집보냈다. 그 후손으로 다윗의 용사 사밧과 요아스 시대 백부장 아사랴가 있다(역대상 2:31,35).

entries.definition: (brothely), son of Bela the son of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 8:4) In (1 Chronicles 8:7) he is called Ahiah, Or Ahijah. The patronymic, Ahohite, is found in (2 Samuel 23:9,28; 1 Chronicles 11:12,29; 27:4)
entries.definition_ko: '형제다운'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 아들 벨라의 아들이다(역대상 8:4); 8:7에서는 아히야로 불린다. '아호아 사람'이라는 파생어가 여러 곳에 나온다.

entries.definition: [Ahoah]
entries.definition_ko: 아호아(AHOAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (my tabernacle) two symbolical names, are described as harlots, the former representing Samaria and the latter Judah. Ezek. 23.
entries.definition_ko: '나의 장막'이라는 뜻으로 각각 사마리아와 유다를 상징하는 음녀로 묘사된 상징적 이름이다(에스겔 23장).

entries.definition: a Danite of great skill as a weaver and embroiderer, whom Moses appointed with Bezaleel to erect the tabernacle. (Exodus 35:30-35) (B.C. 1490.)
entries.definition_ko: 직조와 자수에 뛰어난 단 지파 사람으로 모세가 브살렐과 함께 성막 건축을 맡겼다(출애굽기 35:30-35).

entries.definition: (my tabernacle is exulted), One of the three wives of Esau. (B.C. 1797.) She was the daughter of Anah. (Genesis 36:2,26) In the earlier narrative, (Genesis 26:34) Aholibamah is called Judith, which may have been her original name.
entries.definition_ko: '나의 장막이 높임을 받다'라는 뜻으로 에서의 세 아내 중 하나이며 아나의 딸이다(창세기 36:2). 창세기 26:34에서는 유딧이라 불리며 이것이 본래 이름이었을 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (brother of water, i.e. cowardly), Son of Jabath, a descendant of Judah, and head of one of the families of the Zorathites. (1 Chronicles 4:2)
entries.definition_ko: '물의 형제, 곧 비겁한'이라는 뜻으로 야핫의 아들이며 유다 후손 소라 가문의 우두머리이다(역대상 4:2).

entries.definition: (possession), properly Ahuzzam son of Ashur, the father or founder of Tekoa, by his wife Naarah. (1 Chronicles 4:6)
entries.definition_ko: '소유'라는 뜻으로 아술이 아내 나아라를 통해 낳은 드고아의 창시자 아들이다(역대상 4:6).

entries.definition: (possesions) one of the friends of the Philistine king Abimelech, who accompanied him at his interview with Isaac. (Genesis 26:26) (B.C. about 1877.)
entries.definition_ko: '소유들'이라는 뜻으로 블레셋 왕 아비멜렉의 친구로 이삭과의 회담에 동행했다(창세기 26:26).

entries.definition: (heap of ruins). • A city lying east of Bethel and “beside Bethaven.” (Joshua 7:2; 8:9) It was the second city taken by Israel after the passage of the Jordan, and was “utterly destroyed.” (Joshua 7:3-5; 8:1; Joshua 9:3; 10:1,2; 12:9) • A city of the Ammonites, apparently attached to Heshbon. (Jeremiah 49:3)
entries.definition_ko: '폐허 더미'라는 뜻. (1) 벧엘 동쪽, 벧아웬 곁에 위치한 성읍으로 이스라엘이 요단강을 건넌 후 두 번째로 점령해 완전히 멸한 곳이다(여호수아 7:2). (2) 암몬 사람의 성읍으로 헤스본에 속한 것으로 보인다(예레미야 49:3).

entries.definition: (clamor). • Son of Zibeon, a descendant of Seir and ancestor of one of the wives of Esau, (1 Chronicles 1:40) called in (Genesis 36:24) Ajah = A Iah. He probably died before his father, as the succession fell to his brother Anah. • Father of Rizpah, the concubine of Saul. (2 Samuel 3:7; 21:8,10,11) (B.C. before 1040.)
entries.definition_ko: '외침'이라는 뜻. (1) 세일의 후손 시브온의 아들로 에서의 아내 중 하나의 조상(역대상 1:40); 창세기 36:24에서는 아야라 불린다. (2) 사울의 첩 리스바의 아버지(사무엘하 3:7).

entries.definition: (feminine of Ai), a place named by Isaiah, (Isaiah 10:28) in connection with Migron and Michmash probably the same as Ai.
entries.definition_ko: '아이'의 여성형으로 이사야가 믹론, 믹마스와 함께 언급한 장소이며 아이와 동일시된다(이사야 10:28).

entries.definition: like Aiath probably a variation of the name Ai, mentioned with Michmash and Bethel. (Nehemiah 11:31)
entries.definition_ko: 아얏처럼 '아이'의 변형으로 추정되며 믹마스, 벧엘과 함께 언급된다(느헤미야 11:31).

entries.definition: (place of gazelles). • A city of the Kohathites. (Joshua 21:24; 1 Chronicles 6:69) It was a Levitical city and a city of refuge. It was originally allotted to the tribe of Dan, (Joshua 19:42) Authorized Version, AJALON, which tribe, however, was unable to dispossess the Amorites of the place. (Judges 1:35) Aijalon was one of the towns fortified by Reheboam, (2 Chronicles 11:10) and the last we hear of it is being in the hands of the Philistines. (2 Chronicles 28:18) Being on the very frontier of the two kingdoms, we can understand how Aijalon should be spoken of sometimes, (1 Chronicles 6:69) comp. with 1Chr 6:66As in Ephraim and sometimes, (2 Chronicles 11:10; 1 Samuel 14:31) as in Judah and Benjamin. It is represented by the modern Yalo, a little to the north of the Jaffa road, about 14 miles out of Jerusalem. • A broad and beautiful valley near the city of Aijalon over which Joshua commanded the moon to stand still during the pursuit after the battle of Gibeon. (Joshua 10:12) • A place in Zebulon, mentioned as the burial-place of Elon, one of the Judges. (Judges 12:12)
entries.definition_ko: '노루의 처소'라는 뜻. (1) 고핫 자손의 레위 성읍이자 도피성(여호수아 21:24); 본래 단 지파에 배분되었으나 아모리 족속을 쫓아내지 못했다(사사기 1:35). 르호보암이 요새화했고(역대하 11:10) 훗날 블레셋에 넘어갔다(역대하 28:18). (2) 여호수아가 기브온 전투 후 해에게 멈추라 명한 아름다운 골짜기(여호수아 10:12). (3) 스불론 지파의 한 장소로 사사 엘론의 매장지(사사기 12:12).

entries.definition: (the hind of the morning dawn), found once only in the Bible, in the title of (Psalms 22:1) It probably describes to the musician the melody to which the psalm was to be played.
entries.definition_ko: '새벽의 암사슴'이라는 뜻으로 시편 22편 표제에만 나오며 시편이 연주될 곡조를 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (spring, well). • One of the landmarks on the eastern boundary of Palestine. (Numbers 34:11) It is probably ’Ain el-’Azy, the main source of the Orontes. • One of the southernmost cities of Judah, (Joshua 15:32) afterwards allotted to Simeon, (Joshua 19:7; 1 Chronicles 4:32) and given to the priests. (Joshua 21:16)
entries.definition_ko: '샘, 우물'이라는 뜻. (1) 팔레스타인 동쪽 경계의 지표 중 하나(민수기 34:11). (2) 유다 최남단 성읍으로(여호수아 15:32) 이후 시므온 지파에 배분되고(여호수아 19:7) 제사장들에게 주어졌다(여호수아 21:16).

entries.definition: [Aijalon, Or Ajalon]
entries.definition_ko: 아얄론(AIJALON) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: • (Genesis 36:24)
entries.definition_ko: 창세기 36:24 참조.

entries.definition: (sharp sighted), son of Ezer, one of the “dukes” or chieftains of the Horites, and descendant of Seir. (Genesis 36:27) He is called Jakanin (1 Chronicles 1:42)
entries.definition_ko: '날카로운 시력을 가진'이라는 뜻으로 에셀의 아들이자 호리 족속의 지도자 중 하나이며 세일의 후손이다(창세기 36:27); 역대상 1:42에서는 야간이라 불린다.

entries.definition: Revised Version of (Acts 1:19) for Aceldama.
entries.definition_ko: 아겔다마(ACELDAMA)의 개정역 표기이다(사도행전 1:19).

entries.definition: (insidious). • A descendant of Zerubbabel and son of Elioenai. (1 Chronicles 3:24) • One of the porters or doorkeepers at the east gate of the temple. (B.C. 636-440.) • One of the Nethinim, whole family returned with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:45) (B.C. 536.) • A Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people. (Nehemiah 8:7)
entries.definition_ko: '교활한'이라는 뜻. (1) 스룹바벨의 후손이자 엘료에내의 아들(역대상 3:24). (2) 성전 동문의 문지기 중 하나. (3) 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 가문(에스라 2:45). (4) 에스라의 율법 해설을 도운 레위인(느헤미야 8:7).

entries.definition: (the ascent of, or the going up to); also MAALEH-ACRABBIM (the scorpion pass), A pass between the south end of the Dead Sea and Zin, forming one of the landmarks on the south boundary at once of Judah, (Joshua 15:3) and of the Holy Land. (Numbers 34:4) Also the boundary of the Amorites. (Judges 1:36) As to the name, scorpions abound in the whole of this district.
entries.definition_ko: '오르막' 또는 마알레아그랍빔('전갈 고개')이라는 뜻으로 사해 남단과 신 사이의 고갯길이며 유다와 성지 남쪽 경계의 지표이다(여호수아 15:3). 전갈이 많아 붙여진 이름이다.

entries.definition: from the Arabic al bastraton, a whitish stone or from Alabastron, the place in Egypt where it is found. It occurs only in (Matthew 26:7; Mark 14:3; Luke 7:37) The ancients considered alabaster to be the best material in which to preserve their ointments. The Oriental alabaster (referred to in the Bible) is a translucent carbonate of lime, formed on the floors of limestone caves by the percolation of water. It is of the same material as our marbles, but differently formed. It is usually clouded or banded like agate, hence sometimes called onyx marble. Our common alabaster is different from this, being a variety of gypsum or sulphate of lime, used In its finer forms for vases, etc.; in the coarser it is ground up for plaster of Paris. The noted sculptured slabs from Nineveh are made of this material.
entries.definition_ko: 아랍어 '알 바스라톤' 또는 애굽의 산지 이름 알라바스트론에서 유래했다. 마태복음 26:7 등에만 나오며, 고대인들은 향유를 보존하는 데 최고의 재료로 여겼다. 동방의 설화석고는 반투명한 탄산석회로 석회암 동굴 바닥에 형성된다.

entries.definition: properly Al’emeth (covering), one of the sons of Beecher, the son of Benjamin. (1 Chronicles 7:8)
entries.definition_ko: '덮개'라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 아들 베겔의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 7:8).

entries.definition: (king’s oak), a place within the limits of Asher, named between Achshaph and Amad. (Joshua 19:26) only.
entries.definition_ko: '왕의 상수리나무'라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파 경계, 악삽과 아맛 사이의 한 장소이다(여호수아 19:26).

entries.definition: (virgins), (Psalms 46:1) title; (1 Chronicles 15:20) Some interpret it to mean a musical instrument, and others a melody.
entries.definition_ko: '처녀들'이라는 뜻으로(시편 46편 표제; 역대상 15:20) 악기 또는 곡조를 가리키는 것으로 해석된다.

entries.definition: (covering), a Benjamite, son of Jehoadah or Jarah, (1 Chronicles 8:36; 9:42) and descended from Jonathan the son of Saul. (B.C after 1077.)
entries.definition_ko: '덮개'라는 뜻으로 베냐민 사람이며 여호앗다(또는 야라)의 아들이자 사울의 아들 요나단의 후손이다(역대상 8:36).

entries.definition: • Son of Simon the Cyrenian, who was compelled to bear the cross for our Lord. (Mark 15:21) • One of the kindred of Annas the high priest. (Acts 4:6) • A Jew at Ephesus whom his countrymen put forward during the tumult raised by Demetrius the silversmith, (Acts 19:33) to plead their cause with the mob. • An Ephesian Christian reprobated by St. Paul in (1 Timothy 1:20) as having, together with one Hymenaeus, put from him faith and a good conscience, and so made shipwreck concerning the faith. This may be the same with • Alexander the coppersmith, mentioned by the same apostle, (2 Timothy 4:14) as having done him many mischiefs.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 구레네 사람 시몬의 아들로, 그 아버지가 주님의 십자가를 대신 졌다(마가복음 15:21). (2) 대제사장 안나스의 친족(사도행전 4:6). (3) 에베소의 유대인으로 데메드리오 소요 때 군중 앞에 나섰다(사도행전 19:33). (4) 후메내오와 함께 믿음과 선한 양심을 버려 바울에게 책망받은 에베소 그리스도인(디모데전서 1:20). (5) 바울에게 해를 끼친 구리 세공업자 알렉산더(디모데후서 4:14).

entries.definition: (helper of men—brave) king of Macedon, surnamed the Great, the son of Philip and Olympias, was born at Pella B.C. 356, and succeeded his father B.C. 336. Two years afterwards he crossed the Hellespont (B.C. 334) to carry out the plans of his fathers and execute the mission of (Greece to the civilized world. He subjugated Syria and Palestine B.C. 334-332. Egypt next submitted to him B.C. 332, and in this year he founded Alexandria. In the same year he finally defeated Darius at Gaugamela, who in B.C. 330 was murdered. The next two years were occupied by Alexander in the consolidation of his Persian conquests and the reduction of Bactria. In B.C. 327 he crossed the Indus; turning westward he reached Susa B.C. 325, and proceeded to Babylon B.C. 324, which he chose as the capital of his empire. In the next year (B.C. 323) he died there of intemperance, at the early age of 32, in the midst of his gigantic plans; and those who inherited his conquests left his designs unachieved and unattempted. cf. (Daniel 7:6; 8:5; 11:3) Alexander is intended in (Daniel 2:39) and also Dani 7:6; 8:5-7; 11:3,4 The latter indicating the rapidity of his conquests and his power. He ruled with great dominion, and did according to his will, (Daniel 11:3) “and there was none that could deliver .... out of his hand.” (Daniel 8:7)
entries.definition_ko: '사람들의 조력자, 용맹한'이라는 뜻으로 마케도니아 왕, 별칭 대왕이며 필립과 올림피아스의 아들로 주전 356년 태어나 336년 왕위를 이었다. 헬레스폰트를 건너 수리아와 팔레스타인, 애굽를 정복하고 알렉산드리아를 세웠으며, 다리오를 격파해 바사 제국을 무너뜨렸다. 인더스강까지 진출했다가 바벨론에서 32세에 요절했다. 다니엘 8장과 11장의 예언에서 그의 신속한 정복이 암시된다.

entries.definition: (from Alexander), 3 Ma 3:1; (Acts 18:24; 6:9) the Hellenic, Roman and Christian capital of Egypt. Situation .— (Alexandria was situated on the Mediterranean Sea directly opposite the island of Pharos, 12 miles west of the Canopic branch of the Nile and 120 miles from the present city of Cairo.) It was founded by Alexander the Great, B.C. 332, who himself traced the ground plan of the city. The work thus begun was continued after the death of Alexander by the Ptolemies. Description .— Under the despotism of the later Ptolemies the trade of Alexandria declined, but its population and wealth were enormous. Its importance as one of the chief corn-ports of Rome secured for it the general favor of the first emperors. Its population was mixed from the first. According to Josephus Alexander himself assigned to the Jews a place in his new city. Philo estimated the number of the Alexandrine Jews in his time at a little less than 1,000,000 and adds that two of the five districts of Alexandria were called “Jewish districts,” and that many Jews lived scattered in the remaining three. “For a long period Alexandria was the greatest of known cities.” After Rome became the chief city of the world, Alexandria ranked second to Rome in wealth and importance, and second to Athens only in literature and science. Its collection of books grew to be the greatest library of ancient times, and contained at one time 700,000 rolls or volumes. Here was made the Septuagint translation of the Old Testament into Greek, begun about B.C. 285, especially in grain, was very great. According to the common legend, St. Mark first “preached the gospel in Egypt, and founded the first church in Alexandria.” At the beginning of the second century the number of Christians at Alexandria must have been very large, and the great leaders of Gnosticism who arose there (Basilides, Valentinus) exhibit an exaggeration of the tendency of the Church. PRESENT CONDITION. The city still bears the same name and is a thriving metropolis, with inhabitants from nearly every European and Oriental nation. Cleopatra’s needle, set up by Thotmes in 1500 B.C., was found in Alexandria.
entries.definition_ko: 알렉산더의 이름을 딴 애굽의 헬라·로마·그리스도교 수도로, 주전 332년 알렉산더 대왕이 건설했다. 유대인 인구가 많아 두 구역이 '유대인 구역'으로 불렸으며, 방대한 고대 도서관(70만 권)이 있었고 이곳에서 구약의 칠십인역 번역이 시작되었다(주전 285년경). 마가가 이곳에 첫 교회를 세웠다고 전해진다.

entries.definition: the Jewish colonists of Alexandria, who were admitted to the privileges of citizenship and had a synagogue at Jerusalem. (Acts 6:9)
entries.definition_ko: 알렉산드리아의 유대인 이주민들로 시민권을 인정받았으며 예루살렘에 자기들의 회당을 두었다(사도행전 6:9).

entries.definition: the former occurring in (2 Chronicles 2:8; 9:10,11) the latter in (1 Kings 10:11,12) These words are identical. From (1 Kings 10:11,12; 2 Chronicles 9:10,11) we learn that the almug was brought in great plenty from Ophir for Solomon’s temple and house, and for the construction of musical instruments. It is probable that this tree is the red sandle wood, which is a native of India and Ceylon. The wood is very heavy, hard and fine grained, and of a beautiful garnet color.
entries.definition_ko: 역대하와 열왕기상에 각각 언급되는 같은 나무로(열왕기상 10:11) 솔로몬의 성전과 왕궁, 악기 제작에 오빌에서 대량으로 수입되었다. 인도와 실론산 홍단목으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Alvah]
entries.definition_ko: 알와(ALVAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Alvan]
entries.definition_ko: 알완(ALVAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: a figure of speech, which has been defined by Bishop Marsh, in accordance with its etymology as, “a representation of one thing which is intended to excite the representation of another thing.” (“A figurative representation containing a meaning other than and in addition to the literal.” “A fable or parable; is a short allegory with one definite moral.”—Encyc. Brit.) In every allegory there is a twofold sense—the immediate or historic, which is understood from the words, and the ultimate, which is concerned with the things signified by the words. The allegorical interpretation is not of the words, but of the thing signified by them, and not only may, but actually does, coexist with the literal interpretation in every allegory, whether the narrative in which it is conveyed be of things possible or real. An illustration of this may be seen in (Galatians 4:24) where the apostle gives an allegorical interpretation to the historical narrative of Hagar and Sarah, not treating that narrative as an allegory in itself; as our Authorized Version would lead us to suppose, but drawing from it a deeper sense than is conveyed by the immediate representation. (Addison’s Vision of Mirza and Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress are among the best allegories in all literature.)
entries.definition_ko: 한 사물의 표상을 통해 다른 사물을 암시하는 수사법으로, 표면적(역사적) 의미와 궁극적(상징적) 의미의 이중 구조를 가진다. 바울이 갈라디아서 4:24에서 하갈과 사라의 역사적 이야기에 알레고리적 해석을 부여한 것이 대표적 예이다.

entries.definition: so written in (Revelation 19:6) foll., or more properly Hallelujah, praise ye Jehovah, as it is found in the margin of (Psalms 104:35; 105:45; 106; 111:1; 112:1; 113:1) comp. Psal 113:9; 115:18; 116:19, 117:2 The literal meaning of “hallelujah” sufficiently indicates the character of the Psalms in which it occurs as hymns of praise and thanksgiving.
entries.definition_ko: 요한계시록 19:6에 나오는 표기이며 더 정확히는 '할렐루야', 곧 '여호와를 찬양하라'는 뜻이다(시편 104:35 등). 이 단어가 등장하는 시편들은 찬양과 감사의 성격을 지닌다.

entries.definition: On the first establishment of the Hebrews in Palestine no connections were formed between them and the surrounding nations. But with the extension of their power under the kings alliances became essential to the security of their commerce. Solomon concluded two important treaties exclusively for commercial purposes the first with Hiram king of Tyre (1 Kings 5:2-12; 9:27) the second with a Pharaoh, king of Egypt. (1 Kings 10:28,29) When war broke out between Amaziah I and Jeroboam II, a coalition was formed between Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah on the one side, and Ahaz and Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, on the other. (2 Kings 16:5-9) The formation of an alliance was attended with various religious rites. A victim was slain and divided into two parts, between which the contracting parties passed. (Genesis 15:10) Generally speaking the oath alone is mentioned in the contracting of alliances, either between nations, (Joshua 9:15) or individuals. (Genesis 25:28; 31:53; 1 Samuel 20:17; 2 Kings 11:4) The event was celebrated by a feast. Genesis l.c.; (Exodus 24:11; 2 Samuel 3:12,20) Salt, as symbolical of fidelity, was used on these occasions. Occasionally a pillar or a heap of stones was set up as a memorial of the alliance. (Genesis 31:52) Presents were also sent by the parties soliciting the alliance. (1 Kings 15:18; Isaiah 30:6); 1 Macc 16:18. The fidelity of the Jews to their engagements was conspicuous at all periods of their history, (Joshua 9:18) and any breach of covenant was visited with very severe punishment. (2 Samuel 21:1; Ezekiel 17:16)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인들이 팔레스타인에 정착한 초기에는 주변 민족과 동맹을 맺지 않았으나 왕정 시대에 상업적 필요로 동맹이 맺어졌다. 솔로몬은 두로 왕 히람 및 애굽 바로와 조약을 맺었다. 동맹 체결에는 짐승을 잡아 둘로 나누어 그 사이를 지나가는 의식(창세기 15:10)이나 맹세, 잔치, 소금 사용, 기념비 건립 등의 의식이 동반되었다.

entries.definition: a large strong tree of some description probably an oak. •Allonmore accurately Elon, a place named among the cities of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:33) Probably the more correct construction is to take it with the following word, i.e., “the oak by Zaanannim. [Elon] •AllonBACHUTH (oak of weeping) the tree under which Rebekah’s nurse, Deborah, was buried. (Genesis 35:8) (an oak) a Simeonite, ancestor of Ziza, a prince of his tribe in the reign of Hezekiah (1 Chronicles 4:37) (B.C. 727.)
entries.definition_ko: '큰 나무, 아마도 상수리나무'라는 뜻. (1) 납달리 성읍 중 하나로 더 정확히는 엘론이며(여호수아 19:33) '사아난님 곁 상수리나무'로 읽는 것이 옳다. (2) 알론바굿, 곧 리브가의 유모 드보라가 묻힌 상수리나무(창세기 35:8). (3) 히스기야 시대 시므온 지파 방백 시사의 조상(역대상 4:37).

entries.definition: (measure) the first in order of the descendants of Joktan. (Genesis 10:26; 1 Chronicles 1:20)
entries.definition_ko: '측량'이라는 뜻으로 욕단의 후손 중 맏이이다(창세기 10:26).

entries.definition: (concealed) a city within the tribe of Benjamin, with “suburbs” given to the priests. (Joshua 21:18) [Alemeth]
entries.definition_ko: '숨겨진'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 지파 안의 성읍으로 제사장들에게 '초지'와 함께 주어졌다(여호수아 21:18); 알레멧(ALEMETH)과 동일시된다.

entries.definition: This word is found in (Genesis 43:11; Exodus 25:33,34; 37:19,20; Numbers 17:8; Ecclesiastes 12:5; Jeremiah 1:11) in the text of the Authorized Version. It is invariably represented by the same Hebrew word, shaked meaning hasten. (Jeremiah 1:11,12) The almond tree is a native of Asia and North Africa, but it is cultivated in the milder parts of Europe.” It resembles the peach tree in form, blossom and fruit. It is in fact only another species of the same genus.” The height of the tree is about 12 or 14 feet; the flowers are pink, and arranged for the most part in pairs, the leaves are long, ovate, with a serrated margin and an acute point. The covering of the fruit is down and succulent, enclosing the hard shell which contains the kernel. It is this but for which the tree is chiefly valued. It is curious to observe, in connection with the almond bowls of the golden candlestick, that, in the language of lapidaries, almonds are pieces of rock crystal, even now used in adorning branch candlesticks.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 샤케드('서두르다')로 표현되는 나무로(예레미야 1:11) 복숭아나무를 닮았으며 이스라엘과 북아프리카가 원산지이다. 금촛대의 살구꽃 형상 장식과 관련해 언급된다(출애굽기 25:33).

entries.definition: (concealing the two cakes), one of the latest stations of the Israelites between Dibon-gad and the mountains of Abarim (Numbers 33:46,47) It is probably identical with Beth-diblathaim.
entries.definition_ko: '두 과자를 감추는'이라는 뜻으로 디본갓과 아바림 산 사이 이스라엘의 마지막 진영지 중 하나이며(민수기 33:46) 벧디블라다임과 동일시된다.

entries.definition: The duty of alms-giving, especially in kind, consisting chiefly in portions to be left designedly from produce of the field, the vineyard and the oliveyard, (Leviticus 19:9,10; 23:22; 15:11; 24:19; 26:2-13; Ruth 2:2) is strictly enjoined by the law. Every third year also, (14:28) each proprietor was directed to share the tithe of his produce with “the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow.” The theological estimate of almsgiving among the Jews is indicated in the following passages: (Job 31:17; Proverbs 10:2; 11:4; Esther 9:22; Psalms 112:9; Acts 9:36) the case of Dorcas; (Acts 10:2) of Cornelius; to which may be added Tobit 4:10,11; 14:10,11, and Ecclus. 3:30; 40:24. The Pharisees were zealous in almsgiving, but too ostentatious their mode of performance, for which our Lord finds fault with them. (Matthew 6:2) The duty of relieving the poor was not neglected by the Christians. (Matthew 6:1-4; Luke 14:13; Acts 20:35; Galatians 2:10) Regular proportionate giving was expected. (Acts 11:30; Romans 15:25-27; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4)
entries.definition_ko: 밭, 포도원, 감람원에서 일부러 남겨두는 소산을 가난한 자에게 주도록 율법에 엄격히 규정되어 있었다(레위기 19:9,10). 3년마다 십일조를 레위인·나그네·고아·과부와 나누도록 했다(신명기 14:28). 바리새인들은 구제에 열심이었으나 과시적이어서 주님의 책망을 받았다(마태복음 6:2).

entries.definition: [Algum Or Almug TreesTREES]
entries.definition_ko: 알굼 또는 알묵 나무(ALGUM OR ALMUG TREES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (in Heb. Ahalim, Ahaloth), The name of a costly and sweet-smelling wood which is mentioned in (Numbers 24:6; Psalms 45:8; Proverbs 7:17; Song of Solomon 4:14; John 19:39) It is usually identified with the Aquilaria agollochum, an aromatic wood much valued in India. This tree sometimes grows to the height of 120 feet, being 12 feet in girth.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 아할림/아할롯으로 표현되는 값비싼 향목이며(민수기 24:6) 인도산 침향나무(아퀼라리아 아갈로쿰)로 추정된다.

entries.definition: a place or district, forming with Asher the jurisdiction of the ninth of Solomon’s commissariat officers. (1 Kings 4:16)
entries.definition_ko: 아셀과 함께 솔로몬의 아홉째 지방관 관할구역을 이루던 장소 또는 지역이다(열왕기상 4:16).

entries.definition: (A), the first letter of the Greek alphabet. With Omega, the last letter, it is used in the Old Testament and in the New to express the eternity of God, as including both the beginning and the end. (Revelation 1:8,11; 21:6; 22:13; Isaiah 41:4; 44:6) hence these letters became a favorite symbol of the eternal divinity of our Lord, and were used for this purpose in connection with the cross, or the monogram of Christ (i.e. the first two letters, ch and r, of Christ’s name in Greek). Both Greeks and Hebrews employed the letters of the alphabet as numerals.
entries.definition_ko: 헬라어 알파벳의 첫 글자로, 마지막 글자 오메가와 함께 하나님의 영원하심(처음과 마지막)을 나타내는 데 쓰인다(계시록 1:8). 그리스도의 영원한 신성을 나타내는 상징으로 십자가나 그리스도의 모노그램과 함께 쓰였다.

entries.definition: [Writing]
entries.definition_ko: 문자(WRITING) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (changing) the father of the apostle James the Less, (Matthew 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13) and husband of Mary. (John 19:25) [Mary] In this latter place he is called Clopas (not, as in the Authorized Version, Cleophas).
entries.definition_ko: '변화'라는 뜻으로 사도 야고보(작은 자)의 아버지이며(마태복음 10:3) 마리아의 남편이다(요한복음 19:25); 이곳에서는 글로바로 불린다.

entries.definition: The first altar of which we have any account is that built by Noah when he left the ark. (Genesis 8:20) In the early times altars were usually built in certain spots hallowed by religious associations, e.g., where God appeared. (Genesis 12:7; 13:18; 26:25; 35:1) Though generally erected for the offering of sacrifice, in some instances they appear to have been only memorials. (Genesis 12:7; Exodus 17:15,16) Altars were most probably originally made of earth. The law of Moses allowed them to be made of either earth or unhewn stones. (Exodus 20:24,25) I. The Altar of Burnt Offering . It differed in construction at different times. (1) In the tabernacle, (Exodus 27:1) ff.; Exod 38:1 ff., it was comparatively small and portable. In shape it was square. It as five cubits in length, the same in breadth, and three cubits high. It was made of planks of shittim (or acacia) wood overlaid with brass. The interior was hollow. (Exodus 27:8) At the four corners were four projections called horns made, like the altar itself, of shittim wood overlaid with brass, (Exodus 27:2) and to them the victim was bound when about to be sacrificed. (Psalms 118:27) Round the altar, midway between the top and bottom, ran a projecting ledge, on which perhaps the priest stood when officiating. To the outer edge of this, again, a grating or network of brass was affixed, and reached to the bottom of the altar. At the four corners of the network were four brazen rings, into which were inserted the staves by which the altar was carried. These staves were of the same material as the altar itself. As the priests were forbidden to ascend the altar by steps, (Exodus 20:26) it has been conjectured that a slope of earth led gradually up to the ledge from which they officiated. The place of the altar was at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.)” (Exodus 40:29) (2) In Solomon’s temple the altar was considerably larger in its dimensions. It differed too in the material of which it was made, being entirely of brass. (1 Kings 8:64; 2 Chronicles 7:7) It had no grating, and instead of a single gradual slope, the ascent to it was probably made by three successive platforms, to each of which it has been supposed that steps led. The altar erected by Herod in front of the temple was 15 cubits in height and 50 cubits in length and breadth. According to (Leviticus 6:12,13) a perpetual fire was to be kept burning on the altar. II. The Altar of Incense, called also the golden altar to distinguish it from the altar of burnt offering which was called the brazen altar. (Exodus 38:30) (a) That in the tabernacle was made of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold. In shape it was square, being a cubit in length and breadth and two cubits in height. Like the altar of burnt offering it had horns at the four corners, which were of one piece with the rest of the altar. This altar stood in the holy place, “before the vail that is by the ark of the testimony.” (Exodus 30:6; 40:5) (b) The altar of Solomon’s temple was similar, (1 Kings 7:48; 1 Chronicles 28:18) but was made of cedar overlaid with gold. III. Other Altars . In (Acts 17:23) reference is made to an alter to an unknown God. There were several altars in Athens with this inscription, erected during the time of a plague. Since they knew not what god was offended and required to be propitiated.
entries.definition_ko: 성경 최초의 제단은 노아가 방주에서 나와 지은 것이다(창세기 8:20). 모세 율법은 흙이나 다듬지 않은 돌로 만들도록 규정했다(출애굽기 20:24). 성막의 번제단은 아카시아 나무에 놋을 입혀 만들었고, 솔로몬 성전의 것은 온통 놋으로 더 크게 만들어졌다. 분향단은 금으로 만들어 성소 안에 두었다.

entries.definition: (destroy not), found in the introductory verse to Psalms 57,58,59,75. It was probably the beginning of some song or poem to the tune of which those psalms were to be chanted.
entries.definition_ko: '멸하지 마소서'라는 뜻으로 시편 57, 58, 59, 75편 표제에 나오며 그 시편이 불릴 곡조의 이름으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (a crowd of men) one of the stations of the Israelites on their journey to Sinai, the last before Rephidim. (Numbers 33:13,14)
entries.definition_ko: '사람들의 무리'라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 시내산으로 가는 길에 르비딤 직전 머문 진영지이다(민수기 33:13,14).

entries.definition: (evil), a duke of Edom, (Genesis 36:40) written Aliahin (1 Chronicles 1:51)
entries.definition_ko: '악'이라는 뜻으로 에돔의 족장이며(창세기 36:40) 역대상 1:51에서는 알리아라 불린다.

entries.definition: (tall), a Horite, son of Shobal, (Genesis 36:23) written Alianin (1 Chronicles 1:40)
entries.definition_ko: '키 큰'이라는 뜻으로 호리 사람 소발의 아들이며(창세기 36:23) 역대상 1:40에서는 알리안이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (enduring), an unknown place in Asher, between Alammelech and Misheal. (Joshua 19:26) only.
entries.definition_ko: '지속하는'이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파 안의 알려지지 않은 장소로 알람멜렉과 미살 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 19:26).

entries.definition: (Esther 16:10,17) and Amad’athus . (Esther 12:6) [Hammedatha]
entries.definition_ko: 함므다다(HAMMEDATHA) 항목 참조이다(에스더 16:10).

entries.definition: (labor), an Asherite, son of Helem. (1 Chronicles 7:35)
entries.definition_ko: '수고'라는 뜻으로 아셀 사람 헬렘의 아들이다(역대상 7:35).

entries.definition: (dweller in a valley), a son of Eliphaz by his concubine Timnah grandson of Esau, and chieftain (“duke,” Authorized Version) of Edom. (Genesis 36:12,16; 1 Chronicles 1:36) (B.C. about 1700.)
entries.definition_ko: '골짜기에 거하는 자'라는 뜻으로 엘리바스가 첩 딤나를 통해 낳은 아들이며 에서의 손자이자 에돔의 족장이다(창세기 36:12).

entries.definition: a nomadic tribe of uncertain origin, which occupied the peninsula of Sinai and the wilderness intervening between the southern hill-ranges of Palestine and the border of Egypt. (Numbers 13:29; 1 Samuel 15:7; 27:8) Their wealth consisted in flocks and herds. Mention is made of a “town” (1 Samuel 15:5) but their towns could have been little more than stations or nomadic enclosures. The Amalekites first came in contact with the Israelites at Rephidim, but were signally defeated. (Exodus 17:8-16) In union with the Canaanites they again attacked the Israelites on the borders of Palestine, and defeated them near Hormah. (Numbers 14:45) Saul undertook an expedition against them. (1 Samuel 14:48) Their power was thenceforth broken, and they degenerated into a horde of banditti. Their destruction was completed by David. (1 Samuel 30:1-17)
entries.definition_ko: 출처 불확실한 유목 민족으로 시내 반도와 팔레스타인 남쪽 산지와 애굽 국경 사이 광야에 거주했다(민수기 13:29). 양떼와 가축이 주된 재산이었다. 르비딤에서 이스라엘과 처음 충돌해 크게 패했고(출애굽기 17:8-16), 이후에도 여러 차례 충돌했으나 사울의 원정으로 세력이 크게 꺾였고 다윗에 의해 완전히 진멸되었다(사무엘상 30:1-17).

entries.definition: a mountain in Ephraim, (Judges 12:15) probably so named because the Amalekites once held possession of it.
entries.definition_ko: 에브라임의 한 산으로(사사기 12:15) 아말렉 족속이 한때 이곳을 점유했던 데서 이름이 유래한 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (gathering place), a city in the south of Judah named with Shema and Moladah in (Joshua 15:26) only.
entries.definition_ko: '모이는 곳'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽의 성읍이며 세마, 몰라다와 함께 언급된다(여호수아 15:26).
하만(하만) 참조(에스더 10:7 등).

entries.definition: (a covenant), apparently a mountain in or near Lebanon. (Song of Solomon 4:8) It is commonly assumed that this is the mountain in which the river Abana, (2 Kings 5:12) has its source.
entries.definition_ko: '언약'이라는 뜻으로 레바논 부근의 한 산으로 추정되며(아가 4:8) 아바나강의 발원지로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: (the Lord says, i.e. promises). • Father of Ahitub according to (1 Chronicles 6:7,52) and son of Meraioth, in the line of the high priests. • The high priest in the reign of Jehoshaphat. (2 Chronicles 19:11) He was the son of Azariah. • The head of a Levitical house of the Kohathites. (1 Chronicles 23:13; 24:23) • The head of one of the twenty-four courses of priest. (2 Chronicles 31:15; Nehemiah 10:3; 12:2,13) • One of the sons of Bani in the time of Ezra. (Ezra 10:42) • A priest who returned with Zerubbabel. (Nehemiah 10:3; 12:2,13) • A descendant of Pharez. (Nehemiah 11:4) • An ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet. (Zephaniah 1:1)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 말씀하신다, 곧 약속하신다'는 뜻. (1) 대제사장 계보상 므라욧의 아들이자 아히둡의 아버지(역대상 6:7). (2) 여호사밧 시대의 대제사장(역대하 19:11). (3) 고핫 가문 레위인의 우두머리(역대상 23:13). (4) 24반차 중 하나의 우두머리(역대하 31:15). (5) 에스라 시대 바니의 아들 중 하나(에스라 10:42). (6) 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 제사장(느헤미야 10:3). (7) 베레스의 후손(느헤미야 11:4). (8) 선지자 스바냐의 조상(스바냐 1:1).

entries.definition: (a burden). • Son of Ithra, or Jether, by Abigail, David’s sister. (2 Samuel 17:25) He joined in Absalom’s rebellion, B.C. 1023, was appointed commander-in-chief and suffered defeat by Joab. (2 Samuel 18:6) David, incensed against Joab for killing Absalom, forgave Amasa and appointed him Joab’s successor. (2 Samuel 19:13) Joab afterwards, when they were both in pursuit of the rebel Sheba, pretending to salute Amasa stabbed him with his sword. (2 Samuel 20:10) • A prince of Ephraim, son of Hadlai, in the reign of Ahaz. (2 Chronicles 28:12)
entries.definition_ko: '짐'이라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 누이 아비가일과 이드라(예델) 사이의 아들. 압살롬의 반역에 가담해 총사령관이 되었으나 요압에게 패했다. 다윗이 그를 용서하고 요압의 후임으로 삼았으나, 요압이 세바를 쫓던 중 그에게 입 맞추는 척하며 칼로 찔러 죽였다(사무엘하 20:10). (2) 아하스 시대 에브라임의 방백 하들래의 아들(역대하 28:12).

entries.definition: (burdensome) • A Kohathite, father of Mahath and ancestor of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6:25,35) • Chief of the captains of Judah and Benjamin, who deserted to David while an outlaw at Ziklag. (1 Chronicles 12:18) (B.C. 1060.) • One of the priests who blew trumpets before the ark. (1 Chronicles 15:24) • Another Kohathite, in the reign of Hezekiah. (2 Chronicles 29:12)
entries.definition_ko: '짐을 진'이라는 뜻. (1) 고핫 사람으로 마핫의 아버지이자 사무엘의 조상(역대상 6:25). (2) 다윗이 시글락에 있을 때 그에게 귀순한 유다와 베냐민 지휘관들의 우두머리(역대상 12:18). (3) 언약궤 앞에서 나팔을 분 제사장 중 하나(역대상 15:24). (4) 히스기야 시대 고핫 사람(역대하 29:12).

entries.definition: (burdensome), son of Azareel, a priest in the time of Nehemiah, (Nehemiah 11:13) apparently the same as Maasiai. (1 Chronicles 9:12) (B.C. 440.)
entries.definition_ko: '짐을 진'이라는 뜻으로 아사렐의 아들이며 느헤미야 시대의 제사장이다(느헤미야 11:13); 역대상 9:12의 마아새와 동일 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah bears), son of Zichri and captain of 200,000 warriors of Judah in the reign of Jehoshaphat. (2 Chronicles 17:16) (B.C. 910.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 짊어지신다'는 뜻으로 시그리의 아들이며 여호사밧 시대 유다의 20만 용사를 지휘한 장군이다(역대하 17:16).

entries.definition: [Hamath]
entries.definition_ko: 하맛(하맛) 참조.

entries.definition: (the strength of the Lord). • Son of Joash, and eighth king of Judah, reigned B.C. 837-809. He succeeded to the throne at the age of 25, on the murder of his father, and punished the murderers. In order to restore his kingdom to the greatness of Jehoshaphat’s days, he made war on the Edomites, defeated them in the Valley of Salt, south of the Dead Sea, and took their capital, Selah or Petra, to which he gave the name of Jokteel, i.e. “Godsubdued.” Flushed with his success, he challenged Joash king of Israel to battle, but was completely defeated, and himself was taken prisoner and conveyed by Joash to Jerusalem, which opened its gates to the conqueror. Amaziah lived 15 years after the death of Joash; and in the 29th year of his reign was murdered by conspirators at Lachish, whither he had retired from Jerusalem for safety. (2 Chronicles 25:27) • A descendant of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:34) • A Levite. (1 Chronicles 6:45) • Priest of the golden calf at Bethel who endeavored to drive the prophet Amos from Israel into Judah. (Amos 7:11,12,14)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 힘'이라는 뜻. (1) 요아스의 아들이자 유다의 8대 왕(주전 837-809년 재위). 25세에 즉위해 부친 살해범들을 처벌했으며, 에돔과 싸워 소금 골짜기에서 승리하고 그 수도 셀라(페트라)를 점령해 욕드엘이라 이름 붙였다. 이후 이스라엘 왕 요아스에게 도전했다가 완패해 포로로 잡혔고, 훗날 라기스에서 반역자들에게 암살당했다. (2) 시므온의 후손(역대상 4:34). (3) 레위인(역대상 6:45). (4) 벧엘의 금송아지 제사장으로 선지자 아모스를 이스라엘에서 쫓아내려 했다(아모스 7:11,12,14).

entries.definition: a person of high rank employed by a government to represent it and transact its business at the seat of government of some other power. The earliest examples of ambassadors employed occur in (Numbers 20:14; 21:21; Judges 11:7-19) afterwards in that of the fraudulent Gibeonites, (Joshua 9:4) etc., and in the instances of civic strife mentioned (Judges 11:12) and Judg 20:12Ambassadors are found to have been employed not only on occasions of hostile challenge or insolent menace, (1 Kings 20:2,6; 2 Kings 14:8) but of friendly compliment, of request for alliance or other aid, of submissive deprecation and of curious inquiry. (2 Kings 14:8; 16:7; 18:14; 2 Chronicles 32:31) Ministers are called ambassadors of Christ.
entries.definition_ko: 어떤 정부를 대표해 다른 나라의 정부와 교섭하는 고위직 인물을 가리킨다. 성경에 등장하는 가장 이른 예는 민수기 20:14 등이며, 우호적 요청부터 적대적 도전, 굴복 청원까지 다양한 상황에서 파송되었다. 사역자들도 그리스도의 사신으로 불린다.

entries.definition: embassy, a message of a public nature brought by ambassadors. The word also sometimes includes the ambassadors themselves. (Luke 14:32)
entries.definition_ko: 사절단, 곧 사신들이 전하는 공적 성격의 메시지를 뜻하며 때로는 사신들 자신을 가리키기도 한다(누가복음 14:32).

entries.definition: (Heb. chasmal) occurs only in (Ezekiel 1:4,27; 8:2) It is usually supposed that the Hebrew word chasmal (denotes a metal) and not the fossil resin called amber .
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 하쉬말로 에스겔 1:4 등에만 나오며, 화석 수지인 호박이 아니라 금속을 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: literally “true” and used as a substantive, “that which is true,” “truth,” (Isaiah 65:16) a word used in strong asseverations, fixing, as it were, the stamp of truth upon the assertion which it accompanied, and making it binding as an oath. Comp. (Numbers 5:22) In the synagogues and private houses it was customary for the people or members of the family who were present to say “amen” to the prayers which were offered. (Matthew 6:13; 1 Corinthians 14:16) And not only public prayers, but those offered in private, and doxologies, were appropriately concluded with “amen.” (Romans 9:5; 11:36; 15:33; 16:27; 2 Corinthians 13:14) etc.
entries.definition_ko: 문자적으로 '참되다'는 뜻이며 명사로는 '진리'를 뜻한다(이사야 65:16). 맹세를 확증하는 강한 단언의 말로 쓰였으며, 회당과 가정에서 기도 후에 사람들이 '아멘'이라 화답하는 관습이 있었다(마태복음 6:13).

entries.definition: (Heb. achlamah) a subspecies of quartz of a bluish-violet color. Mention is made of this precious stone, which formed the third in the third row of the high priestly breastplate, in (Exodus 28:19; 39:12) It occurs also in (Revelation 21:20)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 아흘라마로 청자색을 띤 석영의 일종이며, 대제사장 흉패 셋째 줄 세 번째 보석으로 언급된다(출애굽기 28:19). 계시록 21:20에도 등장한다.

entries.definition: (builder), one of Solomon’s servants, (Ezra 2:57) called Amon, Or Amen, Amon in (Nehemiah 7:59)
entries.definition_ko: '건축자'라는 뜻으로 솔로몬의 종 중 하나이며(에스라 2:57) 느헤미야 7:59에서는 아몬이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (true), father of the prophet Jonah. (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1)
entries.definition_ko: '참된'이라는 뜻으로 선지자 요나의 아버지이다(열왕기하 14:25).

entries.definition: (head), The hill of, A hill facing Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon, named as the point to which Joab pursued Abner (2 Samuel 2:24)
entries.definition_ko: '머리'라는 뜻으로 기브온 광야로 가는 길목의 기아 맞은편 언덕이며, 요압이 아브넬을 쫓은 지점으로 언급된다(사무엘하 2:24).

entries.definition: i.e., as explained in the margin of the Authorized Version, my people . (Hosea 2:1)
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역 난외주에 '내 백성'이라는 뜻으로 풀이된다(호세아 2:1).

entries.definition: (people of God). • The spy from the tribe of Dan. (Numbers 13:12) (B.C. 1490.) He perished by the plague for his evil report. • Father of Machir of Lo-debar. (2 Samuel 9:4; 17:27) • Father of Bath-sheba, (1 Chronicles 3:5) called Eliamin (2 Samuel 11:3) • The sixth son of Obed-edom, (1 Chronicles 26:5) and one of the doorkeepers of the temple. (B.C. 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 백성'이라는 뜻. (1) 단 지파 정탐꾼으로 악평을 한 죄로 전염병에 죽었다(민수기 13:12). (2) 로드발 마길의 아버지(사무엘하 9:4). (3) 밧세바의 아버지로 사무엘하 11:3에서는 엘리암이라 불림(역대상 3:5). (4) 오벧에돔의 여섯째 아들로 성전 문지기(역대상 26:5).

entries.definition: (people of praise). • An Ephraimite father of Elishama, the chief of the tribe at the time of the Exodus. (Numbers 1:10; 2:18; 7:48,53; 10:22; 7:26) and, through him, ancestor of Joshua. (B.C. 1491.) • A Simeonite, father of Shemuel. (Numbers 34:20) • The father of Pedahel, prince of the tribe of Naphtali. (Numbers 34:28) • The father-of Talmai king of Geshur. (2 Samuel 13:37) • A descendant of Pharez, son of Judah. (1 Chronicles 9:4)
entries.definition_ko: '찬양의 백성'이라는 뜻. (1) 에브라임 지파 사람으로 출애굽 당시 지파장 엘리사마의 아버지이며 여호수아의 조상(민수기 1:10). (2) 시므온 사람 스무엘의 아버지(민수기 34:20). (3) 납달리 지파 방백 브다헬의 아버지(민수기 34:28). (4) 그술 왕 달매의 아버지(사무엘하 13:37). (5) 유다 베레스의 후손(역대상 9:4).

entries.definition: (one of the prince’s people). • Son of Ram or Aram, and father of Nahshon, or Naasson(as it is written) (Matthew 1:4; Luke 3:32); (Numbers 1:7; 2:3; Ruth 4:19,20; 1 Chronicles 2:10) One of the ancestors of Jesus Christ. • The chief of the 112 sons of Uzziel, a Junior Levitical house of the family of the Kohathites. (Exodus 6:23; 1 Chronicles 15:10,11) • In (1 Chronicles 6:22) Izhar, the son of Kohath, is called Amminadib; probably a clerical error.
entries.definition_ko: '백성의 방백'이라는 뜻. (1) 람 또는 아람의 아들이자 나손의 아버지로 그리스도의 조상 중 하나(마태복음 1:4). (2) 고핫 가문 웃시엘의 112 아들 중 우두머리(출애굽기 6:23). (3) 역대상 6:22에서는 고핫의 아들 이스할을 암미나답이라 부르는데 필사 오류로 추정된다.

entries.definition: Probably another form of Amminadab. He was noted for the swiftness of his chariot. (Song of Solomon 6:12) It is uncertain whether we ought to read here AMMINADIB, with the Authorized Version, or my willing people, as in the margin. Ammishad’da-i (people of the Almighty), the father of Ahiezer, prince of the tribe of Dan at the time of the Exodus. (Numbers 1:12; 2:25; 7:66,71; 10:25) (B.C. 1491.)
entries.definition_ko: 암미나답의 다른 표기로 추정되며, 그 병거의 빠름으로 유명했다(아가 6:12).

entries.definition: (people of the Giver, i.e. God), the son of Benaiah, who commanded the third division of David’s army. (1 Chronicles 27:6) (B.C. 1050.)
entries.definition_ko: '주시는 이(하나님)의 백성'이라는 뜻으로 브나야의 아들이며 다윗 군대 제3사단을 지휘했다(역대상 27:6).

entries.definition: (sons of renown, mountaineers), Am’monites, Children of Ammon, A people descended from Ben-ammi, the son of Lot by his younger daughter. (Genesis 19:38) comp Psal 83:7,8The Ammonites are frequently mentioned with the Moabites (descendants of Ben-ammi’s half-brother), and sometimes under the same name. Comp. (Judges 10:6; 2 Chronicles 20:1; Zephaniah 2:8) etc. The precise position of the territory of the Ammonites is not ascertainable. In the earliest mention of them, (2:20) they are said to have dwelt in their place, Jabbok being their border. (Numbers 21:24; 2:37; 3:16) (i.e. Land or country is, however, but rarely ascribed to them. Their capital city was Rabbath, called also Rabbath Ammon on the Jabbok. We find everywhere traces of the fierce habits of maranders in their incursions.) (1 Samuel 11:2; Amos 1:13) and a very high degree of crafty cruelty to their toes. (Jeremiah 41:6,7; Judges 17:11,12) Moab was the settled and civilized half of the nation of Lot, and Ammon formed its predatory and Bedouin section. On the west of Jordan they never obtained a footing. The hatred in which the Ammonites were held by Israel is stated to have arisen partly from their denial of assistance, (23:4) to the Israelites on their approach to Canaan. But whatever its origin the animosity continued in force to the latest date. The tribe was governed by a king, (Judges 11:12) etc.; (1 Samuel 12:12; 2 Samuel 10:1; Jeremiah 40:14) and by “princes.” (2 Samuel 10:3; 1 Chronicles 19:3) The divinity of the tribe was Molech [Molech], and they were gross idolaters.
entries.definition_ko: '명성의 아들들, 산사람들'이라는 뜻으로 롯이 작은딸에게서 낳은 벤암미의 후손이다(창세기 19:38). 모압 족속과 자주 함께 언급되며 얍복강을 경계로 삼았고 수도는 랍바(랍바암몬)였다. 왕정 체제를 갖췄으며 밀곰(몰렉)을 섬기는 우상숭배 민족이었다.

entries.definition: a woman of Ammonite race. (1 Kings 14:21,31; 2 Chronicles 12:13)
entries.definition_ko: 암몬 족속 여인을 가리킨다(열왕기상 14:21).

entries.definition: See No-Amon.
entries.definition_ko: 노아몬(No-Amon) 참조.

entries.definition: (Matthew 1:4; Luke 3:33) [Amminadab, 1]
entries.definition_ko: 마태복음 1:4의 다른 표기; 암미나답(1) 참조.

entries.definition: (faithful). • Eldest son of David. (B.C. 1052.) He dishonored his half-sister Tamar, and was in consequence murdered by her brother. (2 Samuel 13:1-29) • Son of Shimon. (1 Chronicles 4:20)
entries.definition_ko: '신실한'이라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 맏아들로 이복누이 다말을 욕보였다가 그녀의 오라비 압살롬에게 죽임을 당했다(사무엘하 13:1-29). (2) 시몬의 아들(역대상 4:20).

entries.definition: a priest who returned with Zerubbabel. (Nehemiah 12:7,20) (B.C. 536.)
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 제사장이다(느헤미야 12:7).

entries.definition: (builder). • One of Ahab’s governors. (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Chronicles 18:25) • King of Judah, son and successor of Manasseh, reigned two years, from B.C. 642 to 640. Amon devoted himself wholly to the service of false gods, but was killed in a conspiracy, and was succeeded by his son Josiah.
entries.definition_ko: '건축자'라는 뜻. (1) 아합의 방백 중 하나(열왕기상 22:26). (2) 므낫세의 아들이자 후계자로 유다 왕이 되어 2년간 다스렸으나 우상숭배에 빠져 반역자들에게 살해당했고 아들 요시야가 뒤를 이었다.

entries.definition: (the mysterious), an Egyptian divinity, whose name occurs in that of No-amon. (Nahum 3:8) Amen was one of the eight gods of the first order and chief of the triad of Thebes. He was worshipped at that city as Amen-Ra, or “Amen the Sun.”
entries.definition_ko: '신비로운 자'라는 뜻으로 애굽의 신이며 노아몬(나훔 3:8)이라는 지명에 그 이름이 들어있다. 테베의 주신으로 '아멘라(태양신 아멘)'로 숭배되었다.

entries.definition: (dwellers on the summits, mountaineers), one of the chief nations who possessed the land of Canaan before its conquest by the Israelites. As dwelling on the elevated portions of the country, they are contrasted with the Canaanites, who were the dwellers in the lowlands; and the two thus formed the main broad divisions of the Holy Land, (Numbers 13:29) and see (14:7; 1:7,20) “Mountain of the Amorites;” (1:44; Joshua 5:1; 10:6; 11:3) They first occupied the barren heights west of the Dead Sea, at the place called afterwards Engedi. From this point they stretched west to Hebron. At the date of the invasion of the country, Sihon, their then king, had taken the rich pasture land south of the Jabbok. This rich tract, bounded by the Jabbok on the north, the Arnon on the south, the Jordan on the west and “the wilderness” on the east, (Judges 11:21,22) was, perhaps in the most special sense the “land of the Amorites,” (Numbers 21:31; Joshua 12:2,3; 13:10; Judges 11:21,22) but their possessions are distinctly stated to have extended to the very foot of Hermon, (3:8; 4:48) embracing “Gilead and all Bashan,” (3:10) with the Jordan valley on the east of the river. (4:49) After the conquest of Canaan nothing of importance is heard of the Amorites in the Bible.
entries.definition_ko: '산꼭대기에 거하는 자, 산사람'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘 정복 이전 가나안을 차지한 주요 민족 중 하나이다. 저지대에 거한 가나안 족속과 대비되게 고지대에 거했으며, 시혼 왕 시대에는 얍복강 남쪽의 비옥한 목초지를 차지했다. 정복 이후 성경에서 별다른 중요성 없이 사라진다.

entries.definition: (burden), native of Tekoa in Judah, about six miles south of Bethlehem, originally a shepherd and dresser of sycamore trees, who was called by God s Spirit to be a prophet, although not trained in any of the regular prophetic schools. (Amos 1:1; 7:14,15) He travelled from Judah into the northern kingdom of Israel or Ephraim, and there exercised his ministry, apparently not for any long time. (His date cannot be later than B.C. 808 for he lived in the reigns of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel; but his ministry probably took place at an earlier date, perhaps about the middle of Jeroboam’s reign Nothing is known of the time or manner of his death.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: '짐'이라는 뜻으로 베들레헴 남쪽 약 6마일 드고아 출신이며 본래 목자이자 뽕나무 재배자였으나 하나님의 부르심을 받아 선지자가 되었다(아모스 1:1). 유다에서 북이스라엘로 가서 사역했으며, 웃시야와 여로보암 2세 시대(주전 808년 이전)에 활동했다.

entries.definition: The book of the prophecies of Amos seems to be divided into four principal portions closely connected together. (1) From 1:1 to 2:3 he denounces the sins of the nations bordering on Israel and Judah. (2) From 2:4 to 6:14 he describes the state of those two kingdoms, especially, the former. (3) From 7:1 to 9:10 he relates his visit to Bethel, and sketches the impending punishment of Israel. At last he promises blessings. The chief peculiarity of the style consists in the number of allusions to natural objects and agricultural occupations, as might be expected from the early life of the author.
entries.definition_ko: 아모스의 예언은 크게 네 부분으로 나뉜다: (1) 1:1-2:3 이스라엘과 유다 주변 나라들에 대한 심판, (2) 2:4-6:14 이스라엘과 유다의 죄상, (3) 7:1-9:10 벧엘 방문과 이스라엘에 임할 심판, (4) 마지막으로 회복의 축복 약속. 저자의 목자 출신 배경을 반영해 자연과 농경 생활에 대한 비유가 두드러진다.

entries.definition: (strong), father of the prophet Isaiah, and, according to rabbinical tradition, brother of Amaziah king of Judah. (2 Kings 19:2,20; 20:1; Isaiah 1:1) (B.C. before 756.)
entries.definition_ko: '강한'이라는 뜻으로 선지자 이사야의 아버지이며 랍비 전승에 따르면 유다 왕 아마샤의 형제였다고 한다(이사야 1:1).

entries.definition: (a city surrounded by the sea), a city of Macedonia, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica (Acts 17:1) It was distant 33 Roman miles from Philippi, to the southwest, and about three miles from the sea. Its site is now occupied by a village called Neokhorio ; in Turkish Jeni-Keni, or “New Town.”
entries.definition_ko: '바다로 둘러싸인 도시'라는 뜻으로 마케도니아의 도시이며 바울과 실라가 빌립보에서 데살로니가로 가는 길에 지났다(사도행전 17:1). 빌립보에서 남서쪽으로 로마식 33마일 떨어져 있다.

entries.definition: (large), a Christian at Rome. (Romans 16:8) (A.D. 55.)
entries.definition_ko: '큰'이라는 뜻으로 로마의 한 그리스도인이다(로마서 16:8).

entries.definition: (Revised Version,) (Romans 16:8) (the full name of which Amplias, above, is the contraction. The name in this form is “common in the sepulchral inscriptions of persons connected with Caesar’s household.” (A.D. 55.)—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 암블리아의 정식 이름으로 추정된다(로마서 16:8); '암블리아'는 이 이름의 축약형이다.

entries.definition: (an exalted people). • A Levite of the family of the Kohathites, and father of Moses. (Exodus 6:18,20) (B.C. 1571.) • A son of Dishon and descendant of Seir, (1 Chronicles 1:41) properly “Hamram” = Hemdanin (Genesis 36:26) • One of the sons of Bani in the time of Ezra, who had married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:34) (B.C. 459).
entries.definition_ko: '높은 백성'이라는 뜻. (1) 고핫 가문 레위인으로 모세의 아버지(출애굽기 6:18). (2) 세일의 후손 디손의 아들, 정확히는 '함람'(창세기 36:26의 헴단과 같음). (3) 에스라 시대 이방 여인과 결혼한 바니의 아들(에스라 10:34).

entries.definition: A branch of the great Kohathite family of the tribe of Levi, (Numbers 3:27; 1 Chronicles 26:23) descended from Amram, the father of Moses.
entries.definition_ko: 레위 지파 고핫 가문의 한 분파로 모세의 아버지 아므람의 후손이다(민수기 3:27).

entries.definition: (keeper of the gods) perhaps a Hamite king of Shinar or Babylonia, who joined the victorious incursion of the Elamite Chedorlaomer against the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities of the plain. Gen. 14. (B.C. 1898.)
entries.definition_ko: '신들의 수호자'라는 뜻으로 함 계열 시날(바벨로니아) 왕으로 추정되며 그돌라오멜의 원정에 동참해 소돔과 고모라 등을 공격했다(창세기 14장).

entries.definition: were ornaments, gems, scrolls. etc.. worn as preservatives against the power of enchantments, and generally inscribed with mystic forms or characters. The “earrings” in (Genesis 35:4) were obviously connected with idolatrous worship and were probably amulets taken from the bodies of the slain Shechemites. They are subsequently mentioned among the spoils of Midian. (Judges 8:24) In (Hosea 2:13) is another like reference. The “earrings” in (Isaiah 3:20) were also amulets.
entries.definition_ko: 마법의 힘을 막기 위해 착용한 장신구, 보석, 두루마리 등으로 대개 신비한 문양이나 문자가 새겨져 있었다. 창세기 35:4의 '귀고리'는 우상숭배와 관련된 부적으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (strong). • A Levite of the family of Merari. (1 Chronicles 6:46) • A priest. (Nehemiah 11:12)
entries.definition_ko: '강한'이라는 뜻. (1) 므라리 가문 레위인(역대상 6:46). (2) 제사장(느헤미야 11:12).

entries.definition: (grape-town), a town in the mountains of Judah, (Joshua 15:50) named with Debir and Hebron as once belonging to the Anakim. (Joshua 11:21)
entries.definition_ko: '포도 마을'이라는 뜻으로 유다 산지의 성읍이며 드빌, 헤브론과 함께 한때 아낙 족속에게 속했다(여호수아 15:50).

entries.definition: (one who answers), the son of Zibeon and father of Aholibamah, one of Esau’s wives. (Genesis 36:2,14,25) He is supposed to have discovered the “hot springs” (not “mules,” as in the Authorized Version) in the desert as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father. (B.C. 1797.)
entries.definition_ko: '응답하는 자'라는 뜻으로 시브온의 아들이자 에서의 아내 중 하나인 오홀리바마의 아버지이다(창세기 36:2). 아버지의 나귀를 치던 중 광야에서 온천을 발견한 것으로 전해진다.

entries.definition: (gorge or pass), a place within the border of Issachar, named with Shihon and Rabbith. (Joshua 19:19)
entries.definition_ko: '협곡 또는 통로'라는 뜻으로 잇사갈 지파 경계 내 장소이며 시온, 랍빗과 함께 언급된다(여호수아 19:19).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah answers). • Probably a priest. (Nehemiah 8:4) • One of the “heads of the people” who signed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:22)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 응답하신다'는 뜻. (1) 아마도 제사장(느헤미야 8:4). (2) 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 백성의 지도자 중 하나(느헤미야 10:22).
