entries.definition_ko: '매복'이라는 뜻으로 헤브론 인근 유다 산지의 성읍이다(여호수아 15:52).

entries.definition: (burnt up). Although this word appears in the Authorized Version in its original shape only in (Joshua 18:18) yet in the Hebrew text it is of frequent occurrence. It indicates more particularly the deep-sunken valley or trench which forms the most striking among the many striking natural features of Palestine, and which extends with great uniformity of formation from the slopes of Hermon to the Elanitic Gulf (Gulf of Akabah) of the Red Sea; the most remarkable depression known to exist on the surface of the globe. Through the northern portion of this extraordinary fissure the Jordan rushes through the lakes of Huleh and Gennesaret down its tortuous course to the deep chasm of the Dead Sea. This portion, about 150 miles in length, is known amongst the Arabs by the name of el-Ghor . The southern boundary of the (Ghor is the wall of cliffs which crosses the valley about 10 miles south of the Dead Sea. From their summits, southward to the Gulf of Akabah, the valley changes its name, or, it would be more accurate to say, retains old name of Wady el-Arabah .
entries.definition_ko: '불탄 곳'이라는 뜻으로 헤르몬산 기슭에서 홍해의 아카바만까지 이어지는 팔레스타인의 깊은 균열 지대를 가리킨다. 북쪽 부분(요단강이 흐르는 부분)은 '엘고르'라 불리고 사해 남쪽부터는 '와디 엘아라바'로 불린다.

entries.definition: (desert, barren), a country known in the Old Testament under two designations:— • The East Country, (Genesis 25:6) or perhaps the East, ((Genesis 10:30; Numbers 23:7; Isaiah 2:6) and Land of the Sons of the East, (Genesis 29:1) Gentile name, Sons of the East, (Judges 6:3; 7:12; 1 Kings 4:30; Job 1:3; Isaiah 11:14; Jeremiah 49:28; Ezekiel 25:4) From these passages it appears that Land of the East and Sons of the East indicate, primarily, the country east of Palestine, and the tribes descended from Ishmael and from Keturah; and that this original signification may have become gradually extended to Arabia and its inhabitants generally, though without any strict limitation. • ’Arab and ’Arab, whence Arabia. (2 Chronicles 9:14; Isaiah 21:13; Jeremiah 26:24; Ezekiel 27:21) (Arabia is a triangular peninsula, included between the Mediterranean and Red seas, the Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf. Its extreme length, north and south, is about 1300 miles, and its greatest breadth 1500 miles. -Encyc. Brit.) Divisions .—Arabia may be divided into Arabia Proper, containing the whole peninsula as far as the limits of the northern deserts; Northern Arabia (Arabia Deserta), constituting the great desert of Arabia; and Western Arabia, the desert of Petra and the peninsula of Sinai, or the country that has been called Arabia Petraea, I. Arabia Proper, or the Arabian penninsula consists of high tableland, declining towards the north. Most of it is well peopled, watered by wells and streams, and enjoys periodical rains. The moist fertile tracts are those on the southwest and south. II. Northern Arabia, or the Arabian Desert, is a high, undulating, parched plain, of which the Euphrates forms the natural boundary from the Persian Gulf to the frontier of Syria, whence it is bounded by the latter country and the desert of Petra on the northwest and west, the peninsula of Arabia forming its southern limit. It has few oases, the water of the wells is generally either brackish or unpotable and it is visited by the sand-wind called Samoom . The inhabitants principally descended from Ishmael and from Keturah, have always led a wandering and pastoral life. They conducted a considerable trade of merchandise of Arabia and India from the shore of the Persian Gulf. (Ezekiel 27:20-24) III. Western Arabia includes the peninsula of Sinai [Sinai, Or Sinai] and the desert of Petra; corresponding generally with the limits of Arabia Petraea. The latter name is probably derived from that of its chief city, not from its stony character. It was mostly peopled by descendants of Esau, and was generally known as the land of Edom or Idumea [Edom, Idumaea Or Idumea], as well as by its older appellation, the desert of Seir or Mount Seir. [Seir] Inhabitants .— (Arabia, which once ruled from India to the Atlantic, now has eight or nine millions of inhabitants, about one-fifth of whom are Bedouin or wandering tribes, and the other four-fifths settled Arabs.—Encyc. Brit.) • The descendants of Joktanoccupied the principal portions of the south and southwest of the peninsula, with colonies in the interior. The principal Joktanite kingdom, and the chief state of ancient Arabia, was that of the Yemen. • The ISHMAELITES appear to have entered the peninsula from the northwest. That they have spread over the whole of it (with the exception of one or two districts on the south coast), and that the modern nation is predominantly Ishmaelite, is asserted by the Arabs. • Of the descendants of Keturahthe Arabs say little. They appear to have settled chiefly north of the peninsula in Desert Arabia, from Palestine to the Persian Gulf. • In northern and western Arabia are other peoples, which, from their geographical position and mode of life are sometimes classed with the Arabs, of these are Amalek, the descendants of Esau, etc. (Productions— The productions are varied. The most noted animal is the horse. Camels, sheep, cattle, asses, mules and cats are common. Agricultural products are coffee, wheat, barley, millet, beans, pulse, dates and the common garden plants. In pasture lands Arabia is peculiarly fortunate. In mineral products it is singularly poor, lead being most abundant.—Encyc. Brit.) Religion .— The most ancient idolatry of the Arabs we must conclude to have been fetishism. Magianism, an importation from Chaldaea and Persia, must be reckoned among the religions of the pagan Arabs; but it never had very numerous followers. Christianity was introduced into southern Arabia toward the close of the second century, and about a century later it had made great progress. It flourished chiefly in the Yemen, where many churches were built. Judaism was propagated in Arabia, principally by Karaites, at the captivity. They are now nominally Mohammedans. Language .— Arabic the language of Arabia, is the most developed and the richest of Shemitic languages, and the only one of which we have an extensive literature; it is, therefore, of great importance to the study of Hebrew. Government .— Arabia is now under the government of the Ottoman empire.
entries.definition_ko:
('사막', '메마름'이라는 뜻) 구약에서 두 이름으로 알려진 나라이다. (1) '동방 땅'(창세기 25:6) 또는 '동방'(창세기 10:30; 민수기 23:7; 이사야 2:6)과 '동방 사람의 땅'(창세기 29:1)이며, 그 백성은 '동방 사람'이라 불린다(사사기 6:3; 7:12; 열왕기상 4:30; 욥기 1:3; 이사야 11:14; 예레미야 49:28; 에스겔 25:4). 이 대목들로 보아 동방 땅과 동방 사람은 본디 팔레스타인 동쪽 나라와 이스마엘과 그두라에게서 난 족속을 가리키며, 이 본래 뜻이 차츰 아라비아와 그 주민 전체로 넓어졌으되 엄밀한 한계는 없었던 것으로 보인다. (2) '아랍'이며 여기서 아라비아가 왔다(역대하 9:14; 이사야 21:13; 예레미야 25:24; 에스겔 27:21). 아라비아는 지중해와 홍해와 인도양과 바사 만 사이에 놓인 삼각형 반도이며, 남북 길이가 약 천삼백 마일이고 가장 넓은 데가 천오백 마일이다.
구분. 아라비아는 북쪽 사막의 경계까지 반도 전체를 아우르는 본래의 아라비아와, 아라비아 대사막을 이루는 북아라비아(아라비아 데세르타)와, 페트라 사막과 시내 반도 곧 아라비아 페트라이아라 불린 서아라비아로 나눌 수 있다.
I. 본래의 아라비아 곧 아라비아 반도는 북쪽으로 기울어지는 높은 대지로 이루어진다. 대부분에 사람이 살고 우물과 시내로 물을 얻으며 철따라 비가 온다. 물기 있고 기름진 지역은 남서쪽과 남쪽이다.
II. 북아라비아 곧 아라비아 사막은 높고 굽이지며 메마른 평원으로, 유브라데가 바사 만에서 수리아 국경까지 자연 경계를 이루고 거기서부터 북서쪽과 서쪽으로 수리아와 페트라 사막에 둘리며 남쪽 한계는 아라비아 반도이다. 오아시스가 적고 우물물은 대개 짜거나 마실 수 없으며 사무움이라는 모래바람이 분다. 주로 이스마엘과 그두라에게서 난 주민은 늘 떠돌며 목축하는 삶을 살았고, 바사 만 기슭에서 아라비아와 인도의 물품으로 상당한 교역을 하였다(에스겔 27:20-24).
III. 서아라비아는 시내 반도와 페트라 사막을 아우르며 대체로 아라비아 페트라이아의 한계와 맞는다. 뒤의 이름은 그 바위 같은 성질이 아니라 그 으뜸 성읍의 이름에서 온 것으로 보인다. 주로 에서의 자손이 살았고 두루 에돔 곧 이두매의 땅으로, 또 옛 이름인 세일 광야 곧 세일 산으로 알려졌다.
주민. 한때 인도에서 대서양까지 다스린 아라비아에는 이제 팔구백만이 살며 그 가운데 오분의 일쯤이 베두인 곧 떠도는 족속이고 나머지 오분의 사는 정착한 아랍 사람이다. (1) 욕단의 자손이 반도의 남쪽과 남서쪽의 주요 부분을 차지하고 내륙에도 이주지를 두었다. 으뜸 욕단 왕국이자 옛 아라비아의 으뜸 나라가 예멘이었다. (2) 이스마엘 자손은 북서쪽에서 반도로 들어온 듯하다. 남쪽 해안 한두 지역을 빼고 온 반도에 퍼졌으며 오늘날의 민족이 주로 이스마엘 계통이라고 아랍 사람들은 주장한다. (3) 그두라의 자손에 대하여 아랍 사람은 말하는 바가 적다. 그들은 주로 반도 북쪽 사막 아라비아에 팔레스타인에서 바사 만까지 정착한 듯하다. (4) 북아라비아와 서아라비아에는 지리적 자리와 생활 방식 때문에 때로 아랍 사람과 함께 묶이는 다른 백성이 있으니 아말렉과 에서의 자손 등이다.
산물. 산물은 여러 가지이다. 가장 이름난 짐승은 말이며 낙타와 양과 소와 나귀와 노새와 고양이가 흔하다. 농산물은 커피와 밀과 보리와 기장과 콩과 대추야자와 여느 밭작물이다. 목초지에서는 아라비아가 유난히 복되나 광물에서는 유난히 가난하여 납이 가장 많다.
종교. 아랍 사람의 가장 오래된 우상 숭배는 물신 숭배였다고 보아야 한다. 갈대아와 바사에서 들어온 마기교도 이교 아랍 사람의 종교에 넣어야 하나 따르는 이가 많았던 적은 없다. 그리스도교가 이세기 말 무렵 남아라비아에 들어와 한 세기쯤 뒤에 크게 진전하였고, 주로 예멘에서 번성하여 많은 교회가 세워졌다. 유대교는 포로 때 주로 카라이파를 통하여 아라비아에 퍼졌다. 지금은 이름뿐이나 이슬람교도이다.
말. 아라비아의 말인 아랍 말은 셈 계통 언어 가운데 가장 발달하고 풍부하며 방대한 문헌을 지닌 유일한 말이므로 히브리 말 연구에 매우 중요하다.
정치. 아라비아는 지금 오스만 제국의 다스림 아래 있다.

entries.definition: the nomadic tribes inhabiting the country to the east and south of Palestine, who in the early times of Hebrew history were known as Ishmaelites and descendants of Keturah.
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인 동쪽과 남쪽에 거주한 유목 민족으로 초기 히브리 역사에서는 이스마엘 후손, 그두라 후손으로 알려졌다.

entries.definition: a royal city of the Canaanites, named with Hormah and Libnah. (Joshua 12:14) The wilderness of Judah was to the south of Arad.” (Judges 1:16) It may be identified with a hill, Tel ’Arad, an hour and a half northeast by east from Milh (Moladah), and eight hours from Hebron. (a wild ass), a Benjamite, son of Beriah, who drove out the inhabitants of Gath. (1 Chronicles 8:15) (B.C. 536.)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 호르마, 립나와 함께 언급된 가나안 왕도(여호수아 12:14). (2) 브리아의 아들인 베냐민 사람으로 가드 주민을 쫓아냈다(역대상 8:15).

entries.definition: (wayfaring). • An Asherite, of the sons of Ulla. (1 Chronicles 7:39) • The sons of Arah returned with Zerubbabel in number 775 according to (Ezra 2:5) but 652 according to (Nehemiah 7:10) (B.C. 536.) One of his descendants, Shechaniah, was the father-in-law of Tobiah the Ammonite. (Nehemiah 6:18)
entries.definition_ko: '나그넷길'이라는 뜻. (1) 울라의 아들인 아셀 사람(역대상 7:39). (2) 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 자로 후손 스가냐는 암몬 사람 도비야의 장인이 되었다(에스라 2:5).

entries.definition: (high). • The name by which the Hebrews designated, generally, the country lying to the northeast of Palestine; the great mass of that high tableland which, rising with sudden abruptness from the Jordan and the very margin of the Lake of Gennesaret, stretched at an elevation of no less than 2000 feet above the level of the sea, to the banks of the Euphrates itself. Throughout the Authorized Version the word is, with only a very few exceptions, rendered, as in the Vulgate and LXX., Syria. Its earliest occurrence in the book of Genesis is in the form of Aram-naharaim, i.e. the “highland of or between the two rivers.” (Genesis 24:10) Authorized Version “Mesopotamia.” In the later history we meet with a number of small nations or kingdoms forming parts of the general land of Aram; but as Damascus increased in importance it gradually absorbed the smaller powers, (1 Kings 20:1) and the name of Aram was at last applied to it alone. (Isaiah 7:8) also 1Kin 11:24,25; 15:18etc. • Another Aram is named in (Genesis 22:21) as a son of Kemuel and descendant of Nahor. • An Asherite, one of the sons of Shamer. (1 Chronicles 7:34) • Son of Esrom or Hezron, and the Greek form of the Hebrew Ram. (Matthew 1:3,4; Luke 3:33)
entries.definition_ko: '높은'이라는 뜻. (1) 히브리인들이 팔레스타인 북동쪽 고원 지대를 가리키던 이름으로 대개 '수리아'로 번역된다. 다메섹가 강성해지며 이 이름이 결국 다메섹만을 가리키게 되었다. (2) 나홀의 후손 그무엘의 아들(창세기 22:21). (3) 아셀 사람 세멜의 아들(역대상 7:34). (4) 헤스론의 아들로 헬라어 형태이며 히브리어 람에 해당한다(마태복음 1:3).

entries.definition: a female inhabitant of Aram. (1 Chronicles 7:14)
entries.definition_ko: 아람 여인을 가리킨다(역대상 7:14).

entries.definition: (highlands of two rivers). (Psalms 60:1), title. [Aram]
entries.definition_ko: '두 강 사이의 고지대'라는 뜻으로 시편 60편 표제에 나온다. 아람(1) 참조.

entries.definition: Psal 60:1, title. [Aram, 1]
entries.definition_ko: 시편 60편 표제. 아람(1) 참조.

entries.definition: (wild goat), a Horite, son of Dishan and brother of Uz. Genesis 36:28; 1Chr 1:42
entries.definition_ko: '들염소'라는 뜻으로 호리 사람 디산의 아들이며 우스의 형제이다(창세기 36:28).

entries.definition: (ark), a Jebusite who sold his threshing floor on Mount Moriah to David as a site for an altar to Jehovah, together with his oxen. (2 Samuel 24:18-24; 1 Chronicles 21:25)
entries.definition_ko: '궤'라는 뜻으로 모리아산의 타작마당을 다윗에게 팔아 여호와께 드릴 제단 터로 쓰이게 한 여부스 사람이며 소도 함께 내주었다(사무엘하 24:18-24).

entries.definition: (city of the four), the progenitor of the Anakim, or sons of Anak, from whom their chief city, Hebron, received its name of Kirjath-Arba. (Joshua 14:15; 15:13; 21:11)
entries.definition_ko: '넷의 성읍'이라는 뜻으로 아낙 자손의 조상이며 그 중심 성읍 헤브론은 그의 이름을 따 기럇아르바라 불렸다(여호수아 14:15).

entries.definition: Hebron, or Kirjath-Arba, as “the city of Arbah” is always rendered elsewhere. (Genesis 35:27)
entries.definition_ko: 헤브론 또는 기럇아르바를 가리키며 다른 곳에서는 항상 '아르바 성읍'으로 번역된다(창세기 35:27).

entries.definition: a native of the Arabah or Ghor . [Arabah] Abi-albon the Arbathite was one of David’s mighty men. (2 Samuel 23:31; 1 Chronicles 11:32)
entries.definition_ko: 아라바(요단강 계곡) 출신을 가리키는 말로 다윗의 용사 아비알본이 이렇게 불렸다(사무엘하 23:31).

entries.definition: a native of Arab. Paarai the Arbite was one of David’s guard. (2 Samuel 23:35)
entries.definition_ko: 아랍 출신을 가리키는 말로 다윗의 근위병 바아래가 이렇게 불렸다(사무엘하 23:35).

entries.definition: A triumphal arch erected at Rome, and still remaining there, to commemorate the conquest of Judea and the destruction of Jerusalem by the emperor Titus. It was erected after his death, A.D. 91, by the senate and people of Rome. It was a magnificent structure, decorated with bas-reliefs and inscriptions, and is of especial interest because its historic bas-reliefs represent the captors carrying in triumph to Rome the golden candlestick and sacred utensils from the Jewish temple at Jerusalem. From these we obtain our best idea of their shape.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: 로마에 세워진 개선문으로 티투스 황제의 유대 정복과 예루살렘 파괴를 기념하며(주후 91년) 예루살렘 성전에서 약탈한 금촛대와 성물을 나르는 부조가 새겨져 있어 그 형태를 짐작하게 해준다.

entries.definition: (prince of the people), son of Herod the Great by a Samaritan woman, Malthake, and, with his brother Antipas brought up at Rome. At the death of Herod (B.C. 4) his kingdom was divided between his three sons, Herod Antipas, Archelaus and Philip. Archelaus never properly bore the title of king, (Matthew 2:22) but only that of ethnarch. In the tenth year of his reign, or the ninth according to Dion Cassius, i.e. A.D. 6, a complaint was preferred against him by his brothers and his subjects on the ground of his tyranny, in consequence of which he was banished to Vienne in Gaul, where he is generally said to have died.
entries.definition_ko: '백성의 통치자'라는 뜻으로 헤롯 대왕과 사마리아 여인 말타케 사이의 아들이며, 헤롯 사후 왕국을 분봉왕으로 나눠 받았으나(마태복음 2:22) 폭정으로 형제와 백성의 고발을 받아 갈리아의 비엔으로 추방되었다.

entries.definition: [Arms, Armor]
entries.definition_ko: 무기와 갑옷(ARMS, ARMOR) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: perhaps the inhabitants of Erech, some of whom had been placed as colonists in Samaria. (Ezra 4:9)
entries.definition_ko: 에렉 주민들로 사마리아에 이주해 정착한 것으로 추정된다(에스라 4:9).

entries.definition: (Joshua 16:2) A place in the neighborhood of Bethel, on the boundary between Ephraim and Benjamin. It designates a clan perhaps originally from Erech in Babylonia, of which Hushai was one. [Archite, The]
entries.definition_ko: 벧엘 근처, 에브라임과 베냐민 경계에 위치한 곳으로(여호수아 16:2) 바벨로니아 에렉 출신 씨족을 가리키며 후새가 이 씨족 출신이었다.

entries.definition: (master of the horse), a Christian teacher in Colossae, (Colossians 4:17) called by St. Paul his “fellow soldier,” Phil 2. He was probably a member of Philemon’s family. (A.D. 62.)
entries.definition_ko: '말들의 주인'이라는 뜻으로 골로새의 그리스도인 교사이며(골로새서 4:17) 바울이 '함께 병사 된 자'라 불렀다. 빌레몬 가족의 일원으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (as if from a place named Erech, on the frontiers of Ephraim), the usual designation of David’s friend Hushai. (2 Samuel 15:32; 17:5,14; 1 Chronicles 27:33)
entries.definition_ko: 에브라임 경계 에렉이라는 지명에서 유래한 것으로 추정되는 명칭으로 다윗의 친구 후새를 가리킨다(사무엘하 15:32).

entries.definition: The book of (Genesis 4:17,20,22) appears to divide mankind into two great characteristic sections, viz., the “dwellers in tents” and the “dwellers in cities.” To the race of Shem is attributed (Genesis 10:11,12,22; 11:2-9) the foundation of those cities in the plain of Shinar, Babylon Nineveh and others. The Israelites were by occupation shepherds, and by habit dwellers in tents. (Genesis 47:3) They had therefore originally, speaking properly, no architecture. From the time of the occupation of Canaan they became dwellers in towns and in houses of stone. (Leviticus 14:34,45; 1 Kings 7:10) The peaceful reign and vast wealth of Solomon gave great impulse to architecture; for besides the temple and his other great works, he built fortresses and cities in various places, among which Baalath and Tadmor are in all probability represented by Baalbec and Palmyra. But the reigns of Herod and his successors were especially remarkable for their great architectural works. Not only was the temple restored, but the fortifications and other public buildings of Jerusalem were enlarged and embellished. (Luke 21:5) The town of Caesarea was built on the site of Strato’s Tower; Samaria was enlarged, and received the name of Sebaste. Of the original splendor of these great works no doubt can be entertained; but of their style and appearance we can only conjecture that they were formed on Greek and Roman models. The enormous stones employed the Assyrian Persepolitan and Egyptian buildings find a parallel in the substructions of Baalbec and in the huge blocks which still remain at Jerusalem, relics of the buildings either of Solomon or of Herod.
entries.definition_ko: 창세기는 인류를 '장막에 거하는 자'와 '성읍에 거하는 자'로 나누며, 셈족이 시날 평지에 바벨론과 니느웨 등의 도시를 세운 것으로 기록한다. 이스라엘은 본래 목축민으로 장막 생활을 했으나 가나안 정착 이후 성읍과 석조 가옥에 거하게 되었고, 솔로몬 시대에 건축이 크게 융성했으며 헤롯 시대에도 성전과 여러 건축물이 확장되었다.

entries.definition: (bear-keeper). The Hebrew words ’Ash and ’Aish, rendered “Arcturus” in the Authorized Version of (Job 9:9; 38:32) in conformity with the Vulgate of the former passages are now generally believed to be identical, and to represent the constellation Ursa Major, known commonly as the Great Bear or Charles’ Wain.
entries.definition_ko: '곰지기'라는 뜻으로 욥기 9:9, 38:32의 히브리어 '아쉬'를 흠정역이 불가타를 따라 이렇게 번역했으며, 오늘날에는 큰곰자리를 가리키는 것으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: (one that descending), the son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin. (Genesis 46:21; Numbers 26:40) In (1 Chronicles 8:3) he is called Addar.
entries.definition_ko: '내려오는 자'라는 뜻으로 벨라의 아들이자 베냐민의 손자이며(창세기 46:21) 역대상 8:3에서는 앗달이라 불린다.

entries.definition: the descendants of Ard or Addar, the grandson of Benjamin. (Numbers 26:40)
entries.definition_ko: 아릇(또는 앗달)의 후손들을 가리킨다(민수기 26:40).

entries.definition: (fugitive) a Son of Caleb, the son of Hezron, by his wife Azubah. (1 Chronicles 2:18)
entries.definition_ko: '도망자'라는 뜻으로 헤스론의 아들 갈렙이 아내 아수바를 통해 낳은 아들이다(역대상 2:18).

entries.definition: (heroic), a son of Gad. (Genesis 46:16; Numbers 26:17) His descendants are called Arelites. Numb 26:17.
entries.definition_ko: '영웅적인'이라는 뜻으로 갓의 아들이다(창세기 46:16). 그 후손은 아렐 자손이라 불린다.

entries.definition: a member of the court of Areopagus. (Acts 17:31) [Mars Hill’ HILL]
entries.definition_ko: 아레오바고 법정의 회원을 가리킨다(사도행전 17:31). 아레오바고(MARS HILL) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Mars Hill’ HILL]
entries.definition_ko: 마르스 언덕(MARS HILL) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (graver). • A contemporary of Antiochus Epiphanes, B.C. 170, and Jason. 2 Macc. 5:8. • The Aretas alluded to by St. Paul (2 Corinthians 11:32) was father-in-law of Herod Antipas.
entries.definition_ko: '조각하는 자'라는 뜻. (1) 안티오코스 에피파네스 시대의 인물(마카베오후서 5:8). (2) 바울이 언급한 아레다는 헤롯 안디바의 장인이었다(고린도후서 11:32).

entries.definition: perhaps a Gileadite officer who was governor of Argob. He was either an accomplice of Pekah in the murder of Pekahiah or was slain by Pekah. (2 Kings 15:25) (stony), a tract of country on the east of the Jordan, in Bashan, the kingdom of Og, containing 60 great and fortified cities. In later times it was called Trachonitis, and it is now apparently identified with the Leiah, a very remarkable district south of Damascus and east of the Sea of Galilee. (3:4,13,14)
entries.definition_ko: '돌이 많은'이라는 뜻. (1) 길르앗 사람 관리로 아르곱의 총독이었으며 베가의 반역에 연루되거나 그에게 죽임을 당한 것으로 추정된다(열왕기하 15:25). (2) 요단강 동쪽 바산 땅, 옥 왕국에 속한 지역으로 견고한 성읍 60개를 포함했으며 후대에는 트라코니티스라 불렸다.

entries.definition: (the strong), ninth son of Haman. (Esther 9:9)
entries.definition_ko: '강한 자'라는 뜻으로 하만의 아홉째 아들이다(에스더 9:9).

entries.definition: sixth son of Haman. (Esther 9:8)
entries.definition_ko: 하만의 여섯째 아들이다(에스더 9:8).

entries.definition: (lion). Either one of the accomplices of Pekah in his conspiracy against Pekahiah, or one of the princes of Pekahiah who was put to death with him. (2 Kings 15:20) (B.C. 757.)
entries.definition_ko: '사자'라는 뜻으로 베가가 브가히야를 암살할 때의 공모자 또는 브가히야와 함께 죽임당한 방백 중 하나로 추정된다(열왕기하 15:25).

entries.definition: (lion of God). • One of the “chief men” who under Ezra directed the caravan which he led back from Babylon to Jerusalem. (Ezra 8:16) (B.C. 459.) The word occurs also in reference to two Moabites slain by Benaiah. (2 Samuel 23:20; 1 Chronicles 11:22) Many regard the word as an epithet, “lion-like;” but it seems better to look upon it as a proper name, and translate “two [sons] of Ariel.” • A designation given by Isaiah to the city of Jerusalem. (Isaiah 29:1,2,7) We must understand by it either “lion of God,” as the chief city, or “hearth of God,” a synonym for the altar of burnt offering. On the whole it seems most probable that, as a name given to Jerusalem, Ariel means “lion of God,” whilst the word used by Ezekiel, (Ezekiel 43:15,16) means “hearth of God.”
entries.definition_ko: (1) 에스라가 이끈 바벨론 귀환 무리의 지도자 중 하나(에스라 8:16). (2) 이사야가 예루살렘을 가리켜 쓴 이름으로 '하나님의 사자' 또는 '하나님의 화로'를 뜻한다(이사야 29:1,2,7).

entries.definition: (heights). (Matthew 27:57; Luke 23:51; John 19:38) St. Luke calls it “a city of Judea.” It is identified by many with the modern Ramleh .
entries.definition_ko: '높은 곳들'이라는 뜻으로(마태복음 27:57) 누가는 이를 '유대의 한 성읍'이라 부르며 오늘날의 람레와 동일시된다.

entries.definition: (venerable). • The king of Eliasar, one of the allies of Chedorlaomer in his expedition against his rebellious tributaries. (Genesis 14:1) (B.C. 1921-1912.) • The captain of Nebuchadnezzar’s body-guard. (Daniel 2:14) etc. • Properly Eirioch, or Erioch, mentioned in Judith 1:6as king of the Elymaeans.
entries.definition_ko: '존귀한'이라는 뜻. (1) 엘라살 왕으로 그돌라오멜의 동맹 중 하나(창세기 14:1). (2) 느부갓네살의 근위대장(다니엘 2:14). (3) 유딧서에서 엘람 왕으로 언급되는 인물.

entries.definition: (lion-like), eighth son of Haman. (Esther 9:9)
entries.definition_ko: '사자 같은'이라는 뜻으로 하만의 여덟째 아들이다(에스더 9:9).

entries.definition: (the best ruler), a Thessalonian, (Acts 20:4; 27:2) who accompanied St. Paul on his third missionary journey. (Acts 19:29) He was with the apostle on his return to Asia, (Acts 20:4) and again, Acts 27:2On his voyage to Rome. We trace him afterwards as St. Paul’s fellow prisoner in (Colossians 4:10) and Phle 1:24 Tradition makes him bishop of Apamea.
entries.definition_ko: '가장 뛰어난 통치자'라는 뜻으로 데살로니가 사람이며(사도행전 20:4) 바울의 3차 선교여행에 동행했다. 로마로 가는 항해에도 함께했으며 골로새서 4:10에서는 바울과 함께 갇힌 자로 언급된다.

entries.definition: (the best counsellor), a resident at Rome, some of whose household are greeted in (Romans 16:10) Tradition makes him one of the 70 disciples and reports that he preached the gospel in Britain.
entries.definition_ko: '가장 뛰어난 조언자'라는 뜻으로 로마에 거주한 인물이며 그 집안 사람들이 로마서 16:10에서 문안 인사를 받는다.

entries.definition: A small boat or basket made of the papyrus, a reed which grows in the marshes of Egypt. It was covered with bitumen to make it water tight.
entries.definition_ko: 애굽 습지에서 자라는 파피루스 갈대로 만든 작은 배 또는 바구니로 방수를 위해 역청을 발랐다.

entries.definition: The first piece of the tabernacle’s furniture, for which precise directions were delivered. Exod 25. I. Description.— It appears to have been an oblong chest of shittim (acacia) wood, 2 1/2 cubits long by 1 1/2 broad and deep. Within and without gold was overlaid on the wood, and on the upper side or lid, which was edged round about with gold, the mercy-seat was placed. The ark was fitted with rings, one at each of the four corners, and through these were passed staves of the same wood similarly overlaid, by which it was carried by the Kohathites. (Numbers 7:9; 10:21) The ends of the staves were visible without the veil in the holy place of the temple of Solomon. (1 Kings 8:8) The ark, when transported, was enveloped in the “veil” of the dismantled tabernacle, in the curtain of badgers’ skins and in a blue cloth over all, and was therefore not seen. (Numbers 4:5,20) II. Its purpose was to contain inviolate the divine autograph of the two tables, that “covenant” from which it derived its title. It was also probably a reliquary for the pot of manna and the rod of Aaron. III. History .—Before David’s time its abode was frequently shifted. It sojourned among several, probably Levitical, families, (1 Samuel 7:1; 2 Samuel 6:3,11; 1 Chronicles 13:13; 15:24,25) in the border villages of eastern Judah; and did not take its place in the tabernacle, but dwelt in curtains, i.e. in a separate tent pitched for it in Jerusalem by David. Subsequently the temple, when completed, received, in the installation of the ark in its shrine, the signal of its inauguration by the effulgence of divine glory instantly manifested. It was probably taken captive or destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, 2 Esdr. 10:22, so that there was no ark in the second temple.
entries.definition_ko: 성막 기구 중 가장 먼저 상세한 지시가 내려진 것으로(출애굽기 25장) 아카시아 나무로 만든 직사각형 궤이며 안팎을 금으로 입히고 뚜껑에 속죄소를 두었다. 두 돌판을 보관하는 용도였으며 만나 항아리와 아론의 지팡이도 함께 보관된 것으로 추정된다. 다윗 시대까지 여러 곳을 전전하다 예루살렘에 안치되었고, 성전 완공 후 지성소에 자리 잡았으며 이후 느부갓네살에 의해 사라진 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: [Noah]
entries.definition_ko: 노아(NOAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: from Arka, one of the families of the Canaanites, (Genesis 10:17; 1 Chronicles 1:16) and from the context evidently located in the north of Phoenicia. The site which now bears the name of ’Arka lies on the coast, 2 to 2 1/2 hours from the shore, about 12 miles north of Tripoli and 5 south of the Nahr el-Kebir .
entries.definition_ko: 가나안 족속 중 하나로 아르가에서 유래했으며(창세기 10:17) 페니키아 북부에 위치한다.

entries.definition: (the hill or city of Megiddo). (Revelation 16:16) The scene of the struggle of good and evil is suggested by that battle-field, the plain of Esdraelon, which was famous for two great victories, of Barak over the Canaanites and of Gideon over the Midianites; and for two great disasters, the deaths of Saul and Josiah. Hence it signifies in Revelation a place of great slaughter, the scene of a terrible retribution upon the wicked. The Revised Version gives the name as Har-Magedon, i.e. the hill (as Ar is the city) of Megiddo .—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: '므깃도의 언덕 또는 성읍'이라는 뜻으로(계시록 16:16) 바락이 가나안을 이긴 곳이자 기드온이 미디안을 이긴 곳, 또한 사울과 요시야가 전사한 곳인 에스드라엘론 평지를 배경으로 하며, 계시록에서는 악인들에 대한 큰 심판의 장소를 상징한다.

entries.definition: (land of Aram) is nowhere mentioned under that name in the original Hebrew, though it occurs in the English version, (2 Kings 19:37) for Ararat. Description.—Armenia is that lofty plateau whence the rivers Euphrates, Tigris, Araxes and Acampsis pour down their waters in different directions; the first two to the Persian Gulf, the last two respectively to the Caspian and Euxine seas. It may be termed the nucleus of the mountain system of western Asia. From the centre of the plateau rise two lofty chains of mountains, which run from east to west. Divisions.—Three districts are mentioned in the Bible. (1) ARARAT is mentioned as the place whither the sons of Sennacherib fled. (Isaiah 37:38) It was the central district, surrounding the mountain of that name. (2) Minnionly occurs in (Jeremiah 51:27) It is probably identical with the district Minyas, in the upper valley of the Murad-su branch of the Euphrates. (3) Togarmahis noticed in two passages of (Ezekiel 27:14; 38:6) both of which are in favor of its identity with Armenia. Present condition.—The Armenians, numbering about two millions, are nominally Christians. About half of them live in Armenia. Their favorite pursuit is commerce. The country is divided, as to government, between Russia, Turkey and Persia.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: '아람 땅'이라는 뜻으로 히브리어 원문에는 이 이름이 나오지 않으나 영어 역본에서 아라랏을 대신해 쓰인다(열왕기하 19:37). 유브라데강, 티헬라강, 아락세스강, 아캄프시스강이 발원하는 고원 지대이다.

entries.definition: an ornament universal in the East, especially among women; used by princes as one of the insignia of royalty, and by distinguished persons in general. The word is not used in the Authorized Version, as even in (2 Samuel 1:10) it is rendered by “the bracelet on his arm.”
entries.definition_ko: 동방에서 흔히 쓰인 장신구로 특히 여성들 사이에서, 또한 왕권의 표지로 왕들에게 쓰였다. 흠정역에는 이 단어가 직접 쓰이지 않고 '팔찌'로 번역된다(사무엘하 1:10).

entries.definition: son of Saul by Rizpah. (2 Samuel 21:8)
entries.definition_ko: 사울과 리스바 사이의 아들이다(사무엘하 21:8).

entries.definition: The subject naturally divides itself into— I. Offensive weapons: Arms. II. Defensive weapons: Armor. I. Offensive weapons.— • Apparently the earliest known and most widely used was the Chereb or Sword. Very little can be gathered as to its shape, size, material or mode of use. Perhaps if anything is to be inferred it is that the Chereb is both a lighter and a shorter weapon than the modern sword. It was carried in a sheath, (1 Samuel 17:51; 2 Samuel 20:8; 1 Chronicles 21:27) slung by a girdle, (1 Samuel 25:13) and resting upon the thigh, (Psalms 45:3; Judges 3:16) or upon the hips. (2 Samuel 20:8) • Next we have the Spear; and of this weapon we meet with at least three distinct kinds. A. The Chanith, a “spear,” and that of the largest kind. It was the weapon of Goliath, (1 Samuel 17:7,45; 2 Samuel 21:19; 1 Chronicles 20:5) and also of other giants, (2 Samuel 23:21; 1 Chronicles 11:23) and mighty warriors. (2 Samuel 2:23; 23:18; 1 Chronicles 11:11,20) b. Apparently lighter than the preceding was the Cidon or “javelin.” When not in action the Cidon was carried on the back of the warrior, (1 Samuel 17:6) Authorized Version “target.” c. Another kind of spear was the Romach . In the historical books it occurs in (Numbers 25:7) and 1Kin 18:28And frequently in the later books, as in (1 Chronicles 12:8) (“buckler”); (2 Chronicles 11:12) (It varied much in length, weight and size.) d. The Shelach was probably a lighter missile or “dart.” see (2 Chronicles 23:10; 32:5) (“darts”); (Nehemiah 4:17,23) (see margin); (Job 33:18; 36:12; Joel 2:8) e. Shebet, a rod or staff, is used once only to denote a weapon. (2 Samuel 18:14) • Of missile weapons of offence the chief was undoubtedly the Bow, Kesheth . The Arrowswere carried in a quiver. (Genesis 27:3; Isaiah 22:6; 49:2; Psalms 127:5) From an allusion in Job 6:4they would seem to have been some times poisoned; and (Psalms 120:4) may point to a practice of using arrows with some burning material attached to them. • The Slingis first mentioned in (Judges 20:16) This simple weapon, with which David killed the giant Philistine, was the natural attendant of a shepherd. Later in the monarchy, slingers formed part of the regular army. (2 Kings 3:25) • The BATTLE AXE, (Jeremiah 51:20) a powerful weapon of whose exact form we have no knowledge. II. Armor.— • The Breastplate, enumerated in the description of the arms of Goliath, a “coat of mail,” literally a “breastplate of scales.” (1 Samuel 17:5) This word has furnished one of the names of Mount Hermon. See (3:9) • The Habergeonis mentioned but twice—in reference to the gown of the high priest. (Exodus 28:32; 39:28) It was probably a quilted shirt or doublet. • The Helmetis referred to in (1 Samuel 17:5; 2 Chronicles 26:14; Ezekiel 27:10) • (Greaves) or defences for the feet, made of brass, are named in (1 Samuel 17:6) only. • Two kinds of Shieldare distinguishable. A. The large shield; encompassing, (Psalms 6:12) the whole person. When not in actual conflict it was carried before the warrior. (1 Samuel 17:7,41) b. Of smaller dimensions was the buckler or target, probably for use in hand-to-hand fight. (1 Kings 10:16; 2 Chronicles 9:15,16)
entries.definition_ko: 공격무기(칼, 창, 활과 화살, 물매, 전투용 도끼)와 방어무기(흉갑, 투구, 정강이받이, 방패)로 나뉜다. 칼(헤렙)은 칼집에 넣어 허리띠에 찼고, 창은 하닛(가장 큰 창), 기돈(가벼운 투창), 로마크, 셀라크 등 여러 종류가 있었다. 물매는 다윗이 골리앗을 죽인 무기로 목자들이 흔히 사용했다.

entries.definition: I. JewishARMY.—Every man above 20 years of age was a soldier, (Numbers 1:3) each tribe formed a regiment, with its own banner and its own leader (Numbers 2:2; 10:14) their positions in the camp or on the march were accurately fixed, Numb. 2; the whole army started and stopped at a given signal, (Numbers 10:5,6) thus they came up out of Egypt ready for the fight. (Exodus 13:18) On the approach of an enemy a conscription was made from the general body, under the direction of a muster-master, (20:5; 2 Kings 25:19) by whom also the officers were appointed. (20:9) The army had 31:14) and still further into families. (Numbers 2:34; 2 Chronicles 25:5; 26:12) With the king arose the custom of maintaining a body-guard, which formed the nucleus of a standing army, and David’s band of 600, (1 Samuel 23:13; 25:13) he retained after he became king, and added the Cherethitesand Pelethites. (2 Samuel 15:18; 20:7) David further organized a national militia, divided into twelve regiments under their respective officers, each of which was called out for one month in the year. (1 Chronicles 27:1) ... It does not appear that the system established by David was maintained by the kings of Judah; but in Israel the proximity of the hostile kingdom of Syria necessitated the maintenance of a standing army. The maintenance and equipment of the soldiers at the public expense dated from the establishment of a standing army. It is doubtful whether the soldier ever received pay even under the kings. II. Roman Empire ARMY.—The Roman army was divided into legions, the number of which varied considerably (from 3000 to 6000), each under six tribuni (“chief captains,”) (Acts 21:31) who commanded by turns. The legion was subdivided into ten cohorts (“band,”) (Acts 10:1) the cohort into three maniples, and the maniple into two centuries, containing originally 100 men, as the name implies, but subsequently from 50 to 100 men, according to the strength of the legion. There were thus 60 centuries in a legion, each under the command of a centurion. (Acts 10:1,22; Matthew 8:5; 27:54) In addition to the legionary cohorts, independent cohorts of volunteers served under the Roman standards. One of these cohorts was named the Italian, (Acts 10:1) as consisting of volunteers from Italy. The headquarters of the Roman forces in Judea were at Caesarea.
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘에서는 20세 이상 남자가 모두 군인이었으며 지파별로 편성되었다(민수기 1:3). 다윗은 600명 정예부대와 그렛 및 블렛 사람으로 근위대를 조직했고, 12개 연대로 나뉜 국가 민병대를 두었다(역대상 27:1). 로마 군대는 군단(레기온)으로 나뉘었고, 각 군단은 6명의 천부장이 지휘하는 10개 보병대(코호트)로, 다시 백부장이 지휘하는 백인대로 세분되었다(사도행전 10:1).

entries.definition: In the received Hebrew text “the sons of Arnan” are mentioned in the genealogy of Zerubbabel. (1 Chronicles 3:21)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 본문에는 '아르난의 아들들'이 스룹바벨의 족보에 언급된다(역대상 3:21).

entries.definition: (Used in the Revised Version for Aram in (Luke 3:33) and is probably another name or form of the name of Aram. [Aram, 4])
entries.definition_ko: 누가복음 3:33의 아람과 같은 이름의 다른 형태로 개정역에서 사용된다.

entries.definition: (roaring), the river or torrent which formed the boundary between Moab and the Amorites, on the north of Moab, (Numbers 21:13,14,24,26; Judges 11:22) and afterwards between Moab and Israel (Reuben). (2:24,36; 3:8,12,16; 4:48; Joshua 12:1,2; 13:9,16; Judges 11:13,26) There can be no doubt that the Wady el-Mojeb of the present day is the Arnon. Its principal source is near Katrane, on the Haj route.
entries.definition_ko: '울부짖는'이라는 뜻으로 모압과 아모리의 경계를 이룬 강이며(민수기 21:13) 이후 모압과 이스라엘(르우벤)의 경계가 되었다. 오늘날의 와디 엘모제브로 확인된다.

entries.definition: (a wild ass), a son of Gad, (Numbers 26:17) called Arodiin (Genesis 46:16)
entries.definition_ko: '들나귀'라는 뜻으로 갓의 아들이며(민수기 26:17) 창세기 46:16에서는 아로디라 불린다.

entries.definition: [Arod]
entries.definition_ko: 아롯(AROD) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Arod]
entries.definition_ko: 아롯(AROD) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (ruins). • A city on the torrent Arnon, the southern point of the territory of Sihon king of the Amorites and afterwards of the tribe of Reuben, (2:36; 3:12; 4:48; Joshua 12:2; 13:9,16; Judges 11:26; 2 Kings 10:33; 1 Chronicles 5:8) but later again in possession of Moab. (Jeremiah 48:19) It is the modern Ara’ir, upon the very edge of the precipitous north bank of the Wady Mojeb . • Aroer, “that is ’facing’ Rahbah” (Rabbah of Ammon), a town built by and belonging to Gad. (Numbers 32:34; Joshua 13:25; 2 Samuel 24:5) This is probably the place mentioned in (Judges 11:33) which was shown in Jerome’s time. • Aroer, in (Isaiah 17:2) if a place at all, must be still farther north than either of the two already named. • A town in Judah, named only in (1 Samuel 30:28) perhaps Wady Ar’arah, on the road from Petra to Gaza.
entries.definition_ko: '폐허'라는 뜻. (1) 아르논 강가의 성읍으로 아모리 왕 시혼 영토의 남쪽 끝이었다가 르우벤 지파에 속했으나 후에 다시 모압의 소유가 되었다(예레미야 48:19). (2) 랍바(암몬의 랍바) 맞은편의 갓 지파 성읍(민수기 32:34). (3) 이사야 17:2의 아로엘은 이보다 더 북쪽으로 추정된다. (4) 유다의 한 성읍(사무엘상 30:28).

entries.definition: Hothan the Aroerite was the father of two of David’s captains. (1 Chronicles 11:44)
entries.definition_ko: 아로엘 사람 호단은 다윗의 두 장수의 아버지였다(역대상 11:44).

entries.definition: (strong city), (Isaiah 36:19; 37:13) a city or district in Syria, apparently dependent on Damascus. (Jeremiah 49:23) No trace of its existence has yet been discovered. (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13; Isaiah 10:9)
entries.definition_ko: '견고한 성읍'이라는 뜻으로(이사야 36:19) 다메섹에 종속된 것으로 보이는 수리아의 도시 또는 지역이다(예레미야 49:23). 아직 그 흔적이 발견되지 않았다.

entries.definition: (stronghold of the Chaldees). • The son of Shem and ancestor of Eber. (Genesis 10:22,24; 11:10) • Arphaxad, a king “who reigned over the Medes in Ecbatana,” Judith 1:1-4; perhaps the same as Phraortes, who fell in a battle with the Assyrians, 633 B.C.
entries.definition_ko: '갈대아의 요새'라는 뜻. (1) 셈의 아들이자 에벨의 조상(창세기 10:22). (2) '메대를 다스린' 왕으로 유딧서에 언급되며, 주전 633년 앗수르와의 전투에서 전사한 프라오르테스와 동일 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Arms, Armor]
entries.definition_ko: 무기와 갑옷(ARMS, ARMOR) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (the great warrior). • The first Artaxerxes is mentioned in (Ezra 4:7) and appears identical with Smerdis, the Magian impostor and pretended brother of Cambyses, who usurped the throne B.C. 522, and reigned eight months. • In (Nehemiah 2:1) we have another Artaxerxes. We may safely identify him with Artaxerxes Macrocheir or Longimanus, the son of Xerxces, who reigned B.C. 464425.
entries.definition_ko: '위대한 전사'라는 뜻. (1) 에스라 4:7에 언급된 첫 아닥사스다로 캄비세스의 동생을 사칭한 마고스 사람 스메르디스와 동일 인물로 추정되며 주전 522년 왕위를 찬탈해 8개월간 통치했다. (2) 느헤미야 2:1의 아닥사스다는 크세르크세스의 아들 아르타크세르크세스 롱기마누스(장수왕)와 동일 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (gift of Artemis), a companion of St. Paul. (Titus 3:12) According to tradition he was bishop of Lystra.
entries.definition_ko: '아데미의 선물'이라는 뜻으로 바울의 동역자이며(디도서 3:12) 전승에 따르면 루스드라의 감독이 되었다.

entries.definition: (windows), the third of Solomons commissariat districts. (1 Kings 4:10) It included Sochoh, and was therefore probably a name for the rich corn-growing lowland country.
entries.definition_ko: '창들'이라는 뜻으로 솔로몬의 세 번째 물자 공급 지역이며(열왕기상 4:10) 소고를 포함해 비옥한 저지대 곡창지대를 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (height), a place apparently in the neighborhood of Shechem, at which Abimelech resided. (Judges 9:41)
entries.definition_ko: '높음'이라는 뜻으로 세겜 근처의 한 장소이며 아비멜렉이 거주한 곳이다(사사기 9:41).

entries.definition: (wandering) (Ezekiel 27:8,11) The island of Ruad, which lies off Tortosa (Tartus), two or three miles from the Phoenician coast. In agreement with this is the mention of “the Arvadite, in (Genesis 10:18) and 1Chr 1:16As a son of Canaan, with Zidon, Hamath an other northern localities.
entries.definition_ko: '방황'이라는 뜻으로(에스겔 27:8) 페니키아 해안에서 2~3마일 떨어진 루아드 섬이다. 가나안의 아들로 시돈, 하맛 등과 함께 언급되는 '아르왓 사람'과 관련된다(창세기 10:18).

entries.definition: [Arvad]
entries.definition_ko: 아르왓(ARVAD) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: prefect of the palace at Tirzah to Elah king of Israel, who was assassinated at a banquet in his house by Zimri. (1 Kings 16:9)
entries.definition_ko: 디르사 궁의 시종장으로 이스라엘 왕 엘라가 그의 집에서 잔치하다가 시므리에게 암살당했다(열왕기상 16:9).

entries.definition: (physician, or cure). • Son of Abijah and third king of Judah. (B.C. 956-916.) (His long reign of 41 years was peaceful in its earlier portion, and he undertook the reformation of all abuses, especially of idolatry. He burnt the symbol of his grandmother Maachah’s religion and deposed her from the dignity of “king’s mother,”) and renewed the great altar which the idolatrous priests apparently had desecrated. (2 Chronicles 15:8) Besides this he fortified cities on his frontiers, and raised an army, amounting, according to (2 Chronicles 14:8) to 580,000 men, a number probably exaggerated by an error of the copyist. During Asa’s reign, Zerah, at the head of an enormous host, (2 Chronicles 14:9) attacked Mareshah. There he was utterly defeated, and driven back with immense loss to Gerar. The peace which followed this victory was broken by the attempt of Baasha of Israel to fortify Ramah. To stop this Asa purchased the help of Benhadad I. king of Damascus, by a large payment of treasure, forced Baasha to abandon his purpose, and destroyed the works which he had begun at Ramah. In his old age Asa suffered from gout, He died, greatly loved and honored, in the 41st year of his reign. • Ancestor of Berechiah a Levite who resided in one of the villages of the Netophathites after the return from Babylon. (1 Chronicles 9:16)
entries.definition_ko: '의사, 치유'라는 뜻. (1) 아비야의 아들이자 유다의 셋째 왕으로(주전 956-916년) 41년의 긴 통치 동안 초반에는 평화로웠고 우상숭배 개혁을 단행했으며, 조모 마아가의 우상을 불태우고 그녀를 '왕의 어머니' 지위에서 폐위시켰다. 에디오피아 왕 세라의 대군을 마레사에서 크게 물리쳤으나(역대하 14:9), 말년에는 이스라엘 왕 바아사에 맞서 다메섹 왕 벤하닷에게 재물을 주고 도움을 구했다. 노년에 발에 병이 들어 재위 41년에 죽었다. (2) 포로 후 느도바 마을에 거주한 레위인 브레갸의 조상(역대상 9:16).

entries.definition: (made by God). • Nephew of David, being the youngest son of his sister Zeruiah. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting under his brother Joab at Gibeon, he pursued Abner, who was obliged to kill him in self-defence. (2 Samuel 2:18) ff. [Abner] (B.C. 1050.) • One of the Levites in the reign of Jehoshaphat, who went throughout the cities of Judah to instruct the people in the knowledge of the law. (2 Chronicles 17:8) (B.C. 910.) • A Levite in the reign of Hezekiah, who had charge of the tithes and dedicated things in the temple. (2 Chronicles 31:13) (B.C. 927.) • A priest, father of Jonathan, in the time of Ezra. (Ezra 10:15) He is called AZAEL in 1Esd 9:14. (B.C. before 459.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 지으신'이라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 조카로 누이 스루야의 막내아들이며 발이 빠르기로 유명했다. 기브온 전투에서 아브넬을 추격하다가 자기방어로 나선 아브넬에게 죽임을 당했다(사무엘하 2:18). (2) 여호사밧 시대 유다 성읍들을 다니며 율법을 가르친 레위인(역대하 17:8). (3) 히스기야 시대 십일조와 성전 헌물을 관리한 레위인(역대하 31:13). (4) 에스라 시대 제사장 요나단의 아버지(에스라 10:15).

entries.definition: (the Lord hath made), a servant of King Josiah, sent by him to seek information of Jehovah respecting the book of the law which Hilkiah found in the temple, (2 Kings 22:12,14) also called Asaiah. (2 Chronicles 34:20) (B.C. 641.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지으셨다'는 뜻으로 요시야 왕의 신하이며 힐기야가 성전에서 발견한 율법책에 대해 여호와께 묻도록 파송되었고(열왕기하 22:12) 역대하 34:20에서는 아사야라 불린다.

entries.definition: (the Lord hath made). • A prince of one of the families of the Simeonites in the reign of Hezekiah. (1 Chronicles 4:36) (B.C. 910.) • A Levite in the reign of David, chief of the family of Merari. (1 Chronicles 6:30) With 120 of his brethren he took part in bringing the ark from the house of Obededom to the city of David. (1 Chronicles 15:6,11) • The first-born of “the Shilonite,” from Shiloni, (1 Chronicles 9:5) who with his family dwelt in Jerusalem after the return from Babylon. (B.C. 536.) In (Nehemiah 11:5) he is called Maaseiah. • (2 Chronicles 34:20) [Asahiah]
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지으셨다'는 뜻. (1) 히스기야 시대 시므온 지파 방백(역대상 4:36). (2) 다윗 시대 므라리 가문 레위인의 우두머리로 언약궤를 옮기는 일에 참여했다(역대상 15:6). (3) '실로니 사람'의 맏아들로 포로 후 예루살렘에 거주했으며 느헤미야 11:5에서는 마아세야라 불린다. (4) 아사히야와 동일 인물.

entries.definition: (collector of the people). • A Levite, son of Berechiah, one of the leaders of David’s choir. (1 Chronicles 6:39) Psalms 50and 73-83 are attributed to him; and he was in after times celebrated as a seer as well as a musical composer. (2 Chronicles 29:30; Nehemiah 12:46) (B.C. 1050.) • The father or ancestor of Joah, the chronicler to the kingdom of Judah in the reign of Hezekiah, (2 Kings 18:18,37; Isaiah 36:3,22) probably the same as the preceding. • The keeper of the royal forest or “paradise” of Artaxerxes, (Nehemiah 2:8) a Jew, in high office at the court of Persia. (B.C. 536.) • Ancestor of Mattaniah, the conductor of the temple-choir after the return from Babylon. (1 Chronicles 9:16; Nehemiah 11:17) Most probably the same as 1 and 2.
entries.definition_ko: '백성을 모으는 자'라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 찬양대 지도자 중 하나로 브레갸의 아들 레위인이며(역대상 6:39) 시편 50편과 73-83편이 그의 이름으로 전해진다. (2) 히스기야 시대 유다 왕국 사관 요아의 아버지 또는 조상(열왕기하 18:18). (3) 아닥사스다의 왕실 삼림 관리인으로 바사 궁정의 고위직 유대인(느헤미야 2:8). (4) 포로 후 성전 찬양대 지휘자 맛다냐의 조상(역대상 9:16).

entries.definition: (A school of poetry and musical composers founded by Asaph.)
entries.definition_ko: 아삽이 세운 시가와 음악 작곡의 학파를 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (whom God hath bound (by an oath)), a son of Jehaleleel, in the genealogies of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:16)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 맹세로 매신 자'라는 뜻으로 유다 족보에서 여할렐렐의 아들이다(역대상 4:16).

entries.definition: (upright toward God), one of the sons of Asaph, a musician, (1 Chronicles 25:2) called Jesharelahin ver. 14
entries.definition_ko: '하나님을 향해 올곧은'이라는 뜻으로 음악가 아삽의 아들 중 하나이며(역대상 25:2) 14절에서는 여사렐라라 불린다.

entries.definition: [Ashkelon, Askelon]
entries.definition_ko: 아스글론(ASHKELON) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (worshipper of Neith), daughter of Potipherah, priest, or possibly prince, of On [Potipherah, Or Potipherah], wife of Joseph, (Genesis 41:45) and mother of Manasseh and Ephraim. (Genesis 41:50; 46:20) (B.C. 1715.)
entries.definition_ko: '네이트 여신의 숭배자'라는 뜻으로 온의 제사장(혹은 통치자) 보디베라의 딸이며 요셉의 아내이자 므낫세와 에브라임의 어머니이다(창세기 41:45).

entries.definition: (Luke 2:36; Revelation 7:6) [Asher, Asher]
entries.definition_ko: 아셀(ASHER) 항목 참조(누가복음 2:36; 계시록 7:6).

entries.definition: (Heb. oren), only in (Isaiah 44:14) As the true ash is not a native of Palestine, some understand this to be a species of pine tree. Perhaps the larch (Laryx europaea) may be intended.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '오렌'으로(이사야 44:14) 팔레스타인에 참 물푸레나무가 자생하지 않아 소나무나 낙엽송의 일종으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (smoke), a city in the low country of Judah. (Joshua 15:42) In (Joshua 19:7) and 1Chr 4:32It is mentioned again as belonging to Simeon. It has not yet been identified.
entries.definition_ko: '연기'라는 뜻으로 유다 저지대의 성읍이며(여호수아 15:42) 여호수아 19:7에서는 시므온 지파에 속한 것으로 다시 언급된다. 아직 위치가 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: (I adjure), a proper name, but whether of a person or place is uncertain. (1 Chronicles 4:21)
entries.definition_ko: '내가 맹세한다'는 뜻으로 인명인지 지명인지 불확실한 고유명사이다(역대상 4:21).

entries.definition: (reproof of God), second son of Benjamin and ancestor of the Ashbelites. (Genesis 46:21; Numbers 26:38; 1 Chronicles 8:1)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 책망'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 둘째 아들이며 아스벨 자손의 조상이다(창세기 46:21).

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 1:6; Jeremiah 51:27) [Ashkenaz]
entries.definition_ko: 아스그나스(ASHKENAZ) 항목 참조(역대상 1:6; 예레미야 51:27).

entries.definition: (a stronghold), (Acts 8:40) one of the five confederate cities of the Philistines situated about 30 miles from the southern frontier of Palestine, three from the Mediterranean Sea, and nearly midway between Gaza and Joppa. It was assigned to the tribe of Judah, (Joshua 15:47) but was never subdued by the Israelites. Its chief importance arose from its position on the high road from Palestine to Egypt. It is now an insignificant village, with no memorials of its ancient importance, but is still called Esdud.
entries.definition_ko: '요새'라는 뜻으로(사도행전 8:40) 블레셋의 다섯 동맹 성읍 중 하나로 팔레스타인 남쪽 경계에서 약 30마일, 지중해에서 3마일 떨어진 곳에 위치하며 가사와 욥바 중간쯤이다. 유다 지파에 배정되었으나(여호수아 15:47) 이스라엘에 정복된 적은 없다. 팔레스타인-애굽 간 대로에 위치해 중요했으며 오늘날 에스두드라는 이름의 작은 마을로 남아 있다.

entries.definition: the inhabitants of Ashdod, (Nehemiah 4:7) called Ashdothites in (Joshua 13:3)
entries.definition_ko: 아스돗 주민들을 가리키며(느헤미야 4:7) 여호수아 13:3에서는 아스돗 사람이라 불린다.

entries.definition: (3:17; Joshua 12:3; 13:20) and in Deuteronomy 4:49Authorized Version, translated springs of Pisgah, i.e. a valley or fountain near Mount Pisgah.
entries.definition_ko: 비스가산 근처의 골짜기 또는 샘을 가리키며 흠정역은 '비스가의 샘들'로 번역한다(신명기 3:17).

entries.definition: a place which formed one boundary of the tribe of Manasseh on the south. (Joshua 17:7) Mr. Porter suggests that Teyasir may be the Asher of Manasseh. Handbook, p.348. Apocrypha and New Testament, A’ser (blessed), the eighth son of Jacob, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid. (Genesis 30:13) (B.C. 1753.) The general position of his tribe was on the seashore from Carmel northward with Manasseh on the south, Zebulun and Issachar on the southeast, and Naphtali on the north-east. (Joshua 19:24-31; 17:10,11) and Judg 1:31,32They possessed the maritime portion of the rich plain of Esdraelon;, probably for a distance of 8 or 10 miles from the shore. This territory contained some of the richest soil in all Palestine.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 므낫세 지파 남쪽 경계를 이룬 한 장소(여호수아 17:7). (2) '복 받은 자'라는 뜻으로 야곱과 레아의 몸종 실바 사이에서 난 여덟째 아들이며(창세기 30:13) 그 지파는 갈멜산에서 북쪽 해안을 따라 자리 잡았다(여호수아 19:24-31).

entries.definition: (straight), the name of a Phoenician goddess, or rather of the idol itself (Authorized Version “grove”). Asherah is closely connected with Ashtorethand her worship, (Judges 3:7) comp. Judg 2:3; 6:25; 1Kin 18:19Ashtoreth being, perhaps, the proper name of the goddess, whilst Asherah is the name of her image or symbol, which was of wood. See (Judges 6:25-30; 2 Kings 23:14)
entries.definition_ko: '곧은'이라는 뜻으로 페니키아 여신 또는 그 우상 자체를 가리키며(흠정역 '작은 목상') 아스다롯 숭배와 밀접히 연관된다. 아스다롯이 여신의 고유 이름이라면 아세라는 나무로 만든 그 형상이나 상징물을 가리키는 것으로 보인다(사사기 6:25-30).

entries.definition: descendants of Asher, and members of his tribe. (Judges 1:32)
entries.definition_ko: 아셀의 후손이자 그 지파에 속한 사람들을 가리킨다(사사기 1:32).

entries.definition: The ashes on the altar of burnt offering were gathered into a cavity in its surface. The ashes of a red heifer burnt entire, according to regulations prescribed in Numb. 19, had the ceremonial efficacy of purifying the unclean, (Hebrews 9:13) but of polluting the clean. [Sacrifice] Ashes about the person, especially on the head, were used as a sign of sorrow. [Mourning]
entries.definition_ko: 번제단 위의 재는 제단 표면의 웅덩이에 모아졌다. 규례대로 온전히 태운 붉은 암송아지의 재는 부정한 자를 정결케 하는 의식적 효력이 있었다(히브리서 9:13). 몸에, 특히 머리에 재를 뿌리는 것은 슬픔의 표시로 쓰였다.

entries.definition: a god of the Hamathite colonists in Samaria. (2 Kings 17:30) It has been regarded as identical with the Pan of the Greeks.
entries.definition_ko: 사마리아에 정착한 하맛 이주민들이 섬긴 신으로(열왕기하 17:30) 헬라의 판(Pan) 신과 동일시되기도 한다.

entries.definition: Apocrypha As’calon (migration), one of the five cities of the Philistines, (Joshua 113:3; 1 Samuel 6:17) a seaport on the Mediterranean, 10 miles north of Gaza. Samson went down from Timnath to Ashkelon. (Judges 14:19) In the post-biblical times Ashkelon rose to considerable importance. Near the town were the temple and sacred lake of Derceto, the Syrian Venus. The soil around was remarkable for its fertility. Ashkelon played a memorable part in the struggles of the Crusades.
entries.definition_ko: '이주'라는 뜻으로 블레셋 다섯 성읍 중 하나이며 가사 북쪽 10마일의 지중해 항구도시이다. 삼손이 딤나에서 아스글론으로 내려간 일이 있다(사사기 14:19). 후대에는 십자군 전쟁의 격전지로 중요한 역할을 했다.

entries.definition: (spreading fire), one of the three sons of Gomer, son of Japhet. (Genesis 10:3) We may probably recognize the tribe of Ashkenaz on the northern shore of Asia Minor in the name of Lake Ascanius, and in Europe in the name Scandia, Scandinavia . Knobel considers that Ashkenaz is to be identified with the German race.
entries.definition_ko: '불을 퍼뜨림'이라는 뜻으로 야벳의 손자이자 고멜의 세 아들 중 하나이다(창세기 10:3). 소아시아 북쪽 해안의 아스카니우스 호수, 유럽의 스칸디아·스칸디나비아와 관련된 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: the name of two cities, both in the lowlands of Judah: (1) named between Zoreah and Zanoah, and therefore probably northwest of Jerusalem, (Joshua 15:33) and (2) between Jiptah and Nezib, and therefore to the southwest of Jerusalem. (Joshua 15:43) Each, according, to Robinson’s map (1857), would be about 16 miles from Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 저지대의 두 성읍 이름이다. (1) 소라와 사노아 사이(여호수아 15:33). (2) 입다와 느십 사이(여호수아 15:43).

entries.definition: (horse-nose), the master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar. (Daniel 1:3)
entries.definition_ko: '말의 코'라는 뜻으로 느부갓네살의 내시장이다(다니엘 1:3).

entries.definition: properly As’riel (vow of God). (1 Chronicles 7:14)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 서원'이라는 뜻이다(역대상 7:14).

entries.definition: and once As’taroth (a star), a city on the east of Jordan in Bashan, in the kingdom of Og, doubtless so called from being a seat of the worship of the goddess of the same name. (1:4; Joshua 9:10; 12:4; 13:12)
entries.definition_ko: '별'이라는 뜻으로 요단강 동쪽 바산, 옥 왕국에 속한 도시이며 동명의 여신을 섬기는 곳이었다(여호수아 9:10).

entries.definition: a native or inhabitant of Ashtaroth, (1 Chronicles 11:44) beyond Jordan.
entries.definition_ko: 아스다롯 출신을 가리키는 말이다(역대상 11:44).

entries.definition: (Ashteroth of the two horns or peaks) a place of very great antiquity, the abode of the Rephaim. (Genesis 14:5) The name reappears but once, as Carnaim or Carnion, 1 Macc. 5:26,43,44; 2 Macc. 12:21,26, in “the land of Galaad.” It is probably the modern Es-Sanamein, on the Haj route, about 25 miles south of Damascus.
entries.definition_ko: '두 뿔의 아스다롯'이라는 뜻으로 매우 오래된 곳이며 르바임 족속의 거처였다(창세기 14:5). 마카베오서에서는 갈릴리 땅의 가르나임 또는 가르니온으로 다시 언급된다.

entries.definition: (a star) the principal female divinity of the Phoenicians, called Ishtar by the Assyrians and Astarte by the Greeks and Romans. She was by some ancient writers identified with the moon. But on the other hand the Assyrian Ishtar was not the moon-goddess, but the planet Venus; and Astarte was by many identified with the goddess Venus (or Aphrodite), as well as with the plant of that name. It is certain that the worship of Astarte became identified with that of Venus, and that this worship was connected with the most impure rites is apparent from the close connection of this goddess with Asherah. (1 Kings 11:5,33; 2 Kings 23:13)
entries.definition_ko: 페니키아인의 주요 여신으로 앗수르인은 이슈타르, 헬라·로마인은 아스타르테라 불렀다. 일부 고대 저술가는 달의 여신으로, 다른 이들은 금성(비너스)의 여신으로 동일시했다. 이 숭배는 부도덕한 의식과 연관되었으며 아세라 숭배와도 밀접했다(열왕기상 11:5).

entries.definition: (black), the posthumous son of Hezron by his wife Abiah. (1 Chronicles 2:24; 4:5) He became “father” or founder of the town of Tekoa. (B.C. 1658.)
entries.definition_ko: '검은'이라는 뜻으로 헤스론이 아내 아비야를 통해 낳은 유복자이며 드고아 성읍의 조상이 되었다(역대상 2:24).

entries.definition: (steps), a tribe descended from Dedan, the grandson of Abraham. (Genesis 26:3) Knobel considers them the same with the Asshur of (Ezekiel 27:28) and connected with southern Arabia.
entries.definition_ko: 아브라함의 손자 드단의 후손 부족이다(창세기 26:3).

entries.definition: Only in (2 Samuel 2:9) By some of the old interpreters the name is taken as meaning the Geshurites; but if we follow the Targum of Jonathan, “the Asherites” will denote the inhabitants of the whole of the country west of the Jordan above Jez-reel.
entries.definition_ko: 사무엘하 2:9에만 나오며 일부 해석자는 그술 사람을 뜻한다고 보고, 다른 해석은 요단강 서쪽 이스르엘 위쪽 전 지역 주민을 가리킨다고 본다.

entries.definition: One of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:33)
entries.definition_ko: 아셀 지파 야블렛의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 7:33).

entries.definition: (orient). The passages in the New Testament where this word occurs are the following; (Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10,22,26,27; 20:4,16,18; 21:27; 27:2; Romans 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:19; 2 Corinthians 1:8; 2 Timothy 1:15; 1 Peter 1:1; Revelation 1:4,11) In all these it may be confidently stated that the word is used for a Roman province which embraced the western part of the peninsula of Asia Minor and of which Ephesus was the capital.
entries.definition_ko: '동방'이라는 뜻으로 신약에서 소아시아 반도 서부를 포함하는 로마 속주를 가리키며 에베소가 그 수도였다.

entries.definition: (chief of Asia) (Authorized Version; (Acts 19:31)), officers chosen annually by the cities of that part of the province of Asia of which Ephesus was, under Roman government, the metropolis. They had charge of the public games and religious theatrical spectacles, the expenses of which they bore.
entries.definition_ko: '아시아의 우두머리'라는 뜻으로(사도행전 19:31) 에베소가 수도였던 아시아 속주 도시들이 매년 선출한 관리이며 공공 경기와 종교극 행사를 주관하고 비용을 부담했다.

entries.definition: (created by God). • A Simeonite whose descendant Jehu lived in the reign of Hezekiah. (1 Chronicles 4:35) • One of the five swift writers whom Esdras was commanded to take to write the law and the history of the world. 2 Esd. 14:24.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 지으신'이라는 뜻. (1) 히스기야 시대 예후의 조상인 시므온 사람(역대상 4:35). (2) 에스드라가 율법과 세계 역사를 기록하도록 선택한 다섯 명의 능숙한 서기 중 하나(제2에스드라서 14:24).

entries.definition: (thorn-bush). The children of Asnah were among the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:50)
entries.definition_ko: '가시덤불'이라는 뜻으로 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 자손 중 하나이다(에스라 2:50).

entries.definition: (swift), mentioned in (Ezra 4:10) as the person who settled the Cutheans in the cities of Samaria. He was probably a general of Esarhaddon. (B.C. 712.)
entries.definition_ko: '신속한'이라는 뜻으로 사마리아 성읍들에 구다 사람들을 정착시킨 인물이며(에스라 4:10) 에살핫돈의 장군으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (Heb. pethen), translated (adder in) (Psalms 58:4; 91:13) Probably the Egyptian cobra, a small and very poisonous serpent, a dweller in the holes of walls, (Isaiah 11:8) and a snake upon which the serpent-charmers practiced their art.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '페텐'으로(시편 58:4) 애굽 코브라로 추정되는 작고 매우 독성이 강한 뱀이며 벽 틈에 서식하고 뱀 부리는 자들이 다루는 대상이었다.

entries.definition: the name of some sweet perfume mentioned in Ecclus. 24:15. The Lignum rhodianum, is by some supposed to be the substance indicated by the aspalathus, the plant which yields it is the Convolvulus scoparius if Linnaeus.
entries.definition_ko: 집회서 24:15에 언급된 향료 이름으로 로디언 나무 향으로 추정되며 원료가 되는 식물은 콘볼불루스 스코파리우스로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: third son of Haman. (Esther 9:7)
entries.definition_ko: 하만의 셋째 아들이다(에스더 9:7).

entries.definition: the pool in the “wilderness of Thecoe.” 1 Macc. 9:33. Is it possible that the name is a corruption of lacus Asphaltites?
entries.definition_ko: '드고아 광야'의 못으로(마카베오상 9:33) '아스팔티스(사해) 호수'의 와전된 이름일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: the son of Gilead and great-grandson of Manasseh. (Numbers 26:31; Joshua 17:2) He was the founder of the family of the Asrielites. (B.C. 1444.)
entries.definition_ko: 길르앗의 아들이자 므낫세의 증손이며(민수기 26:31) 아스리엘 가문의 조상이다.

entries.definition: Five Hebrew names of the genus Asinus occur in the Old Testament. • Chamor denotes the male domestic ass. • Athon, the common domestic she-ass. • Air, the name of a wild ass, which occurs (Genesis 32:15; 49:11) • Pere, a species of wild ass mentioned (Genesis 12:16) • Arod occurs only in (Job 39:5) but in what respect it differs from the Pere is uncertain. The ass in eastern countries is a very different animal from what he is in western Europe. The most noble and honorable amongst the Jews were wont to be mounted on asses. (With us the ass is a symbol of stubbornness and stupidity, while in the East it is especially remarkable for its patience, gentleness, intelligence, meek submission and great power of endurance.”—L. Abbott. The color is usually a reddish brown, but there are white asses, which are much prized. The ass was the animal of peace as the horse was the animal of war; hence the appropriateness of Christ in his triumphal entry riding on an ass. The wild ass is a beautiful animal.—ED.) Mr. Lavard remarks that in fleetness the wild ass (Asinus hemippus) equals the gazelle and to overtake it is a feat which only one or two of the most celebrated mares have been known to accomplish.
entries.definition_ko: 구약에는 나귀속을 가리키는 다섯 개의 히브리어 이름(카모르-수나귀, 아돈-암나귀, 아이르-어린 나귀, 페레-들나귀, 아로드-들나귀 일종)이 나온다. 동방에서 나귀는 서구와 달리 고귀함과 인내, 온유함의 상징이었으며 평화의 동물로서 그리스도의 예루살렘 입성에 사용되었다.

entries.definition: second son of Shem, (Genesis 10:22) also the Hebrew form for Assyria. [Assyria, Asshur]
entries.definition_ko: 셈의 둘째 아들이며(창세기 10:22) 앗수르를 가리키는 히브리어 이름이기도 하다.

entries.definition: (captive). • Son of Korah. (Exodus 6:24; 1 Chronicles 6:22) • Son of Ebiasaph, and a forefather of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6:23,37) • Son of Jeconiah, (1 Chronicles 3:17) unless “Jeconiah the captive” be the true rendering.
entries.definition_ko: '포로'라는 뜻. (1) 고라의 아들(출애굽기 6:24). (2) 에비아삽의 아들로 사무엘의 조상(역대상 6:23). (3) 여고냐의 아들(역대상 3:17).

entries.definition: (approaching), a seaport of the Roman province of Asia in the district anciently called Mysia, on the northern shore of the Gulf of Adrn-myttium, and about seven miles from Lesbos. (Acts 20:13,14)
entries.definition_ko: '다가가는'이라는 뜻으로 로마 아시아 속주 미시아 지역의 항구 도시이며 레스보스에서 약 7마일 떨어져 있다(사도행전 20:13).

entries.definition: (Ezra 4:2; Psalms 83:8) [Asshur, Assyria, Asshur; ASSYRIA]
entries.definition_ko: 앗수르(ASSYRIA) 항목 참조(에스라 4:2; 시편 83:8).

entries.definition: was a great and powerful country lying on the Tigris, (Genesis 2:14) the capital of which was Nineveh. (Genesis 10:11) etc. It derived its name apparently from Asshur, the son of Shem, (Genesis 10:22) who in later times was worshipped by the Assyrians as their chief god. • Extent.— The boundaries of Assyria differed greatly at different periods, Probably in the earliest times it was confined to a small tract of low country lying chiefly on the left bank of the Tigris. Gradually its limits were extended, until it came to be regarded as comprising the whole region between the Armenian mountains (lat. 37 30’) upon the north, and upon the south the country about Baghdad (lat. 33 30’). Eastward its boundary was the high range of Zagros, or mountains of Kurdistan; westward it was, according to the views of some, bounded by the Mesopotamian desert, while according to others it reached the Euphrates. • General character of the country.— On the north and east the high mountain-chains of Armenia and Kurdistan are succeeded by low ranges of limestone hills of a somewhat arid aspect. To these ridges there succeeds at first an undulating zone of country, well watered and fairly productive, which extends in length for 250 miles, and is interrupted only by a single limestone range. Above and below this barrier is an immense level tract, now for the most part a wilderness, which bears marks of having been in early times well cultivated and thickly peopled throughout. • Original peopling.—Scripture informs us that Assyria was peopled from Babylon, (Genesis 10:11) and both classical tradition and the monuments of the country agree in this representation. • Date of the foundation of the kingdom.—As a country, Assyria was evidently known to Moses. (Genesis 2:14; 25:18; Numbers 24:22,24) The foundation of the Assyrian empire was probably not very greatly anterior to B.C. 1228. • History.—The Mesopotamian researches have rendered it apparent that the original seat of government was not at Nineveh, but at Kileh-Sherghat, on the right bank of the Tigris. The most remarkable monarch of the earlier kings was called Tiglathpileser. He appears to have been king towards the close of the twelfth century, and thus to have been contemporary with Samuel. Afterwards followed Pul, who invaded Israel in the reign of Menahem (2 Kings 15:29) about B.C. 770, and Shalmaneser who besieged Samaria three years, and destroyed the kingdom of Israel B.C. 721, himself or by his successor Sargon, who usurped the throne at that time. Under Sargon the empire was as great as at any former era, and Nineveh became a most beautiful city. Sargon’s son Sennacherib became the most famous of the Assyrian kings. He began to reign 704 B.C. He invaded the kingdom of Judea in the reign of Hezekiah. He was followed by Esarhaddon, and he by a noted warrior and builder, Sardanapalus. In Scripture it is remarkable that we hear nothing of Assyria after the reign of Esarhaddon, and profane history is equally silent until the attacks began which brought about her downfall. The fall of Assyria, long previously prophesied by Isaiah, (Isaiah 10:5-19) was effected by the growing strength and boldness of the Medes, about 625 B.C. The prophecies of Nahum and Zephaniah (Zephaniah 2:13-15) against Assyria were probably delivered shortly before the catastrophe. • General character of the empire.— The Assyrian monarchs bore sway over a number of petty kings through the entire extent of their dominions. These native princes were feudatories of the great monarch, of whom they held their crown by the double tenure of homage and tribute. It is not quite certain how far Assyria required a religious conformity from the subject people. Her religion was a gross and complex polytheism, comprising the worship of thirteen principal and numerous minor divinities, at the head of all of whom stood the chief god, Asshur, who seems to be the deified patriarch of the nation. (Genesis 10:22) • Civilization of the Assyrians.— The civilization of the Assyrians was derived originally from the Babylonians. They were a Shemitic race originally resident in Babylonia (which at that time was Cushite) and thus acquainted with the Babylonian inventions and discoveries, who ascended the valley of the Tigris and established in the tract immediately below the Armenian mountains a separate and distinct nationality. Still, as their civilization developed it became in many respects peculiar. Their art is of home growth. But they were still in the most important points barbarians. Their government was rude and inartificial, their religion coarse and sensual, and their conduct of war cruel. • Modern discoveries in Assyria.— (Much interest has been excited in reference to Assyria by the discoveries lately made there, which confirm and illustrate the Bible. The most important of them is the finding of the stone tablets or books which formed the great library at Nineveh, founded by Shalmaneser B.C. 860, but embodying tablets written 2000 years B.C. This library was more than doubled by Sardanapalus. These tablets were broken into fragments, but many of them have been put together and deciphered by the late Mr. George Smith, of the British Museum. All these discoveries of things hidden for ages, but now come to light, confirm the Bible.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko:
티헬라 강가에 놓인 크고 강력한 나라로(창세기 2:14) 그 수도는 니느웨였다(창세기 10:11 등). 그 이름은 셈의 아들 앗수르에게서 온 듯하며(창세기 10:22), 그는 후대에 앗수르 사람에게 으뜸 신으로 섬김을 받았다.
(1) 범위. 앗수르의 경계는 때에 따라 크게 달랐다. 아마도 아주 이른 때에는 주로 티헬라 왼쪽 기슭의 낮은 땅 한 자락에 한정되었을 것이다. 차츰 그 한계가 넓어져 마침내 북쪽으로 아르메니아 산지(북위 37도 30분)에서 남쪽으로 바그다드 부근(북위 33도 30분)에 이르는 온 지역을 아우르는 것으로 여겨지게 되었다. 동쪽 경계는 자그로스 곧 쿠르디스탄 산줄기였고, 서쪽은 어떤 이들의 견해로는 메소보다미아 사막이었으나 다른 이들에 따르면 유브라데에 이르렀다.
(2) 지세. 북쪽과 동쪽으로 아르메니아와 쿠르디스탄의 높은 산줄기에 이어 다소 메마른 모습의 낮은 석회암 구릉이 이어진다. 이 산등성이 다음에는 물이 넉넉하고 꽤 기름진 굽이진 지대가 이어져 길이 이백오십 마일에 걸치며 석회암 산줄기 하나로만 끊긴다. 이 경계의 위아래로 광대한 평지가 펼쳐지는데 지금은 대개 황무지이나, 이른 시대에는 두루 잘 경작되고 사람이 빽빽이 살았던 자취를 지닌다.
(3) 처음 사람이 산 일. 성경은 앗수르에 바벨론에서 사람이 옮겨 갔다고 전하며(창세기 10:11), 고전 전승과 그 나라의 유적도 이와 일치한다.
(4) 왕국이 세워진 때. 나라로서의 앗수르는 모세에게 분명히 알려져 있었다(창세기 2:14; 25:18; 민수기 24:22,24). 앗수르 제국의 창건은 아마도 주전 1228년보다 그리 앞서지 않았을 것이다.
(5) 역사. 메소보다미아 연구로 본래의 통치 자리가 니느웨가 아니라 티헬라 오른쪽 기슭의 킬레셰르가트였음이 드러났다. 초기 왕 가운데 가장 두드러진 이는 디글랏빌레셀이라 불렸으니, 십이세기 끝 무렵의 왕으로 사무엘과 같은 때 사람이었던 듯하다. 뒤이어 주전 770년쯤 므나헴 때 이스라엘을 침공한 불이 있었고(열왕기하 15:19), 사마리아를 세 해 에워싼 살만에셀이 있었으니 주전 721년에 그 자신이나 그때 왕위를 빼앗은 후계자 사르곤이 이스라엘 나라를 멸하였다. 사르곤 아래에서 제국은 어느 때 못지않게 컸고 니느웨는 더없이 아름다운 성읍이 되었다. 사르곤의 아들 산헤립은 앗수르 왕 가운데 가장 이름났으니, 주전 704년에 다스리기 시작하여 히스기야 때 유대 나라를 침공하였다. 그 뒤를 에살핫돈이, 다시 이름난 무장이요 건축가인 사르다나팔루스가 이었다. 성경에서 에살핫돈의 치세 뒤로 앗수르에 대한 말이 들리지 않는 것이 눈에 띄며, 세속 역사도 그 몰락을 가져온 공격이 시작되기까지 마찬가지로 잠잠하다. 이사야가 오래전에 예언한 앗수르의 멸망은(이사야 10:5-19) 주전 625년쯤 메대 사람의 힘과 담대함이 자라면서 이루어졌다. 앗수르를 향한 나훔과 스바냐의 예언은(스바냐 2:13-15) 아마도 그 파국 직전에 주어졌을 것이다.
(6) 제국의 성격. 앗수르 군주는 그 영토 전역에 걸쳐 여러 작은 왕을 다스렸다. 이 토착 군주들은 대왕의 봉신으로서 경의와 조공이라는 이중의 조건으로 그 왕관을 지녔다. 앗수르가 속한 백성에게 종교의 일치를 얼마나 요구하였는지는 확실하지 않다. 그 종교는 조잡하고 복잡한 다신교로 주요 신 열셋과 수많은 작은 신을 섬겼고, 그 모두의 우두머리에 으뜸 신 앗수르가 있었으니 이 민족의 신격화된 조상인 듯하다(창세기 10:22).
(7) 문명. 앗수르 사람의 문명은 본래 바벨론 사람에게서 왔다. 그들은 본디 바벨로니아에 살던 셈 계통 종족으로 바벨론의 발명과 발견을 알고 있었는데, 티헬라 골짜기를 거슬러 올라가 아르메니아 산지 바로 아래 지역에 따로 구별된 나라를 세웠다. 그러면서도 그 문명이 발전하며 여러 점에서 독특해졌으니 그 예술은 스스로 자란 것이다. 그러나 가장 중요한 점에서 그들은 여전히 야만이었다. 정치는 거칠고 정교하지 못하였으며 종교는 조잡하고 육욕적이었고 전쟁 수행은 잔혹하였다.
(8) 근대의 발견. 최근 앗수르에서 이루어진 발견이 성경을 확증하고 밝혀 주어 큰 관심을 불러왔다. 그 가운데 가장 중요한 것은 니느웨의 큰 서고를 이루던 돌판 곧 책의 발견이니, 주전 860년 살만에셀이 세웠으되 주전 이천 년에 쓰인 판까지 담고 있었고 사르다나팔루스가 그 규모를 두 배 넘게 늘렸다. 이 판들은 조각조각 깨어졌으나 많은 것이 맞추어져 대영박물관의 고 조지 스미스가 해독하였다. 오랜 세월 감추였다가 이제 드러난 이 모든 발견이 성경을 확증한다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 26:15,17) literally house of the gatherings. Some understand it as the proper name of chambers on the south of the temple others of certain store-rooms, or of the council chambers in the outer court of the temple in which the elders held their celebrations.
entries.definition_ko: '모임의 집'이라는 뜻으로(역대상 26:15) 성전 남쪽 방들 또는 창고, 혹은 장로들이 회의하던 바깥뜰의 회의실을 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (incomparable), a Christian at Rome, saluted by St. Paul. (Romans 16:14)
entries.definition_ko: '비할 데 없는'이라는 뜻으로 로마의 그리스도인이며 바울의 문안을 받는다(로마서 16:14).

entries.definition: (thorn), The threshing-floor of, called also Abel-mizraim, (Genesis 50:10,11) afterwards called Beth-hogla, and known to have lain between the Jordan and Jericho, therefore on the west side of Jordan.
entries.definition_ko: '가시나무'라는 뜻으로 아벨미스라임이라고도 불린 타작마당이며(창세기 50:10) 훗날 벧호글라라 불렸고 요단강과 여리고 사이, 곧 요단강 서쪽에 위치했다.

entries.definition: (a crown) a wife of Jerahmeel, and mother of Onam. (1 Chronicles 2:26)
entries.definition_ko: '면류관'이라는 뜻으로 여라므엘의 아내이자 오남의 어머니이다(역대상 2:26).

entries.definition: (crowns). • One of the towns in the “land of Jazer and land of Gilead,” (Numbers 32:3) east of the Jordan, taken and built by the tribe of Gad. (Numbers 32:34) • A place on the (south?) boundary of Ephraim and Manasseh. (Joshua 16:2,7) It is impossible to say whether Ataroth is or is not the same place as • ATAROTH-ADAR, or -Addar, on the west border of Benjamin, “near the ’mountain’ that is on the south side of the nether Beth-horon.” (Joshua 16:5; 18:13) Perhaps the modern Atara, six miles northeast of Bethel. • “ATAROTH, THE HouseOF Joab,” a place(?) occurring in the list of the descendants of Judah. (1 Chronicles 2:54)
entries.definition_ko: '면류관들'이라는 뜻. (1) 요단강 동쪽 야셀과 길르앗 땅의 성읍으로 갓 지파가 세움(민수기 32:34). (2) 에브라임과 므낫세 경계의 한 장소(여호수아 16:2). (3) 아다롯앗달, 베냐민 서쪽 경계. (4) '요압의 집 아다롯', 유다 족보에 등장하는 곳(역대상 2:54).

entries.definition: (shut up). • The children of Ater were among the porters or gate-keepers of the temple who returned with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:42; Nehemiah 7:45) • The children of ATER OF Hezekiahto the number of 98 returned with Zerubbabel, (Ezra 2:16; Nehemiah 7:21) and were among the heads of the people who signed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:17)
entries.definition_ko: '닫힌'이라는 뜻. (1) 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 성전 문지기의 자손(에스라 2:42). (2) '히스기야의 아델' 자손 98명이 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아왔고(에스라 2:16) 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 백성의 지도자 중 하나였다.

entries.definition: (lodging place). (1 Samuel 30:30) As the name does not occur elsewhere, it has been suggested that it is an error of the transcriber for Ether, a town in the low country of Judah. (Joshua 15:42)
entries.definition_ko: (사무엘상 30:30) 다른 곳에 나오지 않는 이름이라 유다 저지대 성읍 에델의 필사 오류일 가능성이 제기된다(여호수아 15:42).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah made), a descendant of Pharez, the son of Judah, who dwelt at Jerusalem after the return from Babylon, (Nehemiah 11:4) called Uthaiin (1 Chronicles 9:4)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지으신 자'라는 뜻으로 유다의 아들 베레스의 후손이며 포로 후 예루살렘에 거주했고(느헤미야 11:4) 역대상 9:4에서는 우대라 불린다.

entries.definition: (afflicted of the Lord) daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, married Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and introduced into that kingdom the worship of Baal. (B.C. 891.) After the great revolution by which Jehu seated himself on the throne of Samaria she killed all the members of the royal family of Judah who had escaped his sword. (2 Kings 11:1) From the slaughter one infant, named Joash, the youngest son of Ahaziah, was rescued by his aunt Jehosheba wife of Jehoiada, (2 Chronicles 23:11) the high priest. (2 Chronicles 24:6) The child was brought up under Jehoiada’s care, and concealed in the temple for six years, during which period Athaliah reigned over Judah. At length Jehoiada thought it time to produce the lawful king to the people, trusting to their zeal for the worship of God and their loyalty to the house of David. His plan was successful, and Athaliah was put to death.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께 고난당한 자'라는 뜻으로 아합과 이세벨의 딸이며 유다 왕 여호람과 결혼해 바알 숭배를 유다 왕국에 들여왔다. 예후의 반역 이후 유다 왕실 사람들을 모두 죽였으나 갓난아기 요아스가 이모 여호세바의 손에 구출되어 6년간 성전에 숨겨져 있다가, 마침내 대제사장 여호야다가 그를 왕으로 옹립하고 아달랴는 처형되었다(열왕기하 11:1).
