In the towns where professional bakers resided, there were no doubt fixed ovens, in shape and size resembling those in use among ourselves; but more usually each household poured a portable oven, consisting of a stone or metal jar, about three feet high which was heated inwardly with wood, (1 Kings 17:12; Isaiah 44:15; Jeremiah 7:18) or dried grass and flower-stalks. (Matthew 6:30)
entries.definition_ko: 빵을 만드는 관습은 매우 이른 시기부터 있었으며(창세기 18:6) 밀, 보리, 스펠트 등 여러 곡물이 쓰였다. 밀가루를 물이나 우유와 섞어 손(애굽에서는 발도)으로 반죽한 뒤, 시간이 급하면 누룩 없이 즉시 구워 먹었다. 반죽이 부풀면 둥근 과자 모양으로 나누어 손바닥 넓이 정도로 얇게 구웠으며, 마을에는 전문 제빵사의 고정 화덕이 있었지만 대개는 가정마다 돌이나 금속으로 만든 휴대용 화덕을 썼다.

entries.definition: [Arms, Armor]
entries.definition_ko: 무기와 갑옷(ARMS, ARMOR) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [James The Less]
entries.definition_ko: 작은 야고보(JAMES THE LESS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Genesis 11:3) The brick in use among the Jews were much larger than with us, being usually from 12 to 13 inches square and 3 1/2 inches thick; they thus possess more of the character of tiles. (Ezekiel 4:1) The Israelites, in common with other captives, were employed by the Egyptian monarchs in making bricks and in building. (Exodus 1:14; 5:7) Egyptian bricks were not generally dried in kilns, but in the sun. That brick-kilns were known is evident from (2 Samuel 12:31; Jeremiah 43:9) When made of the Nile mud they required straw to prevent cracking. [See Straw]
entries.definition_ko: 유대인들이 쓰던 벽돌은 오늘날 것보다 훨씬 컸으며 대개 12~13인치 정사각형에 두께 3.5인치로 타일에 가까웠다(에스겔 4:1). 이스라엘 백성은 다른 포로들과 함께 애굽 왕들 밑에서 벽돌 만들기와 건축에 동원되었다(출애굽기 1:14). 애굽 벽돌은 대개 가마가 아니라 햇볕에 말렸으며, 나일강 진흙으로 만들 때는 갈라짐을 막기 위해 짚이 필요했다.

entries.definition: [Marriage]
entries.definition_ko: 결혼(MARRIAGE) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Jeremiah 46:4) elsewhere “habergeon,” or “coat of mail.”
entries.definition_ko: 예레미야 46:4에 언급되며 다른 곳에서는 '갑옷' 또는 '흉갑'으로 불린다.

entries.definition: Brimstone, or sulphur, is found in considerable quantities on the shores of the Dead Sea. (Genesis 19:24) It is a well-known simple mineral substance, crystalline, easily melted, very inflammable, and when burning emits a peculiar suffocating odor. It is found in great abundance near volcanoes. The soil around Sodom and Gomorrah abounded in sulphur and bitumen.
entries.definition_ko: 유황은 사해 연안에 상당량 매장되어 있으며(창세기 19:24) 결정질의 잘 녹고 매우 잘 타는 광물로 연소 시 특유의 숨막히는 냄새를 낸다. 화산 근처에 풍부하며 소돔과 고모라 주변 토양에는 유황과 역청이 많았다.

entries.definition: The Hebrew word is used in various senses in the Old Testament, as, • Any kinsman, and not a mere brother; e.g. nephew, (Genesis 13:8; 14:16) husband, (Song of Solomon 4:9) • One of the same tribe. (2 Samuel 19:13) • Of the same people, (Exodus 2:11) or even of a cognate people. (Numbers 20:14) • An ally. (Amos 1:9) • Any friend, (Job 5:15) • One of the same office. (1 Kings 9:13) • A fellow man. (Leviticus 19:17) • Metaphorically of any similarity, as in (Job 30:19) The word adelphos has a similar range of meanings in the New Testament.
entries.definition_ko: 구약의 히브리어는 다양한 의미로 쓰인다 — 단순 친족(조카, 남편 포함), 같은 지파 사람, 같은 민족 또는 동족 민족, 동맹, 친구, 같은 직분자, 동료 인간, 은유적 유사성 등. 신약 헬라어 '아델포스'도 비슷한 범위의 의미를 지닌다.

entries.definition: (wasting). • Son of Abishua and father of Uzzi fifth from Aaron in the line of the high priests in (1 Chronicles 6:5; 6:5,51) (Authorized Version), and in the genealogy of Ezra. (Ezra 7:4) • Son of Jogli, prince of the tribe of Dan, one of the ten men chosen to apportion the land of Canaan between the tribes. (Numbers 34:22)
entries.definition_ko: '소모함'이라는 뜻. (1) 아비수아의 아들이자 웃시의 아버지로 아론으로부터 5대손인 대제사장 계보의 인물(역대상 6:5). (2) 단 지파 방백 요글리의 아들로 가나안 땅 분배를 담당한 열 명 중 하나(민수기 34:22).

entries.definition: (wasting from Jehovah), a Kohathite Levite, of the sons of Heman, one of the musicians in the temple. (1 Chronicles 25:4,13)

entries.definition: (rain). [Month]
entries.definition_ko: '비'라는 뜻. 월(MONTH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: terms used synonymously with ox, oxen, and properly a generic name for horned cattle when a full age and fit for the plough. It is variously rendered “bullock,” (Isaiah 65:25) “cow,” (Ezekiel 4:15) “oxen,” (Genesis 12:16) Kine is used in the Bible as the plural of cow. In (Isaiah 51:20) the “wild bull” (“wild ox” in (14:5)) was possibly one of the larger species of antelope, and took its name from its swiftness. Dr. Robinson mentions larger herds of black and almost harmless buffaloes as still existing in Palestine, and these may be the animal indicated.
entries.definition_ko: '소, 황소'와 동의어로 쓰이며 본래 다 자라 쟁기질에 적합한 뿔 달린 가축 전반을 가리키는 일반명이다. 이사야 51:20의 '들소'는 큰 영양의 일종으로 추정되며 그 빠름에서 이름이 유래했을 수 있다.

entries.definition: (or papyrus), a red growing in the shallow water on the banks of the Nile. It grows to the height of 12 or 15 feet, with a stalk two or three inches in diameter. The stalks are very pliable and can be very closely interwoven, as is evident from their having been used in the construction of arks. (Exodus 2:3,5) Paper was made from this plant, from which it derives its name.
entries.definition_ko: 파피루스로 나일강가 얕은 물에서 자라며 높이 12~15피트, 줄기 지름 2~3인치까지 자란다. 줄기는 매우 유연해 촘촘히 엮을 수 있었으며 방주(모세의 갈대 상자) 제작에 사용되었다(출애굽기 2:3). 종이(paper)라는 단어도 이 식물의 이름에서 유래했다.

entries.definition: (understanding), a son of Jerahmeel, of the family of Pharez in Judah. (1 Chronicles 2:25) (understanding), a son of Jerahmeel, of the family of Pharez in Judah. (1 Chronicles 2:25)
entries.definition_ko: '이해'라는 뜻으로 유다 지파 베레스 가문 여라므엘의 아들이다(역대상 2:25).

entries.definition: (my understanding). • One of the Levites in the time of Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 9:4) • Another Levite, but of earlier date than the preceding. (Nehemiah 11:15)
entries.definition_ko: '나의 이해'라는 뜻. (1) 느헤미야 시대 레위인(느헤미야 9:4). (2) 그보다 이른 시기의 다른 레위인(느헤미야 11:15).

entries.definition: [TOMBS] On this subject we have to notice— • The place of burial, its site and shape; • The mode of burial; • The prevalent notions regarding this duty. • A natural cave enlarged and adapted by excavation, or an artificial imitation of one was the standard type of sepulchre. Sepulchres, when the owner’s means permitted it, were commonly prepared beforehand, and stood often in gardens, by roadsides, or even adjoining houses. Kings and prophets alone were probably buried within towns. (1 Kings 2:10; 16:6,28) Cities soon became populous and demanded cemeteries, (Ezekiel 39:15) which were placed without the walls. Sepulchres were marked sometimes by pillars or by pyramids. Such as were not otherwise noticeable were scrupulously “whited,” (Matthew 23:27) once a year, after the rains before the passover, to warn passers-by of defilement. • “The manner of the Jews” included the use of spices, where they could command the means. (2 Chronicles 16:10) A portion of these was burnt in honor of the deceased, and to this use was probably destined part of the one hundred pounds weight of “myrrh and aloes” in our Lord’s case. In no instance, save that of Saul and his sons, were the bodies burned; and even then the bones were interred, and re-exhumed for solemn entombment. It was the office of the next of kin to perform and preside over the whole funeral office; though public buriers were not unknown in New Testament times. (Acts 5:6,10) The body was borne by the nearest relatives. The grave-clothes were probably of the fashion worn in life, but swathed and fastened with bandages, and the head covered separately. • The precedent of Jacob’s and Joseph’s remains being returned to the land of Canaan was followed, in wish at least, by every pious Jew.
entries.definition_ko: 무덤(TOMBS) 항목 참조. 자연 동굴을 넓히거나 그 형태를 모방해 인공적으로 판 굴이 무덤의 표준 형태였으며, 형편이 되면 미리 준비해 두는 경우가 많았고 정원이나 길가, 집 근처에 자리했다. 왕과 선지자만이 성읍 안에 묻혔던 것으로 보인다. 향료를 사용하는 관습이 있었으며(역대하 16:14) 화장은 사울과 그 아들들의 경우를 제외하고는 행해지지 않았다.

entries.definition: The word is applied to the offering which was wholly consumed by fire on the altar, and the whole of which, except the refuse ashes “ascended” in the smoke to God. The meaning of the whole burnt offering was that which is the original idea of all sacrifice, the offering by the sacrificer of himself, soul and body, to God—the submission of his will to the will of the Lord. The ceremonies of the burnt offering are given in detail in the book of Leviticus. [Sacrifice]
entries.definition_ko: 제단 위에서 완전히 불태워지는 제사를 가리키며 재를 제외한 모든 것이 연기로 하나님께 '올라갔다'. 이는 모든 제사의 근본 개념, 곧 제사 드리는 자가 자신의 영혼과 몸을 하나님께 드리고 자신의 뜻을 여호와의 뜻에 복종시키는 것을 의미한다.

entries.definition: The Hebrew word seneh occurs only in those passages which refer to Jehovah’s appearance to Moses “in the flame of fire in the bush.” (Exodus 3:2,3,4; 33:16) It is quite impossible to say what kind of thorn bush is intended; but it was probably the acacia a small variety of the shittim tree found in the Sinai region.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '스네'는 여호와가 모세에게 '떨기나무 불꽃 가운데서' 나타나신 대목에만 나오며(출애굽기 3:2) 정확한 종은 알 수 없으나 시내 지역에 흔한 작은 아카시아(싯딤나무)의 일종으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Weights And MeasuresAND Measures]
entries.definition_ko: 도량형(WEIGHTS AND MEASURES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: One of the officers of the king’s household, (Nehemiah 1:11) who had charge of the wine and poured it out for the king. The chief butler, as the title signifies, was in charge of the butlers. (Genesis 40:1-13)
entries.definition_ko: 왕실 관리 중 하나로(느헤미야 1:11) 포도주를 관리하고 왕에게 따르는 일을 맡았다. '술 맡은 자의 우두머리'는 이 관리들을 총괄했다(창세기 40:1-13).

entries.definition: Curdled milk. (Genesis 18:8; 32:14; Judges 5:25; Job 20:17) Milk is generally offered to travellers in Palestine in a curdled or sour state, leben, thick, almost like butter. Hasselquist describes the method of making butter employed by the Arab women: “they made butter in a leather bag, hung on three poles erected for the purpose, in the form of a cone, and drawn to and fro by two women.”
entries.definition_ko: 응유(굳힌 우유)를 가리킨다(창세기 18:8). 팔레스타인 여행자들에게는 대개 시큼하게 굳힌 우유(레벤)가 제공되며, 아랍 여성들은 원뿔 모양으로 세운 세 개의 장대에 매단 가죽 부대에서 두 여인이 흔들어 버터를 만들었다.

entries.definition: (contempt). • The second son of Milcah and Nahor. (Genesis 22:21) Elihu “the Buzite” was probably a descendant of Buz. • A name occurring in the genealogies of the tribe of Gad. (1 Chronicles 5:14)
entries.definition_ko: '경멸'이라는 뜻. (1) 밀가와 나홀의 둘째 아들로(창세기 22:21) '부스 사람' 엘리후가 그 후손으로 추정된다. (2) 갓 지파 족보에 나오는 이름(역대상 5:14).

entries.definition: (contempt), father of Ezekiel the prophet. (Ezekiel 1:3)
entries.definition_ko: '경멸'이라는 뜻으로 선지자 에스겔의 아버지이다(에스겔 1:3).

entries.definition_ko: 도량형(MEASURES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition_ko: 유다 저지대의 성읍이다(여호수아 15:40).

entries.definition: • One of the landmarks on the boundary of Asher, (Joshua 19:27) now Kabul, 9 or 10 miles east of Accho . • Name of the land given to Hiram by Solomon. (1 Kings 9:10-13)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 아셀 지파 경계의 지표 중 하나로(여호수아 19:27) 오늘날의 카불이며 악고 동쪽 9~10마일에 위치한다. (2) 솔로몬이 히람에게 준 땅의 이름(열왕기상 9:10).

entries.definition: always in the New Testament the Roman emperor, the sovereign of Judea. (John 19:12,15; Acts 17:7)
entries.definition_ko: 신약에서 항상 로마 황제, 곧 유대의 통치자를 가리킨다(요한복음 19:12).

entries.definition: (Acts 8:40; 9:30; 10:1,24; 11:11; 12:19; 18:22; 21:8,16; 23:23,33; 25:1,4,6,13) was situated on the coast of Palestine, on the line of the great road from Tyre to Egypt, and about halfway between Joppa and Dora. The distance from Jerusalem was about 70 miles; Josephus states it in round numbers as 600 stadia. In Strabo’s time there was on this point of the coast merely a town called “Strato’s Tower,” with a landing-place, whereas in the time of Tacitus Caesarea is spoken of as being the head of Judea. It was in this interval that the city was built by Herod the Great. It was the official residence of the Herodian kings, and of Festus, Felix and the other Roman procurators of Judea. Here also lived Philip the deacon and his four prophesying daughters. Caesarea continued to be a city of some importance even in the time of the Crusades, and the name still lingers on the site (Kaisariyeh), which is a complete desolation, many of the building-stones having been carried to other towns.
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인 해안, 두로에서 애굽로 가는 대로 상에 위치했으며 욥바와 도라 중간쯤, 예루살렘에서 약 70마일 떨어져 있다. 헤롯 대왕이 이 도시를 건설했으며 헤롯 왕조 왕들과 베스도, 벨릭스 등 로마 총독들의 관저였다. 집사 빌립과 그의 예언하는 네 딸이 이곳에 살았다.

entries.definition: is mentioned only in the first two Gospels, (Matthew 16:13; Mark 8:27) and in accounts of the same transactions. It was at the easternmost and most important of the two recognized sources of the Jordan, the other being at Tel-el-Kadi . The spring rises from and the city was built on a limestone terrace in a valley at the base of Mount Hermon 20 miles north of the Sea of Galilee. It was enlarged by Herod Philip, and named after Caesar, with his own name added to distinguish it from Caesarea. Its present name is Banias, a village of some 50 houses, with many interesting ruins. Caesarea Philippi has no Old Testament history, though it has been not unreasonably identified with Baal-gad . It was visited by Christ shortly before his transfiguration, (Matthew 16:13-28) and was the northern limit of his journeys. (Mark 8:27)
entries.definition_ko: 요단강의 두 주요 수원 중 동쪽, 헤르몬산 기슭 석회암 대지 위에 세워진 도시로 갈릴리 호수 북쪽 20마일에 위치한다. 헤롯 빌립이 확장하고 가이사의 이름에 자신의 이름을 더해 명명했다(다른 가이사랴와 구별하기 위해). 오늘날 바니아스라 불리며 그리스도가 변화산 사건 직전 방문하신 곳이자 그분의 여정의 북쪽 한계였다(마태복음 16:13).

entries.definition: The term so rendered in (Jeremiah 5:27) is more properly a trap in which decoy birds were placed. In (Revelation 18:2) the (Greek term means a prison.
entries.definition_ko: 예레미야 5:27의 '새장'은 정확히는 미끼새를 넣는 덫을 가리키며, 계시록 18:2의 헬라어는 감옥을 뜻한다.

entries.definition: (depression), in full JosephCAIAPHAS, high priest of the Jews under Tiberius. (Matthew 26:3,57; John 11:49; 18:13,14,24,28; Acts 4:6) The procurator Valerius Gratus appointed him to the dignity, He was son-in-law of Annas. [Annas]
entries.definition_ko: '억압'이라는 뜻으로 전체 이름은 요셉 가야바이며 티베리우스 치하 유대인의 대제사장이었다(마태복음 26:3). 총독 발레리우스 그라투스가 그를 임명했으며 안나스의 사위였다.

entries.definition: one of the cities in the low country of Judah, named with Zanoah and Gibeah. (Joshua 15:57) (possession). Gen. 4. He was the eldest son of Adam and Eve; he followed the business of agriculture. In a fit of jealousy, roused by the rejection of his own sacrifice and the acceptance of Abel’s, he committed the crime of murder, for which he was expelled from Eden, and led the life of an exile. He settled in the land of Nod, and built a city, which he named after his son Enoch. His descendants are enumerated together with the inventions for which they were remarkable. (B.C. 4000.)
entries.definition_ko: 유다 저지대의 한 성읍으로 사노아, 기브아와 함께 언급된다(여호수아 15:57). 또한 아담과 하와의 맏아들로 농사를 지었으며, 자신의 제사가 거부되고 아벨의 제사가 받아들여지자 질투에 사로잡혀 살인을 저지르고 에덴에서 쫓겨나 유랑의 삶을 살았다. 놋 땅에 정착해 아들 에녹의 이름을 딴 도시를 세웠다.

entries.definition: (possessor) • Son of Enos, aged 70 years when he begat Mahalaleel his son. He lived 840 years afterwards, and died aged 910. (Genesis 6:9-14) • Son of Arphaxad, and father of Sala, according to (Luke 3:36,37) and usually called the second Cainan. The is nowhere named in the Hebrew MSS. It seems certain that his name was introduced into the genealogies of the Greek Old Testament in order to bring them into harmony with the genealogy of Christ in St. Luke’s Gospel.
entries.definition_ko: '소유자'라는 뜻. (1) 에노스의 아들로 70세에 마할랄렐을 낳았고 이후 840년을 더 살아 910세에 죽었다(창세기 5:9-14). (2) 아르박삿의 아들이자 셀라의 아버지로 누가복음 3:36에만 나오는 '둘째 가이난'이며 히브리어 사본에는 없어 헬라어 구약 족보를 누가복음의 그리스도 족보와 조화시키기 위해 삽입된 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (completion, old age), one of the most ancient cities of Assyria. (Genesis 10:11) The site of Calah is probably market by the Nimrud ruins. If this be regarded as ascertained, Calah must be considered to have been at one time (about B.C. 930-720) the capital of the empire.
entries.definition_ko: '완성, 노년'이라는 뜻으로 앗수르에서 가장 오래된 도시 중 하나이다(창세기 10:11). 님루드 유적이 그 위치로 추정되며 주전 930-720년경 제국의 수도였을 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition_ko: 갈대(REED) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (sustenance), a man of Judah, son or descendant of Zerah. (1 Chronicles 2:6) Probably identical with Chalcol.
entries.definition_ko: '양식, 부양'이라는 뜻으로 유다 지파 세라의 아들 또는 후손이다(역대상 2:6). 갈골과 동일 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: a vessel for boiling flesh, for either ceremonial or domestic use. (1 Samuel 2:14; 2 Chronicles 35:13; Job 41:20; Micah 3:3)
entries.definition_ko: 의식용 또는 가정용으로 고기를 삶는 그릇이다(사무엘상 2:14).

entries.definition: (capable). • According to (1 Chronicles 2:9,18,19,42,50) the son of Hezron the son of Pharez the son of Judah, and the father of Hur, and consequently grandfather of Caleb the spy. (B.C. about 1600.) • Son of Jephunneh, one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to Canaan. (Numbers 13:6) (B.C. 1490.) He and Oshea or Joshua the son of Nun were the only two of the whole number who encouraged the people to enter in boldly to the land and take possession of it. Fortyfive years afterwards Caleb came to Joshua and claimed possession of the land of the Anakim, Kirjath-arba or Hebron, and the neighboring hill country. Josh 14. This was immediately granted to him, and the following chapter relates how he took possession of Hebron, driving out the three sons of Anak; and how he offered Achsah his daughter in marriage to whoever would take Kirjath-sepher, i.e. Debir; and how when Othniel, his younger brother, had performed the feat, he not only gave him his daughter to wife, but with her the upper and nether springs of water which she asked for. It is probable that Caleb was a foreigner by birth,—a proselyte, incorporated into the tribe of Judah.
entries.definition_ko: '유능한'이라는 뜻. (1) 역대상 2:9에 따르면 헤스론의 아들이자 유다의 손자이며 훌의 아버지, 곧 정탐꾼 갈렙의 조부이다. (2) 여분네의 아들로 모세가 가나안에 보낸 열두 정탐꾼 중 하나이며(민수기 13:6) 여호수아와 함께 담대히 진격할 것을 권한 유일한 두 사람이었다. 45년 후 여호수아에게 아낙 족속의 땅, 곧 기럇아르바(헤브론)와 그 주변 산악 지대를 요구해 받았고, 아낙의 세 아들을 몰아냈으며, 딸 악사를 기럇세벨(드빌)을 정복하는 자에게 아내로 주겠다고 하여 동생 옷니엘이 그 일을 이루었다. 갈렙은 본래 이방인 출신으로 유다 지파에 편입된 개종자였을 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: The calf was held in high esteem by the Jews as food. (1 Samuel 28:24; Luke 15:23) The molten calf prepared by Aaron for the people to worship, (Exodus 32:4) was probably a wooden figure laminated with gold, a process which is known to have existed in Egypt. [Aaron]
entries.definition_ko: 송아지는 유대인들 사이에서 식용으로 높이 평가되었다(사무엘상 28:24). 아론이 백성을 위해 만든 금송아지는(출애굽기 32:4) 나무에 금을 입힌 형상으로 추정되며 애굽에도 이런 기법이 있었던 것으로 알려져 있다.

entries.definition_ko: 골고다(GOLGOTHA) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The species of camel which was in common use among the Jews and the heathen nations of Palestine was the Arabian or one-humped camel, Camelus arabicus . The dromedary is a swifter animal than the baggage-camel, and is used chiefly for riding purposes; it is merely a finer breed than the other. The Arabs call it the heirie . The speed, of the dromedary has been greatly exaggerated, the Arabs asserting that it is swifter than the horse. Eight or nine miles an hour is the utmost it is able to perform; this pace, however, it is able to keep up for hours together. The Arabian camel carries about 500 pounds. “The hump on the camel’s back is chiefly a store of fat, from which the animal draws as the wants of his system require; and the Arab is careful to see that the hump is in good condition before a long journey. Another interesting adaptation is the thick sole which protects the foot of the camel from the burning sand. The nostrils may be closed by valves against blasts of sand. Most interesting is the provision for drought made by providing the second stomach with great cells in which water is long retained. Sight and smell is exceedingly acute in the camel.”—Johnson’s Encyc. It is clear from (Genesis 12:16) that camels were early known to the Egyptians. The importance of the camel is shown by (Genesis 24:64; 37:25; Judges 7:12; 1 Samuel 27:9; 1 Kings 19:2; 2 Chronicles 14:15; Job 1:3; Jeremiah 49:29,32) and many other texts. John the Baptist wore a garment made of camel hair, (Matthew 3:4; Mark 1:6) the coarser hairs of the camel; and some have supposed that Elijah was clad in a dress of the same stuff.
entries.definition_ko: 유대인과 팔레스타인 이방 민족 사이에 흔히 쓰인 낙타는 아라비아산 단봉낙타이다. 낙타는 약 500파운드를 운반할 수 있으며 혹은 지방 저장고 역할을 하고, 두꺼운 발바닥은 뜨거운 모래로부터 발을 보호하며 콧구멍은 모래바람을 막기 위해 닫힌다. 창세기 12:16을 보면 낙타는 애굽 사람들에게도 일찍부터 알려져 있었다. 세례 요한은 낙타털 옷을 입었다(마태복음 3:4).

entries.definition: (full of grain), the place in which Jair the judge was buried. (Judges 10:5)
entries.definition_ko: '곡식이 가득한'이라는 뜻으로 사사 야일이 묻힌 곳이다(사사기 10:5).

entries.definition: [Encampment]
entries.definition_ko: 진영(ENCAMPMENT) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: There can be no doubt that “camphire” is the Lawsonia alba of botanists, the henna of Arabian naturalists. The henna plant grows in Egypt, Syria, Arabia and northern India. The flowers are white and grow in clusters, and are very fragrant. The whole shrub is from four to six feet high, (Song of Solomon 4:13)
entries.definition_ko: 헤나 나무를 가리키는 것이 확실하며 애굽, 수리아, 아라비아, 북인도에서 자란다. 흰 꽃이 송이로 피며 매우 향기롭고 관목 전체 높이는 4~6피트이다(아가 4:13).

entries.definition: (place of reeds) of Galilee, once Cana in Galilee, a village or town not far from Capernaum, memorable as the scene of Christ’s first miracle, (John 2:1,11; 4:46) as well as of a subsequent one, (John 4:46,54) and also as the native place of the apostle Nathanael. (John 21:2) The traditional site is at Kefr-Kenna, a small village about 4 1/2 miles northwest of Nazareth. The rival site is a village situated farther north, about five miles north of Seffurieh (Sepphoris) and nine north of Nazareth.
entries.definition_ko: '갈대의 장소'라는 뜻으로 갈릴리의 마을이며 가버나움에서 멀지 않고 그리스도의 첫 기적이 일어난 곳이다(요한복음 2:1). 사도 나다나엘의 고향이기도 하다(요한복음 21:2). 전통적으로 나사렛 북서쪽 약 4.5마일의 케프르케나로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: (Ca’nan) (low, flat). • The fourth son of Ham, (Genesis 10:6; 1 Chronicles 1:8) the progenitor of the Phoenicians [Zidon, Or Sidon], and of the various nations who before the Israelite conquest people the seacoast of Palestine, and generally the while of the country westward of the Jordan. (Genesis 10:13; 1 Chronicles 1:13) (B.C. 2347.) • The name “Canaan” is sometimes employed for the country itself.
entries.definition_ko: '낮은, 평평한'이라는 뜻. (1) 함의 넷째 아들로(창세기 10:6) 페니키아인들과 이스라엘 정복 이전 팔레스타인 해안에 거주한 여러 민족의 조상이다. (2) '가나안'이라는 이름은 때로 그 땅 자체를 가리키는 데도 쓰인다.

entries.definition: (lit. lowland), a name denoting the country west of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, and between those waters and the Mediterranean; given by God to Abraham’s posterity, the children of Israel. (Exodus 6:4; Leviticus 25:38) [Palestina And Palestine]
entries.definition_ko: '저지대'라는 뜻으로 요단강과 사해 서쪽, 지중해 사이의 지역을 가리키며 하나님이 아브라함의 후손 이스라엘 자손에게 주신 땅이다(출애굽기 6:4).

entries.definition: the designation of the apostle Simon, otherwise known as “Simon Zelotes.” It occurs in (Matthew 10:4; Mark 3:18) and is derived from a Chaldee or Syriac word by which the Jewish sect or faction of the “Zealots” was designated—a turbulent and seditious sect, especially conspicuous at the siege of Jerusalem. They taught that all foreign rule over Jews was unscriptural, and opposed that rule in every way.
entries.definition_ko: 사도 시몬의 별칭으로 '셀롯 시몬'으로도 알려져 있다(마태복음 10:4). 갈대아어 또는 수리아어 단어에서 유래했으며 유대 종파 '셀롯당'을 가리키는데, 예루살렘 포위 당시 특히 두드러졌던 소란스럽고 선동적인 종파였다.

entries.definition: a word used in two senses: • A tribe which inhabited a particular locality of the land west of the Jordan before the conquest; and • The people who inhabited generally the whole of that country. • In (Genesis 10:18-20) the seats of the Canaanite tribe are given as on the seashore and in the Jordan valley; comp. (Joshua 11:3) • Applied as a general name to the non-Israelite inhabitants of the land, as we have already seen was the case with “Canaan.” Instances of this are, (Genesis 12:6; Numbers 21:3) The Canaanites were descendants of Canaan. Their language was very similar to the Hebrew. The Canaanites were probably given to commerce; and thus the name became probably in later times an occasional synonym for a merchant.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 정복 이전 요단강 서쪽 특정 지역에 거주한 부족. (2) 그 땅 전체 비이스라엘 주민을 가리키는 일반 명칭. 가나안의 후손이며 언어는 히브리어와 매우 유사했다. 상업에 능해 후대에는 이 이름이 '상인'과 동의어로 쓰이기도 했다.

entries.definition: (Matthew 10:4) Used in the Revised Version in place of “Canaanite.” [See Canaanite, The]
entries.definition_ko: 개정역에서 '가나안 사람' 대신 쓰인 표기이다(마태복음 10:4). 가나안 사람(CANAANITE) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (prince of servants), a queen of Ethiopia (Meroe), mentioned (Acts 8:27) (A.D. 38.) The name was not a proper name of an individual, but that of a dynasty of Ethiopian queens.
entries.definition_ko: '종들의 왕후'라는 뜻으로 에디오피아(메로에)의 여왕이며(사도행전 8:27) 개인 이름이 아니라 에디오피아 여왕 왕조의 칭호였다.

entries.definition: in (Matthew 5:15; Mark 4:21) is merely a lamp-stand, made in various forms, to hold up the simple Oriental hand-lamps. which Moses was commanded to make for the tabernacle, is described (Exodus 25:31-37; 37:17-24) It was not strictly a “candlestick,” as it held seven richly-adorned lamps. With its various appurtenances it required a talent of “pure gold;” and it was not moulded, but “of beaten work,” and has been estimated to have been worth in our money over,000. From the Arch of Titus, where the sculptured the spoils taken from Jerusalem, we learn that it consisted of a central stem, with six branches, three on each side. It was about five feet high. [See Arch Of TitusOF TITUS] The candlestick was placed on the south side of the first apartment of the tabernacle, opposite the table of shewbread, (Exodus 25:37) and was lighted every evening and dressed every morning. (Exodus 27:20,21; 30:8) comp. 1Sam 3:2Each lamp was supplied with cotton and about two wineglasses of the purest olive oil, which was sufficient to keep it burning during a long night. In Solomon’s temple, instead of or in addition to this candlestick there were ten golden candlesticks similarly embossed, five in the right and five on the left. (1 Kings 7:49; 2 Chronicles 4:7) They were taken to Babylon. (Jeremiah 52:19) In the temple of Zerubbabel there was again a single candlestick. 1Macc 1:21: 4:49.
entries.definition_ko: 마태복음 5:15의 '등경'은 단순한 등잔대를 가리킨다. 모세가 성막을 위해 만들도록 명령받은 등잔대는 순금 한 달란트로 만든 두들겨 만든 작품이며 중앙 줄기에서 여섯 가지가 뻗어 나온 형태로 높이 약 5피트였다. 티투스 개선문의 부조에 그 형태가 새겨져 있다. 성막 성소 남쪽, 진설병 상 맞은편에 놓였고 매일 저녁 켜고 매일 아침 손질했다. 솔로몬 성전에는 금등잔대 열 개가 있었으나 바벨론으로 가져가졌고, 스룹바벨 성전에는 다시 하나만 있었다.

entries.definition: may be generally described as the “collection of books which form the original and authoritative written rule of the faith and practice of the Christian Church,” i.e. the Old and New Testaments. The word canon, in classical Greek, is properly a straight rod, “a rule” in the widest sense, and especially in the phrases “the rule of the Church,” “the rule of faith,” “the rule of truth,” The first direct application of the term canon to the Scriptures seems to be in the verses of Amphilochius (cir. 380 A.D.), where the word indicates the rule by which the contents of the Bible must be determined, and thus secondarily an index of the constituent books. The uncanonical books were described simply as “those without” or “those uncanonized.” The canonical books were also called “books of the testament,” and Jerome styled the whole collection by the striking name of “the holy library,” which happily expresses the unity and variety of the Bible. After the Maccabean persecution the history of the formation of the Canon is merged in the history of its contents. The Old Testament appears from that time as a whole. The complete Canon of the New Testament, as commonly received at present, was ratified at the third Council of Carthage (A.D. 397), and from that time was accepted throughout the Latin Church. Respecting the books of which the Canon is composed, see the article Bible. (The books of Scripture were not made canonical by act of any council, but the council gave its sanction to the results of long and careful investigations as to what books were really of divine authority and expressed the universally-accepted decisions of the church. The Old Testament Canon is ratified by the fact that the present Old Testament books were those accepted in the time of Christ and endorsed by him, and that of 275 quotations of the Old Testament in the New, no book out of the Canon is quoted from except perhaps the word of Enoch in Jude.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 그리스도교 교회의 신앙과 실천의 원래이자 권위 있는 성문 규범을 이루는 '책들의 모음'을 가리키며 곧 구약과 신약이다. '캐논'이라는 말은 헬라어로 본래 '곧은 막대, 규칙'을 뜻하며 4세기 암필로키우스의 시에서 처음 성경에 직접 적용되었다. 마카베오 항쟁 이후 정경의 역사는 그 내용의 역사와 합쳐진다. 오늘날 통용되는 신약 정경 전체는 제3차 카르타고 공의회(주후 397년)에서 확정되었다.

entries.definition: Judith 10:21; 13:9; 16:19. The canopy of Holofernes is the only one mentioned.
entries.definition_ko: 유딧서 10:21 등에서 홀로페르네스의 차양만이 언급된다.

entries.definition: (Song of Songs), entitled in the Authorized Version THE SONG OF Solomon. It was probably written by Solomon about B.C. 1012. It may be called a drama, as it contains the dramatic evolution of a simple love-story. Meaning.— The schools of interpretation may be divided into three: the mystical or typical, the allegorical, and the literal . • The mystical interpretation owes its origin to the desire to find a literal basis of fact for the allegorical. This basis is either the marriage of Solomon with Pharoah’s daughter or his marriage with an Israelitish woman, the Shulamite. • The allegorical. According to the Talmud the beloved is taken to be God; the loved one, or bride, is the congregation of Israel . In the Christian Church the Talmudical interpretation, imported by Origen, was all but universally received. • The literal interpretation. According to the most generally-received interpretation of the modern literalists, the Song is intended to display the victory of humble and constant love over the temptations of wealth and royalty. Canonicity.— The book has been rejected from the Canon by some critics; but in no case has its rejection been defended on external grounds. It is found in the LXX. and in the translations of Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion. It is contained in the catalog given in the Talmud, and in the catalogue of Melito; and in short we have the same evidence for its canonicity as that which is commonly adduced for the canonicity of any book of the Old Testament.
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서 '솔로몬의 노래'라 불리는 아가서로 주전 1012년경 솔로몬이 쓴 것으로 추정되며 단순한 사랑 이야기의 극적 전개를 담은 일종의 드라마로 볼 수 있다. 해석은 신비적(예표론적), 우의적, 문자적 세 유파로 나뉜다. 정경성 논란은 있었으나 칠십인역, 탈무드 목록 등에 포함되어 구약의 다른 어떤 책 못지않은 증거를 지닌다.

entries.definition: (village of Nahum) was on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. (Matthew 4:13) comp. John 6:24It was in the “land of Gennesaret,” [ (Matthew 14:34) comp. John 6:17,21,24] It was of sufficient size to be always called a “city,” (Matthew 9:1; Mark 1:33) had its own synagogue, in which our Lord frequently taught, (Mark 1:21; Luke 4:33,38; John 6:59) and there was also a customs station, where the dues were gathered both by stationary and by itinerant officers. (Matthew 9:9; 17:24; Mark 2:14; Luke 5:27) The only interest attaching to Capernaum is as the residence of our Lord and his apostles, the scene of so many miracles and “gracious words.” It was when he returned thither that he is said to have been “in the house.” (Mark 2:1) The spots which lay claim to its site are, • Kahn Minyeh, a mound of ruins which takes its name from an old khan hard by. This mound is situated close upon the seashore at the northwestern extremity of the plain (now El Ghuweir). • Three miles north of Khan Minyeh is the other claimant, Tell Hum,—ruins of walls and foundations covering a space of half a mile long by a quarter wide, on a point of the shore projecting into the lake and backed by a very gently-rising ground. It is impossible to locate it with certainty, but the probability is in favor of Tell Hum .
entries.definition_ko: '나훔의 마을'이라는 뜻으로 갈릴리 호수 서쪽 기슭, 게네사렛 땅에 위치했다(마태복음 4:13). 항상 '성읍'이라 불릴 만큼 규모가 있었고 자체 회당이 있어 주님이 자주 가르치셨으며(마가복음 1:21) 세관도 있었다. 주님과 사도들의 거처였으며 많은 기적과 '은혜로운 말씀'의 무대였다. 위치로는 칸 미니예와 텔 훔 두 곳이 후보지로 제시되나 텔 훔이 더 유력하다.

entries.definition: one of the numerous words employed in the Bible to denote a village or collection of dwellings smaller than a city (Ir). Mr Stanley proposes to render it by “hamlet.” In names of places it occurs in Chephar-he-Ammonai, Chephirah, Caphar-salama. To us its chief interest arises from its forming a part of the name of Capernaum, i.e. Capharnahum.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 성읍(이르)보다 작은 마을이나 거주지 무리를 가리키는 데 쓰인 여러 단어 중 하나이며 '작은 마을'로 옮길 수 있다. 그발암모나이, 그비라, 갑살라마 등 지명에 등장하며 가버나움(가바르나훔)이라는 이름의 일부이기도 하다.

entries.definition: (a crown), thrice mentioned as the primitive seat of the Philistines, (2:23; Jeremiah 47:4; Amos 9:7) who are once called Caphtorim . (2:23) Supposed to be in Egypt, or near to it in Africa.
entries.definition_ko: '왕관'이라는 뜻으로 블레셋 족속의 본래 거주지로 세 번 언급되며(신명기 2:23) 갑돌 족속이라고도 불린다. 애굽 또는 그 근처 아프리카 지역으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (province of good horses), (Acts 2:3; 1 Peter 1:1) the largest province in ancient Asia Minor. Cappadocia is an elevated table-land intersected by mountain chains. It seems always to have been deficient in wood, but it was a good grain country, and particularly famous for grazing. Its Roman metropolis was Caesarea. The native Cappadocians seem to have originally belonged to the Syrian stock.
entries.definition_ko: '좋은 말들의 지방'이라는 뜻으로(사도행전 2:9) 고대 소아시아에서 가장 큰 속주였다. 산맥으로 나뉜 고원 지대로 목재는 부족했으나 곡물과 목축에 뛰어났다. 로마 시대 수도는 가이사랴였으며 원주민은 수리아 계통으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: • As a purely military title, “captain” answers to sar in the Hebrew army and tribune in the Roman. The captain of the guard in (Acts 28:16) was probably the prefectus pratorio . • Katsin, occasionally rendered captain, applies Sometimes to a military, (Joshua 10:24; Judges 11:6,11; Isaiah 22:3; Daniel 11:18) sometimes to a civil command, e.g. (Isaiah 1:10; 3:6) • The captain of the temple, mentioned (Luke 22:4; Acts 4:1; 5:24) superintended the guard of priests and Levites who kept watch by night in the temple.
entries.definition_ko: 순수 군사 칭호로서의 '대장'은 히브리 군대의 '사르', 로마의 천부장에 해당한다. '갓친'은 때로는 군사 지휘관을, 때로는 민사 지도자를 가리킨다. '성전 맡은 자'(누가복음 22:4)는 성전에서 밤을 지키는 제사장·레위인 경비대를 감독했다.

entries.definition: A prisoner of war. Such were usually treated with great cruelty by the heathen nations. They were kept for slaves, and often sold; but this was a modification of the ancient cruelty, and a substitute for putting them to death Although the treatment of captives by the Jews seems sometimes to be cruel, it was very much milder than that of the heathen, and was mitigated, as far as possible in the circumstances, by their civil code.
entries.definition_ko: 전쟁 포로를 가리키며 이방 민족들은 대개 매우 잔혹하게 대했고 노예로 삼거나 팔았으나 이는 죽이는 것보다는 완화된 형태였다. 유대인의 포로 대우는 이방 민족보다 훨씬 온건했으며 민법으로 가능한 한 완화되었다.

entries.definition: The present article is confined to the forcible deportation of the Jew; from their native land, and their forcible detention, under the Assyrian or Babylonian kings. Captives of Israel.—The kingdom of Israel was invaded by three or four successive kings of Assyria. Pul or Surdanapalus, according to Rawlinson, imposed a tribute (B.C. 771 or 712), Rawl.) upon Menahem. (2 Kings 15:19) and 1Chr 5:26Tiglath-pileser carried away (B.C. 740) the trans-Jordanic tribes, (1 Chronicles 5:26) and the inhabitants of Galilee, (2 Kings 15:29) comp. Isai 9:1To Assyria. Shalmaneser twice invaded, (2 Kings 17:3,5) the kingdom which remained to Hoshea, took Samaria (B.C. 721) after a siege of three years, and carried Israel away into Assyria. This was the end of the kingdom of the ten tribes of Israel. Captivities of Judah .—Sennacherib (B.C. 713) is stated to have carried into Assyria 200,000 captives from the Jewish cities which he took. (2 Kings 18:13) Nebuchadnezzar, in the first half of his reign (B.C. 606-562), repeatedly invaded Judea, besieged Jerusalem, carried away the inhabitants to Babylon, and destroyed the temple. The 70 years of captivity predicted by Jeremiah, (Jeremiah 25:12) are dated by Prideaux from B.C. 606. The captivity of Ezekiel dates from B.C. 598, when that prophet, like Mordecai the uncle of Esther (Esther 2:6) accompanied Jehoiachin. The captives were treated not as slaves but as colonists. The Babylonian captivity was brought to a close by the decree, (Ezra 1:2) of Cyrus (B.C. 536), and the return of a portion of the nation under Sheshbazzar or Zerubbabel (B.C. 535), Ezra (B.C. 458) and Nehemiah (B.C. 445). Those who were left in Assyria, (Esther 8:9,11) and kept up their national distinctions, were known as The Dispersion. (John 7:35; 1:1; James 1:1) The lost tribes.—Many attempts have been made to discover the ten tribes existing as a distinct community; but though history bears no witness of the present distinct existence, it enables us to track the footsteps of the departing race in four directions after the time of the Captivity. • Some returned and mixed with the Jews. (Luke 2:36; Philemon 3:5) etc. • Some were left in Samaria, mingled with the Samaritans, (Ezra 6:21; John 4:12) and became bitter enemies of the Jews. • Many remained in Assyria, and were recognized as an integral part of the Dispersion; see (Acts 2:1; 26:7) • Most, probably, apostatized in Assyria, adopted the usages and idolatry of the nations among whom they were planted, and became wholly swallowed up in them.
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘은 앗수르 왕들에게 여러 차례 침공당했다 — 불(디글랏빌레셀 3세)이 므나헴에게 조공을 부과했고, 디글랏빌레셀이 요단강 동쪽 지파와 갈릴리 주민을 앗수르로 끌고 갔으며(주전 740년), 살만에셀은 3년의 포위 끝에 사마리아를 함락시켜(주전 721년) 이스라엘을 포로로 끌고 갔다(이스라엘 열 지파 왕국의 종말). 유다는 산헤립이 20만 명을 포로로 끌고 갔다고 하며, 느부갓네살은 재위 전반기(주전 606-562년)에 반복적으로 유다를 침공해 예루살렘을 포위하고 백성을 바벨론으로 끌고 갔으며 성전을 파괴했다. 예레미야가 예언한 70년의 포로 기간은 주전 606년부터 계산된다. 고레스의 칙령(에스라 1:2, 주전 536년)으로 바벨론 포로가 끝났고, 스룹바벨, 에스라, 느헤미야의 인도로 일부 백성이 돌아왔다. 앗수르에 남아 민족적 정체성을 유지한 이들은 '흩어진 자들'(디아스포라)로 알려졌다.

entries.definition: This word represents two Hebrew words. The first may he a general term to denote any bright, sparkling gem, (Isaiah 54:12) the second, (Exodus 28:17; 39:10; Ezekiel 28:13) is supposed to be and smaragdus or emerald.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 두 단어를 나타내며 하나는 밝게 빛나는 보석 전반을 가리키는 일반 용어로 추정되고(이사야 54:12) 다른 하나는(출애굽기 28:17) 에메랄드로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (severe), the seventh of the seven “chamberlains,” i.e. eunuchs, of King Ahasuerus. (Esther 1:10) (B.C. 483.).
entries.definition_ko: '엄격한'이라는 뜻으로 아하수에로 왕의 일곱 내시 중 일곱째이다(에스더 1:10).

entries.definition: (fortress of Chemosh) occupied nearly the site of the later Mabug or Hierapolis. It seems to have commanded the ordinary passage of the Euphrates at Bir or Birekjik . Carchemish appears to have been taken by Pharoah Necho shortly after the battle of Megiddo (cir. B.C. 608), and retaken by Nebuchadnezzar after a battle three years later, B.C. 605. (Jeremiah 46:2)
entries.definition_ko: '그모스의 요새'라는 뜻으로 후대 마붕(히에라볼리) 자리와 거의 같은 위치였으며 유브라데강의 통상적 도하 지점을 지배했다. 므깃도 전투 직후(주전 608년경) 애굽 왕 느고에게 함락되었다가 3년 후(주전 605년) 느부갓네살에게 다시 정복되었다(예레미야 46:2).

entries.definition: (bald head), father of Johanan, (2 Kings 25:23) elsewhere spelt Kareah.
entries.definition_ko: '대머리'라는 뜻으로 요하난의 아버지이며(열왕기하 25:23) 다른 곳에서는 가레아로 표기된다.

entries.definition: the southern part of the region which int he New Testament is called Asia, and the southwestern part of the peninsula of Asia Minor. (Acts 20:15; 27:7)
entries.definition_ko: 신약에서 '아시아'라 불리는 지역의 남부이자 소아시아 반도의 남서부이다(사도행전 20:15).

entries.definition: (fruitful place or park). • A mountain which forms one of the most striking and characteristic features of the country of Palestine. It is a noble ridge, the only headland of lower and central Palestine, and forms its southern boundary, running out with a bold bluff promontory, nearly 600 feet high, almost into the very waves of the Mediterranean, then extending southeast for a little more than twelve miles, when it terminates suddenly in a bluff somewhat corresponding to its western end. In form Carmel is a tolerably continuous ridge, its highest point, about four miles from the eastern end, being 1740 feet above the sea. That which has made the name of Carmel most familiar to the modern world is its intimate connection with the history of the two great prophets of Israel, Elijah and Elisha. (2 Kings 2:25; 4:25; 1 Kings 18:20-42) It is now commonly called Mar Elyas; Kurmel being occasionally, but only seldom, hear. • A town in the mountainous country of Judah, (Joshua 15:55) familiar to us as the residence of Nabal. (1 Samuel 25:2,5,7,40)
entries.definition_ko: '열매 맺는 곳, 곧 공원'이라는 뜻. (1) 팔레스타인 중남부의 남쪽 경계를 이루는 산으로 지중해로 뻗어나가는 높이 약 600피트의 곶에서 시작해 남동쪽으로 12마일 이상 뻗어 있으며 최고점은 해발 1740피트이다. 선지자 엘리야와 엘리사의 역사와 밀접하게 연관되어 유명하다(열왕기상 18:20-42). 오늘날 마르 엘리아스라 불린다. (2) 유다 산악 지대의 성읍으로 나발의 거처로 알려져 있다(사무엘상 25:2).

entries.definition: (vine dresser). • The fourth son of Reuben, the progenitor of the family of the Carmites. (Genesis 46:9; Exodus 6:14; Numbers 26:6; 1 Chronicles 5:3) • A man of the tribe of Judah, father of Achan, the “troubler of Israel.” (Joshua 7:1,18; 1 Chronicles 2:7; 4:1)
entries.definition_ko: '포도 재배자'라는 뜻. (1) 르우벤의 넷째 아들로 갈미 가문의 조상(창세기 46:9). (2) 유다 지파 사람으로 '이스라엘을 괴롭힌 자' 아간의 아버지(여호수아 7:1).

entries.definition: [Handicraft]
entries.definition_ko: 수공업(HANDICRAFT) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: a Christian at Troas. (2 Timothy 4:13)
entries.definition_ko: 드로아의 그리스도인이다(디모데후서 4:13).

entries.definition: This word signifies what we now call “baggage.” In the margin of (1 Samuel 17:20) and 1Sam 26:5-7And there only, “carriage” is employed int he sense of a wagon or cart.
entries.definition_ko: 오늘날 '짐, 수하물'을 뜻하는 단어이며 사무엘상 17:20 등의 난외주에서만 수레나 마차의 의미로 쓰인다.

entries.definition: (illustrious), one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. (Esther 1:14)
entries.definition_ko: '저명한'이라는 뜻으로 바사와 메대의 일곱 방백 중 하나이다(에스더 1:14).

entries.definition: (Genesis 45:19,27; Numbers 7:3,7,8) a vehicle drawn by cattle, (2 Samuel 6:6) to be distinguished from the chariot drawn by horses. Carts and wagons were either open or covered, (Numbers 7:3) and were used for conveyance of person, (Genesis 45:19) burdens, (1 Samuel 6:7,8) or produce. (Amos 2:13) The only cart used in western Asia has two wheels of solid wood.
entries.definition_ko: 소가 끄는 탈것으로(사무엘하 6:6) 말이 끄는 병거와 구별된다. 개방형과 지붕형이 있었으며 사람, 짐, 곡물 운반에 쓰였다.

entries.definition: The arts of carving and engraving were much in request in the construction of both the tabernacle and the temple. (Exodus 31:5; 35:33; 1 Kings 6:18,35; Psalms 74:6) as well as in the ornamentation of the priestly dresses. (Exodus 28:9-36; 2 Chronicles 2:7,14; Zechariah 3:9)
entries.definition_ko: 조각과 세공 기술은 성막과 성전 건축(출애굽기 31:5), 제사장 의복 장식(출애굽기 28:9)에 널리 활용되었다.

entries.definition: (silvery, white), a place of uncertain site on the road between Babylon and Jerusalem. (Ezra 8:17)
entries.definition_ko: '은빛, 흰'이라는 뜻으로 바벨론과 예루살렘 사이 도로변의 위치 불확실한 장소이다(에스라 8:17).

entries.definition: (fortified), a Mizraite people or tribe. (Genesis 10:14; 1 Chronicles 1:12)
entries.definition_ko: '요새화된'이라는 뜻으로 미스라임 계열 민족 또는 부족이다(창세기 10:14).

entries.definition: (Exodus 30:24; Ezekiel 27:19) The cassia bark of commerce is yielded by various kinds of Cinnamomum, which grow in different parts of India. The Hebrew word in (Psalms 45:8) is generally supposed to be another term for cassia.
entries.definition_ko: 출애굽기 30:24 등에 나오며 인도 여러 지역에서 자라는 계피나무 종류에서 얻는 계피 껍질을 가리킨다. 시편 45:8의 히브리어 단어도 계피의 다른 이름으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: [Fenced CitiesCITIES]
entries.definition_ko: 요새 성읍(FENCED CITIES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Acts 28:11) the twin sons of Jupiter and Leda, were regarded as the tutelary divinities of sailors; hence their image was often used as a figure-head for ships. They appeared in heaven as the constellation Gemini . In art they were sometimes represented simply as stars hovering over a ship.
entries.definition_ko: 제우스와 레다의 쌍둥이 아들로(사도행전 28:11) 선원들의 수호신으로 여겨져 그 형상이 배의 이물 장식으로 자주 쓰였다. 하늘에서는 쌍둥이자리로 나타난다.

entries.definition: The representative in the Authorized Version of the Hebrew word chasil and yelek . • Chasil occurs in (1 Kings 8:37; 2 Chronicles 6:28; Psalms 78:46; Isaiah 33:4; Joel 1:4) and seems to be applied to a locust, perhaps in its larva state. • Yelek. [Locust].
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서 히브리어 '카실'과 '옐렉'을 나타내며 각각 애벌레 상태의 메뚜기와 메뚜기(LOCUST)를 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Bull, Bullock].
entries.definition_ko: 소(BULL, BULLOCK) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Acts 27:16) The form given in the Revised Version to Clauda, an island south of Crete. It bears a closer relation to the modern name Gaudonesi of the Greek, the Gauda of P. Mela. (Clauda .—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 사도행전 27:16의 개정역 표기로 글라우다이며 그레데 남쪽의 섬이다.

entries.definition: a sort of ornamental head-dress, (Isaiah 3:18) with a net for its base. The name is derived from the caul, the membranous bag which encloses the heart—the pericardium.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: 그물을 바탕으로 한 장식용 머리쓰개이며(이사야 3:18) 심낭(심장을 감싸는 막)을 뜻하는 '콜'에서 이름이 유래했다.

entries.definition: The most remarkable caves noticed in Scripture are, that in which Lot dwelt after the destruction of Sodom, (Genesis 19:30) the cave of Machpelah, (Genesis 23:17) cave of Makkedah, (Joshua 10:10) cave of Adullam, (1 Samuel 22:1) cave od Engedi, (1 Samuel 24:3) Obadiah’s cave, (1 Kings 18:4) Elijah’s cave in Horeb, (1 Kings 19:9) the rock sepulchres of Lazarus and of our Lord. (Matthew 27:60; John 11:38) Caves were used for temporary dwelling-places and for tombs.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 언급된 대표적 동굴로는 롯이 소돔 멸망 후 거주한 동굴(창세기 19:30), 막벨라 굴(창세기 23:17), 막게다 굴(여호수아 10:10), 아둘람 굴(사무엘상 22:1), 엔게디 굴(사무엘상 24:3), 오바댜의 굴(열왕기상 18:4), 호렙의 엘리야 굴(열왕기상 19:9), 나사로와 주님의 바위 무덤 등이 있다. 동굴은 임시 거처와 무덤으로 쓰였다.

entries.definition: The Hebrew word erez, invariably rendered “cedar” by the Authorized Version, stands for that tree in most of the passages where the word occurs. While the word is sometimes used in a wider sense, (Leviticus 14:6) for evergreen cone-bearing trees, generally the cedar of Lebanon (Cedrus libani) is intended. (1 Kings 7:2; 10:27; Psalms 92:12; Song of Solomon 5:15; Isaiah 2:13; Ezekiel 31:3-6) The wood is of a reddish color, of bitter taste and aromatic odor, offensive to insects, and very durable. The cedar is a type of the Christian, being evergreen, beautiful, aromatic, wide spreading, slow growing, long lived, and having many uses. As far as is at present known, the cedar of Lebanon is confined in Syria to one valley of the Lebanon range, viz., that of the Kedisha river, which flows from near the highest point of the range westward to the Mediterranean, and enters the sea at the port of Tripoli. The grove is at the very upper part of the valley, about 15 miles from the sea, 6500 feet above that level, and its position is moreover above that of all other arboreous vegetation. (“Of the celebrated cedars on Mount Lebanon, eleven groves still remain. The famous B’Sherreh grove is threequarters of a mile in circumference, and contains about 400 trees, young and old. Perhaps a dozen of these are very old; the largest, 63 feet in girth and 70 feet high, is thought by some to have attained the age of 2000 years.”—Johnson’s Encycl.)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '에레즈'는 대부분 레바논 백향목(Cedrus libani)을 가리킨다(열왕기상 7:2). 목재는 붉은 빛을 띠며 쓴맛과 향기로운 냄새가 나 벌레를 물리치고 매우 오래 견딘다. 레바논의 백향목은 오늘날 케디샤 강 계곡 한 곳에만 남아 있으며 그 유명한 브셰레 숲에는 400여 그루가 남아 있고 그중 가장 큰 나무는 둘레 63피트, 높이 70피트로 수령 2000년으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (John 18:1) [SEE Kidron, Or Kedron]
entries.definition_ko: 기드론(KIDRON) 항목 참조(요한복음 18:1).

entries.definition: The descriptions of Scripture, (1 Kings 6:9,15; 7:3; 2 Chronicles 3:5,9; Jeremiah 22:14; Haggai 1:4) and of Josephus, show that the ceilings of the temple and the palaces of the Jewish kings were formed of cedar planks applied to the beams or joists crossing from wall to wall. “Oriental houses seem to have been the reverse of ours, the ceiling being of wood, richly ornamented, and the floor of plaster or tiles.”
entries.definition_ko: 성전과 유대 왕궁의 천장은 벽에서 벽으로 걸친 들보에 백향목 널판을 대어 만들었다(열왕기상 6:9). 동방의 집은 서구와 반대로 천장이 화려하게 장식된 나무였고 바닥은 회반죽이나 타일이었다.

entries.definition: [Coelesyria]
entries.definition_ko: 쾰레시리아(COELESYRIA) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (accurately Cenchre’ae) (millet), the eastern harbor of Corinth (i.e. its harbor on the Saronic Gulf) and the emporium of its trade with the Asiatic shores of the Mediterranean, as Lechaeum on the Crointhian Gulf connected it with Italy and the west. St. Paul sailed from Cenchrae, (Acts 18:18) on his return to Syria from his second missionary journey. An organized church seems to have been formed here. (Romans 16:1)
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 '겐그레애'(기장)라는 뜻으로 고린도의 동쪽 항구(사로니크만 방면)이며 소아시아 지중해 연안과의 교역 중심지였다. 바울이 2차 선교여행 귀환길에 이곳에서 배를 탔으며(사도행전 18:18) 여기에 조직된 교회가 있었던 것으로 보인다(로마서 16:1).

entries.definition: A small portable vessel of metal fitted to receive burning coals from the altar, and on which the incense for burning was sprinkled. (2 Chronicles 26:19; Luke 1:9) The only distinct precepts regarding the use of the censer are found in (Leviticus 16:12) and in (Numbers 4:14) Solomon prepared “censers of pure gold” as part of the temple furniture. (1 Kings 7:50; 2 Chronicles 4:22) The word rendered “censer” in (Hebrews 9:4) probably means the “altar of incense.”
entries.definition_ko: 제단에서 타는 숯을 받아 향을 뿌려 태우는 작은 휴대용 금속 그릇이다(역대하 26:19). 솔로몬은 성전 기구로 '순금 향로'를 준비했다(열왕기상 7:50).

entries.definition: [Taxing]
entries.definition_ko: 인구조사(TAXING) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Army]
entries.definition_ko: 군대(ARMY) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Peter]
entries.definition_ko: 베드로(PETER) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: the husk of corn or wheat which was separated from the grain by being thrown into the air, the wind blowing away the chaff, while the grain was saved. The carrying away of chaff by the wind is an ordinary scriptural image of the destruction of the wicked and of their powerlessness to resist God’s judgments. (Psalms 1:4; Isaiah 17:13; Hosea 13:3; Zephaniah 2:2)
entries.definition_ko: 곡식의 껍질로 공중에 던져 바람에 날려 보내는 방식으로 알곡과 분리했다. 겨가 바람에 날아가는 모습은 악인의 멸망과 하나님의 심판에 저항할 수 없음을 나타내는 성경적 상징으로 자주 쓰인다(시편 1:4).

entries.definition: Chains were used, • As badges of office; • For ornament; • For confining prisoners. • the gold chain placed about Joseph’s neck, (Genesis 41:42) and that promised to Daniel, (Daniel 5:7) are instances of the first use. In (Ezekiel 16:11) the chain is mentioned as the symbol of sovereignty. • Chains for ornamental purposes were worn by men as well as women. (Proverbs 1:9) Judith 10:4. The Midianites adorned the necks of their camels with chains. (Judges 8:21,26) Step-chains were attached to the ankle-rings. (Isaiah 3:16,18) • The means adopted for confining prisoners among the Jews were fetters similar to our handcuffs. (Judges 16:21; 2 Samuel 3:34; 2 Kings 25:7; Jeremiah 39:7) Among the Romans the prisoner was handcuffed to his guard, and occasionally to two guards. (Acts 12:6,7; 21:33)
entries.definition_ko: 사슬은 직위의 표지, 장신구, 죄수 구금용으로 쓰였다. 요셉의 목에 걸린 금사슬(창세기 41:42)과 다니엘에게 약속된 사슬(다니엘 5:7)이 첫 용도의 예이며, 남녀 모두 장신구로 목걸이를 착용했다(잠언 1:9). 유대인의 죄수 구금에는 오늘날의 수갑과 비슷한 족쇄가 쓰였고, 로마에서는 죄수를 경비병에게 수갑으로 묶었다(사도행전 12:6).

entries.definition: only in (Revelation 21:19) The name is applied in modern mineralogy to one of the varieties of agate. It is generally translucent and exhibits a great variety of colors. So named because it was found near the ancient Chalcedon, near Constantinople.
entries.definition_ko: 계시록 21:19에만 나오며 현대 광물학에서 마노의 한 변종을 가리키는 이름으로, 콘스탄티노플 근처 고대 도시 칼케돈 근방에서 발견되어 이름이 유래했다.

entries.definition: (1 Kings 4:31) [Calcol]
entries.definition_ko: 갈골(CALCOL) 항목 참조(열왕기상 4:31).

entries.definition: more correctly Chaldae’a, the ancient name of a country of Asia bordering on the Persian Gulf. Chaldea proper was the southern part of Babylonia, and is used in Scripture to signify that vast alluvial plain which has been formed by the deposits of the Euphrates and the Tigris. This extraordinary flat, unbroken except by the works of man, extends a distance of 400 miles along the course of the rivers, and is on an average about 100 miles in width. In addition to natural advantages these plains were nourished by a complicated system of canals, and vegetation flourished bountifully. It is said to be the only country in the world where wheat grows wild. Herodotus declared (i. 193) that grain commonly returned two hundred fold to the sower, and occasionally three hundred fold. Cities.—Babylonia has long been celebrated for the number and antiquity of its cities. The most important of those which have been identified are Borsippa (Birs-Nimrun), Sippara or Sepharvaim (Mosaib), Cutha (Ibrahim), Calneh (Niffer), Erech (Warka), Ur (Mugheir), Chilmad (Kalwadha), Larancha (Senkereh), Is (Hit), Durabe (Akkerkuf); but besides these there were a multitude of others, the sites of which have not been determined. Present condition—This land, once so rich in corn and wine, is to-day but a mass of mounds, “an arid waste; the dense population of former times is vanished, and no man dwells there.” The Hebrew prophets applied the term “land of the Chaldeans” to all Babylonia and “Chaldeans” to all the subjects of the Babylonian empire.
entries.definition_ko: 페르시아만에 접한 아시아의 고대 나라 이름으로 정확히는 '갈대아'이다. 유브라데강과 티헬라강이 만든 거대한 충적 평야를 가리키며 길이 400마일, 평균 너비 100마일에 이른다. 관개 수로가 발달해 세계에서 유일하게 밀이 야생으로 자라는 곳으로 알려졌으며, 헤로도토스는 파종한 곡식이 200배, 때로는 300배로 돌아온다고 기록했다. 보르십바, 십발라임, 구다, 갈레, 에렉, 우르 등 여러 고대 도시가 있었으나 오늘날은 황폐한 폐허 더미로 남아 있다.

entries.definition: It appears that the Chaldeans (Kaldai or Kaldi) were in the earliest times merely one out of many Cushite tribes inhabiting the great alluvial plain known afterwards as Chaldea or Babylonia. Their special seat was probably that southern portion of the country which is found to have so late retained the name of Chaldea. In process of time, as the Kaldi grew in power, their name gradually prevailed over those of the other tribes inhabiting the country; and by the era of the Jewish captivity it had begun to be used generally for all the inhabitants of Babylonia. It appears that while, both in Assyria and in later Babylonia, the Shemitic type of speech prevailed for civil purposes, the ancient Cushite dialect was retained, as a learned language for scientific and religious literature. This is no doubt the “learning” and the “tongue” to which reference it made in the book of Daniel, (Daniel 1:4) The Chaldeans were really the learned class; they were priests, magicians or astronomers, and in the last of the three capacities they probably effected discoveries of great importance. In later times they seem to have degenerated into mere fortune-tellers.
entries.definition_ko: 갈대아인(칼다이 또는 칼디)은 본래 바벨로니아(갈대아)로 알려진 충적 평야에 거주하던 여러 구스족 부족 중 하나였을 것으로 보이며, 점차 그 이름이 전체 주민을 가리키는 데 쓰이게 되었다. 갈대아어는 학문·종교 문헌의 학술어로 남았으며(다니엘 1:4의 '학문'과 '방언'이 이를 가리킴), 갈대아인은 제사장·마술사·천문학자 계급을 이루었으나 후대에는 단순한 점술가로 전락했다.

entries.definition: [Chaldeans, Or Chaldees]
entries.definition_ko: 갈대아인(CHALDEANS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Lime]
entries.definition_ko: 석회(LIME) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Genesis 43:30; 2 Samuel 18:33; Psalms 19:5; Daniel 6:10) The word chamber in these passages has much the same significance as with us, meaning the private rooms of the house—the guest chamber, as with us, meaning a room set apart for the accommodation of the visiting friend. (Mark 14:14,15; Luke 22:12) The upper chamber was used more particularly for the lodgment of strangers. (Acts 9:37)
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 방은 오늘날과 비슷한 의미로 쓰이며 '손님방'은 방문한 친구를 위해 마련된 방을 가리킨다(마가복음 14:14). 다락방은 특히 나그네를 위한 숙소로 쓰였다(사도행전 9:37).

entries.definition: an officer attached to the court of a king, who formerly had charge of the private apartments or chambers of the palace. He kept the accounts of the public revenues. The office held by Blastus, “the king’s chamberlain,” was entirely different from this. (Acts 12:20) It was a post of honor which involved great intimacy and influence with the king. For chamberlain as used in the Old Testament, see [Eunuch]
entries.definition_ko: 왕궁의 사적인 처소를 담당하던 궁정 관리로 국고 회계도 담당했다. 사도행전 12:20의 '왕의 시종장' 블라스도의 직책은 이와는 다르며 왕과의 친밀함과 영향력을 수반한 명예직이었다. 구약의 '내시'(시종)는 내시(EUNUCH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: a species of lizard. The reference in (Leviticus 11:30) is to some kind of an unclean animal, supposed to be the lizard, known by the name of the “monitor of the Nile,” a large, strong reptile common in Egypt and other parts of Africa.
entries.definition_ko: 도마뱀의 일종으로 레위기 11:30의 언급은 애굽와 아프리카 여러 지역에 흔한 크고 강한 파충류인 '나일강 왕도마뱀'으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (pronounced often shame), the translation of the Hebrew zemer in (14:5) But the translation is incorrect; for there is no evidence that the chamois have ever been seen in Palestine or the Lebanon. It is probable that some mountain sheep is intended.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '제메르'의 번역이나(신명기 14:5) 팔레스타인이나 레바논에 샤무아가 서식했다는 증거가 없어 부정확한 번역으로 보이며 산양의 일종을 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Canaan, Canaan, The Land Of]
entries.definition_ko: 가나안(CANAAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: the capital of a pillar; i.e. the upper part, as the term is used in modern architecture.
entries.definition_ko: 기둥머리, 곧 기둥의 윗부분을 가리키는 오늘날 건축 용어와 같다.

entries.definition: (i.e. cheap man), merchant.
entries.definition_ko: (값싼 사람이라는 뜻에서) 상인을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (ravine of craftsmen), a place near Lydda, a few miles east of Joppa. (1 Chronicles 4:14)
entries.definition_ko: '장인들의 골짜기'라는 뜻으로 룻다 근처, 욥바에서 몇 마일 동쪽에 위치한다(역대상 4:14).

entries.definition: (2 Chronicles 35:20) [Carchemish]
entries.definition_ko: 갈그미스(CARCHEMISH) 항목 참조(역대하 35:20).

entries.definition: a shallow vessel for receiving water or blood, also for presenting offerings of fine flour with oil. (Numbers 7:79) The daughter of Herodias brought the head of St. John the Baptist in a charger, (Matthew 14:8) probably a trencher or platter. [Basin]
entries.definition_ko: 물이나 피를 담거나 고운 가루와 기름 예물을 담는 데 쓰인 얕은 그릇이다(민수기 7:79). 헤로디아의 딸이 세례 요한의 머리를 담아온 '쟁반'도 이 종류로 추정된다(마태복음 14:8).

entries.definition: a vehicle used either for warlike or peaceful purposes, but most commonly the former. The Jewish chariots were patterned after the Egyptian, and consisted of a single pair of wheels on an axle, upon which was a car with high front and sides, but open at the back. The earliest mention of chariots in Scripture is in Egypt, where Joseph, as a mark of distinction, was placed in Pharaoh’s second chariot. (Genesis 41:43) Later on we find mention of Egyptian chariots for a warlike purpose. (Exodus 14:7) In this point of view chariots among some nations of antiquity, as elephants among others, may be regarded as filling the place of heavy artillery in modern times, so that the military power of a nation might be estimated by the number of its chariots. Thus Pharaoh in pursuing Israel took with him 600 chariots. The Philistines in Saul’s time had 30,000. (1 Samuel 13:5) David took from Hadadezer, king of Zobah, 1000 chariots, (2 Samuel 8:4) and from the Syrians a little later 700, (2 Samuel 10:18) who in order to recover their ground, collected 32,000 chariots. (1 Chronicles 19:7) Up to this time the Israelites possessed few or no chariots. They were first introduced by David, (2 Samuel 8:4) who raised and maintained a force of 1400 chariots, (1 Kings 10:25) by taxation on certain cities agreeably to eastern custom in such matters. (1 Kings 9:19; 10:25) From this time chariots were regarded as among the most important arms of war. (1 Kings 22:34; 2 Kings 9:16,21; 13:7,14; 18:24; 23:30; Isaiah 31:1) Most commonly two persons, and sometimes three, rode in the chariot, of whom the third was employed to carry the state umbrella. (1 Kings 22:34; 2 Kings 9:20,24; Acts 8:38) The prophets allude frequently to chariots as typical of power. (Psalms 20:7; 104:3; Jeremiah 51:21; Zechariah 6:1)
entries.definition_ko: 전쟁 또는 평화적 목적으로 쓰인 탈것으로 대부분 전쟁용이었다. 유대의 병거는 애굽식을 본떴으며 축에 바퀴 한 쌍을 달고 앞과 옆이 높으며 뒤가 트인 형태였다. 성경 최초의 병거 언급은 애굽에서 요셉이 바로의 둘째 병거에 태워진 것이다(창세기 41:43). 병거는 고대 국가의 군사력을 가늠하는 척도였으며, 다윗이 처음 이스라엘에 병거를 도입해 1,400대를 유지했다(열왕기상 10:25). 보통 두 사람, 때로 세 사람이 탔으며 셋째는 왕의 양산을 들었다.

entries.definition: (Acts 7:2,4) [Haran]
entries.definition_ko: 하란(HARAN) 항목 참조(사도행전 7:2).

entries.definition: [Hunting]
entries.definition_ko: 사냥(HUNTING) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (a contraction of Chenaniah), one of the Levites who assisted at the solemn purification of the people under Ezra. (Nehemiah 9:4)
entries.definition_ko: '그나냐'의 축약형으로 에스라 시대 백성의 엄숙한 정결 의식을 도운 레위인이다(느헤미야 9:4).

entries.definition: (length), a river in the “land of the Chaldeans.” (Ezekiel 1:3; 3:15,23) etc. It is commonly regarded as identical with the Habor, (2 Kings 17:6) and perhaps the Royal Canal of Nebuchadnezzar,—the greatest of all the cuttings in Mesopotamia.
entries.definition_ko: '길이'라는 뜻으로 '갈대아 땅'의 강이다(에스겔 1:3). 흔히 하볼강(열왕기하 17:6)과 동일시되며 느부갓네살의 '왕의 운하', 곧 메소보다미아 최대의 운하로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (cord), one of the singular topographical terms in which the ancient Hebrew language abounded. We find it always attached to the region of Argob. (3:4,13,14; 1 Kings 4:13)
entries.definition_ko: '줄'이라는 뜻으로 고대 히브리어 특유의 지리 용어이며 항상 아르곱 지역에 붙여 쓰였다(신명기 3:4).

entries.definition: (handful of sheaves), a king of Elam, in the time of Abraham, who with three other chiefs made war upon the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboim and Zoar, and reduced them to servitude. (Genesis 14:17)
entries.definition_ko: '곡식 단 한 움큼'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함 시대 엘람 왕이며 다른 세 방백과 함께 소돔, 고모라, 아드마, 스보임, 소알의 왕들을 쳐서 복속시켰다(창세기 14:17).

entries.definition: is mentioned only three times in the Bible, and on each occasion under a different name in the Hebrew. (1 Samuel 17:18; 2 Samuel 17:29; Job 10:10) It is difficult to decide how far these terms correspond with our notion of cheese, for they simply express various degrees of coagulation. Cheese is not at the present day common among the Bedouin Arabs, butter being decidedly preferred; but there is a substance closely corresponding to those mentioned in 1Sam 17, 2Sam 17, consisting of coagulated buttermilk, which is dried until it become quite hard, and is then ground; the Arabs eat it mixed with butter.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 세 번만 언급되며 매번 다른 히브리어 단어로 표현된다(사무엘상 17:18). 이 단어들이 오늘날의 치즈 개념과 얼마나 일치하는지 판단하기 어려우며 단순히 응고 정도의 차이를 나타내는 것으로 보인다. 오늘날 베두인 아랍인들 사이에서 치즈는 흔치 않고 버터가 더 선호되나, 응고된 버터밀크를 말려 갈아 만든 비슷한 물질이 존재한다.

entries.definition: (perfection), (Ezra 10:30) one who had a strange wife.
entries.definition_ko: '완전함'이라는 뜻으로 이방 아내를 얻은 인물이다(에스라 10:30).

entries.definition: (completed), (Ezra 10:35) another like the above.
entries.definition_ko: '완성된'이라는 뜻으로 위와 비슷한 경우의 인물이다(에스라 10:35).

entries.definition: • A man among the descendants of Judah. • Ezri the son of Chelub, one of David’s officers. (1 Chronicles 27:26)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 유다 후손 중 하나. (2) 다윗의 관리 중 하나인 그룹의 아들 에스리(역대상 27:26).

entries.definition: (capable), the son of Hezron. Same as Caleb. (1 Chronicles 2:9,18,42)
entries.definition_ko: '유능한'이라는 뜻으로 헤스론의 아들이며 갈렙과 같은 인물이다(역대상 2:9).

entries.definition: (those who go about in black, i.e. ascetics). In the Hebrew applied to the priests of the worship of false gods. (2 Kings 23:5; Hosea 10:5) in margin; (Zephaniah 1:4)
entries.definition_ko: '검은 옷을 입고 다니는 자들, 곧 금욕주의자들'이라는 뜻으로 히브리어로 거짓 신들을 섬기는 제사장들을 가리킨다(열왕기하 23:5).

entries.definition: (subduer), the national deity of the Moabites. (Numbers 21:29; Jeremiah 48:7,13,46) In (Judges 11:24) he also appears as the god of the Ammonites. Solomon introduced, and Josiah abolished, the worship of Chemosh at Jerusalem. (1 Kings 11:7; 2 Kings 23:13) Also identified with Baal-peor, Baalzebub, Mars and Saturn.
entries.definition_ko: '정복자'라는 뜻으로 모압 족속의 민족신이다(민수기 21:29). 사사기 11:24에서는 암몬 족속의 신으로도 나타난다. 솔로몬이 예루살렘에 그모스 숭배를 도입했고 요시야가 폐지했다(열왕기상 11:7). 바알브올, 바알세붑, 마르스, 사투르누스와도 동일시된다.

entries.definition: (merchant). • Son of Bilhan, son of Jediael, son of Benjamin, head of a Benjamite house, (1 Chronicles 7:10) probably of the family of the Belaites. [Bela] • Father or ancestor of Zedekiah the false prophet. (1 Kings 22:11,24; 2 Chronicles 18:10,23)
entries.definition_ko: '상인'이라는 뜻. (1) 브누엘의 아들이자 여디아엘의 아들, 베냐민 지파 가문의 우두머리(역대상 7:10). (2) 거짓 선지자 시드기야의 아버지 또는 조상(열왕기상 22:11).

entries.definition: (established by the Lord), chief of the Levites when David carried the ark to Jerusalem. (1 Chronicles 15:22; 26:29)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 세우신'이라는 뜻으로 다윗이 언약궤를 예루살렘으로 옮길 때 레위인의 우두머리였다(역대상 15:22).

entries.definition: (hamlet of the Ammonites), a place mentioned among the town of Benjamin. (Joshua 18:24)
entries.definition_ko: '암몬 사람들의 작은 마을'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 성읍 목록에 언급된다(여호수아 18:24).

entries.definition: (the hamlet), one of the four cities of the Gibeonites, (Joshua 9:17) named afterwards among the towns of Benjamin. (Ezra 2:25; Nehemiah 7:29)
entries.definition_ko: '작은 마을'이라는 뜻으로 기브온 족속의 네 성읍 중 하나이며(여호수아 9:17) 이후 베냐민 성읍 목록에도 언급된다(에스라 2:25).

entries.definition: (lyre), one of the sons of Dishon the Horite “duke.” (Genesis 36:26; 1 Chronicles 1:41)
entries.definition_ko: '수금'이라는 뜻으로 호리 족장 디산의 아들 중 하나이다(창세기 36:26).

entries.definition: (axe-men), (Ezekiel 25:16) same as Cherethites.
entries.definition_ko: '도끼잡이들'이라는 뜻으로(에스겔 25:16) 그렛 족속과 같다.

entries.definition: (executioners) and of King David. (2 Samuel 8:18; 15:18; 20:7,23; 1 Kings 1:38,44; 1 Chronicles 18:17) It is plain that these royal guards were employed as executioners., (2 Kings 11:4) and as couriers, (1 Kings 14:27) But it has been conjectured that they may have been foreign mercenaries, and therefore probably Philistines, of which name Pelethites may be only another form.
entries.definition_ko: '처형자들'이라는 뜻으로 다윗 왕의 근위대를 이룬 부류이다(사무엘하 8:18). 처형과 전령의 임무를 맡았으며 외국인 용병, 아마도 블레셋인이었을 것으로 추정되고 '블렛 사람'이 그 다른 형태일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (cutting, ravine), the torrent-bed or wady in which Elijah hid himself during the early part of the three-years drought. (1 Kings 17:3,5) The position of the Cherith has been much disputed. The argument from probability is in favor of the Cherith being on the east of Jordan, and the name may possibly be discovered there.
entries.definition_ko: '끊음, 협곡'이라는 뜻으로 엘리야가 3년 가뭄 초기에 숨은 시내(와디)이다(열왕기상 17:3). 위치는 논쟁이 있으나 요단강 동쪽일 가능성이 크다.

entries.definition: apparently a place in Babylonia from which some persons of doubtful extraction returned to Judea with Zerubbabel. (Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61)
entries.definition_ko: 바벨로니아의 한 장소로 추정되며 혈통이 불확실한 사람들이 이곳에서 스룹바벨과 함께 유대로 돌아왔다(에스라 2:59).

entries.definition: The symbolical figure so called was a composite creature-form which finds a parallel in the religious insignia of Assyria, Egypt and Persia, e.g. the sphinx, the winged bulls and lions of Nineveh, etc. A cherub guarded paradise. (Genesis 3:24) Figures of Cherubim were placed on the mercy-seat of the ark. (Exodus 25:18) A pair of colossal size overshadowed it in Solomon’s temple with the canopy of their contiguously extended wings. (1 Kings 6:27) Those on the ark were to be placed with wings stretched forth, one at each end of the mercy-seat.” Their wings were to be stretched upwards, and their faces “towards each other and towards the mercy-seat.” It is remarkable that with such precise directions as to their position, attitude and material, nothing, save that they were winged, is said concerning their shape. On the whole it seems likely that the word “cherub” meant not only the composite creature-form, of which the man, lion, ox and eagle were the elements, but, further, some peculiar and mystical form. (Some suppose that the cherubim represented God’s providence among men, the four faces expressing the characters of that providence: its wisdom and intelligence (man), its strength (ox), its kingly authority (lion), its swiftness, far-sighted (eagle). Others, combining all the other references with the description of the living creatures in Revelation, make the cherubim to represent God’s redeemed people. The qualities of the four faces are those which belong to God’s people. Their facing four ways, towards all quarters of the globe, represents their duty of extending the truth. The wings show swiftness of obedience; and only the redeemed can sing the song put in their mouths in (Revelation 5:8-14)—ED).
entries.definition_ko: 앗수르, 애굽, 바사의 종교적 표상(스핑크스, 니느웨의 날개 달린 황소와 사자 등)과 유사한 복합 형상의 상징적 존재이다. 그룹은 에덴동산을 지켰고(창세기 3:24) 언약궤의 속죄소 위에 그 형상이 놓였으며(출애굽기 25:18) 솔로몬 성전에는 거대한 한 쌍이 날개를 펼쳐 궤를 덮었다(열왕기상 6:27). 사람, 사자, 소, 독수리의 요소가 결합된 형상으로 추정되나 정확한 모습은 알려져 있지 않다.

entries.definition: (hopes), a place named as one of the landmarks on the west part of the north boundary of Judah, (Joshua 15:10) probably Kesla, about six miles to the northeast of Ainshems, on the western mountains of Judah.
entries.definition_ko: '희망들'이라는 뜻으로 유다 북쪽 경계 서쪽 지표 중 하나이며(여호수아 15:10) 아인셈스에서 북동쪽으로 약 6마일 떨어진 케슬라로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (increase), fourth son of Nahor. (Genesis 22:22)
entries.definition_ko: '증가'라는 뜻으로 나홀의 넷째 아들이다(창세기 22:22).

entries.definition: (idolatrous), a town in the extreme south of Palestine, (Joshua 15:30) 15 Miles southwest of Beersheba. In (Joshua 19:4) the name is Bethul.
entries.definition_ko: '우상숭배의'라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 최남단의 성읍이며(여호수아 15:30) 브엘세바 남서쪽 15마일에 위치한다. 여호수아 19:4에서는 브두엘이라 불린다.

entries.definition: By this word are translated in the Authorized Version two distinct Hebrew terms: • Aron ; this is invariably used for the ark of the covenant, and, with two exceptions, for that only. The two exceptions alluded to are (a) the “coffin” in which the bones of Joseph were carried from Egypt, (Genesis 50:26) and (b) the “chest” in which Jehoiada the priest collected the alms for the repairs of the temple. (2 Kings 12:9,10; 2 Chronicles 24:8-11) • Genazim, “chests.” (Ezekiel 27:24) only.
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서 두 개의 서로 다른 히브리어 단어를 이 말로 옮긴다. '아론'은 예외적인 두 경우(요셉의 유골함, 여호야다가 성전 보수 헌금을 모은 궤)를 제외하고 항상 언약궤를 가리키며, '게나짐'은 에스겔 27:24에만 나오는 '상자들'을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (Heb. ’armon .) (Genesis 30:37; Ezekiel 31:8) Probably the “palm tree” (Platanus orientalis) is intended. This tree thrives best in low and rather moist situations in the north of Palestine, and resembles our sycamore or buttonwood (Platanus occidentalis).
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '아르몬'으로(창세기 30:37) 아마도 '플라타너스(양버즘나무)'를 가리키는 것으로 추정되며 팔레스타인 북부의 낮고 습한 곳에서 잘 자란다.

entries.definition: (the loins), one of the towns of Issachar. (Joshua 19:18) From its position int he lists it appears to be between Jezreel and Shunem (Salam).
entries.definition_ko: '허리'라는 뜻으로 잇사갈 지파의 성읍 중 하나이며(여호수아 19:18) 이스르엘과 수넴 사이에 위치한 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: (lying), a name which occurs but once, (Genesis 38:5) probably the same as Achzib.
entries.definition_ko: '거짓말'이라는 뜻으로 창세기 38:5에만 나오며 아마 악십과 같은 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (a javelin), the name which in (1 Chronicles 13:9) is given to the threshing-floor at which the accident to the ark took place. In the parallel account in 2Sam 6the name is given as NACHON.
entries.definition_ko: '투창'이라는 뜻으로 역대상 13:9에서 언약궤 사고가 일어난 타작마당의 이름으로 나오며 사무엘하 6장 병행 기록에서는 나곤이라 불린다.

entries.definition: The blessing of offspring, but especially of the male sex, is highly valued among all eastern nations, while a the absence is regarded as one of the severest punishments. (Genesis 16:2; 7:14; 1 Samuel 1:6; 2 Samuel 6:23; 2 Kings 4:14; Isaiah 47:9; Jeremiah 20:15; Psalms 127:3,5) As soon as the child was born it was washed in a bath, rubbed with salt and wrapped in swaddling clothes. (Ezekiel 16:4; Job 38:9; Luke 2:7) On the 8th day the rite of circumcision, in the case of a boy, was performed and a name given. At the end of a certain time (forty days if a son and twice as long if a daughter) the mother offered sacrifice for her cleansing. (Leviticus 12:1-8; Luke 2:22) The period of nursing appears to have been sometimes prolonged to three years. (Isaiah 49:15) 2 Macc. 7:27. The time of weaning was an occasion of rejoicing. (Genesis 21:8) Both boys and girls in their early years were under the care of the women. (Proverbs 31:1) Afterwards the boys were taken by the father under his charge. Daughters usually remained in the women’s apartments till marriage. (Leviticus 21:9; Numbers 12:14; 1 Samuel 9:11) The authority of parents, especially of the father, over children was very great, as was also the reverence enjoined by the law to be paid to parents. The inheritance was divided equally between all the sons except the eldest, who received a double portion. (Genesis 25:31; 49:3; 21:17; Judges 11:2,7; 1 Chronicles 5:1,2) Daughters had by right no portion in the inheritance; but if a man had no son, his inheritance passed to his daughters, who were forbidden to marry out of the father’s tribe. (Numbers 27:1,8; 36:2,8)
entries.definition_ko: 자녀, 특히 아들의 축복은 동방 여러 민족에게 매우 귀히 여겨졌으며 그 부재는 가장 혹독한 형벌 중 하나로 여겨졌다. 아이가 태어나면 목욕시키고 소금으로 문지른 뒤 강보에 쌌으며(에스겔 16:4), 8일째에 남아는 할례를 받고 이름을 얻었다. 유모의 기간은 때로 3년까지 이어졌고 젖을 떼는 것은 기쁨의 계기였다(창세기 21:8). 부모, 특히 아버지의 권위는 매우 컸으며 상속은 장자에게 두 몫을 주고 나머지는 아들들 사이에 균등히 나누었다.

entries.definition: (like his father), a son of David by Abigail. [Abigail]
entries.definition_ko: '아버지를 닮은'이라는 뜻으로 다윗과 아비가일 사이의 아들이다. 아비가일(ABIGAIL) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (pining, sickly), the son of Naomi and husband of Ruth. (Ruth 1:2-5; 4:9) (B.C. 1250.)
entries.definition_ko: '쇠약함, 병약함'이라는 뜻으로 나오미의 아들이자 룻의 남편이다(룻기 1:2-5).

entries.definition: (enclosure), a place or country mentioned in conjunction with Sheba and Asshur. (Ezekiel 27:23)
entries.definition_ko: '둘러싸인 곳'이라는 뜻으로 스바, 앗수르와 함께 언급되는 장소 또는 나라이다(에스겔 27:23).

entries.definition: (longing), a follower and probably a son, of Barzillai the Gileadite, who returned from beyond Jordan with David. (2 Samuel 19:37,38,40) (B C 1023.) David appears to have bestowed on him a possession at Bethlehem, on which, in later times, an inn or khan was standing. (Jeremiah 41:17)
entries.definition_ko: '갈망'이라는 뜻으로 길르앗 사람 바르실래의 추종자이며 아마도 아들로, 다윗과 함께 요단강을 건너 돌아왔다(사무엘하 19:37). 다윗이 베들레헴의 한 소유지를 그에게 주었으며 후대에 그곳에 여관이 세워졌다(예레미야 41:17).

entries.definition: [Chimham]
entries.definition_ko: 김함(CHIMHAM) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (circuit), accurately Cinnareth, a fortified city in the tribe of Naphtali, (Joshua 19:35) only, of which no trace is found in later writers, and no remains by travellers.
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 '긴나레'라는 뜻으로 납달리 지파의 요새화된 성읍이며(여호수아 19:35) 후대 문헌에는 흔적이 없다.

entries.definition: (Numbers 34:11; Joshua 13:27) the inland sea, which is most similarly known to us as the “Lake of Gennesareth” or “Sea of Galilee.”
entries.definition_ko: 우리에게 '게네사렛 호수' 또는 '갈릴리 바다'로 더 잘 알려진 내해이다(민수기 34:11).

entries.definition: [Chinnereth, Chinnereth, Sea Of]
entries.definition_ko: 긴네렛(CHINNERETH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (snowy), an island of the Aegean Sea, 12 miles from Smyrna. It is separated from the mainland by a strait of only 5 miles. Its length is about 12 miles, and in breadth it varies from 8 to 18. Paul passed it on his return voyage from Troas to Caesarea. Acts 20:15it is now called Scio.
entries.definition_ko: '눈 내리는'이라는 뜻으로 스미르나에서 12마일 떨어진 에게해의 섬이며 본토와는 5마일의 해협으로 나뉜다. 바울이 드로아에서 가이사랴로 돌아가는 항해 중 이 섬을 지났다(사도행전 20:15). 오늘날 시오라 불린다.

entries.definition: [Month]
entries.definition_ko: 월(MONTH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (confidence), father of Elidad, the prince of the tribe of Benjamin chosen to assist in the division of the land of Canaan among the tribes. (Numbers 34:21) (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '신뢰'라는 뜻으로 가나안 땅 분배를 도운 베냐민 지파 방백 엘리닷의 아버지이다(민수기 34:21).

entries.definition: (loins of Tabor) a place to the border of which reached the border of Zebulun. (Joshua 19:12) It may be the village Iksal, which is now standing about 2 1/2 miles to the west of Mount Tabor.
entries.definition_ko: '다볼의 허리'라는 뜻으로 스불론 경계가 닿는 곳이다(여호수아 19:12). 오늘날 다볼산 서쪽 약 2.5마일의 익살 마을로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (bruisers), a family or race descended from Javan. (Genesis 10:4; 1 Chronicles 1:7) Authorized Version Kittim. Chittim is frequently noticed in Scripture. (Numbers 24:24; Isaiah 23:1,12; Jeremiah 2:10; Ezekiel 27:6; Daniel 11:30) In the above passages, the “isles of Chittim,” the “ships of Chittim, the “coasts of Chittim,” are supposed to refer to the island of Cyprus. Josephus considered Cyprus the original seat of the Chittim. The name Chittim, which in the first instance had implied to Phoenicians only, passed over to the islands which they had occupied, and thence to the people who succeeded the Phoenicians in the occupation of them.
entries.definition_ko: '치는 자들'이라는 뜻으로 야완의 후손인 가문 또는 민족이다(창세기 10:4). '깃딤의 섬들, 배들, 해안'(민수기 24:24)은 구브로 섬을 가리키는 것으로 추정되며, 요세푸스는 구브로를 깃딤의 본래 거주지로 보았다. 이 이름은 본래 페니키아인만을 가리켰다가 그들이 점유한 섬들로, 이후 그 뒤를 이은 민족들로 확장되었다.

entries.definition: (a statue, perhaps of Saturn), an idol made by the Israelites in the wilderness. [Remphan]
entries.definition_ko: '상, 아마도 토성상'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘 백성이 광야에서 만든 우상이다. 레판(REMPHAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (green herb), a woman mentioned in (1 Corinthians 1:11)
entries.definition_ko: '푸른 풀'이라는 뜻으로 고린도전서 1:11에 언급되는 여인이다.

entries.definition: (1 Samuel 30:30) It may perhaps, be identified with Ashanof Simeon.
entries.definition_ko: 사무엘상 30:30에 언급되며 시므온 지파의 아산과 동일시될 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: one of the cities in which our Lord’s mighty works were done, but named only in his denunciation. Matt. 11:21; Luke 10:13St. Jerome describes it as on the shore of the lake, two miles from Capernaum, but its modern site is uncertain.
entries.definition_ko: 주님의 큰 능력의 역사가 일어난 도시 중 하나이나 오직 그분의 책망 속에서만 언급된다(마태복음 11:21). 히에로니무스는 이곳이 가버나움에서 2마일 떨어진 호숫가에 있다고 기록하나 오늘날 정확한 위치는 불확실하다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 4:22) Perhaps the same as Achzib.
entries.definition_ko: 역대상 4:22에 나오며 아마도 악십과 같은 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Jesus]
entries.definition_ko: 예수(JESUS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The disciples, we are told, (Acts 11:26) were first called Christians at Antioch on the Orontes, somewhere about A.D. 43. They were known to each other as, and were among themselves called, brethren, (Acts 15:1,23; 1 Corinthians 7:12) disciples, (Acts 9:26; 11:29) believers, (Acts 5:14) saints, (Romans 8:27; 15:25) The name “Christian,” which, in the only other cases where it appears in the New Testament, (Acts 26:28; 1 Peter 4:16) is used contemptuously, could not have been applied by the early disciples to themselves, but was imposed upon them by the Gentile world. There is no reason to suppose that the name “Christian” of itself was intended as a term of scurrility or abuse, though it would naturally be used with contempt.
entries.definition_ko: 제자들은 주후 43년경 안디옥에서 처음 '그리스도인'이라 불렸다고 전해진다(사도행전 11:26). 그들 자신은 서로를 형제, 제자, 믿는 자, 성도라 불렀다. '그리스도인'이라는 이름은 신약의 다른 두 용례(사도행전 26:28)에서 경멸적으로 쓰이는 것으로 보아 초대 제자들이 스스로를 부른 이름이 아니라 이방 세계가 그들에게 붙인 이름이었을 것으로 보인다.

entries.term: Chronicles, First And Second Books Of
entries.definition: the name originally given to the record made by the appointed historiographers in the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. In the LXX. these books are called Paralipomena (i.e. things omitted), which is understood as meaning that they are supplementary to the books of Kings. The constant tradition of the Jews is that these books were for the most part compiled by Ezra. One of the greatest difficulties connected with the captivity and return must have been the maintenance of that genealogical distribution of the land which yet was a vital point of the Jewish economy. To supply this want and that each tribe might secure the inheritance of its fathers on its return was one object of the author of these books. Another difficulty intimately connected with the former was the maintenance of the temple services at Jerusalem. Zerubbabel, and after him Ezra and Nehemiah, labored most earnestly to restore the worship of God among the people, and to reinfuse something of national life and spirit into their hearts. Nothing could more effectually aid these designs than setting before the people a compendious history of the kingdom of David, its prosperity under God; the sins that led to its overthrow; the captivity and return. These considerations explain the plan and scope of that historical work which consists of the two books of Chronicles. The first book contains the sacred history by genealogies from the Creation to David, including an account of David’s reign. In the second book he continues the story, giving the history of the kings of Judah, without those of Israel, down to the return from the captivity. As regards the materials used by Ezra, they are not difficult to discover. The genealogies are obviously transcribed from some register in which were preserved the genealogies of the tribes and families drawn up at different times; while the history is mainly drawn from the same document as those used in the books of King.
