[Kings, First And Second Books Of, BOOKS OF]
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘과 유다 왕국의 공식 사관들이 남긴 기록에 본래 붙여진 이름이다. 칠십인역에서는 '빠진 것들'이라는 뜻의 '파랄레이포메나'로 불리며 열왕기서의 보충으로 이해된다. 유대 전통은 이 책들이 대부분 에스라에 의해 편찬되었다고 본다. 첫째 책은 창조부터 다윗까지의 족보와 다윗의 통치를 담고, 둘째 책은 이스라엘 왕들을 제외한 유다 왕들의 역사를 포로 귀환까지 이어간다.

entries.definition: By this term we understand the technical and historical chronology of the Jews and their ancestors from the earliest time to the close of the New Testament Canon. • TECHNICAL CHRONOLOGY.—The technical part of Hebrew chronology presents great difficulties. • HISTORICAL CHRONOLOGY.—The historical part of Hebrew chronology is not less difficult than the technical. The information in the Bible is indeed direct rather than inferential although there is very important evidence of the latter kind, but the present state of the numbers make absolute certainty in many cases impossible. Three principal systems of biblical chronology have been founded, which may be termed (the Long System, the short, and the Rabbinical. There is a fourth, which although an off shoot in part of the last, can scarcely be termed biblical, in as much as it depends for the most part upon theories, not only independent of but repugnant to the Bible: this last is at present peculiar to Baron Bunsen. The principal advocates of the Long chronology are Jackson. Hales and Des-Vignoles. Of the Short chronology Ussher may be considered as the most able advocate The Rabbinical chronology accept the biblical numbers, but makes the most arbitrary corrections. For the date of the Exodus it has been virtually accepted by Bunsen, Lepsius and Lord A. Hervey. The numbers given by the LXX. for the antediluvian patriarchs would place the creation of Adam 2262 years before the end of the flood or B.C. cir. 5361 or 5421.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인과 그 조상들의 최초 시기부터 신약 정경 완성까지의 기술적·역사적 연대기를 가리킨다. 성경 연대기 체계는 크게 장기 체계, 단기 체계, 랍비 체계 세 가지로 나뉘며, 장기 체계의 주요 지지자는 잭슨, 헤일스, 데비뇰이고 단기 체계는 어셔가 가장 유력한 지지자이다.

entries.definition: occurs only in (Revelation 21:20) The true chrysoprase is sometimes found in antique Egyptian jewelry set alternately with bits of lapis-lazuli. It is problem therefore, that this is the stone named as the tenth in the walls of the heavenly Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 계시록 21:20에만 나온다. 진짜 녹옥수는 고대 애굽 보석 세공에서 청금석과 번갈아 세팅된 채로 발견되기도 하며, 이는 천상 예루살렘 성벽의 열 번째 보석으로 언급된 돌일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: one of the precious stones in the foundation of the heavenly Jerusalem. (Revelation 21:20) It has been already stated [Beryl] that the chrysolite of the ancients is identical with the modern oriental topaz the tarhish of the Hebrew Bible.
entries.definition_ko: 천상 예루살렘 기초석의 보석 중 하나이다(계시록 21:20). 고대의 감람석(황옥)은 오늘날 동방의 황옥, 곧 히브리 성경의 '다시스'와 동일한 것으로 이미 언급한 바 있다.

entries.definition: Latin form of CHRYSOPRAS.
entries.definition_ko: '크리소프라수스'의 라틴어 형태이다.

entries.definition: the name of a people in alliance with Egypt in the time of Nebuchadnezzar, (Ezekiel 30:5) and probably of northern Africa.
entries.definition_ko: 느부갓네살 시대 애굽와 동맹한 민족의 이름으로(에스겔 30:5) 아마 북아프리카 지역으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 18:8) called Berothai in (2 Samuel 8:8)
entries.definition_ko: 역대상 18:8에 나오며 사무엘하 8:8에서는 베로대라 불린다.

entries.definition: • The derivation of the word is generally said to be from the Greek kuriakon (kuriakon) “belonging to the Lord.” But the derivation has been too hastily assumed. It is probably connected with kirk, the Latin circus, circulus, the Greek kuklos (kuklos) because the congregations were gathered in circles. • Ecclesia (ekklesia) the Greek word for church, originally meant an assembly called out by the magistrate, or by legitimate authority. It was in this last sense that the word was adapted and applied by the writers of the New Testament to the Christian congregation. In the one Gospel of St. Matthew the church is spoken of no less than thirty-six times as “the kingdom.” Other descriptions or titles are hardly found in the evangelists. It is Christ’s household, (Matthew 10:25) the salt and light of the world, (Matthew 5:13,15) Christ’s flock, (Matthew 26:31; John 10:15) its members are the branches growing on Christ the Vine, John 15; but the general description of it, not metaphorical but direct, is that it is a kingdom, (Matthew 16:19) From the Gospel then we learn that Christ was about to establish his heavenly kingdom on earth, which was to be the substitute for the Jewish Church and kingdom, now doomed to destruction (Matthew 21:43) The day of Pentecost is the birthday of the Christian church. Before they had been individual followers Jesus; now they became his mystical body, animated by his spirit. On the evening of the day of Pentecost, the 3140 members of which the Church consisted were— (1) Apostles; (2) previous Disciples; (3) Converts. In (Acts 2:41) we have indirectly exhibited the essential conditions of church communion. They are (1) Baptism, baptism implying on the part of the recipient repentance and faith; (2) Apostolic Doctrine; (3) Fellowship with the Apostles; (4) The Lord’s Supper; (5) Public Worship. The real Church consists of all who belong to the Lord Jesus Christ as his disciples, and are one in love, in character, in hope, in Christ as the head of all, though as the body of Christ it consists of many parts.
entries.definition_ko: 헬라어 '에클레시아'(교회)는 본래 관원이나 합법적 권위에 의해 소집된 회중을 뜻했으며 신약 저자들은 이를 그리스도인 공동체를 가리키는 데 적용했다. 마태복음에서는 교회가 '하나님 나라'로 36회 이상 언급되며 그리스도의 집, 세상의 소금과 빛, 그리스도의 양떼 등으로 묘사된다. 오순절은 그리스도교 교회의 생일이며, 참된 교회는 주 예수 그리스도께 속한 모든 제자로 이루어져 사랑과 성품, 소망 안에서 하나이며 그리스도를 머리로 삼는 몸을 이룬다.

entries.definition: (chief of two governments), the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel during eight years in the generation immediately following Joshua. (Judges 3:8) (B.C. after 1420.) His yoke was broken from the neck of the people of Israel by Othniel, Caleb’s nephew. (Judges 3:10)
entries.definition_ko: '두 정부의 우두머리'라는 뜻으로 여호수아 이후 세대 이스라엘을 8년간 압제한 메소보다미아 왕이다(사사기 3:8). 갈렙의 조카 옷니엘이 이스라엘 백성의 목에서 그 멍에를 벗겼다(사사기 3:10).

entries.definition: properly Chu’zas (the seer), the house-steward of Herod Antipas. (Luke 8:3)
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 '구사'(선견자)라는 뜻으로 헤롯 안디바의 청지기이다(누가복음 8:3).

entries.definition: [Jordan]
entries.definition_ko: 요단(JORDAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (the land of Celix), a maritime province int he southeast of Asia Minor, bordering on Pamphylia in the west, Lycaonia and Cappadocia in the north, and Syria in the east. (Acts 6:9) Cilicia was from its geographical position the high road between Syria and the west; it was also the native country of St. Paul, hence it was visited by him, firstly, soon after his conversion, (Acts 9:30; Galatians 1:21) and again in his second apostolical journey. (Acts 15:41)
entries.definition_ko: '길릭스의 땅'이라는 뜻으로 소아시아 남동부 해안 속주이며 서쪽으로 밤빌리아, 북쪽으로 루가오니아와 갑바도기아, 동쪽으로 수리아와 접한다(사도행전 6:9). 수리아와 서방을 잇는 지리적 요충지였으며 사도 바울의 고향으로 그가 회심 직후(사도행전 9:30)와 2차 선교여행 때(사도행전 15:41) 방문했다.

entries.definition: a well-known aromatic substance, the rind of the Laurus cinnamomum, called Korunda-gauhah in Ceylon. It is mentioned in (Exodus 30:23) as one of the component parts of the holy anointing oil. In (Revelation 18:13) it is enumerated among the merchandise of the great Babylon.
entries.definition_ko: '라우루스 시나모뭄'의 껍질에서 얻는 잘 알려진 향료로 출애굽기 30:23에서 거룩한 관유 성분 중 하나로 언급되며 계시록 18:13에서는 큰 바벨론의 상품 목록에 포함된다.

entries.definition: (1 Kings 15:20) This was possibly the small enclosed district north of Tiberias, and by the side of the lake, afterwards known as “the plain of Gennesareth.”
entries.definition_ko: 열왕기상 15:20에 나오며 아마도 디베랴 북쪽, 호숫가의 작은 구획으로 후에 '게네사렛 평지'로 알려진 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: was peculiarly, though not exclusively, a Jewish rite. It was enjoined upon Abraham, the father of the nation, by God, at the institution and as the token of the covenant, which assured to him and his descendants the promise of the Messiah. Gen. 17. It was thus made a necessary condition of Jewish nationality. Every male child was to be circumcised when eight days old, (Leviticus 12:3) on pain of death. The biblical notice of the rite describes it as distinctively Jewish; so that in the New Testament “the circumcision” and “the uncircumcision” are frequently used as synonyms for the Jews and the Gentiles. The rite has been found to prevail extensively in both ancient and modern times. Though Mohammed did not enjoin circumcision in the Koran, he was circumcised himself, according to the custom of his country; and circumcision is now as common among the Mohammedans as among the Jews. The process of restoring a circumcised person to his natural condition by a surgical operation was sometimes undergone. Some of the Jews in the time of Antiochus Epiphanes, wishing to assimilate themselves to the heathen around them, “made themselves uncircumcised.” Against having recourse to this practice, from an excessive anti-Judaistic tendency, St. Paul cautions the Corinthians. (1 Corinthians 7:18)
entries.definition_ko: 유대 민족 고유의 의식이며 전유물은 아니었다. 하나님이 아브라함에게 명하셔서 그와 후손에게 메시아의 약속을 보증하는 언약의 표시로 제정되었다(창세기 17장). 남아는 태어난 지 8일째에 반드시 할례를 받아야 했으며(레위기 12:3) 위반하면 죽음의 벌을 받았다. 신약에서는 '할례파'와 '무할례파'가 각각 유대인과 이방인을 가리키는 동의어로 자주 쓰인다.

entries.definition: the father of Saul, (Acts 13:21) usually called Kish.
entries.definition_ko: 사울의 아버지로(사도행전 13:21) 대개 기스라 불린다.

entries.definition: a receptacle for water, either conducted from an external spring or proceeding from rain-fall. The dryness of the summer months and the scarcity of springs in Judea made cisterns a necessity, and they are frequent throughout the whole of Syria and Palestine. On the long-forgotten way from Jericho to Bethel, “broken cisterns” of high antiquity are found at regular intervals. Jerusalem depends mainly for water upon its cisterns, of which almost every private house possesses one or more, excavated in the rock on which the city is built. The cisterns have usually a round opening at the top, sometimes built up with stonework above and furnished with a curb and a wheel for a bucket. (Ecclesiastes 12:6) Empty cisterns were sometimes used as prisons and places of confinement. Joseph was cast into a “pit,” (Genesis 37:22) as was Jeremiah. (Jeremiah 38:6)
entries.definition_ko: 외부 샘이나 빗물을 모으는 물 저장 시설이다. 유대 지역은 여름철 건조함과 샘 부족으로 저수조가 필수적이었으며 예루살렘은 물 공급을 주로 저수조에 의존했다. 빈 저수조는 때로 감옥이나 구금 장소로 쓰였으며 요셉이 '구덩이'에 던져진 것(창세기 37:22)과 예레미야가 던져진 것(예레미야 38:6)이 그 예이다.

entries.definition: The earliest notice in Scripture of city-building is of Enoch by Cain, in the land of his exile. (Genesis 4:17) After the confusion of tongues the descendants of Nimrod founded Babel, Erech, Accad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar, and Asshur, a branch from the same stock, built Nineveh, Rehoboth-by-the-river, Calah and Resen, the last being “a great city.” The earliest description of a city, properly so called, is that of Sodom, (Genesis 19:1-22) Even before the time of Abraham there were cities in Egypt, (Genesis 12:14,15; Numbers 13:22) and the Israelites, during their sojourn there, were employed in building or fortifying the “treasure cities” of Pithom and Raamses. (Exodus 1:11) Fenced cities, fortified with high walls, (3:5) were occupied and perhaps partly rebuilt after the conquest, by the settled inhabitants of Syria on both sides of the Jordan.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 최초로 언급된 도시 건설은 가인이 유배지에서 에녹을 세운 것이다(창세기 4:17). 언어 혼잡 이후 니므롯의 후손이 시날 땅에 바벨, 에렉, 악갓, 갈레를 세웠고 앗수르는 니느웨, 르호봇, 갈라, 레센을 세웠다. 아브라함 이전에도 애굽에 도시가 있었으며 이스라엘 백성은 애굽 체류 중 국고성 비돔과 라암셋을 건축하는 데 동원되었다(출애굽기 1:11).

entries.definition: six Levitical cities specially chosen for refuge to the involuntary homicide until released from banishment by the death of the high priest. (Numbers 35:6,13,15; Joshua 20:2,7,9) There were three on each side of Jordan. •Kedesh, in Naphtali. (1 Chronicles 6:76) •Shechem, in Mount Ephraim. (Joshua 21:21; 1 Chronicles 6:67; 2 Chronicles 10:1) •Hebron, in Judah. (Joshua 21:13; 2 Samuel 5:5; 1 Chronicles 6:55; 29:27; 2 Chronicles 11:10) • On the east side of Jordan - Bezer In The Wilderness, in the tribe of Reuben, in the plains of Moab. (4:43; Joshua 20:8; 21:36) 1Macc. 5:26. • RAMOTH-GILEAD, in the tribe of Gad. (4:43; Joshua 21:38; 1 Kings 22:3) •Golan, in Bashan, in the half-tribe of Manasseh. (4:43; Joshua 21:27; 1 Chronicles 6:71)
entries.definition_ko: 부지중 살인자가 대제사장이 죽을 때까지 피신할 수 있도록 특별히 지정된 여섯 레위 성읍이다(민수기 35:6). 요단강 서쪽에는 납달리의 게데스, 에브라임 산지의 세겜, 유다의 헤브론이, 동쪽에는 르우벤 지파 모압 평지의 베셀, 갓 지파의 길르앗 라못, 므낫세 반 지파 바산의 골란이 있었다.

entries.definition: 1 Macc. 8:5. [Chittim, Kittim]
entries.definition_ko: 깃딤(CHITTIM, KITTIM) 항목 참조(마카베오상 8:5).

entries.definition: The use of this term in Scripture has exclusive reference to the usages of the Roman empire. The privilege of Roman citizenship was originally acquired in various ways, as by purchase, (Acts 22:28) by military services, by favor or by manumission. The right once obtained descended to a man’s children. (Acts 22:28) Among the privileges attached to citizenship we may note that a man could not be bound or imprisoned without a formal trial, (Acts 22:29) still less be scourged. (Acts 16:37) Cic. in Verr. v. 63,66. Another privilege attaching to citizenship was the appeal from a provincial tribunal to the emperor at Rome. (Acts 25:11)
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 이 용어는 오로지 로마 제국의 관례와 관련해 쓰인다. 로마 시민권은 매입, 군 복무, 은혜, 해방 등 다양한 방식으로 얻어졌으며 한번 얻으면 자녀에게 세습되었다(사도행전 22:28). 시민은 정식 재판 없이 결박되거나 투옥될 수 없었고(사도행전 22:29) 매질도 받을 수 없었으며(사도행전 16:37), 지방 법정에서 로마 황제에게 상소할 권리도 있었다(사도행전 25:11).

entries.definition: [Apple Tree, AppleTREE]
entries.definition_ko: 사과나무(APPLE TREE) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (lame), (Acts 27:16) a small island nearly due west of Cape Matala on the south coast of Crete, and nearly due south of Phoenice; now Gozzo .
entries.definition_ko: '절름발이'라는 뜻으로(사도행전 27:16) 그레데 남쪽 해안 마탈라곶 서쪽에 위치한 작은 섬이며 오늘날 고초라 불린다.

entries.definition: (lame), a Christian woman mentioned in (2 Timothy 4:21) as saluting Timotheus.
entries.definition_ko: '절름발이'라는 뜻으로 디모데후서 4:21에서 디모데에게 문안하는 그리스도인 여성으로 언급된다.

entries.definition: (lame), fourth Roman emperor, reigned from 41 to 54 A.D. He was nominated to the supreme power mainly through the influence of Herod Agrippa the First. In the reign of Claudius there were several famines, arising from unfavorable harvests, and one such occurred in Palestine and Syria. (Acts 11:28-30) Claudius was induced by a tumult of the Jews in Rome to expel them from the city. cf. (Acts 18:2) The date of this event is uncertain. After a weak and foolish reign he was poisoned by his fourth wife, Agrippina, the mother of Nero, October 13, A.D. 54.
entries.definition_ko: '절름발이'라는 뜻으로 넷째 로마 황제이며 주후 41-54년 재위했다. 헤롯 아그립바 1세의 영향으로 즉위했으며 재위 중 흉작으로 인한 기근이 여러 차례 있었고 그중 하나가 팔레스타인과 수리아에 미쳤다(사도행전 11:28). 로마의 유대인 소요로 인해 그들을 로마에서 추방했으며(사도행전 18:2), 넷째 아내 아그리피나(네로의 어머니)에게 독살당했다(주후 54년).

entries.definition: [Lysias Claudius]
entries.definition_ko: 루시아 글라우디오(LYSIAS CLAUDIUS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: As the sediment of water remaining in pits or in streets, the word is used frequently in the Old Testament. (Psalms 18:42; Isaiah 57:20; Jeremiah 38:6) and in the New Testament, (John 9:6) a mixture of sand or dust with spittle. It is also found in the sense of potter’s clay. (Isaiah 41:25) The great seat of the pottery of the present day in Palestine is Gaza, where are made the vessels in dark-blue clay so frequently met with. Another use of clay was for sealing. (Job 38:14) Our Lord’s tomb may have been thus sealed, (Matthew 27:66) as also the earthen vessel containing the evidences of Jeremiah’s purchase. (Jeremiah 32:14) The seal used for public documents was rolled on the moist clay, and the tablet was then placed in the fire and baked.
entries.definition_ko: 구덩이나 거리에 남은 물의 침전물을 가리키는 데 자주 쓰인다(시편 18:42). 신약에서는 침과 흙(또는 모래)을 섞은 것을 가리킨다(요한복음 9:6). 토기장이의 진흙(이사야 41:25)이라는 뜻으로도 쓰이며, 오늘날 팔레스타인 도자기의 중심지는 가사이다. 진흙은 봉인 용도로도 쓰였다(욥기 38:14).

entries.definition: (mild, merciful), (Philippians 4:3) a fellow laborer of St. Paul when he was at Philippi. (A.D. 57.) It was generally believed in the ancient Church that this Clement was identical with the bishop of Rome who afterwards became so celebrated.
entries.definition_ko: '온화한, 자비로운'이라는 뜻으로(빌립보서 4:3) 바울이 빌립보에 있을 때의 동역자이다. 고대 교회에서는 이 글레멘드가 후에 유명해진 로마 감독 글레멘드와 동일 인물이라고 널리 믿어졌다.

entries.definition: (of a renowned father), one of the two disciples who were going to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection. (Luke 24:18) Some think the same as Cleophas in (John 19:25) But they are probably two different persons. Cleopas is a Greek name, contracted from Cleopater, while Cleophas, or Clopas as in the Revised Version, is an Aramaic name, the same as Alphaeus.
entries.definition_ko: '유명한 아버지의'라는 뜻으로 부활의 날 엠마오로 가던 두 제자 중 하나이다(누가복음 24:18). 요한복음 19:25의 글로바와 동일 인물로 보는 이도 있으나 실제로는 다른 두 사람으로 보인다. 글로바는 헬라식 이름인 반면 글로바(알패오)는 아람어 이름이다.

entries.definition: Revised Version Clo’pas, the husband of Mary the sister of Virgin Mary. (John 19:25) He was probably dead before Jesus’ ministry began, for his wife and children constantly appear with Joseph’s family in the time of our Lord’s ministry.—Englishman’s Cyc. [Cleopas; Alphaeus]
entries.definition_ko: 개정역에서는 글로바로 표기되며 동정녀 마리아의 자매 마리아의 남편이다(요한복음 19:25). 예수님의 사역이 시작되기 전에 이미 죽은 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Dress]
entries.definition_ko: 의복(DRESS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The shelter given, and refreshment of rain promised, by clouds give them their peculiar prominence in Oriental imagery. When a cloud appears rain is ordinarily apprehended, and thus the “cloud without rain” becomes a proverb for the man of promise without performance. (Proverbs 16:15; Isaiah 18:4; 25:5; Jude 1:12) comp. Prov 25:14The cloud is a figure of transitoriness, (Job 30:15; Hosea 6:4) and of whatever intercepts divine favor or human supplication. (Lamentations 2:1; 3:44) A bright cloud at times visited and rested on the mercy-seat. (Exodus 29:42,43; 1 Kings 8:10,11; 2 Chronicles 5:14; Ezekiel 43:4) and was by later writers named Shechinah.
entries.definition_ko: 구름이 주는 그늘과 비를 약속하는 상징성은 동방의 이미지에서 두드러진다. 구름이 나타나면 대개 비를 예상하므로 '비 없는 구름'은 실행 없는 약속의 속담이 되었다(잠언 16:15). 구름은 덧없음의 상징이며(욥기 30:15) 밝은 구름은 때로 속죄소에 임하여 머물렀고(출애굽기 29:42) 후대 저술가들은 이를 '쉐키나'라 불렀다.

entries.definition: The pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night that God caused to pass before the camp of the children of Israel when in the wilderness. The cloud, which became a pillar when the host moved, seems to have rested at other times on the tabernacle, whence god is said to have “come down in the pillar.” (Numbers 12:5; Exodus 33:9,10) It preceded the host, apparently resting on the ark which led the way. (Exodus 13:21; 40:36) etc.; Numb 9:15-23; 10:34
entries.definition_ko: 하나님이 광야에서 이스라엘 진영 앞에 두신 낮의 구름 기둥과 밤의 불 기둥이다. 진영이 이동할 때 구름은 기둥이 되었고, 다른 때는 성막 위에 머물렀으며 언약궤를 앞서 인도했다(출애굽기 13:21).

entries.definition: patched. (Joshua 9:5)
entries.definition_ko: '기운, 헝겊을 댄'이라는 뜻이다(여호수아 9:5).

entries.definition: (nidus), a city of great consequence, situated at the extreme south west of the peninsula of Asia Minor, on a promontory now called Cape Crio, which projects between the islands of Cos and Rhodes. See (Acts 21:1) It is now in ruins.
entries.definition_ko: 소아시아 반도 남서쪽 끝, 코스섬과 로도스섬 사이로 뻗은 곶(오늘날 크리오곶)에 위치한 중요한 도시였다(사도행전 21:1). 오늘날 폐허로 남아 있다.

entries.definition: The first and most frequent use of the word rendered coal is a live ember, burning fuel. (Proverbs 26:21) In (2 Samuel 22:9,13) “coals of fire” are put metaphorically for the lightnings proceeding from God. (Psalms 18:8,12,13; 140:10) In (Proverbs 26:21) fuel not yet lighted is clearly signified. The fuel meant in the above passage is probably charcoal, and not coal in our sense of the word.
entries.definition_ko: 가장 흔한 용법은 타는 숯불, 곧 연료를 가리킨다(잠언 26:21). 사무엘하 22:9의 '불타는 숯'은 하나님으로부터 나오는 번개를 비유적으로 나타낸다. 언급되는 연료는 대개 오늘날의 석탄이 아니라 목탄으로 보인다.

entries.definition: border, with no more reference to lands bordering on the sea than to any other bordering lands.
entries.definition_ko: '경계'를 뜻하며 바다에 접한 땅이든 아니든 상관없이 쓰인다.

entries.definition: [Dress]
entries.definition_ko: 의복(DRESS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Matthew 26:34; Mark 13:35; 14:30) etc. The domestic cock and hen were early known to the ancient Greeks and Romans, and as no mention is made in the Old Testament of these birds, and no figures of them occur on the Egyptian monuments, they probably came into Judea with the Romans, who, as is well known, prized these birds both as articles of food and for cock-fighting.
entries.definition_ko: 가축화된 수탉과 암탉은 고대 헬라와 로마인들에게 일찍부터 알려졌으나 구약에는 언급이 없고 애굽 유적에도 그 형상이 없어, 식용과 투계용으로 이 새를 귀히 여긴 로마인들과 함께 유대 땅에 들어온 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: [Adder]
entries.definition_ko: 독사(ADDER) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: probably signifies bad weeds or fruit. (Job 31:40)
entries.definition_ko: 나쁜 잡초나 열매를 가리키는 것으로 추정된다(욥기 31:40).

entries.definition: (hollow Syria), the remarkable valley or hollow which intervenes between Libanus and Anti-Libanus, stretching a distance of nearly a hundred miles. The only mention of the region as a separate tract of country which the Jewish Scriptures contain is probably that in (Amos 1:5) where “the inhabitants of the plain of Aven” are threatened in conjunction with those of Damascus. The word is given in the Authorized Version as CELO-SYRIA.
entries.definition_ko: '움푹한 수리아'라는 뜻으로 레바논산과 안티레바논산 사이의 골짜기이며 길이가 거의 100마일에 이른다. 유대 성경에서 별도 지역으로 언급되는 유일한 예는 아마도 아모스 1:5의 '아웬 평지 주민들'일 것이다.

entries.definition: (argaz), a movable box hanging from the side of a cart. (1 Samuel 6:8,11,15) The word is found nowhere else.
entries.definition_ko: '아르가스'로 수레 옆에 매다는 이동식 상자이다(사무엘상 6:8). 다른 곳에는 나오지 않는 단어이다.

entries.definition: [Burial, Sepulchres]
entries.definition_ko: 장례(BURIAL, SEPULCHRES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (all-seeing), a man of the tribe of Judah in the time of Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 3:15; 11:5) (B.C. 536.)
entries.definition_ko: '모든 것을 보는 자'라는 뜻으로 느헤미야 시대 유다 지파 사람이다(느헤미야 3:15).

entries.definition: For the proper sense of this term, as it occurs in (Judges 8:26) see Earrings.
entries.definition_ko: 사사기 8:26에 쓰인 정확한 의미는 귀걸이(EARRINGS) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: In (2 Kings 22:14) it is probable that the word translated “college” represents here not an institution of learning, but that part of Jerusalem known as the “lower city” or suburb, built on the hill Akra, including the Bezetha or new city.
entries.definition_ko: 열왕기하 22:14에서 '학교'로 번역된 단어는 학문 기관이 아니라 예루살렘의 '아래 성읍', 곧 아크라 언덕 위에 세워진 교외 지역, 베데스다(신도시)를 포함한 지역을 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: a designation of Philippi, in (Acts 16:12) After the battle of Actium, Augustus assigned to his veterans those parts of Italy which had espoused the cause of Antony, and transported many of the expelled inhabitants to Philippi, Dyrrhachium and other cities. In this way Philippi was made a Roman colony with the “Jus Italicum.” At first the colonists were all Roman citizens, and entitled to vote at Rome.
entries.definition_ko: 빌립보를 가리키는 명칭이다(사도행전 16:12). 악티움 해전 후 아우구스투스가 안토니우스 편에 섰던 이탈리아 지역 주민들을 빌립보, 디라키움 등으로 이주시켜 로마 식민지로 만들었으며 처음 이주민들은 모두 로마 시민으로 로마에서 투표할 권리가 있었다.

entries.definition: The terms relative to color, occurring in the Bible, may be arranged in two classes, the first including those applied to the description of natural objects, the second those artificial mixtures which were employed in dyeing or painting. The purple and the blue were derived from a small shellfish found in the Mediterranean, and were very costly, and hence they were the royal colors. Red, both scarlet and crimson, was derived from an insect resembling the cochineal. The natural colors noticed in the Bible are white, black, red, yellow and green. The only fundamental color of which the Hebrews appear to have had a clear conception was red ; and even this is not very often noticed.
entries.definition_ko: 성경의 색채 관련 용어는 자연물 묘사와 염색·채색용 인공 혼합물 두 부류로 나뉜다. 자주색과 청색은 지중해의 작은 조개에서 얻어 매우 값비쌌으며 왕실 색이었다. 붉은색(주홍색, 진홍색)은 연지벌레와 비슷한 곤충에서 얻었다. 히브리인이 명확히 인식한 유일한 기본색은 붉은색으로 보인다.

entries.definition: more properly Colos’sae, was a city of Phrygia in Asia Minor, in the upper part of the basin of the Maeander, on the Lycus. Hierapolis and Laodicea were in its immediate neighborhood. (Colossians 1:2; 4:13,15,16) see Reve 1:11; 3:14 St. Paul is supposed by some to have visited Colosse and founded or confirmed the Colossian church on his third missionary journey. (Acts 18:23; 19:1)
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 골로새로 소아시아 프리기아 지방, 마이안더강 유역 상류, 리쿠스강가의 도시였다. 히에라볼리와 라오디게아가 인근에 있었다(골로새서 1:2). 바울은 3차 선교여행 중 골로새를 방문해 교회를 세우거나 견고하게 했을 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: was written by the apostle St. Paul during his first captivity at Rome. (Acts 28:16) (A.D. 62.) The epistle was addressed to Christians of the city of Colosse, and was delivered to them by Tychicus, whom the apostle had sent both to them, (Colossians 4:7,8) and to the church of Ephesus, (Ephesians 6:21) to inquire into their state and to administer exhortation and comfort. The main object of the epistle is to warn the Colossians against the spirit of semi-Judaistic and semi-Oriental philosophy which was corrupting the simplicity of their belief, and was noticeably tending to obscure the eternal glory and dignity of Christ. The similarity between this epistle and that to the Ephesians is striking. The latter was probably written at a later date.
entries.definition_ko: 사도 바울이 로마 첫 투옥 기간(주후 62년경) 동안 쓴 서신으로 골로새 그리스도인들에게 보내졌으며 두기고를 통해 전달되었다. 주요 목적은 반유대적·반동방적 철학 사상이 골로새인들의 순전한 믿음을 오염시켜 그리스도의 영원한 영광과 존엄을 흐리게 하는 것을 경계시키는 것이었다.

entries.definition: (John 14:16) The name given by Christ to the Holy Spirit. The original word is Paraclete, and means first Advocate, a defender, helper, strengthener, as well as comforter.
entries.definition_ko: 그리스도께서 성령께 붙이신 이름이다(요한복음 14:16). 원어는 '파라클레토스'로 본래 변호자, 옹호자, 돕는 자, 힘 주는 자, 위로자를 뜻한다.

entries.definition: From the time that men began to live in cities, trade, in some shape, must have been carried on to supply the town-dwellers with necessaries from foreign as well as native sources, for we find that Abraham was rich, not only in cattle, but in silver, gold and gold and silver plate and ornaments. (Genesis 13:2; 24:22,53) Among trading nations mentioned in Scripture, Egypt holds in very early times a prominent position. The internal trade of the Jews, as well as the external, was much promoted by the festivals, which brought large numbers of persons to Jerusalem. (1 Kings 8:63) The places of public market were chiefly the open spaces near the gates, to which goods were brought for sale by those who came from the outside. (Nehemiah 13:15,16; Zephaniah 1:10) The traders in later times were allowed to intrude into the temple, in the outer courts of which victims were publicly sold for the sacrifice. (Zechariah 14:21; Matthew 21:12; John 2:14)
entries.definition_ko: 사람들이 도시에 모여 살기 시작하면서부터 어떤 형태로든 무역이 이루어졌을 것이며, 아브라함이 가축뿐 아니라 은금과 은금 그릇, 장신구로도 부유했음을 볼 수 있다(창세기 13:2). 애굽는 성경에 언급된 무역 국가 중 이른 시기부터 두드러진 위치를 차지했다. 유대인의 내외 무역은 예루살렘에 많은 사람을 불러모은 절기들로 크게 촉진되었다.

entries.definition: (made by Jehovah), one of the chiefs of the Levites in the time of Josiah. (2 Chronicles 35:9) (B.C. 628).
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지으신'이라는 뜻으로 요시야 시대 레위인 지도자 중 하나이다(역대하 35:9).

entries.definition: The difference between wife and concubine was less marked among the Hebrews than among us, owing to the absence of moral stigma. The difference probably lay in the absence of the right of the bill of divorce, without which the wife could not be repudiated. With regard to the children of wife and of concubine, there was no such difference as our illegitimacy implies. The latter were a supplementary family to the former; their names occur in the patriarchal genealogies, (Genesis 22:24; 1 Chronicles 1:22) and their position and provision would depend on the father’s will. (Genesis 25:6) The state of concubinage is assumed and provided for by the law of Moses. A concubine would generally be either (1) a Hebrew girl bought of her father; (2) a Gentile captive taken in war; (3) a foreign slave bought; or (4) a Canaanitish woman, bond or free. The rights of the first two were protected by the law, (Exodus 21:7; 21:10-14) but the third was unrecognized and the fourth prohibited. Free Hebrew women also might become concubines. To seize on royal concubines for his use was probably the intent of Abner’s act, (2 Samuel 3:7) and similarly the request on behalf of Adonijah was construed. (1 Kings 2:21-24)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인들 사이에서 아내와 첩의 구분은 오늘날보다 도덕적 낙인이 덜했다. 그 차이는 아마도 이혼 증서를 받을 권리의 유무에 있었을 것이며, 아내와 첩의 자녀 사이에는 오늘날 사생아 개념에 해당하는 차별이 없었다. 첩은 대개 (1) 아버지에게서 사들인 히브리 소녀, (2) 전쟁에서 사로잡은 이방 포로, (3) 사들인 외국인 노예, (4) 가나안 여인(노예 또는 자유인) 중 하나였다.

entries.definition: meaning an aqueduct or trench through which water was carried. Tradition, both oral and as represented by Talmudical writers, ascribes to Solomon the formation of the original aqueduct by which water was brought to Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 물을 나르는 수로나 도랑을 가리키며 전승과 탈무드 저술가들은 예루살렘에 물을 끌어온 최초의 수로를 솔로몬이 만들었다고 본다.

entries.definition: (shaphan), a gregarious animal of the class Pachydermata, which is found in Palestine, living in the caves and clefts of the rocks, and has been erroneously identified with the rabbit or coney. Its scientific name as Hyrax syriacus . The hyrax satisfies exactly the expressions in (Psalms 104:18; Proverbs 30:26) Its color is gray or brown on the back, white on the belly; it is like the alpine marmot, scarcely of the size of the domestic cat, having long hair, a very short tail and round ears. It is found on Lebanon and in the Jordan and Dead Sea valleys.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '샤판'으로 팔레스타인 바위 틈과 동굴에 서식하는 후피동물목 동물이며 토끼와 잘못 동일시되어 왔다. 학명은 히락스 수리아쿠스이며 등은 회색 또는 갈색, 배는 흰색이고 알프스 마못과 비슷하나 집고양이만 하며 긴 털과 매우 짧은 꼬리, 둥근 귀를 지녔다.

entries.definition: This describes the Hebrew people in its collective capacity under its peculiar aspect as a holy community, held together by religious rather than political bonds. Sometimes it is used in a broad sense as inclusive of foreign settlers, (Exodus 12:19) but more properly as exclusively appropriate to the Hebrew element of the population. (Numbers 15:15) The congregation was governed by the father or head of each family and tribe. The number of these representatives being inconveniently large for ordinary business, a further selection was made by Moses of 70, who formed a species of standing committee. (Numbers 11:16) Occasionally indeed the whole body of people was assembled at the door of the tabernacle, hence usually called the tabernacle of the congregation. (Numbers 10:3) The people were strictly bound by the acts of their representatives, even in cases where they disapproved of them. (Joshua 9:18)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리 백성 전체를 종교적 유대로 결속된 거룩한 공동체로서 집합적으로 가리키는 말이다. 각 가문과 지파의 아버지 또는 우두머리가 회중을 대표했으며, 대표자 수가 너무 많아 모세가 별도로 70인을 선발해 상임위원회 역할을 하게 했다(민수기 11:16).

entries.definition: [Jeconiah]
entries.definition_ko: 여고냐(JECONIAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (appointed by the Lord), a Levite, ruler of the offerings and tithes in the time of Hezekiah. (2 Chronicles 31:12,13) (B.C. 726.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 임명하신'이라는 뜻으로 히스기야 시대 헌물과 십일조를 관리한 레위인이다(역대하 31:12).

entries.definition: [Priest]
entries.definition_ko: 제사장(PRIEST) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: This term (with one exception)— (Isaiah 1:13) is applied invariably to meetings of a religious character, in contradistinction to congregation.
entries.definition_ko: 이사야 1:13의 예외를 제외하고 항상 종교적 성격의 모임을 가리키며 '회중'과 구별된다.

entries.definition: As meet did not form an article of ordinary diet among the Jews, the art of cooking was not carried to any perfection. Few animals were slaughtered except for purposes of hospitality or festivity. The proceedings on such occasions appear to have been as follows:—On the arrival of a guest, the animal, either a kid, lamb or calf, was killed, (Genesis 18:7; Luke 15:23) its throat being cut so that the blood might be poured out, (Leviticus 7:26) it was then flayed, and was ready for either roasting or boiling. In the former case the animal was preserved entire, (Exodus 12:46) and roasted either over a fire, (Exodus 12:8) of wood, (Isaiah 44:16) or perhaps in an oven, consisting simply of a hole dug in the earth, well heated, and covered up. Boiling, however, was the more usual method of cooking.
entries.definition_ko: 유대인들 사이에서 고기는 일상 식단의 일부가 아니었으므로 요리 기술은 그다지 발달하지 않았다. 짐승은 손님 접대나 잔치를 위해서만 도살되었으며, 손님이 도착하면 새끼 염소나 어린양, 송아지를 잡아 피를 뺀 뒤 가죽을 벗겨 굽거나 삶았다. 삶는 것이 더 일반적인 조리법이었다.

entries.definition: (Acts 21:1) [Cos, Or Coos]
entries.definition_ko: 고스(COS, OR COOS) 항목 참조(사도행전 21:1).

entries.definition: Heb. nechosheth, in the Authorized Version always rendered “brass,” except in (Ezra 8:27) and Jere 15:12It was almost exclusively used by the ancients for common purposes, and for every kind of instrument, as chains, pillars, lavers and the other temple vessels. We read also of copper mirrors, (Exodus 38:8) and even of copper arms, as helmets, spears, etc. (1 Samuel 17:5,6,38; 2 Samuel 21:16)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '네호셋'으로 흠정역에서는 대개 '놋쇠'로 번역되나 대부분 실제로는 구리를 가리킨다. 고대인들은 사슬, 기둥, 물두멍 등 성전 기구와 일상 도구, 거울(출애굽기 38:8), 무기(사무엘상 17:5)에 거의 전적으로 구리를 사용했다.

entries.definition: (Ezekiel 27:16) A production of the sea, formed by minute animals called zoophytes. It is their shell or house. It takes various forms, as of trees, shrubs, hemispheres. The principal colors are red and white. It was used for beads and ornaments. With regard to the estimation in which coral was held by the Jews and other Orientals, it must be remembered that coral varies in price with us. Pliny says that the Indians valued coral as the Romans valued pearls. (Job 28:18)
entries.definition_ko: 바닷속 미세한 동물인 산호충이 만드는 산물이다(에스겔 27:16). 나무, 관목, 반구형 등 다양한 형태를 이루며 주로 붉은색과 흰색을 띠고 장신구와 구슬에 쓰였다. 플리니우스는 인도인들이 산호를 로마인들이 진주를 귀히 여기듯 여겼다고 기록한다(욥기 28:18).

entries.definition: an offering to God of any sort, bloody or bloodless, but particularly in fulfillment of a vow. The law laid down rules for vows, (1) affirmative; (2) negative. (Leviticus 27:1; Numbers 30:1) ... Upon these rules the traditionists enlarged, and laid down that a man might interdict himself by vow, not only from using for himself, bur from giving to another or receiving from him, some particular object, whether of food or any other kind whatsoever. The thing thus interdicted was considered as corban . A person might thus exempt himself from any inconvenient obligation under plea of corban. It was practices of this sort that our Lord reprehended, (Matthew 15:5; Mark 7:11) as annulling the spirit of the law.
entries.definition_ko: 하나님께 드리는 모든 종류의 예물, 특히 서원 성취를 위한 예물을 가리킨다. 율법은 서원에 관한 규정을 두었으며(레위기 27:1) 후대 전통가들은 이를 확대해, 사람이 서원으로 어떤 물건을 자신이 쓰거나 남에게 주거나 받는 것을 금할 수 있다고 규정했다. 그렇게 금지된 것을 '고르반'이라 여겼으며 사람들은 이 명목으로 불편한 의무를 회피할 수 있었다. 주님은 이런 관행이 율법의 정신을 무효화한다고 책망하셨다(마태복음 15:5).

entries.definition: The materials of which cord was made varied according to the strength required; the strongest rope was probably made of strips of camel hide, as still used by the Bedouins. The finer sorts were made of flax, (Isaiah 19:9) and probably of reeds and rushes. In the New Testament the term is applied to the whip which our Saviour made, (John 2:15) and to the ropes of a ship. (Acts 27:32)
entries.definition_ko: 밧줄의 재료는 필요한 강도에 따라 달랐으며 가장 강한 밧줄은 낙타 가죽 끈으로 만들어 오늘날 베두인들도 여전히 사용한다. 더 고운 종류는 아마(이사야 19:9)나 갈대, 골풀로 만들었다. 신약에서는 주님이 만드신 채찍(요한복음 2:15)과 배의 밧줄(사도행전 27:32)에도 이 단어가 쓰인다.

entries.definition: (Jude 1:11) [Korah, 1]
entries.definition_ko: 고라(KORAH) 1번 항목 참조(유다서 1:11).

entries.definition: The plant called Coriandrum sativum is found in Egypt, Persia and India, and has a round tall stalk; it bears umbelliferous white or reddish flowers, from which arise globular, grayish, spicy seed-corns, marked with fine striae. It is mentioned twice in the Bible. (Exodus 16:31; Numbers 11:7)
entries.definition_ko: '코리안드룸 사티붐'이라는 식물로 애굽, 바사, 인도에서 자라며 둥글고 키가 크고 우산 모양의 흰색 또는 붉은빛 꽃이 피고 회색의 향신료 씨앗을 맺는다. 성경에 두 번 언급된다(출애굽기 16:31).

entries.definition: an ancient and celebrated city of Greece, on the Isthmus of Corinth, and about 40 miles west of Athens. In consequence of its geographical position it formed the most direct communication between the Ionian and AEgean seas. A remarkable feature was the AcroCorinthus, a vast citadel of rock, which rises abruptly to the height of 2000 feet above the level of the sea, and the summit of which is so extensive that it once contained a whole town. The situation of Corinth, and the possession of its eastern and western harbors, Cenchreae and Lechaeum, are the secrets of its history. Corinth was a place of great mental activity, as well as of commercial and manufacturing enterprise. Its wealth was so celebrated as to be proverbial; so were the vice and profligacy of its inhabitants. The worship of Venus where was attended with shameful licentiousness. Corinth is still an episcopal see. The city has now shrunk to a wretched village, ont he old site and bearing the old name, which, however, is corrupted into Gortho . St. Paul preached here, (Acts 18:11) and founded a church, to which his Epistles to the Corinthians are addressed. [EPISTLES TO THE Corinthians, First Epistle To The, Corinthians, Second Epistle To The]
entries.definition_ko: 고린도 지협에 위치한 헬라의 유서 깊은 도시로 아덴에서 서쪽으로 약 40마일 떨어져 있다. 이오니아해와 에게해를 잇는 최단 교통로였으며 해발 2000피트까지 솟은 거대한 바위 요새 아크로고린도스가 특징이다. 동쪽 항구 겐그레아와 서쪽 항구 레카이온을 보유해 상업과 제조업이 번성했으며 부유함으로 유명한 만큼 주민들의 방탕함으로도 악명 높았다. 바울이 이곳에서 전도하여(사도행전 18:11) 교회를 세웠고 고린도 서신들이 이 교회에 보내졌다.

entries.definition: was written by the apostle St. Paul toward the close of his nearly three-years stay at Ephesus, (Acts 19:10; 20:31) which, we learn from (1 Corinthians 16:8) probably terminated with the Pentecost of A.D. 57 or 58. The bearers were probably (according to the common subscription) Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus. It appears to have been called forth by the information the apostles had received of dissension in the Corinthian church, which may be thus explained:—The Corinthian church was planted by the apostle himself, (1 Corinthians 3:6) in his second missionary journey. (Acts 18:1) seq. He abode in the city a year and a half. (Acts 18:11) A short time after the apostle had left the city the eloquent Jew of Alexandria, Apollos, went to Corinth, (Acts 19:1) and gained many followers, dividing the church into two parties, the followers of Paul and the followers of Apollos. Later on Judaizing teachers from Jerusalem preached the gospel in a spirit of direct antagonism to St. Paul personally. To this third party we may perhaps add a fourth, that, under the name of “the followers of Christ,” (1 Corinthians 2:12) sought at first to separate themselves from the factious adherence to particular teachers, but eventually were driven by antagonism into positions equally sectarian and inimical to the unity of the church. At this momentous period, before parties had become consolidated and that distinctly withdrawn from communion with one another, the apostle writes; and in the outset of the epistle, 1Cor 1-4:21, we have this noble and impassioned protest against this fourfold rending of the robe of Christ.
entries.definition_ko: 사도 바울이 에베소에 거의 3년간 머문 시기 말엽에 쓴 것으로 주후 57 또는 58년 오순절 무렵 끝난 것으로 추정된다. 스데바나, 브드나도, 아가이고가 편지를 전달했을 것으로 보인다. 바울이 2차 선교여행 중 세운 고린도 교회에(사도행전 18:1) 분열이 생겼다는 소식을 듣고 쓴 것으로, 바울파와 아볼로파, 유대주의 교사들을 따르는 파, '그리스도파'로 나뉜 파벌 문제를 다룬다.

entries.definition: was written a few months subsequent to the first, in the same year—about the autumn of A.D. 57 or 58—at Macedonia. The epistle was occasioned by the information which the apostle had received form Titus, and also, as it would certainly seem probable, from Timothy, of the reception of the first epistle. This information, as it would seem from our present epistle, was mainly favorable; the better part of the church were returning to their spiritual allegiance to the founder, (2 Corinthians 1:13,14; 7:9,15,16) but there was still a faction who strenuously denied Paul’s claim to apostleship. The contents of this epistle comprise, (1) the apostle’s account of the character of his spiritual labors, chs. 1-7; (2) directions about the collections, chs. 8,9; (3) defence of his own apostolical character, chs. 10-13:10. The words in (1 Corinthians 5:9) seem to point to further epistles to the church by Paul, but we have no positive evidence of any.
entries.definition_ko: 첫 서신 몇 달 후, 같은 해 가을(주후 57~58년경) 마케도니아에서 쓰였다. 디도(그리고 아마도 디모데)로부터 첫 서신을 받아들인 소식을 듣고 쓴 것으로, 대체로 긍정적이었으나 여전히 바울의 사도직을 부인하는 파벌이 남아 있었다. 내용은 자신의 영적 사역에 대한 설명, 헌금에 관한 지침, 자신의 사도적 권위에 대한 변호로 구성된다.

entries.definition: the representative in the Authorized Version of the Hebrew words kaath and shalac . As to the former, see Pelican. Shalac occurs only as the name of an unclean bird in (Leviticus 11:17; 14:17) The word has been variously rendered. The etymology points to some plunging bird. The common cormorant (phalacrocorax carbo), which some writers have identified with the shalac, is unknown in the eastern Mediterranean; another species is found south of the Red Sea, but none on the west coast of Palestine.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '카아트'와 '샬라크'를 흠정역이 이 단어로 옮겼다. '샬라크'는 레위기 11:17 등에서 부정한 새의 이름으로만 나오며 어원상 물속으로 뛰어드는 새를 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: The most common kinds were wheat, barley, spelt, Authorized Version, (Exodus 9:32) and Isai 28:25“Rye;” (Ezekiel 4:9) “fitches” and millet; oats are mentioned only by rabbinical writers. Our Indian corn was unknown in Bible times. Corn-crops are still reckoned at twentyfold what was sown, and were anciently much more. (Genesis 41:22) The Jewish law permitted any one in passing through a filed of standing corn to pluck and eat. (23:25) see also Matt 12:1From Solomon’s time, (2 Chronicles 2:10,15) as agriculture became developed under a settled government, Palestine was a cornexporting country, and her grain was largely taken by her commercial neighbor Tyre. (Ezekiel 27:17) comp. Amos 8:5
entries.definition_ko: 가장 흔한 곡물은 밀, 보리, 스펠트('호밀', 출애굽기 9:32), 조 등이었으며 귀리는 랍비 문헌에만 언급된다. 오늘날의 옥수수는 성경 시대에 알려지지 않았다. 유대 율법은 지나가는 사람이 서 있는 곡식 밭에서 이삭을 뜯어 먹는 것을 허용했다(신명기 23:25). 솔로몬 시대부터 팔레스타인은 곡물 수출국이 되었고 그 곡물 상당량이 상업 이웃 두로로 갔다(에스겔 27:17).

entries.definition: (of a horn), a Roman centurion of the Italian cohort stationed in Caesarea, (Acts 10:1) etc., a man full of good works and alms-deeds. With his household he was baptized by St. Peter, and thus Cornelius became the firstfruits of the Gentile world to Christ.
entries.definition_ko: '뿔의'라는 뜻으로 가이사랴에 주둔한 이탈리아 부대의 로마 백부장이며(사도행전 10:1) 선행과 구제에 힘쓴 사람이었다. 온 집안과 함께 베드로에게 세례를 받아 이방 세계에서 그리스도께 돌아온 첫 열매가 되었다.

entries.definition: The “corner” of the field was not allowed, (Leviticus 19:9) to be wholly reaped. It formed a right of the poor to carry off what was so left, and this was a part of the maintenance from the soil to which that class were entitled. Under the scribes, minute legislation fixed one-sixtieth as the portion of a field which was to be left for the legal “corner.” The proportion being thus fixed, all the grain might be reaped, and enough to satisfy the regulation subsequently separated from the whole crop. This “corner” was, like the gleaning, tithe-free.
entries.definition_ko: 밭의 '모퉁이'는 완전히 거두지 못하게 했으며(레위기 19:9) 가난한 자들이 그것을 거둘 권리가 있었다. 후대 서기관들은 밭의 60분의 1을 법적 '모퉁이'로 남기도록 세밀하게 규정했다.

entries.definition: a quoin or cornerstone, of great importance in binding together the sides of a building. The phrase “corner-stone” is sometimes used to denote any principal person, as the princes of Egypt, (Isaiah 19:13) and is thus applied to our Lord. (Isaiah 28:16; Matthew 21:42; 1 Peter 2:6,7)
entries.definition_ko: 건물의 양 벽을 결합하는 데 매우 중요한 모퉁잇돌을 가리킨다. '모퉁잇돌'이라는 표현은 애굽의 방백들처럼(이사야 19:13) 중요한 인물을 가리키는 데도 쓰이며 주님께 적용되기도 한다(이사야 28:16).

entries.definition: (Heb. shophar), a loud-sounding instrument, made of the horn of a ram or a chamois (sometimes of an ox), and used by the ancient Hebrews for signals, (Leviticus 25:9) and much used by the priests. (1 Chronicles 15:28)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '쇼파르'로 숫양이나 샤무아(때로는 소)의 뿔로 만든 큰 소리를 내는 악기이며 고대 히브리인들이 신호용으로 사용했고(레위기 25:9) 제사장들도 많이 사용했다(역대상 15:28).

entries.definition: (now Stanchio or Stanko). This small island of the Grecian Archipelago has several interesting points of connection with the Jews. Herod the Great conferred many favors on the island. St. Paul, on the return from his third missionary journey, passed the night here, after sailing from Miletus. Probably referred to in (Acts 21:1)
entries.definition_ko: 오늘날의 스탄키오 또는 스탄코로 헬라 군도의 작은 섬이며 헤롯 대왕이 여러 은혜를 베풀었다. 바울이 3차 선교여행 귀환길에 밀레도에서 항해해 이곳에서 밤을 보냈다(사도행전 21:1).

entries.definition: (a diviner), son of Elmodam, in the line of Joseph the husband of Mary. (Luke 3:28)
entries.definition_ko: '점술가'라는 뜻으로 마리아의 남편 요셉 계보에서 엘모담의 아들이다(누가복음 3:28).

entries.definition: Cotton is now both grown and manufactured in various parts of Syria and Palestine; but there is no proof that, till they came in contact with Persia, the Hebrews generally knew of it as a distinct fabric from linen. [Linen]
entries.definition_ko: 오늘날 수리아와 팔레스타인 여러 지역에서 재배·제조되나 바사와 접촉하기 전 히브리인들이 이를 아마포와 구별되는 별도 직물로 알았다는 증거는 없다.

entries.definition: [Bed]
entries.definition_ko: 침상(BED) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: • The great council of the Sanhedrin, which sat at Jerusalem. [Sanhedrin] • The lesser courts, (Matthew 10:17; Mark 13:9) of which there were two at Jerusalem and one in each town of Palestine. The constitution of these courts is a doubtful point. The existence of local courts, however constituted, is clearly implied in the passages quoted from the New Testament; and perhaps the “judgment,” (Matthew 5:21) applies to them. • A kind of jury or privy council, (Acts 25:12) consisting of a certain number of assessors, who assisted Roman governors in the administration of justice and in other public matters.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘에 있던 대공회 산헤드린(SANHEDRIN)과, 예루살렘에 둘, 팔레스타인 각 마을마다 하나씩 있던 소법정(마태복음 10:17), 그리고 로마 총독의 사법 행정을 돕던 배심원단 성격의 자문단(사도행전 25:12)이 있었다.

entries.definition: (Heb. chatser), an open enclosure surrounded by buildings, applied in the Authorized Version most commonly to the enclosures of the tabernacle and the temple. (Exodus 27:9; 40:33; Leviticus 6:16; 1 Kings 6:36; 7:8; 2 Kings 23:12; 2 Chronicles 33:5) etc.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '하체르'로 건물로 둘러싸인 개방된 구역을 가리키며 흠정역에서는 대개 성막과 성전의 뜰을 가리키는 데 쓰인다(출애굽기 27:9).

entries.definition: The Heb. berith means primarily “a cutting,” with reference to the custom of cutting or dividing animals in two and passing between the parts in ratifying a covenant. (Genesis 15; Jeremiah 34:18,19) In the New Testament the corresponding word is diathece (diatheke), which is frequently translated testament in the Authorized Version. In its biblical meaning two parties the word is used— • Of a covenant between God and man; e.g. God covenanted with Noah, after the flood, that a like judgment should not be repeated. It is not precisely like a covenant between men, but was a promise or agreement by God. The principal covenants are the covenant of works—God promising to save and bless men on condition of perfect obedience—and the covenant of grace, or God’s promise to save men on condition of their believing in Christ and receiving him as their Master and Saviour. The first is called the Old Covenant, from which we name the first part of the bible the Old Testament, the Latin rendering of the word covenant. The second is called the New Covenant, or New Testament. • Covenant between man and man, i.e. a solemn compact or agreement, either between tribes or nations, (Joshua 9:6,15; 1 Samuel 11:1) or between individuals, (Genesis 31:44) by which each party bound himself to fulfill certain conditions and was assured of receiving certain advantages. In making such a covenant God was solemnly invoked as witness, (Genesis 31:50) and an oath was sworn. (Genesis 21:31) A sign or witness of the covenant was sometimes framed, such a gift, (Genesis 21:30) or a pillar or heap of stones erected. (Genesis 31:52)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '베리트'는 본래 '자르는 것'을 뜻하며 짐승을 둘로 나누어 그 사이를 지나며 언약을 맺던 관습에서 유래했다(창세기 15장). 신약의 대응어 '디아테케'는 흠정역에서 자주 '유언'으로 번역된다. 하나님과 사람 사이의 언약(행위 언약, 은혜 언약)과 사람과 사람 사이의 언약(부족·국가 간, 개인 간)으로 나뉜다.

entries.definition: [Bull, Bullock]
entries.definition_ko: 소(BULL, BULLOCK) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (thorn), a man among the descendants of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:8)
entries.definition_ko: '가시'라는 뜻으로 유다 후손 중 하나이다(역대상 4:8).

entries.definition: (deceitful), daughter of Zur, a chief of the Midianites. (Numbers 25:15,18)
entries.definition_ko: '속이는'이라는 뜻으로 미디안 방백 술의 딸이다(민수기 25:15).

entries.definition: The crane (Grus cinerea) is a native of Europe and Asia. It stand about four feet high. Its color is ashen gray, with face and neck nearly black. It feeds on seeds, roots, insects and small quadrupeds. It retires in winter to the warmer climates. (Jeremiah 8:7)
entries.definition_ko: 유럽과 아시아 원산의 새로(그루스 시네레아) 키는 약 4피트이며 색은 잿빛 회색에 얼굴과 목은 거의 검다. 씨앗, 뿌리, 곤충, 작은 짐승을 먹으며 겨울에는 더 따뜻한 지역으로 이동한다(예레미야 8:7).

entries.definition: To create is to cause something to exist which did not exist before, as distinguished from make, to re-form something already in existence.
entries.definition_ko: 이전에 존재하지 않던 것을 존재하게 하는 것으로, 이미 존재하는 것을 다시 형성하는 '만들다'와 구별된다.

entries.definition: (The creation of all things is ascribed in the Bible to God, and is the only reasonable account of the origin of the world. The method of creation is not stated in Genesis, and as far as the account there is concerned, each part of it may be, after the first acts of creation, by evolution, or by direct act of God’s will. The word create (bara) is used but three times in the first chapter of Genesis— (1) as to the origin of matter; (2) as to the origin of life; (3) as to the origin of man’s soul; and science has always failed to do any of these acts thus ascribed to God. All other things are said to be made . The order of creation as given in Genesis is in close harmony with the order as revealed by geology, truth discoverable by man, is one of the strongest proofs that the Bible was inspired by God.—Ed.)
entries.definition_ko: 만물의 창조는 성경에서 하나님께 돌려지며 세상 기원에 대한 유일한 합리적 설명이다. 창세기는 창조의 방법을 명시하지 않으며 최초의 창조 행위 이후 각 부분은 진화나 하나님의 직접적 의지로 이루어졌을 수 있다. '창조하다'(바라)라는 단어는 창세기 1장에서 물질의 기원, 생명의 기원, 인간 영혼의 기원, 이렇게 세 번만 쓰이며 그 외에는 모두 '만들다'로 표현된다.

entries.definition: [Loan]
entries.definition_ko: 대출(LOAN) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (growing), (2 Timothy 4:10) an assistant of St. Paul, said to have been one of the seventy disciples.
entries.definition_ko: '자라는'이라는 뜻으로(디모데후서 4:10) 바울의 조력자이며 70인 제자 중 하나였다고 전해진다.

entries.definition: the modern Candia. This large island, which closes int he Greek Archipelago on the south, extends through a distance of 140 miles between its extreme points. Though exceedingly bold and mountainous, this island has very fruitful valleys, and in early times it was celebrated for its hundred cities. It seems likely that a very early acquaintances existed between the Cretans and the Jews. Cretans, (Acts 2:11) were among those who were at Jerusalem at the great Pentecost. In [Acts 27:7-12We have an account of Paul’s shipwreck near this island; and it is evident from (Titus 1:5) that the apostle himself was here at no long interval of time before he wrote the letter. The Cretans were proverbial liars. (Titus 1:12)
entries.definition_ko: 오늘날의 칸디아로 헬라 군도 남쪽을 막는 큰 섬이며 길이 140마일에 이른다. 산악 지형이지만 비옥한 골짜기가 있어 옛날에는 백 개의 도시로 유명했다. 오순절에 예루살렘에 있던 사람들 중 그레데인도 있었으며(사도행전 2:11) 바울이 이 섬 근처에서 파선당했고(사도행전 27:7) 디도에게 보낸 편지로 보아 그 직전에 이 섬에 있었던 것으로 보인다. 그레데인은 거짓말쟁이로 유명했다(디도서 1:12).

entries.definition: (Acts 2:11) Cretans, inhabitants of Crete.
entries.definition_ko: 그레데(CRETE) 섬 주민을 가리킨다(사도행전 2:11).

entries.definition: (Isaiah 3:22) The original word means some kind of female ornament, probably a reticule or richly ornamented purse, often made of silk inwrought with gold or silver.
entries.definition_ko: 이사야 3:22에 언급되며 원어는 여성용 장신구, 아마도 금실이나 은실로 수놓은 화려한 손가방을 가리키는 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (curled), ruler of the Jewish synagogue at Corinth, (Acts 18:8) baptized with his family by St. Paul. (1 Corinthians 1:14) (A.D. 50.)
entries.definition_ko: '곱슬머리'라는 뜻으로 고린도 회당장이며(사도행전 18:8) 온 가족과 함께 바울에게 세례받았다(고린도전서 1:14).

entries.definition: As the emblem of a slave’s death and a murderer’s punishment, the cross was naturally looked upon with the profoundest horror. But after the celebrated vision of Constantine, he ordered his friends to make a cross of gold and gems, such as he had seen, and “the towering eagles resigned the flags unto the cross,” and “the tree of cursing and shame” “sat upon the sceptres and was engraved and signed on the foreheads of kings.” (Jer. Taylor, “Life of Christ,” iii., xv. 1.) The new standards were called by the name Labarum, and may be seen on the coins of Constantine the Great and his nearer successors. The Latin cross on which our Lord suffered, was int he form of the letter T, and had an upright above the cross-bar, on which the “title” was placed. There was a projection from the central stem, on which the body of the sufferer rested. This was to prevent the weight of the body from tearing away the hands. Whether there was also a support to the feet (as we see in pictures) is doubtful. An inscription was generally placed above the criminal’s head, briefly expressing his guilt, and generally was carried before him. It was covered with white gypsum, and the letter were black.
entries.definition_ko: 노예의 죽음과 살인자의 형벌의 상징으로 십자가는 본래 극도의 공포로 여겨졌으나 콘스탄티누스의 환상 이후 로마의 상징이 되었다. 주님이 고난받으신 라틴식 십자가는 T자 형태였으며 죄패를 놓을 수직 기둥이 가로대 위로 솟아 있었고, 몸을 지탱하는 중앙 돌출부가 있어 손이 체중에 찢기지 않게 했다.

entries.definition: This ornament, which is both ancient and universal, probably originated from the fillets used to prevent the hair from being dishevelled by the wind. Such fillets are still common; they gradually developed into turbans, which by the addition of ornamental or precious materials assumed the dignity of mitres or crowns. Both the ordinary priests and the high priest wore them. The crown was a symbol of royalty, and was worn by kings, (2 Chronicles 23:11) and also by queens. (Esther 2:17) The head-dress of bridegrooms, (Ezekiel 24:17; Isaiah 61:10) Bar. 5:2, and of women, (Isaiah 3:20) a head-dress of great splendor, (Isaiah 28:5) a wreath of flowers, (Proverbs 1:9; 4:9) denote crowns. In general we must attach to it the notion of a costly turban irradiated with pearls and gems of priceless value, which often form aigrettes for feathers, as in the crowns of modern Asiatics sovereigns. Such was probably the crown which weighed (or rather “was worth”) a talent, mentioned in (2 Samuel 12:30) taken by David from the king of Ammon at Rabbah, and used as the state crown of Judah. (2 Samuel 12:30) In (Revelation 12:3; 19:12) allusion is made to “many crowns” worn in token of extended dominion. The laurel, pine or parsley crowns given to victors int he great games of Greece are finely alluded to by St. Paul. (1 Corinthians 9:25; 2 Timothy 2:5) etc.
entries.definition_ko: 고대부터 보편적으로 쓰인 장신구로 바람에 머리카락이 흐트러지지 않게 하는 머리띠에서 유래한 것으로 추정된다. 점차 터번으로 발전했고 장식 재료가 더해지며 관의 위엄을 갖추게 되었다. 왕관은 왕권의 상징으로 왕과 왕후 모두 착용했으며(역대하 23:11), 신랑의 머리 장식(에스겔 24:17), 화관(잠언 1:9) 등도 이 단어로 표현된다.

entries.definition: (Matthew 27:29) Our Lord was crowned with thorns in mockery by the Roman soldiers. Obviously some small flexile thorny shrub is meant perhaps Capparis spinosa. “Hasselquist, a Swedish naturalist, supposes a very common plant naba or nubka of the Arabs, with many small and sharp sines; soft, round and pliant branches; leaves much resembling ivy, of a very deep green, as if in designed mockery of a victor’s wreath.”—Alford.
entries.definition_ko: 로마 병사들이 조롱의 뜻으로 주님께 씌운 가시관이다(마태복음 27:29). 작고 유연한 가시 관목, 아마도 카파리스 스피노사가 쓰였을 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: was in used among the Egyptians, (Genesis 40:19) the Carthaginians, the Persians, (Esther 7:10) the Assyrians, Scythains, Indians, Germans, and from the earliest times among the Greeks and Romans. Whether this mode of execution was known to the ancient Jews is a matter of dispute. Probably the Jews borrowed it from the Romans. It was unanimously considered the most horrible form of death. Among the Romans the degradation was also a part of the infliction, and the punishment if applied to freemen was only used in the case of the vilest criminals. The one to be crucified was stripped naked of all his clothes, and then followed the most awful moment of all. He was laid down upon the implement of torture. His arms were stretched along the crossbeams, and at the centre of the open palms the point of a huge iron nail was placed, which, by the blow of a mallet, was driven home into the wood. Then through either foot separately, or possibly through both together, as they were placed one over the other, another huge nail tore its way through the quivering flesh. Whether the sufferer was also bound to the cross we do not know; but, to prevent the hands and feet being torn away by the weight of the body, which could not “rest upon nothing but four great wounds,” there was, about the centre of the cross, a wooden projection strong enough to support, at least in part, a human body, which soon became a weight of agony. Then the “accursed tree” with its living human burden was slowly heaved up and the end fixed firmly in a hole in the ground. The feet were but a little raised above the earth. The victim was in full reach of every hand that might choose to strike. A death by crucifixion seems to include all that pain and death can have of the horrible and ghastly,—dizziness, cramp, thirst, starvation, sleeplessness, traumatic fever, tetanus, publicity of shame, long continuance of torment, horror of anticipation, mortification of untended wounds, all intensified just up to the point at which they can be endured at all, but all stopping just short of the point which would give to the sufferer the relief of unconsciousness. The unnatural position made every movement painful; the lacerated veins and crushed tendons throbbed with incessant anguish; the wounds, inflamed by exposure, gradually gangrened; the arteries, especially of the head and stomach, became swollen and oppressed with surcharged blood; and, while each variety of misery went on gradually increasing, there was added to them the intolerable pang of a burning and raging thirst. Such was the death to which Christ was doomed.—Farrar’s “Life of Christ. ” The crucified was watched, according to custom, by a party of four soldiers, (John 19:23) with their centurion, (Matthew 27:66) whose express office was to prevent the stealing of the body. This was necessary from the lingering character of the death, which sometimes did not supervene even for three days, and was at last the result of gradual benumbing and starvation. But for this guard, the persons might have been taken down and recovered, as was actually done in the case of a friend of Josephus. Fracture of the legs was especially adopted by the Jews to hasten death. (John 19:31) In most cases the body was suffered to rot on the cross by the action of sun and rain, or to be devoured by birds and beasts. Sepulture was generally therefore forbidden; but in consequence of (21:22,23) an express national exception was made in favor of the Jews. (Matthew 27:58) This accursed and awful mode of punishment was happily abolished by Constantine.
entries.definition_ko: 애굽 사람(창세기 40:19), 카르타고인, 바사인(에스더 7:10), 앗수르인, 스키타이인, 인도인, 게르만족, 그리고 고대 헬라와 로마인들 사이에서 쓰인 처형 방식이다. 로마인들 사이에서는 굴욕도 형벌의 일부였으며 자유인에게 적용될 경우 가장 흉악한 범죄자에게만 쓰였다. 십자가형은 어지러움, 경련, 갈증, 굶주림, 불면, 외상열, 파상풍, 수치의 공개성, 오랜 고통 지속 등 인간이 겪을 수 있는 거의 모든 고통을 포함했다. 십자가 처형자는 시신 도난을 막기 위해 백부장을 포함한 네 명의 병사에게 감시받았으며(요한복음 19:23), 유대인들은 죽음을 앞당기기 위해 다리를 꺾는 방법을 특히 사용했다(요한복음 19:31). 이 저주받고 끔찍한 처형 방식은 콘스탄티누스에 의해 폐지되었다.

entries.definition: a small vessel for holding water, such as was carried by Saul when on his night expedition after David, (1 Samuel 26:11,12,16) and by Elijah. (1 Kings 19:6)
entries.definition_ko: 물을 담는 작은 그릇으로 사울이 다윗을 쫓던 밤 원정 때(사무엘상 26:11)와 엘리야가(열왕기상 19:6) 지니고 다닌 것으로 언급된다.

entries.definition: the representative in the Authorized Version of two Hebrew words. • Zecucith occurs only in (Job 28:17) where “glass” probably is intended. • kerach occurs in numerous passages in the Old Testament to denote “ice,” “frost,” etc.; but once only (Ezekiel 1:22) as is generally understood, to signify “crystal.” The ancients supposed rock-crystal to be merely ice congealed by intense cold. The similarity of appearance between ice and crystal caused no doubt the identity of the terms to express these substances. The Greek word occurs in (Revelation 4:6; 21:1) It may mean either “ice” or “crystal.”
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서 두 히브리어 단어를 나타낸다. '제쿠키트'는 욥기 28:17에만 나오며 '유리'를 뜻하는 것으로 추정되고, '케라흐'는 대개 '얼음, 서리'를 뜻하나 에스겔 1:22에서만 '수정'을 가리키는 것으로 이해된다. 고대인들은 수정을 극심한 추위로 얼어붙은 얼음으로 여겼다.

entries.definition: [Weights And MeasuresAND Measures]
entries.definition_ko: 도량형(WEIGHTS AND MEASURES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (Leviticus 11:16; 14:15) the name of some of the larger petrels which abound in the east of the Mediterranean.
entries.definition_ko: 지중해 동부에 흔한 대형 슴새류의 일종을 가리킨다(레위기 11:16).

entries.definition: (Heb. kishshuim). This word occurs in (Numbers 11:5) as one of the good things of Egypt produces excellent cucumbers, melons, etc., the Cucumis chate being the best of its tribe yet known. Besides the Cucumis chate, the common cucumber (C. sativus), of which the Arabs distinguish a number of varieties, is common in Egypt. “Both Cucumis chate and C. sativus,” says Mr. Tristram, “are now grown in great quantities in Palestine. On visiting the Arab school in Jerusalem (1858) I observed that the dinner which the children brought with them to school consisted, without exception, of a piece of barley cake and a raw cucumber, which they ate rind and all.” The “lodge in a garden of cucumbers,” (Isaiah 1:8) is a rude temporary shelter erected int eh open grounds where vines, cucumbers, gourds, etc., are grown, in which some lonely man or boy is set to watch, either to guard the plants from robbers or to scare away the foxes and jackals from the vines.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '키슈임'으로 민수기 11:5에서 애굽의 좋은 것들 중 하나로 언급된다. 애굽는 훌륭한 오이와 멜론을 생산했으며 오늘날에도 팔레스타인에서 대량 재배된다. '참외밭의 원두막'(이사야 1:8)은 포도, 오이, 박 등이 자라는 노지에 세운 임시 거처로 도둑이나 여우, 자칼로부터 작물을 지키기 위해 지어졌다.

entries.definition: one of the cultivated plants of Palestine. (Isaiah 28:25,27; Matthew 23:23) It is an umbelliferous plant something like fennel. The seeds have a bitterish warm taste and an aromatic flavor. The Maltese are said to grow it at the present day, and to thresh it in the manner described by Isaiah.
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인에서 재배된 식물 중 하나로(이사야 28:25) 회향과 비슷한 미나리과 식물이며 씨앗은 쌉쌀하면서 따뜻한 맛과 향기로운 풍미를 지닌다.

entries.definition: The cups of the Jews, whether of metal or earthenware, were possibly borrowed, in point of shape and design, from Egypt and from the Phoenicians, who were celebrated in that branch of workmanship. Egyptian cups were of various shapes, either with handles or without them. In Solomon’s time all his drinking vessels were of gold, none of silver. (1 Kings 10:21) Babylon is compared to a golden cup. (Jeremiah 51:7) The great laver, or “sea,” was made with a rim like the rim of a cup (cos), with flowers of lilies,” (1 Kings 7:26) a form which the Persepolitan cups resemble. The cups of the New Testament were often no doubt formed on Greek and Roman models. They were sometimes of gold. (Revelation 17:4)
entries.definition_ko: 유대인의 컵은 금속이든 토기든 애굽와 페니키아의 형태와 디자인을 빌려왔을 가능성이 있다. 솔로몬 시대에는 왕의 모든 음료 그릇이 금이었고 은은 하나도 없었다(열왕기상 10:21). 큰 물두멍('바다')은 컵의 테두리 모양으로 만들어졌고 백합꽃 문양이 있었다(열왕기상 7:26). 신약의 컵은 헬라·로마식 모델을 따랐을 것이며 때로 금으로 만들어졌다(계시록 17:4).

entries.definition: an officer of high rank with Egyptian, Persian and Assyrian as well as Jewish monarchs. (1 Kings 10:5) It was his duty to fill the king’s cup and present it to him personally. (Nehemiah 1:11) The chief cupbearer, or butler, to the king of Egypt was the means of raising Joseph to his high position. (Genesis 40:1,21; 41:9)
entries.definition_ko: 애굽, 바사, 앗수르, 유대 왕실에 모두 있었던 고위 관직으로(열왕기상 10:5) 왕의 잔을 채워 직접 바치는 임무를 맡았다(느헤미야 1:11). 애굽 왕의 수석 술 맡은 자는 요셉을 높은 지위에 오르게 한 계기가 되었다(창세기 40:1).

entries.definition: the name of a son of Ham, apparently the eldest, and of a territory or territories occupied by his descendants. The Cushites appear to have spread along tracts extending from the higher Nile to the Euphrates and Tigris. History affords many traces of this relation of Babylonia, Arabia and Ethiopia. (black), a Benjamite mentioned only in the title to (Psalms 7:1) He was probably a follower of Saul, the head of his tribe. (B.C. 1061).
entries.definition_ko: 함의 아들 중 하나로 아마도 맏이이며, 그 후손들이 점유한 지역을 가리키기도 한다. 구스 족속은 상 나일강에서 유브라데강과 티헬라강에 이르는 지역에 퍼져 살았던 것으로 보인다. 또한 시편 7편 표제에만 언급되는 베냐민 사람으로 사울을 따른 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (blackness), (Habakkuk 3:7) possibly the same as Cushan-rishathaim (Authorized Version Chushan-) king of Mesopotamia. (Judges 3:8,10)
entries.definition_ko: '검음'이라는 뜻으로(하박국 3:7) 메소보다미아 왕 구산리사다임과 같은 인물로 추정된다(사사기 3:8).

entries.definition: Properly “the Cushite,” “the Ethiopian,” a man apparently attached to Joab’s person. (2 Samuel 18:21-25,31,32)
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 '구스 사람, 에디오피아 사람'이라는 뜻으로 요압을 섬긴 것으로 보이는 인물이다(사무엘하 18:21).

entries.definition: one of the countries whence Shalmaneser introduced colonists into Samaria. (2 Kings 17:24,30) Its position is undecided.
entries.definition_ko: 살만에셀이 사마리아에 이주민을 데려온 나라 중 하나이며(열왕기하 17:24) 위치는 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: Cuttings in the flesh, or the laceration of one’s body for the “propitiation of their gods,” (1 Kings 18:28) constituted a prominent feature of idolatrous worship, especially among the Syrians. The Israelites were prohibited from indulging in such practices. (Leviticus 19:28; 21:5; 14:1; Jeremiah 16:6)
entries.definition_ko: 자신의 신들을 달래기 위해 몸을 베는 행위로(열왕기상 18:28) 특히 수리아인들 사이에서 우상숭배의 두드러진 특징이었다. 이스라엘 백성은 이런 관습이 금지되었다(레위기 19:28).

entries.definition: a pecussive musical instrument. Two kinds of cymbals are mentioned in (Psalms 150:5) “loud cymbals” or castagnettes, and “high-sounding cymbals.” The former consisted of our small plates of brass or of some other hard metal; two plates were attached to each hand of the performer, and were struck together to produce a great noise. The latter consisted of two larger plates, on held in each hand and struck together as an accompaniment to other instruments. Cymbals were used not only in the temple but for military purposes, and also by Hebrew women as a musical accompaniment to their national dances. Both kinds of cymbals are still common in the East.
entries.definition_ko: 타악기의 일종으로 시편 150:5에 두 종류('큰 소리 나는 제금'과 '높은 소리 나는 제금')가 언급된다. 성전뿐 아니라 군사 목적, 히브리 여성들의 민속 춤 반주로도 쓰였다.

entries.definition: (Heb. tirzah). The Hebrew word is found only in (Isaiah 44:14) We are quite unable to assign any definite rendering to it. The true cypress is a native of the Taurus. The Hebrew word points to some tree with a hard grain, and this is all that can be positively said of it.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '티르자'로 이사야 44:14에만 나오며 정확한 번역은 알 수 없으나 단단한 결을 지닌 나무를 가리키는 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: an island of Asia in the Mediterranean. It is about 140 miles long and 50 miles wide at the widest part. Its two chief cities were Salamis, at the east end of the island, and Paphos, at the west end. “Cyprus occupies a distinguished place in both sacred and profane history. It early belonged to the Phoenicians of the neighboring coast; was afterwards colonized by Greeks’ passed successively under the power of the Pharaohs, Persians, Ptolemies and Romans, excepting a short period of independence in the fourth century B.C. It was one of the chief seats of the worship of Venus, hence called Cypria. Recently the discoveries in Cyprus by Cesnola have excited new interest.—Appleton’s Am. Encyc. It was the native place of Barnabas, (Acts 4:36) and was visited by Paul. (Acts 13:4-13; 15:39; 21:3) See also (Acts 27:4)
entries.definition_ko: 지중해의 섬으로 길이 약 140마일, 최대 너비 50마일이다. 주요 도시는 동쪽 끝의 살라미와 서쪽 끝의 바보였다. 페니키아인들이 일찍부터 소유했다가 헬라 사람들의 식민지가 되었고 이후 파라오, 바사, 프톨레마이오스, 로마의 지배를 차례로 받았다. 바나바의 고향이며(사도행전 4:36) 바울이 방문했다(사도행전 13:4).

entries.definition: the principal city of that part of northern Africa which was sufficiently called Cyrenaica, lying between Carthage and Egypt, and corresponding with the modern Tripoli. Though on the African coast, it was a Greek city, and the Jews were settled there in large numbers. The Greek colonization of this part of Africa under Battus began of early as B.C. 631. After the death of Alexander the Great it became a dependency of Egypt, and a Roman province B.C. 75. Simon, who bore our Saviour’s cross, (Matthew 27:32) was a native of Cyrene. Jewish dwellers in Cyrenaica were in Jerusalem at Pentecost, (Acts 2:10) and gave their name to one of the synagogues in Jerusalem. (Acts 6:9) Christian converts from Cyrene were among those who contributed actively to the formation of the first Gentile church at Antioch. (Acts 11:20)
entries.definition_ko: 북아프리카 카르타고와 애굽 사이 지역인 키레나이카의 주요 도시로 오늘날의 트리폴리에 해당한다. 아프리카 해안에 위치했으나 헬라 사람의 도시였고 유대인도 많이 정착해 있었다. 주님의 십자가를 대신 진 시몬이 이곳 출신이었으며(마태복음 27:32) 오순절에 예루살렘에 있던 구레네 유대인들이 예루살렘의 한 회당에 이름을 붙였다(사도행전 6:9).

entries.definition: (warrior), the Greek form of the Roman name of Quirinus. The full name is Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. He was consul B.C. 12, and was made governor of Syria after the banishment of Archelaus in A.D. 6. He probably was twice governor of Syria; his first governorship extended from B.C. 4 (the year of Christ’s birth) to B.C. 1. It was during this time that he was sent to make the enrollment which caused Joseph and Mary to visit Bethlehem. (Luke 2:2) The second enrollment is mentioned in (Acts 5:37)
entries.definition_ko: 로마 이름 퀴리누스의 헬라식 형태로 전체 이름은 푸블리우스 술피키우스 퀴리누스이다. 주전 12년 집정관을 지냈고 주후 6년 아켈라오 추방 후 수리아 총독이 되었다. 아마 두 차례 수리아 총독을 지냈을 것으로 보이며 첫 임기(주전 4년, 그리스도 탄생의 해) 중 요셉과 마리아가 베들레헴을 방문하게 한 호적 등록을 시행했다(누가복음 2:2).

entries.definition: (the sun), the founder of the Persian empire—see (2 Chronicles 36:22,23; Daniel 6:28; 10:1,13)—was, according to the common legend, the son of Cambyses, a Persian of the royal family of the Achaemenidae. When he grew up to manhood his courage and genius placed him at the head of the Persians. His conquests were numerous and brilliant. He defeated and captured the Median king B.C. 559. In B.C. 546 (?) he defeated Croesus, and the kingdom of lydia was the prize of his success. Babylon fell before his army, and the ancient dominions of Assyria were added to his empire B.C. 538. The prophet Daniel’s home for a time was at his court. (Daniel 6:28) The edict of Cyrus for the rebuilding of the temple, (2 Chronicles 36:22,23; Ezra 1:1-4; 3:7; 4:3; 5:13,17; 6:3) was in fact the beginning of Judaism; and the great changes by which the nation was transformed into a church are clearly marked. His tomb is still shown at Pasargadae, the scene of his first decisive victory.
entries.definition_ko: '태양'이라는 뜻으로 바사 제국의 창시자이며(역대하 36:22) 전설에 따르면 아케메네스 왕가의 바사인 캄비세스의 아들이다. 메대 왕을 격파하고(주전 559년), 리디아의 크로이소스를 물리쳐 그 왕국을 얻었으며(주전 546년경), 바벨론을 함락시켜 옛 앗수르 영토를 제국에 병합했다(주전 538년). 선지자 다니엘이 한때 그의 궁정에 있었다(다니엘 6:28). 성전 재건을 명한 고레스의 칙령(역대하 36:22)은 사실상 유대교의 시작을 알렸다.

entries.definition: (pasture), (Joshua 21:28) or Daberath, a town on the boundary of Zebulun. (Joshua 19:12) Under the name of Debarieh it still lies at the western foot of Tabor.
entries.definition_ko: '초원'이라는 뜻으로 다브랏이라고도 하며(여호수아 21:28) 스불론 경계의 성읍이다(여호수아 19:12). 오늘날 다볼산 서쪽 기슭의 데바리예에 남아 있다.

entries.definition: (a hill-place), a town on the boundary of Zebulun. (Joshua 19:11)
entries.definition_ko: '언덕 지대'라는 뜻으로 스불론 경계의 성읍이다(여호수아 19:11).

entries.definition: [See Dabareh]
entries.definition_ko: 다브랏(DABAREH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (a fish), apparently the masculine, (1 Samuel 5:3,4) correlative of Atargatis, was the national god of the Philistines. The most famous temples of Dagon were at Gaza, (Judges 16:21-30) and Ashdod. (1 Samuel 5:5,6; 1 Chronicles 10:10) The latter temple was destroyed by Jonathan in the Maccabaean wars. Traces of the worship of Dagon likewise appear in the names Caphar-dagon (near Jamnia) and Beth-dagon in Judah, (Joshua 15:41) and Asher. (Joshua 19:27) Dagon was represented with the face and hands of a man and the tail of a fish. (1 Samuel 5:5) The fish-like form was a natural emblem of fruitfulness, and as such was likely to be adopted by seafaring tribes in the representation of their gods.
entries.definition_ko: '물고기'라는 뜻으로 여신 아타르가티스에 대응하는 남신이며 블레셋 족속의 민족신이다. 가장 유명한 다곤 신전은 가사(사사기 16:21)와 아스돗(사무엘상 5:5)에 있었으며 후자는 마카베오 전쟁 중 요나단이 파괴했다. 다곤은 사람의 얼굴과 손, 물고기의 꼬리를 가진 형상으로 표현되었다.

entries.definition: (freed by Jehovah) a descendant of the royal family of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:24)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 자유케 하신'이라는 뜻으로 유다 왕실 후손이다(역대상 3:24).

entries.definition: a town on the west side of the Sea of Galilee, near Magdala. (Matthew 15:39) and Mark 8:10[Magdala] Dalmnnutha probably stood at the place called ’Ain-el-Barideh, “the cold fountain.”
entries.definition_ko: 갈릴리 호수 서쪽, 막달라 근처의 마을이다(마태복음 15:39).

entries.definition: a mountainous district on the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea. St. Paul sent Titus there. (2 Timothy 4:10)
entries.definition_ko: 아드리아해 동쪽 해안의 산악 지대이다. 바울이 디도를 이곳으로 보냈다(디모데후서 4:10).

entries.definition: (swift), the second of the ten sons of Hamam (Esther 9:7) (B.C. 610.)
entries.definition_ko: '신속한'이라는 뜻으로 하만의 열 아들 중 둘째이다(에스더 9:7).

entries.definition: (a heifer), an Athenian woman converted to Christianity by St. Paul’s preaching. (Acts 17:34) (A.D 48.) Chrysostom and others held her to have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.
entries.definition_ko: '암송아지'라는 뜻으로 바울의 설교로 그리스도교로 회심한 아덴 여인이다(사도행전 17:34).

entries.definition: one of the most ancient and most important of the cities of Syria. It is situated 130 miles northeast of Jerusalem, in a plain of vast size and of extreme fertility, which lies east of the great chain of Anti-Libanus, on the edge of the desert. This fertile plain, which is nearly circular and about 30 miles in diameter, is due to the river Barada, which is probably the “Abana” of Scripture. Two other streams the Wady Helbon upon the north and the Awaj, which flows direct from Hermon upon the south, increase the fertility of the Damascene plain, and contend for the honor of representing the “Pharpar” of Scripture. According to Josephus, Damascus was founded by Uz grandson of Shem. It is first mentioned in Scripture in connection with Abraham, (Genesis 14:15) whose steward was a native of the place. (Genesis 15:2) At one time david became complete master of the whole territory, which he garrisoned with israelites. (2 Samuel 8:5,6) It was in league with Baasha, king of Israel against Asa, (1 Kings 15:19; 2 Chronicles 16:3) and afterwards in league with Asa against Baasha. (1 Kings 15:20) Under Ahaz it was taken by Tiglath-pileser, (2 Kings 16:7,8,9) the kingdom of Damascus brought to an end, and the city itself destroyed, the inhabitants being carried captive into Assyria. (2 Kings 16:9) comp. Isai 7:8and Amos 1:5Afterwards it passed successively under the dominion of the Assyrians, Babylonians, Persians, Macedonians, Romans and Saracens, and was at last captured by the Turks in 1516 A.D. Here the apostle Paul was converted and preached the gospel. (Acts 9:1-25) Damascus has always been a great centre for trade. Its present population is from 100,000 to 150,000. It has a delightful climate. Certain localities are shown as the site of those scriptural events which specially interest us in its history. Queen’s Street, which runs straight through the city from east to west, may be the street called Straight. (Acts 9:11) The house of Judas and that of Ananias are shown, but little confidence can be placed in any of these traditions.
entries.definition_ko: 수리아에서 가장 오래되고 중요한 도시 중 하나로 예루살렘 북동쪽 130마일, 안티레바논 산맥 동쪽 사막 가장자리의 광대하고 매우 비옥한 평야에 위치한다. 이 평야는 바라다강(성경의 '아바나'로 추정)에서 형성되었다. 요세푸스에 따르면 셈의 손자 우스가 다메섹를 세웠다고 전해진다. 아브라함과 관련해 처음 언급되며(창세기 14:15) 다윗이 한때 완전히 정복해 이스라엘 수비대를 두었다(사무엘하 8:5). 아하스 시대에 디글랏빌레셀에게 정복되어 다메섹 왕국이 멸망하고 주민이 앗수르로 끌려갔다. 사도 바울이 이곳에서 회심하고 복음을 전했다(사도행전 9:1).

entries.definition: (a judge). • The fifth son of Jacob, and the first of Bilhah, Rachel’s maid. (Genesis 30:6) (B.C. after 1753.) The origin of the name is given in the exclamation of Rachel. The records of Dan are unusually meagre. Only one son is attributed to him, (Genesis 46:23) but his tribe was, with the exception of Judah, the most numerous of all. In the division of the promised land Dan was the last of the tribes to receive his portion, which was the smallest of the twelve. (Joshua 19:48) But notwithstanding its smallness it had eminent natural advantages. On the north and east it was completely embraced by its two brother tribes Ephraim and Benjamin, while on the southeast and south it joined Judah, and was thus surrounded by the three most powerful states of the whole confederacy. It was a rich and fertile district; but the Amorites soon “forced them into the mountain,” (Judges 1:34) and they had another portion granted them. Judges 18. In the “security” and “quiet,” (Judges 18:7,10) of their rich northern possession the Danites enjoyed the leisure and repose which had been denied them in their original seat. In the time of David Dan still kept its place among the tribes. (1 Chronicles 12:35) Asher is omitted, but the “prince of the tribe of Dan” is mentioned in the list of (1 Chronicles 27:22) But from this time forward the name as applied to the tribe vanishes; it is kept alive only by the northern city. In the genealogies of 1Chr 2-12, Dan is omitted entirely. Lastly, Dan is omitted from the list of those who were sealed by the angel in the vision of St. John. (Revelation 7:5-7) • The well-known city, so familiar as the most northern landmark of Palestine, in the common expression “from Dan even to beersheba.” The name of the place was originally Laishor Leshem. (Joshua 19:47) After the establishment of the Danites at Dan it became the acknowledged extremity of the country. It is now Tell el-Kadi, a mound, three miles from Banias, from the foot of which gushes out one of the largest fountains in the world, the main source of the Jordan.
entries.definition_ko: '재판자'라는 뜻. (1) 야곱의 다섯째 아들이자 라헬의 몸종 빌하의 첫아들이다(창세기 30:6). 그 지파는 유다를 제외하고 가장 인구가 많았으나 약속의 땅 분배 때 가장 작은 몫을 받았다(여호수아 19:48). 에브라임과 베냐민, 유다에 둘러싸인 비옥한 땅이었으나 아모리 족속에게 밀려 산지로 쫓겨나 별도의 땅을 얻었다(사사기 18장). (2) 팔레스타인 최북단 경계로 잘 알려진 도시로 '단에서 브엘세바까지'라는 표현에 등장한다. 본래 이름은 라이스 또는 레셈이었으며(여호수아 19:47) 단 지파가 정착한 후 그 이름을 얻었다. 오늘날 텔엘카디이며 세계 최대 규모의 샘 중 하나가 그 기슭에서 솟아나 요단강의 주요 수원을 이룬다.

entries.definition: a musical instrument of percussion, supposed to have been used by the Hebrews at an early period of their history. The dance is spoken of in Holy Scripture universally as symbolical of some rejoicing, and is often coupled for the sake of contrast with mourning, as in (Ecclesiastes 3:4) comp. Psal 30:11; Matt 11:17In the earlier period it is found combined with some song or refrain, (Exodus 15:20; 32:18,19; 1 Samuel 21:11) and with the tambourine (Authorized Version “timbrel”), more especially in those impulsive outbursts of popular feeling which cannot find sufficient vent in voice or in gesture singly. Dancing formed a part of the religious ceremonies of the Egyptians, and was also common in private entertainments. For the most part dancing was carried on by the women, the two sexes seldom and not customarily intermingling. The one who happened to be near of kin to the champion of the hour led the dance. In the earlier period of the Judges the dances of the virgins of Shiloh. (Judges 21:19-23) were certainly part of a religious festivity. Dancing also had its place among merely festive amusements, apart from any religious character. (Jeremiah 31:4,13; Mark 6:22)
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 춤은 보편적으로 기쁨의 상징으로 언급되며 종종 슬픔과 대조된다(전도서 3:4). 초기에는 노래나 후렴, 소고와 함께 나타났으며(출애굽기 15:20) 대체로 여성들이 추었고 남녀가 함께 추는 일은 드물었다. 애굽 사람의 종교 의식의 일부였으며 사적인 잔치에서도 흔했다.
