entries.definition: (fertile), a place mentioned only in (Ezekiel 27:18) Geographers have hitherto represented Helbon as identical with the city of Aleppo, called Haleb by the Arabs; but there are strong reasons against this, and the ancient city must be identified with a village within a few miles of Damascus still bearing the ancient name Helbon, and still celebrated as producing the finest grapes in the country.
entries.definition_ko: '비옥한'이라는 뜻으로 에스겔 27:18에만 언급된다. 지리학자들은 오랫동안 헬본을 아랍인들이 할렙이라 부르는 알레포와 동일시해왔으나 강한 반론이 있으며, 오늘날 다메섹에서 몇 마일 떨어진 곳에 여전히 헬본이라는 고대 이름을 지닌 마을과 동일시되는 것이 옳으며 이 지역은 지금도 최상급 포도로 유명하다.

entries.definition: (worldly). • The twelfth captain of the monthly courses for the temple service. (1 Chronicles 27:15) (B.C. 1014.) • An Israelite who seems to have returned from the captivity. (Zechariah 6:10) (B.C. 520.)
entries.definition_ko: '세속적인'이라는 뜻. (1) 성전 봉사 12개월 반차 중 열둘째 반차의 대장(역대상 27:15). (2) 포로에서 돌아온 것으로 보이는 이스라엘 사람(스가랴 6:10).

entries.definition: (milk), or He’led (transient) son of Baanah the Netophathite, one of the heroes of King David’s guard. (2 Samuel 23:29; 1 Chronicles 11:30)
entries.definition_ko: '젖'이라는 뜻(또는 헬렛, '덧없는'이라는 뜻)으로 느도바 사람 바아나의 아들이며 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나이다(사무엘하 23:29).

entries.definition: (portion), one of the descendants of Manasseh, and second son of Gilead, (Numbers 26:30) and founder of the Helekites. (B.C. 1445.)
entries.definition_ko: '몫'이라는 뜻으로 므낫세의 후손이자 길르앗의 둘째 아들이며(민수기 26:30) 헬렉 자손의 조상이다.

entries.definition: (strength). • A descendant of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:35) • A man mentioned only in (Zechariah 6:14) Apparently the same as Heldai.
entries.definition_ko: '힘'이라는 뜻. (1) 아셀의 후손(역대상 7:35). (2) 스가랴 6:14에만 언급되며 헬대와 같은 인물로 보인다.

entries.definition: (exchange), the place from which the boundary of the tribe of Naphtali started. (Joshua 19:33)
entries.definition_ko: '교환'이라는 뜻으로 납달리 지파 경계가 시작되는 지점이다(여호수아 19:33).

entries.definition: (strength). • One of “the thirty” of David’s guard, (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:27) an Ephraimite, and captain of the seventh monthly course. (1 Chronicles 27:10) (B.C. 1016.) • A man of Judah, son of Azariah. (1 Chronicles 2:39)
entries.definition_ko: '힘'이라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 '삼십 용사' 중 하나로 에브라임 사람이며 일곱째 월반 대장이었다(사무엘하 23:26). (2) 아사랴의 아들인 유다 사람(역대상 2:39).

entries.definition: (portion), the town named as the starting-point for the boundary of the tribe of Asher, (Joshua 19:25) and allotted with its “suburbs” to the Gershonite Levites. ch. (Joshua 21:31) Perhaps Yerka, seven miles from Acre.
entries.definition_ko: '몫'이라는 뜻으로 아셀 지파 경계의 시작점으로 언급되는 성읍이며(여호수아 19:25) 그 '주변 지역'과 함께 게르손 가문 레위인에게 배정되었다(여호수아 21:31). 아마도 아코에서 7마일 떨어진 예르카로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (ascending), the father of Joseph the husband of the Virgin Mary, (Luke 13:23) perhaps the grandfather of Mary herself. [See Genealogy Of Jesus ChristOF JESUS CHRIST]
entries.definition_ko: '올라감'이라는 뜻으로 성모 마리아의 남편 요셉의 아버지이며(누가복음 3:23) 마리아 자신의 조부일 가능성도 있다.

entries.definition: [See On]
entries.definition_ko: 온(ON) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (field of rock), a smooth piece of ground, apparently close to the pool of Gibeon, where the combat took place between the two parties of Joab’s men and Abner’s men which ended in the death of the whole of the combatants, and brought on a general battle. (2 Samuel 2:16)
entries.definition_ko: '바위의 밭'이라는 뜻으로 기브온 못 근처의 평평한 땅이며 요압의 부하들과 아브넬의 부하들이 결투를 벌여 양측 전원이 죽고 전면전으로 이어진 곳이다(사무엘하 2:16).

entries.definition: In the Old Testament this is the word generally and unfortunately used by our translators to render the Hebrew Sheol . It really means the place of the dead, the unseen world, without deciding whether it be the place of misery or of happiness. It is clear that in many passages of the Old Testament Sheol can only mean “the grave,” and is rendered in the Authorized Version; see, for example, (Genesis 37:35; 42:38; 1 Samuel 2:6; Job 14:13) In other passages, however, it seems to Involve a notion of punishment, and is therefore rendered in the Authorized Version by the word “hell.” But in many cases this translation misleads the reader. In the New Testament “hell” is the translation of two words, Hades and Gehenna . The word Hades, like Sheol sometimes means merely “the grave,” (Acts 2:31; 1 Corinthians 15:55; Revelation 20:13) or in general “the unseen world.” It is in this sense that the creeds say of our Lord, “He went down into hell,” meaning the state of the dead in general, without any restriction of happiness or misery. Elsewhere in the New Testament Hades is used of a place of torment, (Matthew 11:23; Luke 16:23; 2 Peter 2:4) etc.; consequently it has been the prevalent, almost the universal, notion that Hades is an intermediate state between death and resurrection, divided into two parts one the abode of the blest and the other of the lost. It is used eleven times in the New Testament, and only once translated “grave.” (1 Corinthians 15:55) The word most frequently used (occurring twelve times) in the New Testament for the place of future punishment is Gehenna or Gehenna of fire . This was originally the valley of Hinnom, south of Jerusalem, where the filth and dead animals of the city were cast out and burned; a fit symbol of the wicked and their destruction. [See Hinnom]
entries.definition_ko: 구약에서 이 단어는 번역자들이 히브리어 '스올'을 옮기는 데 흔히 사용했으나 이는 다소 부적절하다. 스올은 실제로 죽은 자들의 장소, 곧 보이지 않는 세계를 뜻할 뿐 그것이 고통의 장소인지 행복의 장소인지는 결정하지 않는다. 많은 구절에서 스올은 단순히 '무덤'을 뜻하며, 다른 구절에서는 형벌의 개념을 내포해 흠정역이 '지옥'으로 번역했다. 신약에서 '지옥'은 두 단어, 곧 '하데스'와 '게헨나'의 번역이다.

entries.definition: (Grecian), the term applied in the New Testament to Greek-speaking or “Grecian” Jews. The Hellenists as a body included not only the proselytes of Greek (or foreign) parentage, but also those. Jews who, by settling in foreign countries, had adopted the prevalent form of the current Greek civilization, and with it the use of the common Greek dialect. (Acts 6:1; 9:29)
entries.definition_ko: '헬라 사람' 또는 '헬라식'을 가리키며 신약에서 헬라어를 사용하는 유대인들을 가리키는 용어이다. 헬레니스트에는 헬라(또는 외국) 혈통의 개종자뿐 아니라 외국에 정착해 당시 헬라 문명 형태와 공용 헬라어 방언을 받아들인 유대인들도 포함되었다(사도행전 6:1).

entries.definition: [Arms, Armor]
entries.definition_ko: 무기와 갑옷(ARMS, ARMOR) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (strong), father of Eliab, of the tribe of Zebulun. (Numbers 1:9; 2:7; 7:24,29; 10:16) (B.C. 1491.)
entries.definition_ko: '강한'이라는 뜻으로 스불론 지파 엘리압의 아버지이다(민수기 1:9).

entries.definition: The importance which the later Jews, especially the Pharisees, (Matthew 23:5) attached to the hem or fringe of their garments was founded upon the regulation in (Numbers 15:38,39) which gave a symbolical meaning to it. [See Dress]
entries.definition_ko: 후대 유대인들, 특히 바리새인들이 옷단의 술에 부여한 중요성은(마태복음 23:5) 민수기 15:38의 규정에 근거하며 그것에 상징적 의미를 부여했다.

entries.definition: (exterminating). Hori and Hemam were sons of Lotan, the eldest son of Seir. (Genesis 36:22)
entries.definition_ko: '멸절시키는'이라는 뜻으로 호리와 헤맘은 세일의 맏아들 로단의 아들들이다(창세기 36:22).

entries.definition: (faithful) • Son of Zerah. (1 Chronicles 2:6; 1 Kings 4:31) • Son of Joel and grandson of Samuel the prophet, a Kohathite. He is called “the singer,” rather the musician, (1 Chronicles 6:33) and was the first of the three Levites to whom was committed the vocal and instrumental music of the temple service in the reign of David. (1 Chronicles 15:16-22) The 88th Psalm is ascribed to him. (B.C. 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '신실한'이라는 뜻. (1) 세라의 아들(역대상 2:6). (2) 요엘의 아들이자 선지자 사무엘의 손자인 고핫 가문 사람으로 '찬양자'(정확히는 음악가)라 불리며 다윗 시대 성전 예배의 성악과 기악을 맡은 세 레위인 중 첫째였다(역대상 15:16). 시편 88편이 그의 이름으로 전해진다.

entries.definition: (heat), a person or place named in the genealogical lists of Judah, as the origin of the Kenites, and the “father” of the house of Rechab. (1 Chronicles 2:55) (B.C. 1445.)
entries.definition_ko: '열기'라는 뜻으로 유다 족보에서 겐 족속의 기원이자 레갑 가문의 '아버지'로 언급되는 인물 또는 장소이다(역대상 2:55).

entries.definition: (pleasant), the eldest son of Dishon, son of Anah the Horite. (Genesis 36:26) [Amram, 2] (B.C. about 1500.)
entries.definition_ko: '즐거운'이라는 뜻으로 호리 사람 아나의 아들 디산의 맏아들이다(창세기 36:26).

entries.definition: the common ground or dwarf hemlock, a bitter, poisonous plant. The Hebrew rosh is rendered “hemlock” in two passages, (Hosea 10:4; Amos 6:12) but elsewhere “gall.” [Gall] (It is possible that the plant is rather the poppy than an hemlock.—Cook.)
entries.definition_ko: 일반적인 땅독말풀 또는 왜소한 독당근으로 쓴맛이 나는 독성 식물이다. 히브리어 '로쉬'는 호세아 10:4, 아모스 6:12에서 '독초'로 번역되나 다른 곳에서는 '쓸개(쓴 것)'로 번역된다.

entries.definition: The hen is nowhere noticed in the Bible except in (Matthew 23:37; Luke 13:34) That a bird so common in Palestine should receive such slight notice is certainly peculiar. (rest), probably a son of Zephaniah, and apparently the same who is called Josiah in (Zechariah 6:10)
entries.definition_ko: 암탉은 마태복음 23:37 외에는 성경에 언급되지 않는다. 스바냐의 아들로 추정되며 스가랴 6:10에서는 요시야라 불리는 인물이다.

entries.definition: (troubling), a city the Assyrian kings had reduced shortly before the time of Sennacherib. (2 Kings 19:13; Isaiah 37:13) At no great distance from Sippara (now Mosaib) is an ancient town called And or Anah, which may be the same as Hena. It is 20 miles from Babylon on the Euphrates.
entries.definition_ko: '혼란'이라는 뜻으로 산헤립 시대 직전 앗수르 왕들이 정복한 도시이다(열왕기하 19:13). 십바라(오늘날의 모사입) 근처에 아나 또는 아나라 불리는 고대 도시가 있어 헤나와 동일한 곳으로 추정되며 유브라데강변 바벨론에서 20마일 거리이다.

entries.definition: (grace of Hadad), the head of a family of the Levites who took a prominent part in the rebuilding of the temple. (Ezra 3:9)
entries.definition_ko: '하닷의 은혜'라는 뜻으로 성전 재건에 주도적 역할을 한 레위인 가문의 우두머리이다(에스라 3:9).

entries.definition: • Enoch, 2. (1 Chronicles 1:3) • Hanoch, 1. (1 Chronicles 1:33)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 에녹 2번 항목 참조(역대상 1:3). (2) 하녹 1번 항목 참조(역대상 1:33).

entries.definition: a place in ancient Canaan which occurs in the lists of conquered kings. (Joshua 12:17) It was on the west of Jordan. Comp. (Joshua 12:7) and 1Kin 4:10 (a well). • The youngest of the sons of Gilead, (Numbers 26:32) and head of the family of the Hepherites. (B.C. before 1450.) • Son of Ashur, the “father of Tekoa.” (1 Chronicles 4:6) (B.C. about 1445.) • The Mecherathite, one of the heroes of David’s guard. (1 Chronicles 11:36) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 고대 가나안의 한 장소로 정복된 왕들의 목록에 나오며 요단강 서쪽에 위치했다(여호수아 12:17). (2) '우물'이라는 뜻으로 길르앗의 막내아들이며 헤벨 자손의 조상(민수기 26:32). (3) 아술의 아들, '드고아의 아버지'(역대상 4:6). (4) 므게랏 사람으로 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나(역대상 11:36).

entries.definition: the family of Hepher the son of Gilead. (Numbers 26:32)
entries.definition_ko: 길르앗의 아들 헤벨의 가문이다(민수기 26:32).

entries.definition: • A name signifying “my delight in her,” which is to be borne by the restored Jerusalem. (Isaiah 62:4) • The queen of King Hezekiah and the mother of Manasseh. (2 Kings 21:1) (B.C. 709696.)
entries.definition_ko: '내 기쁨이 그녀에게 있다'는 뜻으로 회복된 예루살렘에게 붙여질 이름이며(이사야 62:4) 히스기야 왕의 왕비이자 므낫세의 어머니이기도 하다(열왕기하 21:1).

entries.definition: one who makes public proclamation. The only notice of this officer in the Old Testament occurs in (Daniel 3:4) The term “herald” might be substituted for “preacher” in (1 Timothy 2:7; 2 Timothy 1:11; 2 Peter 2:5)
entries.definition_ko: 공적으로 선포하는 자를 가리킨다. 구약에서 유일한 언급은 다니엘 3:4이며 '전파자'(디모데전서 2:7)를 이 단어로 대체할 수 있다.

entries.definition: (a collection of cattle), Herdsmen. The herd was greatly regarded in both the patriarchal and the Mosaic period. The ox was the most precious stock next to horse and mule. The herd yielded the most esteemed sacrifice, (Numbers 7:3; Psalms 69:31; Isaiah 66:3) also flesh meat, and milk, chiefly converted probably, into butter and cheese. (32:14; 2 Samuel 17:29) The agricultural and general usefulness of the ox in ploughing, threshing, and as a beast of burden, (1 Chronicles 12:40; Isaiah 46:1) made a slaughtering of him seem wasteful. Herdsmen, etc., in Egypt were a low, perhaps the lowest, caste; but of the abundance of cattle in Egypt, and of the care there bestowed on them, there is no doubt. (Genesis 47:6,17; Exodus 9:4,20) So the plague of hail was sent to smite especially the cattle, (Psalms 78:48) the firstborn of which also were smitten. (Exodus 12:29) The Israelites departing stipulated for, (Exodus 10:26) and took “much cattle” with them. ch. (Exodus 12:38) Cattle formed thus one of the traditions of the Israelitish nation in its greatest period, and became almost a part of that greatness. The occupation of herdsman was honorable in early times. (Genesis 47:6; 1 Samuel 11:5; 1 Chronicles 27:29; 28:1) Saul himself resumed it in the interval of his cares as king, also Doeg was certainly high in his confidence (1 Samuel 21:7) Pharaoh made some of Joseph’s brethren “rulers over his cattle.” David’s herd-masters were among his chief officers of state. The prophet Amos at first followed this occupation.
entries.definition_ko: 가축 떼는 족장 시대와 모세 시대 모두 크게 중시되었다. 소는 말과 노새 다음으로 귀한 가축이었고 가장 존귀한 제사물이었으며(민수기 7:3) 고기와 우유(주로 버터·치즈로 가공)를 공급했다. 밭갈이·타작·짐 운반에도 유용해(역대상 12:40) 도살하는 것이 낭비로 여겨졌다.

entries.definition: (the sun), (Judges 1:35) a city of Dan, in Mount Ephraim, near Ajalon; possibly identical with Mount Jearim (Ir-shemesh, city of the gun).
entries.definition_ko: '태양'이라는 뜻으로(사사기 1:35) 아얄론 근처 에브라임 산지의 단 지파 성읍이며 이르세메스(태양의 성읍)와 동일한 곳일 가능성이 있다.

entries.definition: (artificer), a Levite attached to the tabernacle (1 Chronicles 9:15) (B.C. 536.)
entries.definition_ko: '기술자'라는 뜻으로 성막에 속한 레위인이다(역대상 9:15).

entries.definition: (Mercury), the name of a Christian resident at Rome to whom St. Paul sends greetings in his Epistle to the Romans. (Romans 16:14) (A.D. 55.) Irenaeus, Tertullian and Origen agree in attributing to him the work called The shepherd . It was never received into the canon, but yet was generally cited with respect only second to that which was paid to the authoritative books of the New Testament.
entries.definition_ko: '메르쿠리우스'라는 뜻으로 바울이 로마서에서 문안한 로마의 그리스도인이다(로마서 16:14). 이레니우스, 테르툴리아누스, 오리게네스는 모두 그를 '목자'라는 저작의 저자로 여겼다.

entries.definition: (Mercury), a Christian mentioned in (Romans 16:14) According to tradition he was one of the seventy disciples, and afterward bishop of Dalmatia. (A.D. 55.)
entries.definition_ko: '메르쿠리우스'라는 뜻으로 로마서 16:14에 언급된 그리스도인이다. 전승에 따르면 칠십 인 제자 중 하나였고 후에 달마디아의 감독이 되었다.

entries.definition: a person mentioned by St. Paul in the latest of all his epistles, (2 Timothy 1:15) when all in Asia had turned away from him. (A.D. 64.)
entries.definition_ko: 바울이 마지막 서신(디모데후서 1:15)에서 언급한 인물로 아시아의 모든 사람이 그를 저버렸을 때를 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (a peak, summit), a mountain on the northeastern border of Palestine, (3:8; Joshua 12:1) over against Lebanon, (Joshua 11:17) adjoining the plateau of Bashan. (1 Chronicles 5:23) It stands at the southern end, and is the culminating point of the antiLibanus range; it towers high above the ancient border city of Dan and the fountains of the Jordan, and is the most conspicuous and beautiful mountain in Palestine or Assyria. At the present day it is called Jebel esh-Sheikh, “the chief mountain,” and Jebel eth-Thelj, “snowy mountain.” When the whole country is parched with the summer sun, white lines of snow streak the head of Hermon. This mountain was the great landmark of the Israelites. It was associated with their northern border almost as intimately as the sea was with the western. Hermon has three summits, situated like the angles of a triangle, and about a quarter of a mile from each other. In two passages of Scripture this mountain is called Baal-hermon, (Judges 3:3; 1 Chronicles 5:23) possibly because Baal was there worshipped. (It is more than probable that some part of Hermon was the scene of the transfiguration, as it stands near Caesarea Philippi, where we know Christ was just before that event—ED.) The height of Hermon has never been measured, though it has often been estimated. It may safely be reckoned at 10,000 feet.
entries.definition_ko: '봉우리, 정상'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북동 경계의 산이며(신명기 3:8) 레바논 맞은편, 바산 고원에 인접해 있다. 안티레바논 산맥 남쪽 끝이자 최고봉으로 단성과 요단강 수원지 위로 높이 솟아 팔레스타인에서 가장 두드러지고 아름다운 산이다. 오늘날 '주요 산'이라는 뜻의 제벨 에스셰이크, '눈 덮인 산'이라는 뜻의 제벨 에트텔지라 불린다. 세 봉우리가 삼각형 모양으로 서로 약 0.25마일 간격으로 위치한다. 성경 두 곳에서는 바알헤르몬이라 불린다(사사기 3:3).

entries.definition: Properly “the Hermons,” with reference to the three summits of Mount Hermon. (Psalms 42:6) (Psal 42:7).
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 '헤르몬들'로 헤르몬산의 세 봉우리를 가리킨다(시편 42:6).

entries.definition: (hero-like). This family though of Idumean origin and thus alien by race, was Jewish in faith. I. HEROD THE GREAT was the second son of Antipater, an Idumean, who was appointed procurator of Judea by Julius Caesar, B.C. 47. Immediately after his father’s elevation when only fifteen years old, he received the government of Galilee and shortly afterward that of Coele-Syria. Though Josephus says he was 15 years old at this time, it is generally conceded that there must be some mistake, as he lived to be 69 or 70 years old, and died B.C. 4; hence he must have been 25 years old at this time.—ED.) In B.C. 41 he was appointed by Antony tetrarch of Judea. Forced to abandon Judea the following year, he fled to Rome, and received the appointment of king of Judea. In the course of a few years, by the help of the Romans he took Jerusalem (B.C. 37), and completely established his authority throughout his dominions. The terrible acts of bloodshed which Herod perpetrated in his own family were accompanied by others among his subjects equally terrible, from the number who fell victims to them. According to the well-known story) he ordered the nobles whom he had called to him in his last moment to be executed immediately after his decease, that so at least his death might be attended by universal mourning. It was at the time of his fatal illness that he must have caused the slaughter of the infants at Bethlehem. (Matthew 2:16-18) He adorned Jerusalem with many splendid monuments of his taste and magnificence. The temple, which he built with scrupulous care, was the greatest of these works. The restoration was begun B.C. 20, and the temple itself was completed in a year and a half. But fresh additions were constantly made in succeeding years, so that it was said that the temple was “built in forty and six years,” (John 2:20) the work continued long after Herod’s death. (Herod died of a terrible disease at Jericho, in April, B.C. 4, at the age of 69, after a long reign of 37 years.—ED.) II. HEROD Antipas, Antipaswas the son of Herod the Great by Malthake, a Samaritan. He first married a daughter of Aretas, “king of Arabia Petraea,” but afterward Herodias, the wife of his half-brother, Herod Philip. Aretas, indignant at the insult offered to his daughter, found a pretext for invading the territory of Herod, and defeated him with great loss. This defeat, according to the famous passage in Josephus, was attributed by many to the murder of John the Baptist, which had been committed by Antipas shortly before, under the influence of Herodias. (Matthew 14:4) ff.; Mark 6:17ff.; Luke 3:19At a later time the ambition of Herodias proved the cause of her husband’s ruin. She urged him to go to Rome to gain the title of king, cf. (Mark 6:14) but he was opposed at the court of Caligula by the emissaries of Agrippa, and condemned to perpetual banishment at Lugdunum, A.D. 39. Herodias voluntarily shared his punishment, and he died in exile. Pilate took occasion from our Lord’s residence in Galilee to bend him for examination, (Luke 23:6) ff., to Herod Antipas, who came up to Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover. The city of Tiberias, which Antipas founded and named in honor of the emperor, was the most conspicuous monument of his long reign. III. HEROD PHILIP I. (Philip,) (Mark 6:17) was the son of Herod the Great and Mariamne. He married Herodias the sister of Agrippa I by whom he had a daughter, Salome. He was excluded from all share in his father’s possessions in consequence of his mother’s treachery, and lived afterward in a private station. IV. HEROD PHILIP II. was the son of Herod the Great and Cleopatra. He received as his own government Batanea Trachonitis, Auramtis (Gaulanitis), and some parts about Jamnia, with the title of tetrarch. Luke 3:1. He built a new city on the site of Paneas, near the sources of the Jordan, which be called Caesarea Philippi, (Matthew 16:13; Mark 8:27) and raised Bethsaida to the rank of a city under the title of Julias and died there A.D. 34. He married Salome, the daughter of Herod Philip I. and Herodias. V. HEROD AGRIPPA I. was the son of Aristobulus and Berenice, and grandson of Herod the Great. He was brought up at Rome, and was thrown into prison by Tiberius, where he remained till the accession of Caligula, who made him king, first of the tetrarchy of Philip and Lysanias; afterward the dominions of Antipas were added, and finally Judea and Samaria. Unlike his predessors, Agrippa was a strict observer of the law, and he sought with success the favor of the Jews. It is probable that it was with this view he put to death James the son of Zebedee, and further imprisoned Peter. (Acts 12:1) ff. But his sudden death interrupted his ambitious projects. (Acts 12:21,23) VI. HEROD AGRIPPA II—was the son of Herod Agrippa I. In A.D. 62 the emperor gave him the tetrarches formerly held by Philip and Lysanias, with the title of king. (Acts 25:13) The relation in which he stood to his sister Berenice, (Acts 25:13) was the cause of grave suspicion. It was before him that Paul was tried. (Acts 26:28)
entries.definition_ko: '영웅 같은'이라는 뜻. 이두매 혈통이나 신앙은 유대교를 따른 가문이다. I. 헤롯 대왕은 율리우스 카이사르가 주전 47년 유대 총독으로 임명한 이두매 사람 안티파터의 둘째 아들로, 아버지가 요직에 오른 직후 갈릴리, 곧이어 쾰레시리아의 통치를 맡았다. 주전 41년 안토니우스에 의해 유대 분봉왕으로 임명되었고 이듬해 로마로 피신했다가 유대 왕으로 임명받았다. 로마의 도움으로 예루살렘을 점령(주전 37년)하고 전 영토에서 권위를 확립했다. 자기 가족 내에서 저지른 끔찍한 유혈 사태와 함께 신하들 사이에서도 마찬가지로 참혹한 일들을 저질렀다. 임종 직전 베들레헴의 영아 학살을 명한 것으로 보이며(마태복음 2:16), 예루살렘 성전을 정성 들여 재건했다. 주전 4년 4월, 69세로 참혹한 병으로 여리고에서 죽었다. II. 헤롯 안디바는 헤롯 대왕과 사마리아 여인 말타케의 아들로, 처음에는 아라비아 페트라 왕 아레다의 딸과 결혼했으나 후에 이복형제 헤롯 빌립의 아내 헤로디아와 결혼했다. 이 결혼으로 아레다에게 대패했으며 이는 세례 요한의 처형에 대한 보복으로 여겨지기도 했다. 야망 많은 헤로디아의 부추김으로 왕 칭호를 얻으려 로마에 갔다가 아그립바의 사주로 실각해 루그두눔으로 영구 추방되었다(주후 39년). III. 헤롯 빌립 1세는 헤롯 대왕과 마리암네의 아들로 헤로디아와 결혼해 딸 살로메를 낳았으나 어머니의 배신으로 아버지 유산에서 제외되어 이후 평민으로 살았다. IV. 헤롯 빌립 2세는 헤롯 대왕과 클레오파트라의 아들로 바다네아·트라코니티스·아우라니티스(가울라니티스) 등을 분봉왕으로 다스렸으며 요단강 수원 근처 바네아스에 새 도시를 세워 가이사랴 빌립보라 이름지었다. V. 헤롯 아그립바 1세는 아리스도불로와 버니게의 아들이자 헤롯 대왕의 손자로 세베대의 아들 야고보를 죽이고 베드로를 투옥했다(사도행전 12:1). VI. 헤롯 아그립바 2세는 헤롯 아그립바 1세의 아들로 주후 62년 빌립과 리사니아의 옛 분봉국을 받았으며 그 앞에서 바울이 재판받았다(사도행전 26:28).

entries.definition: (from Herod). (Matthew 22:15) ff.; Mark 12:13ff. Canon Cook describes these persons as “that party among the Jews who were supporters of the Herodian family as the last hope of retaining for the Jews a fragment of national government, as distinguished from absolute dependence upon Rome as a province of the empire. Supporters of the family of Herod, who held their dominions by the grant of the Roman emperor, would be in favor of paying tribute to the supreme power. (Matthew 22:16)
entries.definition_ko: 헤롯 가문을 지지한 유대인 정파로(마태복음 22:15) 로마의 속주로 완전히 종속되기보다는 유대 민족 정부의 일부라도 유지할 마지막 희망으로 헤롯 왕가를 지지했다. 헤롯 가문의 통치는 로마 황제의 허락에 의한 것이었으므로 이들은 로마에 조공 바치는 것을 지지하는 입장이었다.

entries.definition: daughter of Aristobulus, one of the sons of Mariamne and Herod the Great, and consequently sister of Agrippa I. She first married Herod Philip I.; then she eloped from him to marry Herod Antipas her step-uncle. The head of John the Baptist was granted at the request of Herodias. (Matthew 14:8-11; Mark 6:24-28) (A.D. 29.) She accompanied Antipas into exile to Lugdunum
entries.definition_ko: 헤롯 대왕과 마리암네의 아들인 아리스도불로의 딸로 아그립바 1세의 누이이다. 처음에는 헤롯 빌립 1세와 결혼했다가 그를 떠나 시숙(계부의 형제) 헤롯 안디바와 결혼했다. 세례 요한의 목이 헤로디아의 요청으로 넘겨졌다(마태복음 14:8). 안디바가 유배될 때 함께 루그두눔으로 따라갔다.

entries.definition: a relative of St. Paul, to whom he sends his salutation amongst the Christians of the Roman church. (Romans 16:11) (A.D. 55.)
entries.definition_ko: 바울의 친척으로 로마 교회 그리스도인들 사이에서 그가 문안을 전한 인물이다(로마서 16:11).

entries.definition: (Leviticus 11:19; 14:18) a common large, wading, unclean bird. Nearly all of the species known in English ornithology are found in the vicinity of Palestine. Canon Cook and others think the bird intended is the plover (Charadrius aedicnemus), a greedy, thick kneed, high-flying migratory bird, very common in the East, on the banks of rivers and shores of lakes.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: 레위기 11:19에 언급된 흔한 대형 섭금류, 부정한 새이다. 다른 견해로는 물떼새를 가리킨다는 설도 있다.

entries.definition: (kindness), the son of Hesed or Ben-Chesed, was commissary for Solomon. (1 Kings 4:10) (B.C. about 995.)
entries.definition_ko: '친절'이라는 뜻으로 헤셋(벤헤셋)의 아들이며 솔로몬의 물자 담당관이었다(열왕기상 4:10).

entries.definition: (stronghold), the capital city of Sihon king of the Amorites. (Numbers 21:26) It stood on the western border of the high plain—Mishor, (Joshua 13:17)—and on the boundary line between the tribes of Reuben and Gad. The ruins of Hesban, 20 miles east of the Jordan, on the parallel of the northern end of the Dead Sea mark the site, as they bear the name; of the ancient Heshbon. There are many cisterns among the ruins. Comp. (Song of Solomon 7:4)
entries.definition_ko: '요새'라는 뜻으로 아모리 왕 시혼의 수도이다(민수기 21:26). 고원(미솔)의 서쪽 경계이자 르우벤과 갓 지파 사이 경계에 위치했다. 요단강 동쪽 20마일, 사해 북단과 같은 위도의 헤스반 폐허가 고대 헤스본의 위치를 나타내며 그 이름도 그대로 지니고 있다.

entries.definition: (rich soil), a place named, with others, as lying in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 15:27)
entries.definition_ko: '풍요로운 흙'이라는 뜻으로 유다 최남단의 여러 성읍과 함께 언급된다(여호수아 15:27).

entries.definition: (enclosed), the son of Reuben, (Numbers 26:6) and ancestor of the Hezronites. (B.C. about 1700.)
entries.definition_ko: '둘러싸인'이라는 뜻으로 르우벤의 아들이며(민수기 26:6) 헤스론 자손의 조상이다.

entries.definition: (terror), the forefather of the nation of the Hittites. In the genealogical tables of (Genesis 10:15) and 1Chr 1:13Heth is a son of Canaan. (Genesis 24:3,4; 28:1,2)
entries.definition_ko: '공포'라는 뜻으로 헷 족속의 시조이며 창세기 10:15의 족보표에서는 가나안의 아들로 나온다.

entries.definition: (hiding-place), the name of a place on the northern border of Palestine. (Ezekiel 47:15; 48:1) In all probability the “way of Hethlon” is the pass at the northern end of Lebanon, and is thus identical with “the entrance of Hamath” in (Numbers 34:8) etc.
entries.definition_ko: '숨는 곳'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북쪽 경계의 한 장소이다(에스겔 47:15). '헤들론으로 가는 길'은 레바논 북쪽 끝 고갯길로 추정되며 민수기 34:8의 '하맛 어귀'와 동일한 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: (strong), a Benjamite, one of the Bene-Elpaal, a descendant of Shaaraim. (1 Chronicles 8:17) (B.C. 598.)
entries.definition_ko: '강한'이라는 뜻으로 벨라임 가문 사아라임 후손인 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 8:17).

entries.definition: (the might of Jehovah). • Twelfth king of Judah, son of the apostate Ahaz and Abi or Abijah, ascended the throne at the age of 25, B.C. 726. Hezekiah was one of the three most perfect kings of Judah. (2 Kings 18:5) Ecclus. 49:4. His first act was to purge and repair and reopen with splendid sacrifices and perfect ceremonial the temple. He also destroyed a brazen serpent, said to have been the one used by Moses in the miraculous healing of the Israelites, (Numbers 21:9) which had become an object of adoration. When the kingdom of Israel had fallen, Hezekiah invited the scattered inhabitants to a peculiar passover, which was continued for the unprecedented period of fourteen days. (2 Chronicles 29:30,31) At the head of a repentant and united people, Hezekiah ventured to assume the aggressive against the Philistines and in a series of victories not only rewon the cities which his father had lost, (2 Chronicles 28:18) but even dispossessed them of their own cities except Gaza, (2 Kings 18:8) and Gath. He refused to acknowledge the supremacy of Assyria. (2 Kings 18:7) Instant war was imminent and Hezekiah used every available means to strengthen himself. (2 Kings 20:20) It was probably at this dangerous crisis in his kingdom that we find him sick and sending for Isaiah, who prophesies death as the result. (2 Kings 20:1) Hezekiah’s prayer for longer life is heard. The prophet had hardly left the palace when he was ordered to return and promise the king immediate recovery and fifteen years more of life. (2 Kings 20:4) An embassy coming from Babylon ostensibly to compliment Hezekiah on his convalescence, but really to form an alliance between the two powers, is favorably received by the king, who shows them the treasures which he had accumulated. For this Isaiah foretells the punishment that shall befall his house. (2 Kings 20:17) The two invasions of Sennacherib occupy the greater part of the scripture records concerning the reign of Hezekiah. The first of these took place in the third year of Sennacherib, B.C. 702, and occupies only three verses. (2 Kings 18:13-16) Respecting the commencement of the second invasion we have full details in (2 Kings 18:17) seq.; 2Chr 32:9seq.; Isai 36:1... Sennacherib sent against Jerusalem an army under two officers and his cupbearer, the orator Rabshakeh, with a blasphemous and insulting summons to surrender; but Isaiah assures the king he need not fear, promising to disperse the enemy. (2 Kings 19:6,7) Accordingly that night “the angel of the Lord went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred fourscore and five thousand.” Hezekiah only lived to enjoy for about one year more his well-earned peace and glory. He slept with his fathers after a reign of twenty-nine years, in the 56th year of his age, B.C. 697. • Son of Neariah, one of the descendants of the royal family of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:23) • The same name, though rendered in the Authorized Version Hizkiah, is found in (Zephaniah 1:1) • Ater of Hezekiah. [Ater]
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 힘'이라는 뜻. (1) 유다의 열두째 왕으로 배교자 아하스와 아비(아비야)의 아들이며 25세에 즉위했다(주전 726년). 유다의 가장 완전한 세 왕 중 하나로 꼽힌다(열왕기하 18:5). 성전을 정결케 하고 보수해 성대한 제사와 완전한 의식으로 다시 열었으며, 모세가 만든 놋뱀이 숭배 대상이 되자 이를 부수었다. 이스라엘 왕국 멸망 후 흩어진 백성을 특별한 유월절로 초청해 이례적으로 14일간 지켰다. 블레셋에 맞서 승리를 거두어 아버지가 잃은 성읍들을 되찾았고 가사와 가드를 제외한 그들의 성읍까지 차지했다. 앗수르의 종주권을 거부해 산헤립의 두 차례 침공을 받았으나 이사야의 예언대로 여호와의 사자가 하룻밤에 앗수르 진영 18만 5천 명을 쳐 구원받았다. 재위 29년, 56세에 죽었다(주전 697년). (2) 유다 왕실 후손 느아랴의 아들(역대상 3:23). (3) 스바냐 1:1의 히스기야로도 표기됨. (4) 아델의 조상 또는 자손.

entries.definition: (vision), a king of Aram (Syria), father of Tabrimon and grandfather of Ben-hadad I. (1 Kings 15:18) He is probably identical with Rezon, the contemporary of Solomon, in (1 Kings 11:23) (B.C. before 928.)
entries.definition_ko: '환상'이라는 뜻으로 아람(수리아) 왕이며 다브림몬의 아버지이자 벤하닷 1세의 조부이다(열왕기상 15:18). 솔로몬 시대의 르손과 동일 인물로 추정된다(열왕기상 11:23).

entries.definition: (Swine). • A priest in the time of David, leader of the seventeenth monthly course in the service. (1 Chronicles 24:15) (B.C. 1014.) • One of the heads of the people (lay-men) who sealed the solemn covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:20) (B.C. 410.)
entries.definition_ko: '돼지'라는 뜻. (1) 다윗 시대 성전 봉사 열일곱째 반차의 우두머리 제사장(역대상 24:15). (2) 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 평신도 우두머리 중 하나(느헤미야 10:20).

entries.definition: (enclosed), one of the thirty heroes of David’s guard. (2 Samuel 23:35) (B.C. 1046.) In the parallel list, (1 Chronicles 11:37) the name appears as HEZRO.
entries.definition_ko: '둘러싸인'이라는 뜻으로 다윗의 삼십 근위 용사 중 하나이며(사무엘하 23:35) 병행 목록인 역대상 11:37에서는 헤스로라 나온다.

entries.definition: (surrounded by a wall). • A son of Reuben. (Genesis 46:9; Exodus 6:14) • A son of Pharez. (Genesis 46:12; Ruth 4:18)
entries.definition_ko: '벽으로 둘러싸인'이라는 뜻. (1) 르우벤의 아들(창세기 46:9). (2) 베레스의 아들(창세기 46:12).

entries.definition: (descendants of Hezron), The. • Descendants of Hezron the son of Reuben. (Numbers 26:6) • A branch of the tribe of Judah, descendants of Hezron the son of Pharez. (Numbers 26:21)
entries.definition_ko: (1) 르우벤의 아들 헤스론의 후손(민수기 26:6). (2) 베레스의 아들 헤스론의 후손인 유다 지파의 한 분파(민수기 26:21).

entries.definition: (for the rejoicing of Jehovah), one of the thirty-seven heroes of David’s guard. (2 Samuel 23:30) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 기쁨을 위해'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 삼십칠 용사 중 하나이다(사무엘하 23:30).

entries.definition: (rapid), one of the rivers of Eden, the river which “goeth eastward to Assyria,” (Genesis 2:14) and which Daniel calls “the great river,” (Daniel 10:4) seems to have been rightly identified by the LXX. with the Tigris. Dekel is clearly an equivalent of Digla or Dighath, a name borne by the Tigris in all ages. The name now in use among the inhabitants of Mesopotamia is Dijleh .
entries.definition_ko: '빠른'이라는 뜻으로 에덴의 강 중 하나이며 '앗수르 동쪽으로 흐르는' 강이고(창세기 2:14) 다니엘은 이를 '큰 강'이라 부른다(다니엘 10:4). 칠십인역이 티헬라강과 동일시한 것이 옳은 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: (God liveth), a native of Bethel, who rebuilt Jericho in the reign of Ahab, (1 Kings 16:34) (B.C. after 915), and in whom was fulfilled the curse pronounced by Joshua, (Joshua 6:26) five hundred years before.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님은 살아 계신다'는 뜻으로 벧엘 출신이며 아합 시대에 여리고를 재건했고(열왕기상 16:34) 500년 전 여호수아가 선포한 저주가 그에게서 성취되었다(여호수아 6:26).

entries.definition: (holy city), a city of Phrygia, situated above the junction of the rivers Lycus and Maeander, near Colossae and Laodicea mentioned only in (Colossians 4:13) as the seat of a church probably founded by Epaphras.
entries.definition_ko: '거룩한 도시'라는 뜻으로 리쿠스강과 마이안더강 합류점 위쪽, 골로새와 라오디게아 근처에 위치한 브루기아의 도시이며 골로새서 4:13에만 언급되고 에바브라가 세운 교회가 있었던 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (meditation), a word which occurs three times in the book of Psalms— (Psalms 9:16; 19:14; 92:3) (margin). The word has two meanings, one of a general character, implying thought; reflection, and another, in (Psalms 9:16) and Psal 92:3Of a technical nature, the precise meaning of which cannot at this distance of time be determined. (Canon Cook says that it probably means an interlude giving musical expression to the feelings suggested by the preceding words.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: '묵상'이라는 뜻으로 시편에 세 번 나온다(시편 9:16). 일반적으로는 사색·성찰을 뜻하나 시편 9:16, 92:3에서는 정확한 의미를 오늘날 확정할 수 없는 전문 용어로 쓰인다.

entries.definition: The first distinct separation of Aaron to the office of the priesthood, which previously belonged to the first-born was that recorded (Exodus 28:1) ... We find from the very first the following characteristic attributes of Aaron and the high priests his successors, as distinguished from the other priests: Aaron alone was anointed, (Leviticus 8:12) whence one of the distinctive epithets of the high priest was “the anointed priest.” (Leviticus 4:3,5,16; 21:10) see (Numbers 35:25) The anointing of the sons of Aaron, i.e. the common priests seems to have been confined to sprinkling their garments with the anointing oil. (Exodus 29:21; 28:41) etc. The high priest had a peculiar dress, which passed to his successor at his death. This dress consisted of eight parts: (a) The breastplate, or, as it is further named, vs. (Exodus 28:15,29,30) the breastplate of judgment. The breastplate was originally two spans long and one span broad, but when doubled it was square, the shape in which it was worn. On it were the twelve precious stones, set in four rows, three in a row, thus corresponding to the twelve tribes—each stone having the name of one of the children of Israel engraved upon it. (b) The ephod . This consisted of two parts, of which one covered the back and the other the front, i.e. the breast and upper part of the body. These parts were clasped together on the shoulder with two large onyx stones, each having engraved on it six of the names of the tribes of Israel. They were further united by a “curious girdle” of gold blue purple, scarlet and fine twined linen round the waist. [Ephod; Girdle] (C) The robe of the ephod. This was of inferior material to the ephod itself being all of blue, ver. 31, which implied its being only of “woven work.” ch. (Exodus 39:22) It was worn immediately under the ephod, and was longer than it. The skirt of this robe had a remarkable trimming of pomegranates in blue, red and crimson, with a bell of gold between each pomegranate alternately. The bells were to give a sound when the high priest went in and came out of the holy place. (d) The mitre or upper turbin, with its gold plate, engraved with “Holiness to the Lord,” fastened to it by a ribbon of blue. (e) The broidered coat was a tunic or long skirt of linen with a tessellated or diaper pattern, like the setting of stone. (f) The girdle, also of linen, was wound round the body several times from the breast downward, and the ends hung down to the ankles. (g) The breeches or drawers, of linen, covered the loins and thighs; and (h) The bonnet was a turban of linen, partially covering the head, but not in the form of a cone like that of the high priest when the mitre was added to it. These last four were common to all priests. The high priest alone was permitted to enter the holy of holies, which he did once a year, on the great day of atonement, when he sprinkled the blood of the sin offering on the mercy seat, and burnt incense within the veil (Leviticus 16:1) ... The manslayer might not leave the city of refuge during the lifetime of the existing high priest. It was also forbidden to the high priest to follow a funeral, or rend his clothes for the dead. It does not appear by whose authority the high priests were appointed to their office before there were kings of Israel. After this the office seems to have been used for political rather than religious purposes. Though at first chosen for life, we find that Solomon deposed Abiathar, (1 Kings 2:35) and that Herod appointed a number of high priests, which may account for there being at least two living in Christ’s time, Annas and Caiaphas. (Luke 3:2) The usual are for entering upon the functions of the priesthood, according to (2 Chronicles 31:17) is considered to have been 20 years, though a priest or high priest was not actually incapacitated if he had attained to puberty. Again, according to (Leviticus 21:17-21) no one that had a blemish could officiate at the altar. The theological view of the high priesthood does not fall within the scope of this work. It must suffice therefore to indicate that such a view would embrace the consideration of the office, dress, functions and ministrations of the high priest considered as typical of the priesthood of our Lord Jesus Christ, and as setting forth under shadows the truths which are openly taught under the gospel. This had been done to a great extent in the Epistle to the Hebrews. It would also embrace all the moral and spiritual teaching supposed to be intended by such symbols.
entries.definition_ko:
첫 아들에게 속해 있던 제사장 직분에 아론을 뚜렷이 구별하여 세운 최초의 일이 출애굽기 28:1에 기록되어 있다. 다른 제사장들과 구별되는 아론과 그 뒤를 이은 대제사장들의 특징적 속성을 처음부터 다음과 같이 볼 수 있다. 아론만이 기름부음을 받았으니(레위기 8:12) 이로 인해 대제사장의 독특한 칭호 가운데 하나가 '기름부음 받은 제사장'이었다(레위기 4:3,5,16; 21:10; 민수기 35:25 참조). 아론의 아들들, 곧 일반 제사장의 기름부음은 관유를 그 옷에 뿌리는 데 그친 것으로 보인다(출애굽기 29:21; 28:41).

대제사장은 독특한 예복을 입었으며 그것은 그가 죽으면 후계자에게 넘어갔다. 이 예복은 여덟 부분으로 이루어졌다.

(가) 흉패, 달리 '판결 흉패'라고도 불린다(출애굽기 28:15,29,30). 흉패는 본래 길이가 두 뼘 너비가 한 뼘이었으나 겹치면 네모가 되었으니 그 모양으로 착용했다. 그 위에 열두 보석을 넉 줄로 한 줄에 셋씩 물려 열두 지파에 대응하게 했고, 각 보석에는 이스라엘 자손 중 한 사람의 이름을 새겼다.

(나) 에봇. 두 부분으로 되어 하나는 등을 덮고 다른 하나는 앞, 곧 가슴과 상체를 덮었다. 이 두 부분은 어깨 위에서 큰 호마노 두 개로 이어 매었는데 각 보석에는 이스라엘 지파의 이름 여섯씩을 새겼다. 또 금실과 청색·자색·홍색 실과 가늘게 꼰 베실로 된 '정교한 띠'로 허리를 둘러 서로 이었다.

(다) 에봇 받침 겉옷. 에봇 자체보다 못한 재료로 온통 청색이었으니(31절) 이는 다만 '짜서 만든 것'임을 뜻한다(출애굽기 39:22). 에봇 바로 아래에 입었고 에봇보다 길었다. 이 겉옷 가장자리에는 청색·홍색·자색의 석류 장식이 달렸고 석류 사이마다 번갈아 금방울을 달았다. 방울은 대제사장이 성소에 들어가고 나올 때 소리가 나게 하려는 것이었다.

(라) 관, 곧 위쪽 두건. '여호와께 성결'이라 새긴 금패를 청색 끈으로 매어 달았다.

(마) 반포 속옷. 보석을 물린 자리처럼 바둑판 무늬 또는 마름모 무늬가 있는 세마포의 긴 옷이었다.

(바) 띠. 이 또한 세마포로 가슴에서부터 아래로 여러 번 몸을 둘렀고 그 끝이 발목까지 늘어졌다.

(사) 세마포 속바지. 허리와 넓적다리를 가렸다.

(아) 두건. 머리를 부분적으로 덮는 세마포 관이나, 관을 더한 대제사장의 것처럼 고깔 모양은 아니었다. 이 마지막 네 가지는 모든 제사장에게 공통된 것이었다.

대제사장만이 지성소에 들어갈 수 있었으니, 해마다 한 번 대속죄일에 들어가 속죄제의 피를 속죄소에 뿌리고 휘장 안에서 향을 살랐다(레위기 16:1 이하). 살인자는 당시의 대제사장이 살아 있는 동안 도피성을 떠날 수 없었다. 또 대제사장은 장례를 따라가거나 죽은 자를 위해 옷을 찢는 일이 금지되었다.

이스라엘에 왕이 있기 전에는 누구의 권한으로 대제사장이 임명되었는지 드러나지 않는다. 그 후로는 이 직분이 종교적 목적보다 정치적 목적으로 쓰인 것으로 보인다. 처음에는 종신으로 택했으나 솔로몬이 아비아달을 폐한 것을 보며(열왕기상 2:35), 헤롯은 여러 대제사장을 세웠으니 그리스도 당시에 안나스와 가야바 두 사람이 함께 살아 있었던 것도 이로써 설명될 수 있다(누가복음 3:2). 역대하 31:17에 따라 제사장 직무를 시작하는 통상의 나이는 스무 살로 여겨지나, 제사장이나 대제사장이 성년에 이르렀다면 실제로 자격이 없는 것은 아니었다. 또 레위기 21:17-21에 따라 흠 있는 자는 제단에서 섬길 수 없었다.

대제사장직에 대한 신학적 고찰은 이 책의 범위에 들지 않는다. 다만 그런 고찰은 대제사장의 직분과 예복과 기능과 섬김을 우리 주 예수 그리스도의 제사장직의 예표로, 또 복음에서 밝히 가르쳐진 진리를 그림자로 드러낸 것으로 살피는 일을 포함하리라는 점만 밝혀 둔다. 이는 히브리서에서 상당 부분 이루어졌다. 또한 그런 상징들이 뜻한 바로 여겨지는 모든 도덕적·영적 가르침도 거기 포함될 것이다.

entries.definition: Though during the sway of the Romans over Palestine they made a few substantial roads for their carts and chariots, yet for the most of the time, as today, the Jews had nothing such as we call roads, but only footpaths through which animals walk in single file. These are never cared for, no repairs are made or obstacles removed. This fact brings into striking prominence the figure of repairing a highway for the return Of the captives, or the coming of the great King. On special occasions kings had roads prepared for the progress of their armies, or their own going from place to place.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: 로마 지배 시기 팔레스타인에서 수레와 전차를 위한 견고한 도로 일부가 건설되었으나 대부분의 시기에는 오늘날처럼 짐승이 한 줄로 지나다니는 좁은 오솔길뿐이었고 정비나 보수는 이루어지지 않았다. 이런 사실은 포로 귀환자나 위대한 왕의 오심을 위해 '대로를 수축하라'는 비유적 표현을 두드러지게 만든다.

entries.definition: (place of caves), the name of city of Judah allotted with its suburbs to the priests. (1 Chronicles 6:58)
entries.definition_ko: '동굴들의 장소'라는 뜻으로 그 주변 지역과 함께 제사장에게 배정된 유다의 성읍이다(역대상 6:58).

entries.definition: (God is my portion) • Father of Eliakim. (2 Kings 18:37; Isaiah 22:20; 36:22) [Eliakim] • High priest in the reign of Josiah. (2 Kings 22:4) seq. 2Chr 34:9Seq.; 1 Esd. 1:8. (B.C. 623.) His high priesthood was rendered particularly illustrious by the great reformation effected under it by King Josiah, by the solemn Passover kept at Jerusalem in the 18th year of that king’s reign, and above all by the discovery which he made of the book of the law of Moses in the temple. • A Merarite Levite, son of Amzi (1 Chronicles 6:45) hebr. 30. • Another Merarite Levite, second son of Hosah. (1 Chronicles 26:11) • One of those who stood on the right hand of Ezra when he read the law to the people; doubtless a Levite, and probably a priest. (Nehemiah 8:4) (B.C 410.) • A priest of Anathoth, father of the prophet Jeremiah. (Jeremiah 1:1) (B.C. before 628.) • Father of Gemariah, who was one of Zedekiah’s envoys to Babylon. (Jeremiah 29:3) (B.C. long before 587.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님은 나의 분깃이시다'라는 뜻. (1) 엘리아김의 아버지(열왕기하 18:37). (2) 요시야 재위 시 대제사장으로(열왕기하 22:4) 성전에서 모세의 율법책을 발견한 것으로 유명하며 이는 요시야 왕의 대개혁과 예루살렘에서 지킨 성대한 유월절로 이어졌다. (3) 암시의 아들인 므라리 가문 레위인(역대상 6:45). (4) 호사의 둘째 아들인 또 다른 므라리 가문 레위인(역대상 26:11). (5) 에스라가 율법을 낭독할 때 그 오른편에 섰던 인물, 레위인 또는 제사장으로 추정(느헤미야 8:4). (6) 아나돗의 제사장이자 선지자 예레미야의 아버지(예레미야 1:1). (7) 시드기야가 바벨론에 보낸 사절 중 하나인 그마랴의 아버지(예레미야 29:3).

entries.definition: (praise), a native of Pirathon in Mount Ephraim, father of Abdon, one of the judges of Israel. (Judges 12:13,15)
entries.definition_ko: '찬양'이라는 뜻으로 에브라임 산지 비라돈 출신이며 이스라엘 사사 압돈의 아버지이다(사사기 12:13).

entries.definition: From the Hebrew Gibeah, meaning a curved round hill. But our translators have also employed the same English word for the very different term har, which has a much more extended sense than gibeah, meaning a whole district. For instance, in (Exodus 24:4) the “hill” is the same which is elsewhere in the same chapter, vs. (Exodus 24:12,13,18) etc., and book consistently and accurately rendered “mount” and “mountain.” The “country of the hills,” in (1:7; Joshua 9:1; 10:40; 11:16) is the elevated district of Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim, which is correctly called “the mountain” in the earliest descriptions of Palestine, (Numbers 13:29) and in many subsequent passages.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '기브아'(둥근 언덕을 뜻함)에서 유래한 번역어이나, 우리 번역자들은 '하르'(훨씬 넓은 지역, 곧 산지 전체를 뜻함)도 같은 영어 단어로 옮겼다. '산지의 땅'(신명기 1:7)은 유다·베냐민·에브라임의 고지대를 가리키며 초기 팔레스타인 묘사에서는 정확히 '산지'로 번역된다(민수기 13:29).

entries.definition: [Weights And MeasuresAND Measures]
entries.definition_ko: 도량형(WEIGHTS AND MEASURES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: the female of the common stag or Cervus elaphus . It is frequently noticed in the poetical parts of Scripture as emblematic of activity, (Genesis 49:21; Psalms 18:33) gentleness, (Proverbs 5:19) feminine modesty, (Song of Solomon 2:7; 3:5) earnest longing, (Psalms 42:1) and maternal affection. (Jeremiah 14:5) Its shyness and remoteness from the haunts of men are also alluded to, (Job 39:1) and its timidity, causing it to cast its young at the sound of thunder. (Psalms 29:9)
entries.definition_ko: 수사슴(Cervus elaphus)의 암컷을 가리키며 성경 시가서에서 민첩함(창세기 49:21), 온유함(잠언 5:19), 여성적 정숙함(아가 2:7), 간절한 갈망(시편 42:1), 모성애(예레미야 14:5)의 상징으로 자주 언급된다.

entries.definition: Both ancient Egyptian and modern Oriental doors were and are hung by means of pivots turning in sockets on both the upper and lower sides. (1 Kings 7:50) In Syria, and especially the Hauran, there are many ancient doors consisting of stone slabs with pivots carved out of the same piece, inserted in sockets above and below, and fixed during the building of the house. The allusion in (Proverbs 26:14) is thus clearly explained.
entries.definition_ko: 고대 애굽와 오늘날 동방의 문은 위아래 소켓에서 회전하는 돌쩌귀 방식으로 달려 있었다(열왕기상 7:50). 잠언 26:14의 언급이 이로써 명확히 설명된다.

entries.definition: (lamentation), Valley of, otherwise called “the valley of the son” or “children of Hinnom,” a deep and narrow ravine, with steep, rocky sides, to the south and west of Jerusalem, separating Mount Zion to the north from the “hill of evil counsel,” and the sloping rocky plateau of the “plain of Rephaim” to the south. The earliest mention of the valley of Hinnom is in (Joshua 15:8; 18:16) where the boundary line between the tribes of Judah and Benjamin is described as passing along the bed of the ravine. On the southern brow, overlooking the valley at its eastern extremity Solomon erected high places for Molech, (1 Kings 11:7) whose horrid rites were revived from time to time in the same vicinity the later idolatrous kings. Ahaz and Manasseh made their children “pass through the fire” in this valley, (2 Kings 16:3; 2 Chronicles 28:3; 33:6) and the fiendish custom of infant sacrifice to the fire-gods seems to have been kept up in Tophet, which was another name for this place. To put an end to these abominations the place was polluted by Josiah, who renders it ceremonially unclean by spreading over it human bones and other corruptions, (2 Kings 23:10,13,14; 2 Chronicles 34:4,5) from which time it appears to have become the common cesspool of the city, into which sewage was conducted, to be carried off by the waters of the Kidron. From its ceremonial defilement, and from the detested and abominable fire of Molech, if not from the supposed ever-burning funeral piles, the later Jews applied the name of this valley—Ge Hinnom, Gehenna (land of Hinnom)—to denote the place of eternal torment. In this sense the word is used by our Lord. (Matthew 5:29; 10:28; 23:15; Mark 9:43; Luke 12:5)
entries.definition_ko: '애곡'이라는 뜻으로 '힌놈의 아들(자녀)의 골짜기'라고도 불리며 예루살렘 남쪽과 서쪽의 깊고 좁은 협곡이며 시온산과 '악한 모략의 언덕', 르바임 평지의 경사진 바위 대지 사이를 갈라놓는다. 솔로몬은 이 골짜기 동쪽 끝 언덕에 몰렉을 위한 산당을 세웠고(열왕기상 11:7) 아하스와 므낫세는 이곳에서 자녀를 불 가운데로 지나게 했다(열왕기하 16:3). 요시야가 사람의 뼈 등을 뿌려 이곳을 의식적으로 부정하게 만들어 이런 가증한 일을 종식시켰으며(열왕기하 23:10) 이후 예루살렘의 공동 쓰레기장이 되었다. 이 의식적 부정함과 몰렉의 혐오스러운 불에서 후대 유대인들은 이 골짜기의 이름 '게힌놈(게헨나)'을 영원한 형벌의 장소를 가리키는 데 사용하게 되었으며 주님도 이 의미로 사용하셨다(마태복음 5:29).

entries.definition: [Behemoth]
entries.definition_ko: 베헤못(BEHEMOTH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (a noble race), an Adullamite, the friend of Judah. (Genesis 38:1,12) and see Genesis38:20
entries.definition_ko: '고귀한 혈통'이라는 뜻으로 아둘람 사람이며 유다의 친구이다(창세기 38:1).

entries.definition: (noble). • The king of Tyre who sent workmen and materials to Jerusalem, first, (2 Samuel 5:11; 1 Chronicles 14:1) to build a palace for David (B.C. 1064), whom he ever loved, (1 Kings 5:1) and again, 1Kin 5:10; 7:13; 2Chr 2:16To build the temple for Solomon, with whom he had a treaty of peace and commerce (1 Kings 5:11,12) He admitted Solomon’s ships issuing from Joppa, to a share in the profitable trade of the Mediterranean, (1 Kings 10:22) and the Jewish sailors, under the guidance of Tyrians, were taught to bring the gold of India, (1 Kings 9:26) to Solomon’s two harbors on the Red Sea. • Hiram was the name of a man of mixed race, (1 Kings 7:13,40) the principal architect and engineer sent by King Hiram to Solomon.
entries.definition_ko: '고귀한'이라는 뜻. (1) 두로 왕으로 다윗을 위한 왕궁 건축에 일꾼과 재료를 보냈고(사무엘하 5:11) 다시 솔로몬 성전 건축을 위해서도 그렇게 했으며 그와 평화·통상 조약을 맺었다(열왕기상 5:11). 솔로몬의 배들이 욥바에서 나와 지중해 무역에 참여하도록 허락했고 유대 선원들이 두로 사람들의 인도로 인도의 금을 홍해의 솔로몬 두 항구로 가져오는 법을 배우게 했다. (2) 혼혈 혈통의 사람으로(열왕기상 7:13) 히람 왕이 솔로몬에게 보낸 주요 건축가이자 기술자였다.

entries.definition: (descendans of Heth), The, the nation descended from Cheth (Authorized Version Heth), the second son of Canaan. Abraham bought from the “children of Heth” the field and the cave of Machpelah, belonging to Ephron the Hittite. ’They were then settled at the town which was afterwards, under its new name of Hebron, to become one of the most famous cities of Palestine, and which then bore the name of Kir-jatharba. (Genesis 23:19; 25:9) When the Israelites entered the promised land, we find the Hittites taking part against the invader, in equal alliance with the other Canaanite tribes. (Joshua 9:1; 11:3) etc. Henceforward the notices of the Hittites are very few and faint. We meet with two individuals, both attached to the person of David— • “Ahimelech the Hittite,” (1 Samuel 26:6) • Uriah the Hittite,” one of “the thirty” of David’s body-guard. (2 Samuel 23:39; 1 Chronicles 11:41)
entries.definition_ko: 가나안의 둘째 아들 헷에게서 나온 민족이다. 아브라함은 '헷 족속'에게서 에브론의 밭과 막벨라 굴을 샀으며 이곳은 후에 헤브론(당시 이름 기럇아르바)이라는 팔레스타인의 유명한 성읍이 되었다(창세기 23:19). 이스라엘이 약속의 땅에 들어갈 때 헷 족속은 다른 가나안 부족들과 동맹해 침입자에 맞섰다(여호수아 9:1). 이후 다윗과 관련된 두 인물 — '헷 사람 아히멜렉'(사무엘상 26:6)과 다윗의 삼십 근위병 중 하나인 '헷 사람 우리아'(사무엘하 23:39) — 외에는 거의 언급되지 않는다.

entries.definition: (villagers), The, descendants—the six in order— of Canaan the son of Ham. (Genesis 10:17; 1 Chronicles 1:15) We first encounter the actual people of the Hivites at the time of Jacob’s return to Canaan. (Genesis 34:2) We next meet with the Hivites during the conquest of Canaan. (Joshua 9:7; 11:19) The main body of the Hivites were at this time living in the northern confines of western Palestine— “under Hermon, in the land of Mizpeh,” (Joshua 11:3)—“in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entering in of Hamath.” (Judges 3:3) comp. 2Sam 24:7
entries.definition_ko: 함의 아들 가나안의 여섯째 후손이다(창세기 10:17). 야곱이 가나안으로 돌아올 때 처음 실제 히위 족속과 마주치며(창세기 34:2) 가나안 정복 시기에도 다시 등장한다(여호수아 9:7). 당시 대부분의 히위 족속은 팔레스타인 서부 북쪽 경계, '헤르몬 아래 미스바 땅'과 레바논산에 거주했다(여호수아 11:3).

entries.definition: (might of Jehovah), an ancestor of Zephaniah the prophet. (Zephaniah 1:1) (B.C. before 635.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 힘'이라는 뜻으로 선지자 스바냐의 조상이다(스바냐 1:1).

entries.definition: (might of Jehovah), one of those. who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:17) (B.C. 410.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 힘'이라는 뜻으로 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 인물 중 하나이다(느헤미야 10:17).

entries.definition: (beloved). This name is found in two places only (Numbers 10:29; Judges 4:11) Hobab was brother-in-law to Moses. (B.C. 1530.)
entries.definition_ko: '사랑받는'이라는 뜻으로 모세의 처남이었다(민수기 10:29).

entries.definition: (hiding-place), the place to which Abraham pursued the kings who had pillaged Sodom. (Genesis 14:15) It was situated “to the north of Damascus.”
entries.definition_ko: '숨는 곳'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함이 소돔을 약탈한 왕들을 추격한 곳이며(창세기 14:15) '다메섹 북쪽'에 위치했다.

entries.definition: (splendor), one of the sons of Zophah, among the descendants of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:37)
entries.definition_ko: '광채'라는 뜻으로 아셀 후손 소바의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 7:37).

entries.definition: (Praise ye Jehovah), son of the royal line of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:24) (B.C. about 406.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와를 찬양하라'는 뜻으로 유다 왕실 후손이다(역대상 3:24).

entries.definition: (Praise ye Jehovah). • A man of Manasseh, one of the heads of the half tribe on the east of Jordan (1 Chronicles 5:24) (B.C. 720.) • A man of Benjamin, son of Has-senuah. (1 Chronicles 9:7) • A Levite, who seems to have given his name to an important family in the tribe. (Ezra 2:40) (B.C. before 536.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와를 찬양하라'는 뜻. (1) 요단강 동쪽 므낫세 반 지파 우두머리 중 하나(역대상 5:24). (2) 하스누아의 아들인 베냐민 사람(역대상 9:7). (3) 지파 내 중요한 가문의 이름이 된 레위인(에스라 2:40).

entries.definition: (new moon), a woman named in the genealogies of Benjamin, (1 Chronicles 8:9) as the wife of Shaharaim.
entries.definition_ko: '초승달'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 족보에서 사하라임의 아내로 언급되는 여성이다(역대상 8:9).

entries.definition: (praise ye Jehovah). (Nehemiah 7:43) [Hodaviah]
entries.definition_ko: '여호와를 찬양하라'는 뜻이다(느헤미야 7:43). 호다위야(HODAVIAH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (majesty of Jehovah), one of the two wives of Ezra, a man of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:19) She is doubtless the same person as Jehudijah in ver. 18.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 위엄'이라는 뜻으로 유다 사람 에스라의 두 아내 중 하나이다(역대상 4:19). 18절의 여후디야와 동일 인물로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (majesty of Jehovah). • A Levite in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 8:7) and probably also (Nehemiah 9:5; 10:10) (B.C. 410.) • Another Levite at the same time. (Nehemiah 10:13) • A layman; one of the “heads” of the people at the same time. (Nehemiah 10:18)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 위엄'이라는 뜻. (1) 에스라·느헤미야 시대 레위인(느헤미야 8:7). (2) 같은 시기 다른 레위인(느헤미야 10:13). (3) 같은 시기 백성의 '우두머리' 중 하나인 평신도(느헤미야 10:18).

entries.definition: (partridge), the third of the five daughters of Zelophehad. (Numbers 26:33; 27:1; 36:11; Joshua 17:3) (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '자고새'라는 뜻으로 슬로브핫의 다섯 딸 중 셋째이다(민수기 26:33).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah impels), king of Hebron at the time of the conquest of Canaan. (Joshua 10:3) (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 재촉하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 가나안 정복 당시 헤브론 왕이다(여호수아 10:3).

entries.definition: or more correctly OLOFERNES, was, according to the book of Judith, a general of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians., Judith 2:4, who was slain by the Jewish heroine Judith during the siege of Bethulia. (B.C. 350.)
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 올로페르네스로 유딧서에 따르면 앗수르 왕 느부갓네살의 장군이며 베툴리아 포위전 중 유대 여걸 유딧에게 죽임을 당했다.

entries.definition: (sandy). • A town in the mountains of Judah. One of the first group, of which Debir was apparently the most considerable. (Joshua 15:51; 21:15) [Hilen] • A city of Moab. (Jeremiah 48:21) only. No identification of it has yet taken place.
entries.definition_ko: '모래의'라는 뜻. (1) 유다 산악 지대의 성읍으로 드빌이 가장 두드러진 첫 그룹에 속한다(여호수아 15:51). (2) 모압의 성읍(예레미야 48:21)으로 아직 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: (destruction), the form under which, in (1 Chronicles 1:39) an Edomite name appears which in (Genesis 36:22) is given Hemam.
entries.definition_ko: 역대상 1:39에서 창세기 36:22의 에돔 이름 헤맘이 이 형태로 나타난다.

entries.definition: [Weights And MeasuresAND Measures]
entries.definition_ko: 도량형(WEIGHTS AND MEASURES) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The Hebrew debash in the first place applied to the product of the bee, to which exclusively we give the name of honey. All travellers agree in describing Palestine as a land “flowing with milk and honey,” (Exodus 3:8) bees being abundant even in the remote parts of the wilderness, where they deposit their honey in the crevices of rocks or in hollow trees. In some parts of northern Arabia the hills are so well stocked with bees that no sooner are hives placed than they are occupied. In the second place the term debash applies to a decoction of the juice of the grape, which is still called dibs, and which forms an article of commerce in the East, it was this, and not ordinary beehoney, which Jacob sent to Joseph, (Genesis 43:11) and which the Tyrians purchased from Palestine. (Ezekiel 27:17) A third kind has been described by some writers as a “vegetable” honey, by which is meant the exudations of certain trees and shrubs, such as the Tamarix mannifera, found in the peninsula of Sinai, or the stunted oaks of Luristan and Mesopotamia . The honey which Jonathan ate in the wood, (1 Samuel 14:25) and the “wild honey” which supported John the Baptist, (Matthew 3:42) have been referred to this species. But it was probably the honey of wild bees.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '데바쉬'는 우선적으로 벌의 산물, 곧 우리가 꿀이라 부르는 것을 가리킨다. 여행자들은 팔레스타인을 '젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅'으로 묘사하며(출애굽기 3:8) 벌들은 광야 오지에서도 흔해 바위 틈이나 속 빈 나무에 꿀을 저장했다. 또한 '데바쉬'는 포도즙을 졸인 것(오늘날의 딥스)을 가리키기도 하며 야곱이 요셉에게 보낸 것도 이것이었다(창세기 43:11). 요나단이 숲에서 먹은 꿀(사무엘상 14:25)과 세례 요한을 지탱한 '석청'(마태복음 3:4)은 야생 벌꿀로 보인다.

entries.definition: Various kinds of hooks are noticed in the Bible, of which the following are the most important: • Fishing hooks. (Job 41:2; Isaiah 19:8); Habb 1:15 • A ring, such as in our country is placed through the nose of a bull, and similarly used in the East for leading about lions— (Ezekiel 19:4) where the Authorized Version has “with chains—camels and other animals. Called “thorn” in (Job 41:2) A similar method was adopted for leading prisoners. (2 Chronicles 33:11) • The hooks of the pillars of the tabernacle. (Exodus 26:32,37; 27:10) ff.; Exod 38:13 ff. • A vinedressers pruning-hook. (Isaiah 2:4; 18:5; Micah 4:3; Joel 3:10) • A flesh-hook for getting up the joints of meat out of the boiling-pot. (Exodus 27:3; 1 Samuel 2:13,14) • Probably “hooks” used for the purpose of hanging up animals to flay them. (Ezekiel 40:43)
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 언급된 여러 종류의 갈고리 중 주요한 것은 낚싯바늘(욥기 41:2), 소나 사자·낙타 등을 끌 때 코에 꿰는 고리(에스겔 19:4), 포로를 끌 때도 쓰인 방법(역대하 33:11), 성막 기둥의 갈고리(출애굽기 26:32), 포도나무 가지치기 낫(이사야 2:4), 삶은 고기를 건져내는 고기 갈고리(출애굽기 27:3), 짐승을 매달아 가죽을 벗기는 데 쓰인 갈고리(에스겔 40:43) 등이다.

entries.definition: (pugilist) and Phinehas(brazen mouth), the two sons of Eli, who fulfilled their hereditary sacerdotal duties at Shiloh. Their brutal rapacity and lust, (1 Samuel 2:12-17,22) filled the people with disgust and indignation, and provoked the curse which was denounced against their father’s house, first by an unknown prophet, (1 Samuel 2:27-36) and then by Samuel. ch. (1 Samuel 3:11-14) They were both cut off in one day in the flower of their age, and the ark which they had accompanied to battle against the Philistines was lost on the same occasion. (1 Samuel 4:10,11) (B.C. 1130.)
entries.definition_ko: '권투 선수'라는 뜻(비느하스는 '놋 입'이라는 뜻)으로 엘리의 두 아들이며 실로에서 세습 제사 직무를 수행했다. 그들의 잔혹한 탐욕과 음욕(사무엘상 2:12)이 백성에게 혐오와 분노를 불러일으켰고 아버지 집안에 대한 저주를 초래했다. 둘 다 하루 만에 젊은 나이에 죽었고 그들이 함께 블레셋과의 전투에 나갔던 언약궤도 같은 날 빼앗겼다(사무엘상 4:10).

entries.definition: (mountain), Mount. • The mountain on which Aaron died. (Numbers 20:25,27) It was “on the boundary line,” (Numbers 20:23) or “at the edge,” ch. (Numbers 33:37) of the land of Edom. It was the halting-place of the people next after Kadesh, ch. (Numbers 20:22; 33:37) and they quitted it for Zalmonah, ch. (Numbers 33:41) in the road to the Red Sea. ch. (Numbers 21:4) It was during the encampment at Kadesh that Aaron was gathered to his fathers. Mount Hor is situated on the eastern side of the great valley of the Arabah, the highest and most conspicuous of the whole range of the sandstone mountains of Edom, having close beneath it on its: eastern side the mysterious; city of Petra. It is now the Jebel Nebi-Harim “the mountain of the prophet Aaron.” Its height is 4800 feet above the Mediterranean; that is to say, about 1700 feet above the town of Petra, 4800 above the level of the Arabah, and more than 6000 above the Dead Sea. The mountain is marked far and near by its double top, which rises like a huge castellated building from a lower base, and is surmounted by a circular dome of the tomb of Aaron, a distinct white spot on the dark red surface of the mountain. The chief interest of Mount Hor consists in the prospect from its summit, the last view of Aaron—that view which was to him what Pisgah was to his brother. • A mountain, entirely distinct from the preceding, named in (Numbers 34:7,8) only, as one of the marks of the northern boundary of the land which the children of Israel were about to conquer. This Mount Hor is the great chain of Lebanon itself.
entries.definition_ko: '산'이라는 뜻. (1) 아론이 죽은 산으로(민수기 20:25) 에돔 땅의 경계에 위치했으며 백성이 가데스 다음으로 머문 곳이었다. 요단강 동쪽 아라바 계곡의 동쪽에 위치하며 에돔 사암산맥 중 가장 높고 눈에 띄는 산으로, 그 동쪽 아래에 신비로운 도시 페트라가 있다. 오늘날에는 '선지자 아론의 산'이라는 뜻의 제벨 네비하룬으로 불리며 높이는 해발 4800피트이다. (2) 앞의 산과는 전혀 다른 산으로 민수기 34:7에만 언급되며 이스라엘이 정복할 땅의 북쪽 경계 지표 중 하나이다. 이 호르산은 레바논 산맥 전체를 가리키는 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: (mountainous), king of Gezer at the time of the conquest of the southwestern part of Palestine. (Joshua 10:33)
entries.definition_ko: '산이 많은'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 남서부 정복 당시 게셀 왕이다(여호수아 10:33).

entries.definition: (desert). [Sinai, Or Sinai]
entries.definition_ko: '광야'라는 뜻. 시내(SINAI) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (sacred), one of the fortified places in the territory of Naphtali; named with Iron and Migdalel. (Joshua 19:38) Van Deuteronomy Velde suggests Hurah as the site of Horem.
entries.definition_ko: '거룩한'이라는 뜻으로 납달리 영토의 요새화된 곳 중 하나이며 이론, 믹달엘과 함께 언급된다(여호수아 19:38).

entries.definition: (conspicous mountain), the name of the desert station where the Israelites encamped, (Numbers 33:32) probably the same as Gudgodah. (10:7)
entries.definition_ko: '눈에 띄는 산'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 진 친 광야 진영지의 이름이며(민수기 33:32) 굿고다(신명기 10:7)와 같은 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (cave-dweller). • A Horite, son of Lotan the son of Seir. (Genesis 36:22; 1 Chronicles 1:39; Genesis 36:30) • A man of Simeon, father of Shaphat. (Numbers 13:5)
entries.definition_ko: '동굴 거주자'라는 뜻. (1) 세일의 아들 로단의 아들인 호리 사람(창세기 36:22). (2) 시므온 사람으로 사밧의 아버지(민수기 13:5).

entries.definition: and Ho’rites (descendants of Hori), the aboriginal inhabitants of Mount Seir, (Genesis 14:6) and probably allied to the Emim and Raphaim. The name Horite appears to have been derived from their habits as “cave-dwellers” Their excavated dwellings are still found in hundreds in the sandstone cliffs and mountains of Edom, and especially in Petra.
entries.definition_ko: 호리(HORI)의 후손인 '호리 족속'으로 세일산의 원주민이며(창세기 14:6) 에밈, 르바임과 관련이 있는 것으로 보인다. 호리라는 이름은 이들이 '동굴 거주자'였던 습성에서 유래한 것으로 보이며 오늘날에도 에돔의 사암 절벽과 산악 지대, 특히 페트라에서 그들이 파낸 거처가 수백 개씩 발견된다.

entries.definition: (a place laid waste), or Zephath, (Judges 1:17) was the chief town of a king of a Canaanitish tribe on the south of Palestine, which was reduced by Joshua, and became a city of the territory of Judah, (Joshua 15:30; 1 Samuel 30:30) but apparently belonged to Simeon. (1 Chronicles 4:30)
entries.definition_ko: '황폐해진 곳'이라는 뜻으로(또는 스밧, 사사기 1:17) 팔레스타인 남쪽 가나안 부족 왕의 수도였으나 여호수아에게 정복되어 유다 영토의 성읍이 되었다(여호수아 15:30). 시므온에 속한 것으로도 언급된다(역대상 4:30).

entries.definition: The word “horn” is often used metaphorically to signify strength and honor, because horns are the chief weapons and ornaments of the animals which possess them; hence they are also used as a type of victory. Of strength the horn of the unicorn was the most frequent representative, (33:17) etc., but not always; comp. (1 Kings 22:11) where probably horns of iron, worn defiantly and symbolically on the head, are intended. Among the Druses upon Mount Lebanon the married women wear silver horns on their heads. In the sense of honor, the word horn stands for the abstract “my horn,” (Job 16:16) “all the horn of Israel,” (1 Samuel 2:3) and so for the supreme authority. It also stands for the concrete, whence it comes to mean king, kingdom. (Daniel 8:2) etc.; Zech 1:18Out of either or both of these last two metaphors sprang the idea of representing gods with horns.
entries.definition_ko: '뿔'이라는 단어는 흔히 힘과 명예를 은유적으로 나타내는 데 쓰이는데, 뿔이 그 소유 동물의 주요 무기이자 장식이기 때문이며 승리의 상징으로도 쓰인다. 힘의 상징으로는 들소의 뿔이 가장 자주 대표로 쓰이며, 명예의 의미로는 '내 뿔'(욥기 16:16), '이스라엘의 온 뿔'(사무엘상 2:3)처럼 절대 권위를 나타내는 데도 쓰이고, 왕이나 나라를 뜻하는 데까지 확장된다(다니엘 8:2).

entries.definition: The hornet bears a general resemblance to the common wasp, only it is larger. It is exceedingly fierce and voracious, especially in hot climates and its sting is frequently dangerous. In Scripture the hornet is referred to only by the means which Jehovah employed for the extirpation of the Canaanites. (Exodus 23:28; 7:20; Joshua 24:12) Wisd. 12:8. (It is said that the Phaselitae, a Phoenician people, were driven from their locality by hornets; and other examples are given in Paxton’s “Illustrations of Scripture,” 1:303.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 일반 말벌과 비슷하나 더 크며 매우 사납고 탐욕스럽다. 특히 더운 기후에서 그 침은 종종 위험하다. 성경에서는 여호와가 가나안 족속을 몰아내기 위해 사용하신 수단으로만 언급된다(출애굽기 23:28).

entries.definition: (two caverns), a town of Moab, possibly a sanctuary, named with Zoar and Luhith. (Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:3,5,34)
entries.definition_ko: '두 동굴'이라는 뜻으로 모압의 성읍이며 아마도 성소였던 것으로 보이고 소알, 루힛과 함께 언급된다(이사야 15:5).

entries.definition: (native of Horonaim), The, the designation of Sanballat. (Nehemiah 2:10,19; 13:28) It is derived by Gesenius from Horonaim.
entries.definition_ko: '호로나임 출신'이라는 뜻으로 산발랏에게 붙은 명칭이다(느헤미야 2:10).

entries.definition: The most striking feature in the biblical notices of the horse is the exclusive application of it to warlike operations; in no instance is that useful animal employed for the purposes of ordinary locomotion or agriculture, if we except (Isaiah 28:28) The animated description of the horse in (Job 39:19-25) applies solely to the war-horse. The Hebrews in the patriarchal age, as a pastoral race, did not stand in need of the services Of the horse, and for a long period after their settlement in Canaan they dispensed with it, partly in consequence of the hilly nature of the country, which only admitted of the use of chariots in certain localities, (Judges 1:19) and partly in consequence to the prohibition in (17:16) which would be held to apply at all periods. David first established a force of cavalry and chariots, (2 Samuel 8:4) but the great supply of horses was subsequently effected by Solomon through his connection with Egypt. (1 Kings 4:26) Solomon also established a very active trade in horses, which were brought by dealers out of Egypt and resold, at a profit, to the Hittites. With regard to the trappings and management of the horse we have little information. The bridle was placed over the horse’s nose, (Isaiah 30:28) and a bit or curb is also mentioned. (2 Kings 19:28; Psalms 32:9; Proverbs 26:3; Isaiah 37:29) In the Authorized Version it is incorrectly given “bridle,” with the exception of (Psalms 32:1) ... Saddles were not used until a late period. The horses were not shod, and therefore hoofs are hard “as flint,” (Isaiah 5:28) were regarded as a great merit. The chariot-horses were covered with embroidered trappings (Ezekiel 27:20) Horses and chariots were used also in idolatrous processions, as noticed in regard to the sun. (2 Kings 23:11)
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 말에 대한 두드러진 특징은 전쟁 용도로만 배타적으로 언급된다는 점이며 일상 이동이나 농사에 쓰인 예는 없다(이사야 28:28 제외). 히브리인들은 족장 시대 목축민으로서 말이 필요 없었고, 가나안 정착 후에도 산악 지형과 신명기 17:16의 금지 규정으로 오랫동안 말을 두지 않았다. 다윗이 처음 기병과 병거대를 창설했으며(사무엘하 8:4) 솔로몬이 애굽와의 관계를 통해 대량 공급을 이루었다(열왕기상 4:26).

entries.definition: Heb. ’alukah, occurs once only, viz. (Proverbs 30:16) There is little doubt that ’alukah denotes some species of leech, or rather is the generic term for any bloodsucking annelid.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '알루카'로 잠언 30:16에만 나오며 거머리의 일종 또는 흡혈성 환형동물 전반을 가리키는 일반 명칭으로 보인다.

entries.definition: a Merarite Levite, chosen by David to be one of the first doorkeepers to the ark after its arrival in Jerusalem. (1 Chronicles 16:38) (B.C. 1014.) (refuge), a city of Asher, (Joshua 19:29) The next landmark on the boundary to Tyre.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 므라리 가문 레위인으로 언약궤가 예루살렘에 도착한 후 다윗이 세운 첫 문지기 중 하나였다(역대상 16:38). (2) '피난처'라는 뜻으로 아셀의 성읍이며(여호수아 19:29) 두로로 가는 경계의 다음 지표이다.

entries.definition: (save now). “Save, we pray!” the cry of the multitudes as they thronged in our Lord’s triumphal procession into Jerusalem. (Matthew 21:9,15; Mark 11:9,10; John 12:13) The Psalm from which it was taken, the 118th, was one with which they were familiar from being accustomed to recite the 25th and 26th verses at the feast of tabernacles, forming a part of the great hallel. Ps. 113-118.
entries.definition_ko: '이제 구원하소서'라는 뜻으로 무리가 주님의 예루살렘 승리 입성 행렬에 몰려들며 외친 함성이다(마태복음 21:9). 이 말이 인용된 시편 118편은 초막절에 25, 26절을 낭송하는 관습(대할렐의 일부) 덕분에 익숙한 시편이었다.

entries.definition: (salvation), son of Beeri, and first of the minor prophets. Probably the life, or rather the prophetic career, of Hosea extended from B.C. 784 to 723, a period of fifty-nine years. The prophecies of Hosea were delivered in the kingdom of Israel. Jeroboam II was on the throne, and Israel was at the height of its earthly splendor. Nothing is known of the prophet’s life excepting what may be gained from his book.
entries.definition_ko: '구원'이라는 뜻으로 브에리의 아들이며 소선지자 중 첫째이다. 그의 생애, 정확히는 예언 활동은 주전 784년부터 723년까지 59년에 걸친 것으로 추정된다. 호세아의 예언은 이스라엘 왕국에서 선포되었으며 당시 여로보암 2세가 왕위에 있어 이스라엘이 지상 영화의 정점에 있던 시기였다.

entries.definition: This book consists of fourteen chapters. It is easy to recognize two great divisions in the book: (1) ch. 1 to 3; (2) ch. 4 to end. The subdivision of these several parts is a work of greater difficulty— • The first division should probably be subdivided into three separate poems, each originating in a distinct aim, and each after its own fashion attempting to express the idolatry of Israel by imagery borrowed from the matrimonial relation. • Attempts have been made to subdivide the second part of the book. These divisions are made either according to reigns of contemporary kings or according to the subject-matter of the poem. The prophecies were probably collected by Hosea himself toward the end of his career. Of his style Eichhorn says, “His discourse is like a garland woven of a multiplicity of flowers; images are woven upon images, metaphor strung upon metaphor. Like a bee he flies from one flower-bed to another, that he may suck his honey from the most varied pieces....Often he is prone to approach to allegory; often he sinks down in obscurity.”
entries.definition_ko: 14장으로 구성되며 크게 두 부분(1-3장, 4장 이후)으로 나뉜다. 첫 부분은 이스라엘의 우상숭배를 혼인 관계의 이미지로 표현하는 세 개의 독립된 시로 세분될 수 있다. 아이히호른은 그의 문체를 '다양한 꽃으로 엮은 화환과 같다'고 평가하며 이미지와 은유가 겹겹이 짜여 있고 벌처럼 이 꽃밭 저 꽃밭을 옮겨 다니며 꿀을 빨아들이나 때로 알레고리에 가까워지고 때로 모호함에 빠진다고 말한다.

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah aids). • A man who assisted in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem after it had been rebuilt by Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 12:32) (B.C. 446.). • The father of a certain Jezaniah or Azariah, who was a man of note after, the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezsar. (Jeremiah 42:1; 43:2) (B.C. after 588.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 도우시는 자'라는 뜻. (1) 느헤미야가 재건한 예루살렘 성벽 봉헌식을 도운 인물(느헤미야 12:32). (2) 느부갓네살의 예루살렘 파괴 후 유력 인물이었던 여사냐(또는 아사랴)의 아버지(예레미야 42:1).

entries.definition: (haste), one of the early kings of Edom. Genesis36:34,36; 1Chr 1:45,46
entries.definition_ko: '서두름'이라는 뜻으로 초기 에돔 왕 중 하나이다(창세기 36:34).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah hears), one of the sons of Jeconiah or Jehoiachin, the last king but one of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:18)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으신다'는 뜻으로 유다의 마지막에서 둘째 왕 여고냐(여호야긴)의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 3:18).

entries.definition: (salvation). • The nineteenth, last and best king of Israel. He succeeded Pekah, whom he slew in a successful conspiracy, thereby fulfilling a prophecy of Isaiah. (Isaiah 7:16) In the third year of his reign (B.C. 726) Shalmaneser cruelly stormed the strong caves of Beth-arbel, (Hosea 8:14) and made cruel tributary, (2 Kings 17:3) for three years. At the end of this period Hoshea entered into a secret alliance with So, king, of Egypt, to throw off the Assyrian yoke. The alliance did him no good; it was revealed, to the court of Nineveh by the Assyrian party in Ephraim, and Hoshea was immediately seized as a rebellious vasal, shut up in prison, and apparently treated with the utmost indignity. (Micah 5:1) Of the subsequent fortunes of Hoshea nothing is known. • The son of Nun, i.e. Joshua, (32:44) and also in Numb 13:8Though to there the Authorized Version has Oshea. • Shon of Azaziah, (1 Chronicles 27:20) like his great namesake, a man of Ephraim, ruler of his tribe in the time of King David. (B.C. 1019.) • One of the heads of the people who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:23) (B.C. 410.)
entries.definition_ko: '구원'이라는 뜻. (1) 이스라엘의 열아홉째이자 마지막이며 가장 나은 왕으로 베가를 성공적인 모반으로 죽이고 왕위를 이어 이사야의 예언을 성취했다(이사야 7:16). 재위 3년째(주전 726년) 살만에셀이 벧아르벨의 견고한 굴들을 잔혹하게 함락시켰고(호세아 8:14) 3년간 조공을 강요했다(열왕기하 17:3). 이후 애굽 왕 소와 비밀 동맹을 맺어 앗수르의 멍에를 벗으려 했으나 에브라임의 친앗수르파가 니느웨 궁정에 이를 밀고해 반역한 봉신으로 즉시 붙잡혀 투옥되고 극도의 모욕을 당한 것으로 보인다(미가 5:1). 그 후의 운명은 알려지지 않았다. (2) 눈의 아들, 곧 여호수아의 본래 이름(신명기 32:44). (3) 아사시야의 아들로(역대상 27:20) 다윗 시대 에브라임 지파장. (4) 느헤미야와 언약을 맺은 백성의 우두머리 중 하나(느헤미야 10:23).

entries.definition: Hospitality was regarded by most nations of the ancient world as one of the chief virtues. The Jewish laws respecting strangers (Leviticus 19:33,34) and the poor, (Leviticus 23:14) seq. Deuteronomy 15:7And concerning redemption (Leviticus 25:23) seq., etc. are framed in accordance with the spirit of hospitality. In the law compassion to strangers is constantly enforced by the words “for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.” (Leviticus 19:34) And before the law, Abraham’s entertainment of the angels, (Genesis 18:1) seq., and Lot’s, (Genesis 19:1) are in exact agreement with its precepts, and with modern usage. Comp. (Exodus 2:20; Judges 13:15; 19:17,20,21) In the New Testament hospitality is yet more markedly enjoined; and in the more civilized state of society which then prevailed, its exercise became more a social virtue than a necessity of patriarchal life. The good Samaritan stands for all ages as an example of Christian hospitality. The neglect of Christ is symbolized by inhospitality to our neighbors. (Matthew 25:43) The apostles urged the Church to “follow after hospitality,” (Romans 12:13) cf. 1Tim 5:10To remember Abraham’s example, (Hebrews 13:2) to “use hospitality one to another without grudging,” (1 Peter 4:9) while a bishop must be a “lover of hospitality (Titus 1:8) cf. 1Tim 3:2The practice of the early Christians was in accord with these precepts. They had all things in common, and their hospitality was a characteristic of their belief. In the patriarchal ages we may take Abraham’s example as the most fitting, as we have of it the fullest account. “The account,” says Mr. Lane, “of Abraham’s entertaining the three angels related in the Bible, presents a perfect picture of the manner in which a modern Bedawee sheikh receives travellers arriving at his encampment.” The Oriental respect for the covenant of bread and salt, or salt alone, certainly sprang from the high regard in which hospitality was held.
entries.definition_ko: 환대는 고대 세계 대부분의 민족에게 주요 덕목으로 여겨졌다. 나그네에 관한 유대 율법(레위기 19:33)과 가난한 자, 속량에 관한 규정들은 환대의 정신에 따라 만들어졌다. 율법 이전에도 아브라함이 천사들을 접대한 일(창세기 18:1)과 롯의 접대(창세기 19:1)가 이 정신 및 오늘날 관습과 정확히 일치한다. 신약에서는 환대가 더욱 강조되며 선한 사마리아인은 모든 시대 그리스도인 환대의 모범으로 남아 있다.

entries.definition: (signet ring), a man of Asher, son of Heber, of the family Of Beriah. (1 Chronicles 7:32) (B.C. 1490.)
entries.definition_ko: '인장 반지'라는 뜻으로 아셀 사람 헤벨의 아들, 브리아 가문이다(역대상 7:32).

entries.definition: (signet ring), a man of Aroer, father of Shamu and Jehiel. (1 Chronicles 11:44) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '인장 반지'라는 뜻으로 아로엘 사람이며 사마와 여이엘의 아버지이다(역대상 11:44).

entries.definition: (fullness), the thirteenth son of Heman, “the king’s seer,” (1 Chronicles 25:4,28) and therefore a Kohathite Levite. (B.C. 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '충만함'이라는 뜻으로 왕의 선견자 헤만의 열셋째 아들이며 고핫 가문 레위인이다(역대상 25:4).

entries.definition: The ancient Hebrews were probably unacquainted with the division of the natural day into twenty-four parts; but they afterwards parcelled out the period between sunrise and sunset into a series of divisions distinguished by the sun’s course. The early Jews appear to have divided the day into four parts, (Nehemiah 9:3) and the night into three watches, (Judges 7:19) and even in the New Testament we find a trace of this division in (Matthew 20:1-5) At what period the Jews first became acquainted with the division of the day into twelve hours is unknown, but it is generally supposed they learned it from the Babylonians during the captivity. It was known to the Egyptians at a very early period. They had twelve hours of the day and of the night. There are two kinds of hours, viz. (1) the astronomical or equinoctial hour, i.e. the 24th part of a civil day, and (2) the natural hour, i.e. the 12th part of the natural day, or of the time between sunrise and sunset. These are the hours meant in the New Testament, (John 11:9) etc., and it must be remembered that they perpetually vary in length, so as to be very different at different times of he year. For the purpose of prayer the old division of the day into four portions was continued in the temple service. as we see from (Acts 2:15; 3:1; 10:9)
entries.definition_ko: 고대 히브리인들은 하루를 24등분하는 방식을 몰랐을 것이며 후에 일출부터 일몰까지를 태양의 경로에 따라 여러 구간으로 나누었다. 초기 유대인들은 낮을 네 부분으로(느헤미야 9:3), 밤을 세 경(사사기 7:19)으로 나눈 것으로 보인다. 하루를 12시간으로 나누는 방식을 언제 처음 알게 되었는지는 알 수 없으나 대개 포로기 바벨론인들에게서 배운 것으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: The houses of the rural poor in Egypt, as well as in most parts of Syria, Arabia and Persia, are generally mere huts of mud or sunburnt bricks. In some parts of Palestine and Arabia stone is used, and in certain districts caves in the rocks are used as dwellings. (Amos 5:11) The houses are usually of one story only, viz., the ground floor, and often contain only one apartment. Sometimes a small court for the cattle is attached; and in some cases the cattle are housed in the same building, or the live in a raised platform, and, the cattle round them on the ground. (1 Samuel 28:24) The windows are small apertures high up in the walls, sometimes grated with wood. The roofs are commonly but not always flat, and are usually formed of plaster of mud and straw laid upon boughs or rafters; and upon the flat roofs, tents or “booths” of boughs or rushes are often raised to be used as sleeping-places in summer. The difference between the poorest houses and those of the class next above them is greater than between these and the houses of the first rank. The prevailing plan of eastern houses of this class presents, as was the case in ancient Egypt, a front of wall, whose blank and mean appearance is usually relieved only by the door and a few latticed and projecting windows. Within this is a court or courts with apartments opening into them. Over the door is a projecting window with a lattice more or less elaborately wrought, which, except in times of public celebrations is usually closed. (2 Kings 9:30) An awning is sometimes drawn over the court, and the floor is strewed with carpets on festive occasions. The stairs to the upper apartments are in Syria usually in a corner of the court. Around part, if not the whole, of the court is a veranda, often nine or ten feet deep, over which, when there is more than one floor, runs a second gallery of like depth, with a balustrade. When there is no second floor, but more than one court, the women’s apartments—hareems, harem or haram—are usually in the second court; otherwise they form a separate building within the general enclosure, or are above on the first floor. When there is an upper story, the ka’ah forms the most important apartment, and thus probably answers to the “upper room,” which was often the guest-chamber. (Luke 22:12; Acts 1:13; 9:37; 20:8) The windows of the upper rooms often project one or two feet, and form a kiosk or latticed chamber. Such may have been “the chamber in the wall.” (2 Kings 4:10,11) The “lattice,” through which Ahasiah fell, perhaps belonged to an upper chamber of this kind, (2 Kings 1:2) as also the “third loft,” from which Eutychus fell. (Acts 20:9) comp. Jere 22:13Paul preached in such a room on account of its superior rise and retired position. The outer circle in an audience in such a room sat upon a dais, or upon cushions elevated so as to be as high as the window-sill. From such a position Eutychus could easily fall. There are usually no special bed-rooms in eastern houses. The outer doors are closed with a wooden lock, but in some cases the apartments are divided from each other by curtains only. There are no chimneys, but fire is made when required with charcoal in a chafing-dish; or a fire of wood might be made in the open court of the house (Luke 22:65) Some houses in Cairo have an apartment open in front to the court with two or more arches and a railing, and a pillar to support the wall above. It was in a chamber of this size to be found in a palace, that our Lord was being arraigned before the high priest at the time when the denial of him by St. Peter took place.
