He “turned and looked” on Peter as he stood by the fire in the court, (Luke 22:56,61; John 18:24) whilst he himself was in the “hall of judgment.” In no point do Oriental domestic habits differ more from European than in the use of the roof. Its flat surface is made useful for various household purposes, as drying corn, hanging up linen, and preparing figs and raisins. The roofs are used as places of recreation in the evening, and often as sleeping-places at night. (1 Samuel 9:25,26; 2 Samuel 11:2; 16:22; Job 27:18; Proverbs 21:9; Daniel 4:29) They were also used as places for devotion and even idolatrous worship. (2 Kings 23:12; Jeremiah 19:13; 32:29; Zephaniah 1:6; Acts 10:9) At the time of the feast of tabernacles booths were erected by the Jews on the top of their houses. Protection of the roof by parapets was enjoined by the law. (22:8) Special apartments were devoted in larger houses to winter and summer uses. (Jeremiah 36:22; Amos 3:15) The ivory house of Ahab was probably a palace largely ornamented with inlaid ivory. The circumstance of Samson’s pulling down the house by means of the pillars may be explained by the fact of the company being assembled on tiers of balconies above each other, supported by central pillars on the basement; when these were pulled down the whole of the upper floors would fall also. (Judges 16:26)
entries.definition_ko:
애굽과 수리아와 아라비아와 바사 대부분에서 시골 가난한 이들의 집은 대개 진흙이나 볕에 말린 벽돌로 지은 오두막에 지나지 않는다. 팔레스타인과 아라비아의 어떤 곳에서는 돌을 쓰고, 어떤 지역에서는 바위굴을 거처로 쓴다(아모스 5:11). 집은 대개 한 층 곧 지면층뿐이며 방이 하나뿐인 경우가 많다. 때로 가축을 위한 작은 뜰이 딸리고, 어떤 경우에는 가축을 같은 건물에 두어 사람은 높인 단에 살고 가축은 그 아래 땅에 둔다(사무엘상 28:24). 창은 벽 높이 난 작은 구멍이며 때로 나무 격자를 댄다. 지붕은 흔히, 다만 늘 그렇지는 않게 평평하며 대개 나뭇가지나 서까래 위에 진흙과 짚을 섞은 회를 발라 만든다. 이 평평한 지붕 위에 나뭇가지나 갈대로 장막 곧 '초막'을 세워 여름에 잠자리로 쓰는 일이 많다.
가장 가난한 집과 그 위 계층의 집 사이의 차이가, 그 계층의 집과 최상층의 집 사이의 차이보다 크다. 이 계층의 동방 집의 흔한 배치는 옛 애굽에서 그러하였듯 앞면이 벽이어서, 그 밋밋하고 초라한 모습이 대개 문과 격자를 댄 몇몇 내민 창으로만 덜어진다. 그 안에 뜰이 하나 또는 여럿 있고 방들이 그리로 열린다. 문 위에는 다소 정교하게 만든 격자를 댄 내민 창이 있는데, 공적인 잔치 때 말고는 대개 닫아 둔다(열왕기하 9:30). 때로 뜰 위에 차일을 치고, 잔치 때에는 바닥에 양탄자를 깐다. 위층으로 오르는 층계는 수리아에서는 대개 뜰 한 모퉁이에 있다. 뜰의 일부, 때로는 전부를 둘러 흔히 아홉이나 열 자 깊이의 회랑이 있고, 층이 하나 이상이면 그 위로 난간을 둔 같은 깊이의 둘째 회랑이 돈다. 둘째 층이 없되 뜰이 둘 이상이면 여인의 거처인 하렘이 대개 둘째 뜰에 있고, 그렇지 않으면 전체 울 안에 따로 된 건물을 이루거나 위층에 있다. 위층이 있으면 '카아'가 가장 중요한 방을 이루니, 아마도 흔히 손님방으로 쓰인 '다락방'에 해당할 것이다(누가복음 22:12; 사도행전 1:13; 9:37; 20:8). 위층 방의 창은 흔히 한두 자 내밀어 격자를 댄 방을 이루는데, 열왕기하 4:10,11의 '벽에 작은 방'이 그런 것이었을 수 있다. 아하시야가 떨어진 '난간'도(열왕기하 1:2) 아마 이런 위층 방의 것이었을 터이고, 유두고가 떨어진 '삼층'도 그러하다(사도행전 20:9). 바울이 그런 방에서 전한 것은 그 방이 더 높고 외졌기 때문이다. 그런 방에서 청중의 바깥쪽은 단 위나 창턱 높이만큼 높인 방석에 앉았으니, 그런 자리에서 유두고가 쉽게 떨어질 수 있었다.
동방 집에는 대개 따로 된 침실이 없다. 바깥문은 나무 자물쇠로 잠그나 어떤 경우에는 방과 방 사이를 휘장으로만 가른다. 굴뚝이 없고 필요하면 화로에 숯으로 불을 피우거나 집 뜰에서 나무로 불을 피운다(누가복음 22:55). 카이로의 어떤 집에는 뜰을 향하여 앞이 트인 방이 있어 아치 둘 이상과 난간이 있고 기둥 하나가 그 위 벽을 받친다. 궁에 있을 법한 이만한 크기의 방에서, 베드로가 주님을 부인하던 때에 주님이 대제사장 앞에서 심문받고 계셨다. 주님은 '돌이켜' 뜰의 불 곁에 선 베드로를 '보셨으니'(누가복음 22:56,61; 요한복음 18:24), 그때 주님 자신은 '재판정'에 계셨다.
동방의 살림 습관이 유럽과 가장 크게 다른 점은 지붕의 쓰임이다. 그 평평한 면이 곡식을 말리고 빨래를 널고 무화과와 건포도를 만드는 등 여러 살림에 쓰인다. 지붕은 저녁에 쉬는 자리로 쓰이고 밤에는 잠자리로 쓰이는 일이 많다(사무엘상 9:25,26; 사무엘하 11:2; 16:22; 욥기 27:18; 잠언 21:9; 다니엘 4:29). 또 기도하는 자리로, 심지어 우상 숭배의 자리로도 쓰였다(열왕기하 23:12; 예레미야 19:13; 32:29; 스바냐 1:5; 사도행전 10:9). 초막절에는 유대인이 집 지붕 위에 초막을 세웠다. 율법은 지붕에 난간을 두어 보호하도록 명하였다(신명기 22:8). 큰 집에서는 겨울과 여름의 쓰임을 위하여 방을 따로 두었다(예레미야 36:22; 아모스 3:15). 아합의 상아궁은 아마도 상아를 많이 박아 꾸민 궁이었을 것이다. 삼손이 기둥으로 집을 무너뜨린 일은, 무리가 아래층의 가운데 기둥으로 받친 여러 층의 발코니에 모여 있었다는 사실로 설명할 수 있으니, 그 기둥이 무너지면 위층 전체가 함께 무너졌을 것이다(사사기 16:26).

entries.term: How The Prophetic Gift Was Received
entries.definition: —We learn from Holy Scripture that it was by the agency of the Spirit of God that the prophets received the divine communication; but the means by which the divine Spirit communicated with the human spirit, and the conditions of the latter under which the divine communications were received, have not been clearly declared to us. They are however, indicated. In (Numbers 12:6-8) we have an exhaustive division of the different ways in which the revelations of God are made to man. • Direct declaration and manifestation: “I will speak mouth to mouth, apparently, and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold.” • Vision. • Dream. not though it must be allowed that Scripture language seems to point out the state of dream and of trance or ecstasy, as a condition in which the human instrument received the divine communications, it does not follow that all the prophetic revelations were thus made. Had the prophets a full knowledge of that and could not have. They were the “spokesmen” of God, (Exodus 7:1) the “mouth” by which his words were uttered, or they were enabled to view and empowered to describe pictures. Presented to their spiritual intuition; but there are no grounds for believing that, contemporaneously with this miracle, there was wrought another miracle, enlarging the understanding of the prophet so as to grasp the whole of the divine counsels which he was gazing into, or which he was the instrument of enunciating. Names.—Of the sixteen prophets, four are usually called the great prophets, namely, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and Daniel, and twelve the Minor prophets, namely, Hosea, Joel, Amos, Obadiah, Jonah, Micah, Nahum, Habakuk,Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi. They may be divided into four groups: the prophets of the northern kingdom—Hosea, Amos, Joel, Jonah; the prophets of the southern kingdom—Isaiah, Jeremiah, Obadiah, Micah, Nahum, Habakkuk, Zephaniah; the prophets of the captivity—Ezekiel and Daniel; the prophets of the return—Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. They may be arranged in the following chronological order, namely, Joel, Jonah, Hoses, Amos, Isaiah, Micah, Nahum, Zephaniah, Habakkuk, Obadiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi. Use of prophecy.—Predictive prophecy is at once a part and an evidence of revelation; at the time that it is delivered and until its fulfillment, a part; after it has been fulfilled, an evidence. As an evidence, fulfilled prophecy is as satisfactory as anything can be; for who can know the future except the Ruler who disposes future events? and from whom can come prediction except from him who knows the future? Development of Messianic prophecy.—Prediction, in the shape of promise and threatening, begins with the book of Genesis. Immediately upon the Fall, hopes of recovery and salvation are held out, but the manner in which this salvation is to be effected is left altogether indefinite. All that is at first declared is that it shall come through a child of woman. (Genesis 3:15) By degrees the area is limited: it is to come through the family of Shem, (Genesis 9:26) through the family of Abraham, (Genesis 12:3) of Isaac, (Genesis 25:18) of Jacob, (Genesis 28:14) of Judah, (Genesis 49:10) Balaam seems to say that it will be wrought by a warlike Israelitish King, (Numbers 24:17) Jacob, by a peaceful Ruler of the earth, (Genesis 49:10) Moses, by a Prophet like himself, i.e. a revealer of a new religious dispensation. (15:15) Nathan’s announcement, (2 Samuel 7:16) determines further that the salvation is to come through the house of David, and through a descendant of David who shall be himself a king. This promise is developed by David himself in the Messianic psalms. Between Solomon and Hezekiah intervened some two hundred years, during which the voice of prophecy was silent. The Messianic conception entertained at this time by the Jews might have been that of a King of the royal house of David who would arise and gather under his peaceful sceptre his own people and strangers. Sufficient allusion to his prophetical and priestly offices had been made to create thoughtful consideration, but as yet there was, no clear delineation of him in these characters. It was reserved for the prophets to bring out these features more distinctly. In this great period of prophetism there is no longer any chronological development of Messianic prophecy, as in the earlier period previous to Solomon. Each prophet adds a feature, one more, another less clearly combine the feature, and we have the portrait; but it does not grow gradually and perceptibly under the hands of the several artists. Its culminating point is found in the prophecy contained in (Isaiah 52:13-15) and Isai 52:53Prophets of the New Testament .—So far as their predictive powers are concerned, the Old Testament prophets find their New Testament counterpart in the writer of the Apocalypse; but in their general character, as specially illumined revealers of God’s will, their counterpart will rather be found, first in the great Prophet of the Church and his forerunner, John the Baptist, and next in all those persons who were endowed with the extraordinary gifts of the Spirit in the apostolic age, the speakers with tongues and the interpreters of tongues, the prophets and the discerners of spirits, the teachers and workers of miracles. (1 Corinthians 12:10,28) That Predictive powers did occasionally exist in the New Testament prophets is proved by the case of Agabus, (Acts 11:23) but this was not their characteristic. The prophets of the New Testament were supernaturally illuminated expounders and preachers.
entries.definition_ko:
선지자가 하나님의 영의 역사로 신적 전달을 받았음을 성경에서 배우나, 하나님의 영이 사람의 영과 소통하신 수단과 그 전달을 받을 때 사람 편의 상태가 어떠하였는지는 뚜렷이 밝혀져 있지 않고 다만 암시된다. 민수기 12:6-8에는 하나님의 계시가 사람에게 주어지는 여러 방식이 남김없이 나뉘어 있다. (1) 직접 선언과 나타나심 곧 '내가 그와는 대면하여 명백히 말하고 은밀한 말로 하지 아니하며 그는 또 여호와의 형상을 보거늘', (2) 환상, (3) 꿈이다. 성경의 표현이 꿈과 비몽사몽 곧 황홀의 상태를 사람이라는 도구가 신적 전달을 받는 상태로 가리키는 듯하나, 그렇다고 모든 예언의 계시가 그렇게 주어졌다고 볼 것은 아니다. 선지자들이 자기가 전한 것을 온전히 알았는가 하면 그렇지 않았고 그럴 수도 없었다. 그들은 하나님의 '대변자'요(출애굽기 7:1) 그 말씀이 발설되는 '입'이었으며, 또는 자기 영적 직관에 제시된 그림을 보고 그려 낼 힘을 받았다. 그러나 이 이적과 나란히, 자기가 들여다보거나 발설하는 도구가 된 하나님의 온 계획을 붙잡도록 선지자의 이해를 넓히는 또 하나의 이적이 행하여졌다고 믿을 근거는 없다.
이름. 열여섯 선지자 가운데 넷은 대개 대선지자라 불리니 이사야와 예레미야와 에스겔과 다니엘이요, 열둘은 소선지자라 불리니 호세아·요엘·아모스·오바댜·요나·미가·나훔·하박국·스바냐·학개·스가랴·말라기이다. 넷으로 나눌 수 있으니 북왕국의 선지자는 호세아·아모스·요엘·요나요, 남왕국의 선지자는 이사야·예레미야·오바댜·미가·나훔·하박국·스바냐이며, 포로기의 선지자는 에스겔과 다니엘이요, 돌아옴의 선지자는 학개·스가랴·말라기이다. 연대순으로는 요엘, 요나, 호세아, 아모스, 이사야, 미가, 나훔, 스바냐, 하박국, 오바댜, 예레미야, 에스겔, 다니엘, 학개, 스가랴, 말라기의 차례로 놓을 수 있다.
예언의 쓰임. 예고하는 예언은 계시의 한 부분이자 계시의 증거이다. 주어진 때부터 이루어지기까지는 한 부분이요, 이루어진 뒤에는 증거이다. 증거로서 이루어진 예언은 어떤 것 못지않게 만족스러우니, 장차 올 일을 정하시는 통치자 말고 누가 미래를 알겠으며, 미래를 아시는 이 말고 누구에게서 예고가 나오겠는가.
메시아 예언의 전개. 약속과 위협의 형태를 띤 예고가 창세기에서 시작된다. 타락 직후에 회복과 구원의 소망이 주어지나 그 구원이 어떻게 이루어질지는 온전히 막연히 남는다. 처음에 밝혀진 것은 그것이 여자의 후손을 통하여 오리라는 것뿐이다(창세기 3:15). 차츰 범위가 좁아져 셈의 가문(9:26), 아브라함의 가문(12:3), 이삭(26:4)과 야곱(28:14)과 유다(49:10)를 통하여 오게 된다. 발람은 그것이 전쟁하는 이스라엘 왕으로 이루어지리라 말하는 듯하고(민수기 24:17), 야곱은 땅의 평화로운 다스리는 이로(창세기 49:10), 모세는 자기 같은 선지자 곧 새 종교 경륜을 계시하는 이로 말한다(신명기 18:15). 나단의 선포가(사무엘하 7:16) 구원이 다윗의 집을 통하여, 또 스스로 왕이 되실 다윗의 자손을 통하여 오리라고 더 정한다. 이 약속을 다윗 자신이 메시아 시편에서 펼친다. 솔로몬과 히스기야 사이에 이백 년쯤이 놓이는데 그동안 예언의 소리가 잠잠하였다. 이때 유대인이 품은 메시아 관념은 다윗 왕가에서 일어나 자기 백성과 나그네를 평화로운 규 아래 모을 왕이었을 것이다. 그 선지자직과 제사장직에 대한 언급이 생각을 불러일으킬 만큼은 있었으나 아직 그런 성격으로 뚜렷이 그려지지는 않았고, 이 특징을 더 뚜렷이 드러내는 일이 선지자들에게 남겨졌다. 예언의 이 큰 시기에는 솔로몬 이전 시기와 달리 메시아 예언의 연대순 전개가 더는 없다. 선지자마다 한 특징을 더하되 어떤 이는 더 뚜렷이 어떤 이는 덜 뚜렷이 더하며, 그 특징들을 합하면 초상이 되나 여러 화가의 손 아래 차츰 눈에 띄게 자라나지는 않는다. 그 절정은 이사야 52:13-53장의 예언에서 발견된다.
신약의 선지자. 예고하는 능력에서 구약 선지자에 상응하는 신약의 인물은 요한계시록의 기자이나, 하나님의 뜻을 특별히 비추어 계시하는 이라는 일반적 성격에서는 교회의 큰 선지자와 그 앞선 자 세례 요한, 그다음으로 사도 시대에 성령의 특별한 은사를 받은 모든 이 곧 방언 말하는 자와 통역하는 자, 선지자와 영들 분별하는 자, 교사와 능력 행하는 자에게서 그 상응을 찾을 수 있다(고린도전서 12:10,28). 신약의 선지자에게 예고의 능력이 이따금 있었음은 아가보의 경우가 증명하나(사도행전 11:28) 그것이 그들의 특징은 아니었다. 신약의 선지자는 초자연적으로 비추심을 받은 해설자요 전파자였다.

entries.definition: (incised), a place on the boundary of Naphtali. (Joshua 19:34) It has been recovered in Yakuk, a village in the mountains of Naphtali west of the upper end of the Sea of Galilee.
entries.definition_ko: '새겨진'이라는 뜻으로 납달리 경계의 한 장소이다(여호수아 19:34). 갈릴리 호수 상류 서쪽 납달리 산지의 야쿠크 마을로 확인되었다.

entries.definition: a name which in (1 Chronicles 6:75) is erroneously used for HELKATH, which see.
entries.definition_ko: 역대상 6:75에서 헬갓을 잘못 쓴 이름이다. 헬갓(HELKATH) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (circle), the second son of Aram, and grandson of Shem. (Genesis 10:23) The strongest evidence is in favor of the district about the roots of Lebanon.
entries.definition_ko: '원'이라는 뜻으로 아람의 둘째 아들이자 셈의 손자이다(창세기 10:23). 레바논 산기슭 지역과 관련짓는 견해가 가장 유력하다.

entries.definition: (weasel), a prophetess, whose husband, Shallum, was keeper of the wardrobe in the time of King Josiah. It was to her that Josiah had recourse, when Hilkiah found a book of the law, to procure an authoritative opinion on it. (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22) (B.C. 623.)
entries.definition_ko: '족제비'라는 뜻으로 여선지자이며 남편 살룸은 요시야 왕 시대 예복 관리자였다. 힐기야가 율법책을 발견했을 때 요시야가 그 권위 있는 해석을 구하러 찾아간 인물이 바로 그녀였다(열왕기하 22:14).

entries.definition: (place of lizards), a city of Judah one of those in the mountain districts the next to Hebron. (Joshua 15:54)
entries.definition_ko: '도마뱀의 장소'라는 뜻으로 헤브론 다음에 나열되는 유다 산악 지대의 성읍이다(여호수아 15:54).

entries.definition: Hunting, as a matter of necessity, whether for the extermination of dangerous beasts or for procuring sustenance betokens a rude and semi-civilized state; as an amusement, it betokens an advanced state. The Hebrews as a pastoral and agricultural people, were not given to the sports of the field; the density of the population, the earnestness of their character, and the tendency of their ritual regulations, particularly those affecting food, all combined to discourage the practice of hunting. The smaller of catching animals was, first, either by digging a pitfall; or, secondly, by a trap which was set under ground, (Job 18:10) in the run of the animal, (Proverbs 22:5) and caught it by the leg, (Job 18:9) or lastly by the use of the net, of which there were various kinds, as or the gazelle, (Isaiah 51:20) Authorized Version, “wild bull,” and other animals of that class.
entries.definition_ko: 위험한 짐승을 없애거나 식량을 구하기 위한 필요에 의한 사냥은 미개하고 반문명적인 상태를 나타내며 오락으로서의 사냥은 진보된 상태를 나타낸다. 목축·농경 민족이었던 히브리인들은 들놀이식 사냥을 즐기지 않았으며, 인구밀도, 진지한 성품, 특히 음식 관련 의식 규정이 모두 사냥의 관행을 억제하는 방향으로 작용했다. 작은 동물을 잡는 방법으로는 함정을 파거나 땅속에 덫을 설치하는 것, 또는 다양한 종류의 그물이 쓰였다.

entries.definition: (coast-man), a son of Benjamin, founder of the family of the Huphamites. (Numbers 26:39) (B.C. 1688.)
entries.definition_ko: '해안 사람'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 아들이며 후바 자손의 조상이다(민수기 26:39).

entries.definition: descendants of Hupham, of the tribe of Benjamin. (Numbers 26:39)
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 지파 후밤의 후손이다(민수기 26:39).

entries.definition: (protected), a priest in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 24:13)
entries.definition_ko: '보호받는'이라는 뜻으로 다윗 시대 제사장이다(역대상 24:13).

entries.definition: (protected), head of a Benjamite family (Genesis 46:21; 1 Chronicles 7:12) Hur (hole). • A man who is mentioned with Moses and Aaron on the occasion of the battle with Amalek at Raphidim, (Exodus 17:10) when with Aaron he stayed up the hands of Moses. ver. (Exodus 17:12) (B.C. 1491.) He is mentioned again in ch. (Exodus 24:14) as being, with Aaron, left in charge of the people by Moses during his ascent of Sinai. The Jewish tradition is that he was the husband of Miriam, and that he was identical with • The grandfather of Bezaleel, the chief artificer of the tabernacle. (Exodus 31:2; 35:30; 38:22) • The fourth of the five kings of Midian who were slain with Balaam after the “matter of Peor.” (Numbers 31:8) (B.C. 1451.) In a later mention of them, (Joshua 13:21) they are called princes of Midian and dukes. • Father of Rephaiah, who was ruler of half of the environs of Jerusalem, and assisted Nehemiah in the repair of the wall. (Nehemiah 3:9) (B.C. before 446.) • The “son of Hur”—Ben-Hur—was commissariat officer for Solomon in Mount Ephraim. (1 Kings 4:8) (B.C. 995.)
entries.definition_ko: '보호받는'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 가문의 우두머리이다(창세기 46:21). 훌('구멍'이라는 뜻)은 (1) 아말렉과의 라비딤 전투에서 아론과 함께 모세의 손을 붙든 인물(출애굽기 17:10). (2) 성막의 수석 장인 브살렐의 조부(출애굽기 31:2). (3) 발람과 함께 죽임당한 미디안의 다섯 왕 중 넷째(민수기 31:8). (4) 예루살렘 주변 절반을 다스리며 느헤미야의 성벽 보수를 도운 르바야의 아버지(느헤미야 3:9). (5) 솔로몬의 에브라임 산지 물자 담당관 벤훌의 아버지(열왕기상 4:8).

entries.definition: (linon-weaver), one of David’s guard—Hurai of the torrents of Gaash, according to the list of (1 Chronicles 11:32) [Hiddai]
entries.definition_ko: '삼베 짜는 자'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 근위병 중 하나로 역대상 11:32 목록에서는 '가아스 시내의 후래'라 불린다. 히대(HIDDAI) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (noble born). • A Benjamite; son of Bela, the first-born of the patriarch. (1 Chronicles 8:5) • The form in which the name of the king of Tyre in alliance with David and Solomon—and elsewhere given as Hiram, Or Huram— appears in Chronicles. (1 Chronicles 14:1; 2 Chronicles 2:3,11,12; 8:2,18; 9:10,21) • The same Change occurs in Chronicles in the name of Hiram the artificer, which is given as Hiram, Or Huramin (2 Chronicles 2:13; 4:11,16) [Hiram, Or Huram]
entries.definition_ko: '고귀하게 태어난'이라는 뜻. (1) 베냐민의 아들 벨라의 아들(역대상 8:5). (2) 다윗·솔로몬과 동맹한 두로 왕의 이름이 역대기에서 나타나는 형태이며 다른 곳에서는 히람으로 나온다(역대상 14:1). (3) 같은 변화가 기술자 히람의 이름에도 나타나 역대하에서는 후람으로 표기된다(역대하 2:13).

entries.definition: (very poor), an ancestor of Shallum the husband of Huldah. (2 Kings 22:14) (B.C. before 623.)
entries.definition_ko: '매우 가난한'이라는 뜻으로 훌다의 남편 살룸의 조상이다(열왕기하 22:14).

entries.definition: (linen-weaver), a Gadite; father of Abihail- (1 Chronicles 5:14)
entries.definition_ko: '베 짜는 자'라는 뜻으로 갓 사람이며 아비하일의 아버지이다(역대상 5:14).

entries.definition: [Marriage]
entries.definition_ko: 결혼(MARRIAGE) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (haste), a name which occurs in the genealogies of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:4)
entries.definition_ko: '서두름'이라는 뜻으로 유다 지파 족보에 나오는 이름이다(역대상 4:4).

entries.definition: (hasting) an Archite i.e. possibly an inhabitant of a place called Erec. (2 Samuel 15:32) ff.; (2 Samuel 16:16) ff. He is called the “friend” of David. (2 Samuel 15:37) comp. 1Chr 27:33To him David confided the delicate and dangerous part of a pretended adherence to the cause of Absalom. (B.C. about 1023.) He was probably the father of Baana. (1 Kings 4:16)
entries.definition_ko: '서두르는'이라는 뜻으로 '아기 사람', 곧 에렉이라는 곳의 주민으로 추정되며 다윗의 '친구'라 불렸다(사무엘하 15:37). 다윗은 압살롬 편에 거짓으로 가담한 척하는 위험한 임무를 그에게 맡겼다. 아마도 바아나의 아버지였을 것이다(열왕기상 4:16).

entries.definition: (inhabitant of Hushah), The, the designation of two of the heroes of David’s guard. •Sibbechai. (2 Samuel 21:18; 1 Chronicles 11:29; 20:4; 27:11) Josephus, however, called him a Hittite. •Mebunnai, (2 Samuel 23:27) a mere corruption of Sibbechai.
entries.definition_ko: '후사 출신'이라는 뜻으로 다윗의 근위 용사 두 명에게 붙은 명칭이다 — 십브개(사무엘하 21:18, 요세푸스는 그를 헷 사람이라 부름)와 므분내(사무엘하 23:27, 십브개의 와전된 표기로 추정됨).

entries.definition: (who makes haste). • In (Genesis 46:23) “the children of Dan” are said to have been Hushim. The name is plural, as if of a tribe rather than an individual. In (Numbers 26:42) the name is changed to Shuham. • A Benjamite, (1 Chronicles 7:12) and here again apparently the plural nature of the name is recognized, and Hushim are stated to be “the sons of Aher.” • One of the two wives of Shaharaim. (1 Chronicles 8:8) (B.C. 1450.)
entries.definition_ko: '서두르는 자'라는 뜻. (1) 창세기 46:23의 '단의 아들들'이 후심으로 불리며 이름이 복수형이라 부족을 가리키는 것으로 보이고 민수기 26:42에서는 수함으로 바뀐다. (2) 베냐민 사람으로(역대상 7:12) 여기서도 복수형 성격이 인정되어 '아헬의 아들들'로 언급된다. (3) 사하라임의 두 아내 중 하나(역대상 8:8).

entries.definition: This word in (Luke 16:16) describes really the fruit of a particular kind of tree, viz. the carob or Ceratonia siliqua of botanists. It belongs to the locust family. This tree is very commonly met with in Syria and Egypt, it produces pods, shaped like a horn, varying in length from six to ten inches, and about a finger’s breadth, or rather more; it is dark-brown, glossy, filled with seeds and has a sweetish taste. It is used much for food by the poor, and for the feeding of swine.
entries.definition_ko: 누가복음 15:16의 이 단어는 실제로는 특정 나무의 열매, 곧 캐럽나무(구주콩나무)를 가리키며 메뚜기콩과에 속한다. 수리아와 애굽에 흔하며 뿔 모양의 꼬투리를 맺고 길이는 6~10인치, 검은 갈색에 광택이 있으며 씨가 가득하고 단맛이 나 가난한 자들의 식량과 돼지 사료로 널리 쓰인다.

entries.definition: (light, sandy soil), the eldest son of Nahor and Milcah. (Genesis 22:21) (B.C. about 1900).
entries.definition_ko: '빛, 모래땅'이라는 뜻으로 나홀과 밀가의 맏아들이다(창세기 22:21).

entries.definition: (fixed), according to the general opinion of the Jews, was the queen of Nineveh at the time when Nahum delivered his prophecy. (Nahum 2:7) (B.C. about 700.) The moderns follow the rendering in the margin of our English Bible—“that which was established.” Still it is not improbable that after all Huzzab may really be a proper name. It may mean “the Zab country,” or the fertile tract east of the Tigris, watered by the upper and lower Zab rivers.
entries.definition_ko: 유대인들의 일반적 견해에 따르면 나훔이 예언할 당시 니느웨의 왕비였다(나훔 2:7). 현대 학자들은 흠정역 난외의 '견고히 세워진 것'이라는 번역을 따르는 경향이 있으며, 일부는 이를 고유명사로 보아 티헬라강 상·하 자브강이 흐르는 비옥한 '자브 지역'을 가리킨다고 해석하기도 한다.

entries.definition: used in the Revised Version for jacinth in (Revelation 9:17) It is simply another English spelling of the same Greek word.
entries.definition_ko: 개정역에서 계시록 9:17의 '자킨트'를 대신해 쓰인 단어로 같은 헬라어 단어의 다른 영어 철자일 뿐이다.

entries.definition: Authorities differ as to whether the term tzabu’a in (Jeremiah 12:9) means a “hyaena” or a “speckled bird.” The only other instance in which it occurs is as a proper name, Zeboim, (1 Samuel 13:18) “the valley of hyaenas, “Aquila; (Nehemiah 11:34) The striped hyaena (Hyaena striata) is found in Africa, Asia Minor, Arabia and Persia, and is more common in Palestine than any other carnivorous animals except perhaps the jackal. The hyaena is among the mammals what the vulture is among birds,—the scavenger of the wilderness, the woods and the shore.—It often attacks animals, and Sometimes digs up the dead bodies of men and beasts. From this last habit the hyaena has been regarded as a horrible and mysterious creature. Its teeth are so powerful that they can crack the bones of an ox with ease.—Appelton’s Encyc. The hyaena was common in ancient as in modern Egypt, and is constantly depicted upon monuments; it must therefore have been well known to the Jews.
entries.definition_ko: 예레미야 12:9의 '차부아'가 '하이에나'를 뜻하는지 '얼룩무늬 새'를 뜻하는지에 대해 학자들 사이에 이견이 있다. 줄무늬하이에나는 아프리카, 소아시아, 아라비아, 바사에 서식하며 팔레스타인에서는 자칼 다음으로 흔한 육식동물이다. 새 중의 독수리처럼 광야·숲·해안의 청소부 역할을 하며 이따금 사람과 짐승의 시신을 파헤치는 습성으로 두렵고 신비로운 존재로 여겨졌다.

entries.definition: (belonging to marriage), the name of a person occurring twice in the correspondence between St. Paul and Timothy; the first time classed with Alexander, (1 Timothy 1:20) and the second time classed with Philetus. (2 Timothy 2:17,18) (A.D. 66-7.) He denied the true doctrine of the resurrection.
entries.definition_ko: '결혼에 속한'이라는 뜻으로 바울과 디모데 사이의 서신에 두 번 언급되며 처음에는 알렉산더와 함께(디모데전서 1:20), 두 번째는 빌레도와 함께(디모데후서 2:17) 언급된다. 부활의 참된 교리를 부인했다.

entries.definition: a religious song or psalm. (Ephesians 5:19; Colossians 3:16) Our Lord and his apostles sung a hymn after the last supper. In the jail at Philippi, Paul and Silas “sang hymns” (Authorized Version “praises”) unto God, and so loud was their song that their fellow prisoners heard them.
entries.definition_ko: 종교적 노래 또는 찬송이다(에베소서 5:19). 주님과 사도들은 최후의 만찬 후 찬송을 불렀다. 빌립보 감옥에서 바울과 실라도 '찬미'를 불렀고 그 소리가 커서 다른 죄수들이 들었다.

entries.definition: (Heb. ezob.) The ezob was used for sprinkling in some of the sacrifices and purifications of the Jews. In consequence of its detergent qualities, or from its being associated with the purificatory Services, the psalmist makes use of the expression, “Purge me with ezob .” (Psalms 51:7) It is described in (1 Kings 4:33) as growing on or near walls. (Besides being thus fit for sprinkling, having cleansing properties and growing on walls, the true hyssop should be a plant common to Egypt, Sinai and Palestine, and capable of producing a stick three or four feet long since on a stalk of hyssop the sponge of vinegar was held up to Christ on the cross. (John 19:29) it is impossible to precisely identify the plant because the name was given not to a particular plant but to a family of plants associated together by Hyssop, qualities easily noticed rather than by close botanical affinities. Different species of the family may have been used at different times. The hyssop of the Bible is probably one (or all) of three plants:— • The common hyssop is “a shrub with low, bushy stalks 1 1/2 feet high, small pear shaped, close-setting opposite leaves all the stalks and branches terminated by erect whorled spikes of flowers of different colors in the varieties. It is a hardy plant, with an aromatic smell and a warm, pungent taste; a native of the south of Europe and the East.”—ED.) • Bochart decides in favor of marjoram, or some plant like it, and to this conclusion, it must be admitted, all ancient tradition points. (This is the Origanum maru, the z’atar of the Arabs. The French consul at Sidon exhibited to Dr. Thomson (“The Land and the Book,” i. 161) a specimen of this “having the fragrance of thyme, with a hot, pungent taste, and long slender stems.” Dr. Post of Beirut, in the American edition of Smith’s large Dictionary, favors this view.—ED.) • But Dr.Royle, after a careful investigation of the subject, arrives at the conclusion that the hyssop is no other than the caperplant, or Capparis spinosa of Linnaeus. The Arabic name of this plant, asuf, by which it is sometimes though not commonly, described, bears considerable resemblance to the Hebrew. “It is a bright-green creeper, which climbs from the fissures of the rocks, is supposed to possess cleansing properties, and is capable of yielding a stick to which a sponge might be attached.”—Stanky, “Sinai and Palestine,” 23.—It produces a fruit the size of a walnut, called the mountain pepper.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '에조브'는 유대인의 일부 제사와 정결 의식에서 뿌리는 데 쓰였다. 세정 성질 때문인지 정결 의식과의 연관성 때문인지 시편 기자는 '우슬초로 나를 정결하게 하소서'라는 표현을 사용한다(시편 51:7). 열왕기상 4:33에서는 담벼락에서 자라는 것으로 묘사된다. 정확한 식물 종은 확정하기 어려우나 일반 우슬초, 마조람, 케이퍼 식물(카파리스 스피노사) 등 여러 견해가 있다.

entries.definition: (whom God chooses), one of the sons of David, (2 Samuel 5:15; 1 Chronicles 3:6; 14:6) (born in Jerusalem. B.C. after 1044.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 택하신 자'라는 뜻으로 예루살렘에서 태어난 다윗의 아들 중 하나이다(사무엘하 5:15).

entries.definition: (devouring the people), a city of Manasseh, with villages or towns dependent on it. (Judges 1:27) It appears to have been situated in the territory of either Issachar or Asher. (Joshua 17:11) The ascent of Gur was “at Ibleam,” (2 Kings 9:27) somewhere near the present Jenin, probably to the north of it.
entries.definition_ko: '백성을 삼키는'이라는 뜻으로 므낫세 지파의 성읍이며 그에 속한 마을들이 있었다(사사기 1:27). 잇사갈 또는 아셀 영토 안에 위치했던 것으로 보이며 '구르로 올라가는 길'이 이 성읍 근처에 있었다(열왕기하 9:27).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah will build up), son of Jehoram, a Benjamite. (1 Chronicles 9:8)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 세우실 자'라는 뜻으로 여로함의 아들, 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 9:8).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah will build up), a Benjamite. (1 Chronicles 9:8)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 세우실 자'라는 뜻의 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 9:8).

entries.definition: (Hebrew), a Merarite Levite of the family of Jaaziah, (1 Chronicles 24:27) in the time of David. (B.C. 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '히브리인'이라는 뜻으로 다윗 시대 므라리 가문 야아시야 족속의 레위인이다(역대상 24:27).

entries.definition: (illustrious), a native of Bethlehem of Zebulun, who judged Israel for seven years after Jephthah. (Judges 12:8,10) (B.C. 1137.)
entries.definition_ko: '저명한'이라는 뜻으로 스불론의 베들레헴 출신이며 입다 이후 7년간 이스라엘을 다스린 사사이다(사사기 12:8).

entries.definition: (inglorious), the son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli. (1 Samuel 4:21) (B.C. about 1100.)
entries.definition_ko: '영광이 없다'는 뜻으로 비느하스의 아들이자 엘리의 손자이다(사무엘상 4:21).

entries.definition: (little image), the modern Konieh, was the capital of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor. It was a large and rich city, 120 miles north from the Mediterranean Sea, at the foot of the Taurus mountains, and on the great line of communication between Ephesus and the western coast of the peninsula on one side, and Tarsus, Antioch and the Euphrates on the other. Iconium was a well-chosen place for missionary operations. (Acts 14:1,3,21,22; 16:1,2; 18:23) Paul’s first visit here was on his first circuit, in company with Barnabas; and on this occasion he approached it from Antioch in Pisidia, which lay to the west. The modern Konieh is between two and three miles in circumference and contains over 30,000 inhabitants. It contains manufactories of carpets and leather.
entries.definition_ko: '작은 형상'이라는 뜻으로 오늘날의 코니예, 소아시아 루가오니아의 수도였다. 지중해에서 북쪽으로 120마일, 타우루스 산맥 기슭에 위치한 크고 부유한 도시로 에베소와 서부 해안, 다소·안디옥·유브라데강을 잇는 교통 요충지였다. 선교 활동에 적합한 곳이었다(사도행전 14:1). 바울이 바나바와 함께 1차 순회 중 비시디아 안디옥에서 이곳을 방문했다.

entries.definition: (memorial of God), one of the cities of the tribe of Zebulun, named between Shimron and Bethlehem. (Joshua 19:15)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 기념'이라는 뜻으로 스불론 지파 성읍 중 하나이며 시므론과 베들레헴 사이에 언급된다(여호수아 19:15).

entries.definition: (stout), one of the three sons of Abi-Etam, among the families of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:3)
entries.definition_ko: '강건한'이라는 뜻으로 아비에담의 세 아들 중 하나, 유다 가문에 속한다(역대상 4:3).

entries.definition: (timely or lovely). • The father of Abinadab. (1 Kings 4:14) • A descendant of Gershom, son of Levi. (1 Chronicles 6:21) • Son of Zechariah, ruler of the tribe of Manasseh east of Jordan in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 27:21) (B.C. 1014.) • A seer whose “visions” against Jeroboam incidentally contained some of the acts of Solomon. (2 Chronicles 9:29) He appears to have written a chronicle or story relating to the life and reign of Abijah. (2 Chronicles 13:22) (B.C. 961.) • The grandfather of the prophet Zechariah. (Zechariah 1:1,7) • The chief of those who assembled at Casiphia at the time of the second caravan from Babylon. He was one of the Nethinim. (Ezra 8:17) comp. Ezra 8:20(B.C. 536.)
entries.definition_ko: '때에 맞는' 또는 '사랑스러운'이라는 뜻. (1) 아비나답의 아버지(열왕기상 4:14). (2) 레위 자손 게르솜의 후손(역대상 6:21). (3) 다윗 시대 요단 동편 므낫세 반 지파 지도자, 스가랴의 아들(역대상 27:21). (4) 여로보암에 대한 '환상'을 기록한 선견자로 솔로몬의 행적 일부도 담았으며(역대하 9:29) 아비야의 생애와 통치에 관한 기록도 남긴 것으로 보인다(역대하 13:22). (5) 선지자 스가랴의 조부(스가랴 1:1). (6) 바벨론에서 온 둘째 무리 중 가시뱌에 모인 자들의 우두머리, 느디님 사람(에스라 8:17).

entries.definition: An image or anything used as an object of worship in place of the true God. Among the earliest objects of worship, regarded as symbols of deity, were the meteoric stones, which the ancients believed to have been images of the Gods sent down from heaven. From these they transferred their regard to rough unhewn blocks, to stone columns or pillars of wood, in which the divinity worshipped was supposed to dwell, and which were connected, like the sacred stone at Delphi, by being anointed with oil and crowned with wool on solemn days. Of the forms assumed by the idolatrous images we have not many traces in the Bible. Dagon, the fish-god of the Philistines, was a human figure terminating in a fish; and that the Syrian deities were represented in later times in a symbolical human shape we know for certainty. When the process of adorning the image was completed, it was placed in a temple or shrine appointed for it. Epist. (Jeremiah 12:1; Jeremiah 19:1) ... Wisd. 13:15; (1 Corinthians 8:10) From these temples the idols were sometimes carried in procession, Epist. (Jeremiah 4:26) on festival days. Their priests were maintained from the idol treasury, and feasted upon the meats which were appointed for the idols’ use. Bel and the Dragon 3,13.
entries.definition_ko: 참 하나님 대신 예배 대상으로 쓰이는 형상이나 물건을 가리킨다. 가장 이른 예배 대상 중 하나는 하늘에서 내려온 신의 형상으로 여겨진 운석이었으며, 이후 조각하지 않은 돌덩이, 돌기둥, 나무 기둥 등으로 옮겨갔고 델포이의 신성한 돌처럼 기름을 붓고 양털관을 씌우는 의식이 행해졌다. 블레셋의 물고기 신 다곤은 인간 형상에 물고기 몸이 이어진 형태였다. 형상이 완성되면 신전이나 사당에 안치되었고 축제일에는 행렬로 옮겨지기도 했으며 제사장은 우상에게 바친 제물로 잔치를 벌였다.

entries.definition: strictly speaking denotes the worship of deity in a visible form, whether the images to which homage is paid are symbolical representations of the true God or of the false divinities which have been made the objects of worship in his stead. I. History of idolatry among the Jews.—The first undoubted allusion to idolatry or idolatrous customs in the Bible is in the account of Rachel’s stealing her father’s teraphim. (Genesis 31:19) During their long residence in Egypt the Israelites defiled themselves with the idols of the land, and it was long before the taint was removed. (Joshua 24:14; Ezekiel 20:7) In the wilderness they clamored for some visible shape in which they might worship the God who had brought them out of Egypt. (Exodus 32:1) ... until Aaron made the calf, the embodiment of Apis and emblem of the productive power of nature. During the lives of Joshua and the elders who outlived him they kept true to their allegiance; but the generation following who knew not Jehovah nor the works he had done for Israel, swerved from the plain path of their fathers and were caught in the toils of the foreigner. (Judges 2:1) ... From this time forth their history becomes little more than a chronicle of the inevitable sequence of offence and punishment. (Judges 2:12,14) By turns each conquering nation strove to establish the worship of its national God. In later times the practice of secret idolatry was carried to greater lengths. Images were set up on the corn-floors, in the wine-vats, and behind the doors of private houses, (Isaiah 57:8; Hosea 9:1,2) and to check this tendency the statute in (27:15) was originally promulgated. Under Samuel’s administration idolatry was publicly renounced, (1 Samuel 7:3-6) but in the reign of Solomon all this was forgotten, even Solomon’s own heart being turned after other gods. (1 Kings 11:14) Rehoboam perpetuated the worst features of Solomon’s idolatry. (1 Kings 14:22-24) erected golden calves at Beth-el and at Dan, and by this crafty state’ policy severed forever the kingdoms of Judah and Israel. (1 Kings 12:26-33) The successors of Jeroboam followed in his steps, till Ahab. The conquest of the ten tribes by Shalmaneser was for them the last scene Of the drama of abominations which had been enacted uninterruptedly for upwards of 250 years. Under Hezekiah a great reform was inaugurated, that was not confined to Judah and Benjamin, but spread throughout Ephraim and Manasseh. (2 Chronicles 31:1) and to all external appearances idolatry was extirpated. But the reform extended little below the surface. (Isaiah 29:13) With the death of Josiah ended the last effort to revive among the people a purer ritual. If not a purer faith. The lamp of David, which had long shed but a struggling ray, flickered for a while and then went out in the darkness of Babylonian Captivity. Though the conquests of Alexander caused Greek influence to be felt, yet after the captivity better condition of things prevailed, and the Jews never again fell into idolatry. The erection of synagogues had been assigned as a reason for the comparative purity of the Jewish worship after the captivity, while another cause has been discovered in the hatred for images acquired by the Jews in their intercourse with the Persians. II. Objects of idolatry .—The sun and moon were early selected as outward symbols of all-pervading power, and the worship of the heavenly bodies was not only the most ancient but the most prevalent system of idolatry. Taking its rise in the plains of Chaldea, it spread through Egypt, Greece, Scythia, and even Mexico and Ceylon. Comp. (4:19; 17:3; Job 31:20-28) In the later times of the monarchy, the planets or the zodiacal signs received, next to the sun and moon, their share of popular adoration. (2 Kings 23:5) Beast-worship, as exemplified in the calves of Jeroboam, has already been alluded to of pure hero-worship among the Semitic races we find no trace. The singular reverence with which trees have been honored is not without example in the history of the Hebrew. The terebinth (oak) at Mamre, beneath which Abraham built an altar, (Genesis 12:7; 13:18) and the memorial grove planted by him at Beersheba, (Genesis 21:33) were intimately connected with patriarchal worship. Mountains and high places were chosen spots for offering sacrifice and incense to idols, (1 Kings 11:7; 14:23) and the retirement of gardens and the thick shade of woods offered great attractions to their worshippers. (2 Kings 16:4; Isaiah 1:29; Hosea 4:13) The host of heaven was worshipped on the house-top. (2 Kings 23:12; Jeremiah 19:3; 32:29; Zephaniah 1:5) (The modern objects of idolatry are less gross than the ancient, but are none the less idols. Whatever of wealth or honor or pleasure is loved and sought before God and righteousness becomes an object of idolatry.—ED.) III. Punishment of idolatry .—Idolatry to an Israelite was a state offence, (1 Samuel 15:23) a political crime of the greatest character, high treason against the majesty of his king. The first and second commandments are directed against idolatry of every form. Individuals and communities were equally amenable to the rigorous code. The individual offender was devoted to destruction, (Exodus 22:20) his nearest relatives were not only bound to denounce him and deliver him up to punishment, (13:2-10) but their hands were to strike the first blow, when, on the evidence of two witnesses at least, he was stoned. (17:2-5) To attempt to seduce others to false worship was a crime of equal enormity. (13:6-10) IV. Attractions of idolatry .—Many have wondered why the Israelites were so easily led away from the true God, into the worship of idols. (1) Visible, outward signs, with shows, pageants, parades, have an attraction to the natural heart, which often fail to perceive the unseen spiritual realities. (2) But the greatest attraction seems to have been in licentious revelries and obscene orgies with which the worship of the Oriental idols was observed. This worship, appealing to every sensual passion, joined with the attractions of wealth and fashion and luxury, naturally was a great temptation to a simple, restrained, agricultural people, whose worship and law demands the greatest purity of heart and of life.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 엄밀히 말하면 눈에 보이는 형상으로 신을 예배하는 것을 뜻한다. 성경에서 우상숭배에 대한 첫 확실한 언급은 라헬이 아버지의 드라빔을 훔친 사건이다(창세기 31:19). 애굽 체류 중 이스라엘은 그 땅의 우상들로 자신을 더럽혔고(여호수아 24:14) 광야에서는 아론이 금송아지를 만들었다(출애굽기 32:1). 여호수아와 그를 이어 산 장로들의 생애 동안은 신실했으나 다음 세대는 곁길로 빠졌다(사사기 2:1). 솔로몬의 마음도 다른 신들에게로 돌아섰고(열왕기상 11:14) 여로보암은 벧엘과 단에 금송아지를 세워 남북 왕국을 영구히 갈라놓았다(열왕기상 12:26). 히스기야 때 큰 개혁이 있었으나(역대하 31:1) 표면적이었고, 요시야의 죽음으로 순수한 예배 회복의 마지막 시도가 끝나 바벨론 포로기의 어둠 속으로 사그라들었다. 포로 후에는 회당 설립과 바사인들과의 교류에서 얻은 형상에 대한 혐오 덕분에 유대인들이 다시는 우상숭배에 빠지지 않았다. 해와 달, 행성, 짐승(여로보암의 송아지), 나무(마므레의 상수리나무), 산과 높은 곳, 정원과 숲, 하늘의 뭇별이 옥상에서 숭배 대상이 되었다. 우상숭배는 이스라엘 사람에게 국가적 범죄, 왕에 대한 반역죄로 취급되어 개인과 공동체 모두 엄격한 처벌(돌로 침)을 받았다.

entries.definition: (red). [Edom, Idumaea Or Idumea]
entries.definition_ko: '붉은'이라는 뜻. 에돔(EDOM, IDUMAEA) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (whom God will avenge). • One of the spies, son of Joseph, of the tribe of Issachar. (Numbers 13:7) (B.C. 1490.) • One of the heroes of David’s guard, son of Nathan of Zobah. (2 Samuel 23:36) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 보복하실 자'라는 뜻. (1) 잇사갈 지파 요셉의 아들, 열두 정탐꾼 중 하나(민수기 13:7). (2) 소바 사람 나단의 아들로 다윗의 근위 용사(사무엘하 23:36).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah makes great), a prophet or holy man—“the man of God”—named once only, (Jeremiah 36:4) as the father of Hanan. (B.C. before 406.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 크게 하실 자'라는 뜻으로 하나님의 사람으로 불리는 선지자, 하난의 아버지로 한 번만 언급된다(예레미야 36:4).

entries.definition: (whom God will avenge), a son of Nehemiah; a descendant of the royal house of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:22) (B.C. 406.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 보복하실 자'라는 뜻으로 느헤미야의 아들이며 유다 왕실 후손이다(역대상 3:22).

entries.definition: (ruins). • The partial or contracted form of the name IJE-ABARIM. (Numbers 33:45) • A town in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 16:29)
entries.definition_ko: '폐허들'이라는 뜻. (1) 이예아바림의 축약형(민수기 33:45). (2) 유다 최남단의 성읍(여호수아 15:29).

entries.definition: (ruin of Abarim), one of the later halting-places of the children of Israel. (Numbers 21:11; 33:44) It was on the boundary—the southeast boundary— of the territory of Moab; in the waste uncultivated “wilderness” on its skirts.
entries.definition_ko: '아바림의 폐허'라는 뜻으로 이스라엘이 후기에 머문 진영지 중 하나이며(민수기 21:11) 모압 영토 동남쪽 경계, 경작되지 않은 광야 변두리에 위치했다.

entries.definition: (a ruin), a town in the north of Palestine, belonging to the tribe of Naphtali. It was taken and plundered by the captains of Ben-hadad, (1 Kings 15:20; 2 Chronicles 16:4) and a second time by Tiglath-pileser. (2 Kings 16:29) It was situated a few miles northwest of the site of Dan, in a fertile and beautiful little plain called Merj’ Ayun .
entries.definition_ko: '폐허'라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북부, 납달리 지파 성읍이다. 벤하닷의 지휘관들에게 함락·약탈당했고(열왕기상 15:20) 후에 디글랏빌레셀에게 다시 침탈당했다(열왕기하 15:29). 단 유적지 북서쪽 몇 마일, 비옥하고 아름다운 소평원 메르지아윤에 위치했다.

entries.definition: (perverse), the father of Ira the Tekoite. (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:28; 27:9) (B.C. before 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '비뚤어진'이라는 뜻으로 드고아 사람 이라의 아버지이다(사무엘하 23:26).

entries.definition: (exalted), an Ahohite, one of the heroes of David’s guard (1 Chronicles 11:29) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '높여진'이라는 뜻으로 아호아 사람, 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나이다(역대상 11:29).

entries.definition: an extensive district lying along the eastern coast of the Adriatic, from the boundary of Italy on the north of Epirus on the south, and contiguous to Moessia and Macedonia on the east. (Romans 6:19)
entries.definition_ko: 아드리아해 동쪽 연안을 따라 북쪽 이탈리아 경계부터 남쪽 에피루스까지, 동쪽으로 모이시아·마케도니아와 접한 넓은 지역이다(로마서 15:19).

entries.definition: [Idol]
entries.definition_ko: 우상(IDOL) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (whom God will fill up), father or progenitor of Micaiah the prophet. (2 Chronicles 18:7,8) The form IMLAH is employed in the parallel narrative. (1 Kings 12:8,9) (B.C. before 896.)
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 채우실 자'라는 뜻으로 선지자 미가야의 아버지(또는 조상)이다(역대하 18:7). 병행 기사(열왕기상 22:8)에서는 임라 형태로 나온다.

entries.definition: that is, God with us, the title applied by the apostle Matthew to the Messiah, born of the Virgin, (Matthew 1:23; Isaiah 7:14) because Jesus was God united with man, and showed that God was dwelling with men.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 우리와 함께 계시다'는 뜻으로 마태가 동정녀에게서 나신 메시아에게 붙인 칭호이다(마태복음 1:23). 예수님이 하나님과 사람이 하나 되신 분이며 하나님이 사람과 함께 거하심을 보이신 분이기 때문이다.

entries.definition: (talkative). • The founder of an important family of priests. (1 Chronicles 9:12; Nehemiah 11:13) This family had charge of, and gave its name to, the sixteenth course of the service. (1 Chronicles 24:14) (B.C. 1014.) • Apparently the name of a place in Babylonia. (Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61)
entries.definition_ko: '말 많은'이라는 뜻. (1) 중요한 제사장 가문의 창시자로(역대상 9:12) 성전 봉사 열여섯째 반차의 이름이 되었다(역대상 24:14). (2) 바벨론의 한 지명으로 보임(에스라 2:59).

entries.definition: (holding back), a descendant of Asher, son of Helem. (1 Chronicles 7:35) comp. 1Chr 7:40(B.C. about 1461.)
entries.definition_ko: '억제하는'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 후손, 헬렘의 아들이다(역대상 7:35).

entries.definition: (holding back). • The first born of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:30) (B.C. 1706.) • Kore ben-Imnah, the Levite, assisted in the reforms of Hezekiah. (2 Chronicles 31:14) (B.C. 726.)
entries.definition_ko: '억제하는'이라는 뜻. (1) 아셀의 맏아들(역대상 7:30). (2) 레위인 고레벤임나, 히스기야의 개혁을 도움(역대하 31:14).

entries.definition: (stubborn), a descendant of Asher, of the family of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:36) (B.C. after 1445.)
entries.definition_ko: '완고한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 후손, 소바 가문이다(역대상 7:36).

entries.definition: from the Latin “to burn,” “a mixture of gums or spices and the like, used for the purpose of producing a perfume when burned;” or the perfume itself of the spices, etc., burned in worship. The incense employed in the service of the tabernacle walls compounded of the perfumes stacte, onycha, galbanum and pure frankincense. All incense which was not made of these ingredients was forbidden to be offered. (Exodus 30:9) Aaron, as high priest, was originally appointed to offer incense each morning and evening. The times of offering incense were specified in the instructions first given to Moses. (Exodus 30:7,8) When the priest entered the holy place with the incense, all the people were removed from the temple, and from between the porch and the altar. Cf. (Luke 1:10) Profound silence was observed among the congregation who were praying without, cf. (Revelation 8:1) and at a signal from the perfect the priest cast the incense on the fire and, bowing reverently toward the holy of holies, retired slowly backward. The offering of incense has formed part of the religious ceremonies of most ancient nations. It was an element in the idolatrous worship of the Israelites. (2 Chronicles 34:25; Jeremiah 11:12,17; 48:35) It would seem to be symbolical, not of itself, but of that which makes acceptable, the intercession of Christ. In (Revelation 8:3,4) the incense is of as something distinct from offered with the prayers of, all the saints cf. (Luke 1:10) and in Reve 6:8 It is the golden vials, and not the odors or incense, which are said to be the prayers of saints.
entries.definition_ko: 라틴어 '태우다'에서 유래한 단어로 태워서 향기를 내기 위한 고무·향료 등의 혼합물, 또는 예배 중 태우는 향료 자체를 가리킨다. 성막 봉사에 쓰인 향은 소합향·나감향·풍자향·순수 유향을 섞어 만들었으며 이 재료가 아닌 것으로 만든 향은 금지되었다(출애굽기 30:9). 아론은 매일 아침저녁 향을 피우도록 임명되었으며 제사장이 향을 들고 성소에 들어갈 때 백성은 성전과 현관·제단 사이에서 물러나 깊은 침묵 속에 기도했다(누가복음 1:10). 향은 그 자체가 아니라 사람을 받아들여지게 하는 그리스도의 중보를 상징하는 것으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: The name of India does not occur in the Bible before the book of Esther where it is noticed as the limit of the territories of Ahasuerus in the east, as Ethiopia was in the west. (Esther 1:1; 8:9) The India of the book of Esther is not the peninsula of Hindostan, but the country surrounding the Indus, the Punjab and perhaps Scinde . The people and productions of that country must have been tolerably well known to the Jews. An active trade was carried on between India and western Asia. The trade opened by Solomon with Ophir through the Red Sea consisted chiefly of Indian articles.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 인도라는 이름은 에스더서 이전에는 나오지 않으며 아하수에로 왕국의 동쪽 경계로 언급된다(구스가 서쪽 경계, 에스더 1:1). 에스더서의 인도는 오늘날의 인도 반도가 아니라 인더스강 주변, 펀자브와 신드 지역을 가리키는 것으로 보인다. 솔로몬이 홍해를 통해 오빌과 벌인 무역품 대부분이 인도산 물품이었다.

entries.definition: [Heir]
entries.definition_ko: 상속자(HEIR) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: [Writing]
entries.definition_ko: 쓰기(WRITING) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: The Hebrew word (malon) thus rendered literally signified “a lodging-place for the night.” Inns, in our sense of the term were, as they still are, unknown in the East, where hospitality is religiously practiced. The khans or caravanserais are the representatives of European inns, and these were established but gradually. The halting-place of a caravan was selected originally on account of its proximity to water or pasture, by which the travellers pitched their tents and passed the night. Such was undoubtedly the “inn” at which occurred the Incident in the life of Moses narrated in (Exodus 4:24) comp. Genesis42:27 On the more frequented routes, remote from towns, (Jeremiah 9:2) caravanserais were in course of time erected, often at the expense of the wealthy. “A caravanserai is a large and substantial square building... Passing through strong gateway, the guest enters a large court, in the centre of which is a spacious raised platform, used for sleeping upon at night or for the devotions of the faithful during the day. Around this court are arranged the rooms of the building.”
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '말론'은 문자적으로 '하룻밤 묵는 곳'을 뜻한다. 오늘날 동방에서 환대가 신성한 의무로 여겨지듯 우리가 아는 형태의 여관은 예나 지금이나 드물다. '칸'(카라반사라이)이 유럽의 여관에 해당하며 점차 세워졌다. 대상의 야영지는 본래 물이나 목초지 근처로 선택되었으며 모세의 생애 사건(출애굽기 4:24)에 나오는 '여관'도 이런 형태였을 것이다. 사람이 많이 다니는 길목에는 부유한 자들의 재정으로 카라반사라이가 세워지기도 했다.

entries.definition: Dr. Knapp given as the definition of inspiration, “an extra-ordinary divine agency upon teachers while giving instruction, whether oral or written, by which they were taught what and how they should write or speak.“ Without deciding on any of the various theories of inspiration, the general doctrine of Christians is that the Bible is so inspired by God that it is the infallible guide of men, and is perfectly trustworthy in all its parts, as given by God.
entries.definition_ko: 크납 박사는 영감을 '가르치는 자들에게 임하는 비상한 신적 작용으로, 이를 통해 그들이 무엇을, 어떻게 쓰거나 말해야 할지 배우게 되는 것'이라 정의했다. 다양한 영감 이론과 무관하게 그리스도인들의 일반적 교리는 성경이 하나님께 영감되어 사람들의 무오한 지침이며 모든 부분에서 완전히 신뢰할 수 있다는 것이다.

entries.definition: in the Authorized Version, means urgent, urgently or fervently, as will be seen from the following passages: (Luke 7:4; 23:23; Acts 26:7; Romans 12:12)
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서는 '긴급한', '간절히'를 뜻하며(누가복음 7:4) 등의 구절에서 확인된다.

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah frees), a descendant of Benjamin, one of the Bene-Shashak. (1 Chronicles 8:25)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 자유케 하실 자'라는 뜻으로 베냐민 후손, 브네사삭 가문이다(역대상 8:25).

(2 Samuel 23:38; 1 Chronicles 11:40) • Another of David’s guard, a Tekoite, son of Ikkesh- (2 Samuel 23:26; 1 Chronicles 11:28) (B.C. 1046-1014.)
entries.definition_ko: '성읍을 지키는 자'라는 뜻. (1) '야일 사람'으로 다윗의 고위 관리 목록에 나옴(사무엘하 20:26). (2) 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나(사무엘하 23:38). (3) 드고아 사람 익게스의 아들로 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나(사무엘하 23:26).

entries.definition_ko: '날쌘'이라는 뜻으로 에녹의 아들이자 가인의 손자, 므후야엘의 아버지이다(창세기 4:18).

entries.definition: (belonging to a city), a leader of the Edomites, (Genesis 36:43; 1 Chronicles 1:54) i.e. the chief of a family or tribe. No identification of him has been found.
entries.definition_ko: '성읍에 속한'이라는 뜻으로 에돔의 지도자(족장)이다(창세기 36:43). 신원이 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: (seen by the Lord), son of Shelemiah, a captain in the ward, who met Jeremiah in the gate of Jerusalem called the “gate of Benjamin” accused him of being about to desert to the Chaldeans; and led him back to the princes. (Jeremiah 37:13,14) (B.C. 589.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 보신'이라는 뜻으로 셀레먀의 아들이자 초소 대장으로 예루살렘 '베냐민 문'에서 예레미야를 만나 갈대아인에게 투항하려 한다고 고발하고 방백들에게 끌고 갔다(예레미야 37:13).

entries.definition: (serpent city), a name which, like many other names of places, occurs in the genealogical lists of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:12)
entries.definition_ko: '뱀의 성읍'이라는 뜻으로 다른 여러 지명들처럼 유다 족보 목록에 나온다(역대상 4:12).

entries.definition: is mentioned with brass as the earliest of known metals. (Genesis 4:22) The natural wealth in iron of the soil of Canaan is indicated by describing it as a land whose stones are iron.” (8:9) (Recent explorations have shown that iron ore is abundant in the northern part of Palestine.—ED.) The book of Job contains passages which indicate that iron was a metal well known. Sheet-iron was used for cooking utensils. (Ezekiel 4:3) cf. Levi 7:9 That it was plentiful in the time of David appears from (1 Chronicles 22:3) The market of Tyre was supplied with bright or polished iron by the merchants of by Dan and Javan. (Ezekiel 27:19) The Chalybes of the Pontus were celebrated as workers in iron in very ancient times. The product of their labor is supposed to be alluded to in (Jeremiah 16:12) as being of superior quality. Specimens of Assyrian ironwork overlaid with bronze were discovered by Mr. Layard, and are now in the British Museum. Iron weapons of various kinds were found at Nimroud, but fell to pieces on exposure to the air. (pious), one of the cities of Naphtali, (Joshua 19:38) hitherto totally unknown.
entries.definition_ko: 놋과 함께 가장 먼저 알려진 금속으로 언급된다(창세기 4:22). 가나안 땅의 풍부한 철 매장량은 '돌이 철이요'라는 표현으로 나타난다(신명기 8:9). 욥기에는 철이 잘 알려진 금속이었음을 보여주는 구절들이 있으며 얇은 철판은 조리 도구로 쓰였다(에스겔 4:3). 다윗 시대에는 철이 풍부했음이 역대상 22:3에서 확인되며 두로 시장은 단과 야완 상인들을 통해 광택 낸 철을 공급받았다(에스겔 27:19). 별도로 '이론'('경건한'이라는 뜻)은 아직 확인되지 않은 납달리 지파 성읍이다(여호수아 19:38).

entries.definition: (God heals), one of the cities of Benjamin. (Joshua 18:27) No trace has yet been discovered of its situation.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 고치신다'는 뜻으로 베냐민 지파 성읍 중 하나이다(여호수아 18:27). 위치가 아직 밝혀지지 않았다.

entries.definition: (city of the sun), a city of the Danites (Joshua 19:41) probably identical with Bethshemesh.
entries.definition_ko: '태양의 성읍'이라는 뜻으로 단 지파의 성읍이며(여호수아 19:41) 벧세메스와 동일한 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: (watch), the eldest son of the great Caleb son of Jephunneh. (1 Chronicles 4:15) (B.C. 1451.)
entries.definition_ko: '파수'라는 뜻으로 위대한 갈렙벤여분네의 맏아들이다(역대상 4:15).

entries.definition: (laughter), the son whom Sara bore to Abraham, in the hundredth year of his age, at Gerar. (B.C. 1897.) In his infancy he became the object of Ishmael’s jealousy; and in his youth the victim, in intention, of Abraham’s great sacrificial act of faith. When forty years old he married Rebekah his cousin, by whom, when he was sixty, he had two sons, Esau and Jacob. Driven by famine to Gerar, he acquired great wealth by his flocks but was repeatedly dispossessed by the Philistines of the wells which he sunk at convenient stations. After the deceit by which Jacob acquired his father’s blessing Isaac sent his son to seek a wife in Padan-aram; and all that we know of him during the last forty-three years of his life in that he saw that God, with a large and prosperous family, return to him at Hebron. (Genesis 36:27) before he died there, at the age of 180 years. He was buried by his two sons in the cave of Machpelah. In the New Testament reference is made to the offering of Isaac (Hebrews 11:17; James 2:21) and to his blessing his sons. (Hebrews 11:20) In (Galatians 4:28-31) he is contrasted with Ishmael. In reference to the offering up of Isaac by Abraham, the primary doctrine taught are those of sacrifice and substitution, as the means appointed by God for taking away sin; and, as co-ordinate with these, the need of the obedience of faith, on the part of man, to receive the benefit. (Hebrews 11:17) The animal which God provided and Abraham offered was in the whole history of sacrifice the recognized type of “the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sins of the world.” Isaac is the type of humanity itself, devoted to death for sin.
entries.definition_ko: '웃음'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함이 백 세에 그랄에서 사라를 통해 얻은 아들이다. 어릴 때 이스마엘의 시기의 대상이 되었고 청년기에는 아브라함의 위대한 신앙의 제사(모리아산 번제)의 대상이 될 뻔했다. 40세에 사촌 리브가와 결혼했고 60세에 에서와 야곱 쌍둥이를 낳았다. 기근으로 그랄에 갔다가 양떼로 큰 부를 얻었으나 블레셋 사람들에게 우물을 여러 차례 빼앗겼다. 야곱이 속임수로 아버지의 축복을 얻은 후 리브가의 뜻에 따라 밧단아람으로 아내를 구하러 보냈다. 180세에 헤브론에서 죽어 두 아들에게 막벨라 굴에 묻혔다. 신약에서는 그의 번제(히브리서 11:17)와 아들들을 축복한 일(히브리서 11:20)이 언급되며 갈라디아서 4:28에서는 이스마엘과 대조된다. 아브라함이 이삭을 제물로 바친 사건은 대속을 통한 죄사함이라는 원리와 믿음의 순종의 필요성을 가르치며, 하나님이 예비하신 짐승은 '세상 죄를 지고 가는 하나님의 어린 양'의 모형이 된다.

entries.definition: the prophet, son of Amoz. The Hebrew name signifies Salvation of Jahu (a shortened form of Jehovah), He prophesied concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, (Isaiah 1:1) covering probably 758 to 698 B.C. He was married and had two sons. Rabbinical tradition says that Isaiah, when 90 years old, was sawn asunder in the trunk of a carob tree by order of Manasseh, to which it is supposed that reference is made in (Hebrews 11:37)
entries.definition_ko: 선지자 아모스의 아들. 히브리어 이름은 '여호와의 구원'을 뜻한다. 유다 왕 웃시야, 요담, 아하스, 히스기야 시대(대략 주전 758~698년경)에 유다와 예루살렘에 대해 예언했다(이사야 1:1). 결혼해 두 아들을 두었다. 랍비 전승에 따르면 90세에 므낫세의 명으로 톱질당해 죽었다고 하며 이는 히브리서 11:37의 배경으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: I. Chapters 1-5 contain Isaiah’s prophecies in the reigns of Uzziah and Jotham, foretelling that the present prosperity of Judah should be destroyed, and that Israel should be brought to desolation. In chs. 6, 7 he announces the birth of the child Immanuel, which in ch. 9 is more positively predicted. Chs. 9-12 contain additional prophecies against Israel, chs. (Isaiah 10:5-12) (6) being the most highly-wrought passages in the whole book. Chs. 13-23 contain chiefly a collection of utterances, each of which is styled a “burden,” fore-telling the doom of Babylon, Philistia, Moab, Ethiopia, Egypt and Tyre. The ode of triumph in ch. (Isaiah 14:3-23) is among the most poetical passages in all literature. Chs. 24-27 form one prophecy, essentially connected with the preceding ten “burdens,” chs. 13-23, of which it is in effect a general summary. Chs. 23-35 predict the Assyrian invasion, and chs. 36-39 have reference to this invasion; prophecies that were so soon fulfilled. (2 Kings 19:35) II. The last 27 chapters form a separate prophecy, and are supposed by many critics to have been written in the time of the Babylonian captivity, and are therefore ascribed to a “later Isaiah;” but the best reasons are in favor of but one Isaiah. This second part falls into three sections, each consisting of nine chapters:— • The first section, chs 40-48 has for its main topic the comforting assurance of the deliverance from Babylon by Koresh (Cyrus), who is even named twice. ch. (Isaiah 41:2,3,25; 44:28; 45:1-4,13; 46:11; 48:14,15) • The second section, chs. 49-56, is distinguished from the first by several features. The person of Cyrus as well as his name and the specification of Babylon, disappear altogether. Return from exile is indeed spoken of repeatedly and at length, ch. (Isaiah 49:9-26; 51:9-52; 12; 55:12,13; 57:14) but in such general terms as admit of being applied to the spiritual and Messianic as well as to the literal restoration. • This section is mainly occupied with various practical exhortations founded upon the views of the future already set forth. In favor of the authenticity of the last 27 chapters the following reasons may be advanced:— (a) The unanimous testimony of Jewish and Christian tradition, comp. Ecclus. 48:24, and the evidence of the New Testament quotations. (Matthew 3:3; Luke 4:17; Acts 8:28; Romans 10:16,20) (b) The unity of design which connects these last 27 chapters with the preceding; the oneness of diction which pervades the whole book; the peculiar elevation and grandeur of style which characterize the second part as well as the first; the absence of any other name than Isaiah’s claiming the authorship; lastly, the Messianic predictions which mark its inspiration and remove the chief ground of objection against its having been written by Isaiah. In point of style we can find no difficulty in recognizing in the second part the presence of the same plastic genius as we discover in the first.
entries.definition_ko: 1~5장은 웃시야·요담 시대의 예언으로 유다의 번영이 무너지고 이스라엘이 황폐해질 것을 예고한다. 6~7장은 임마누엘의 탄생을 예고하며 9장에서 더 구체적으로 예언된다. 13~23장은 바벨론·블레셋·모압·에디오피아·애굽·두로에 대한 '경고'들을 모은 것이다. 24~27장은 앞선 예언들의 종합이며 28~35장은 앗수르 침공을 예고, 36~39장은 그 침공과 직접 관련된다. 마지막 27장(40~66장)은 많은 비평가들이 바벨론 포로기의 '제2 이사야' 저작으로 보나 한 명의 이사야 저작설이 더 설득력 있는 근거를 지닌다. 첫 부분(40~48장)은 고레스를 통한 바벨론 구원 약속을, 둘째 부분(49~56장)은 영적·메시아적 회복을, 셋째 부분은 실천적 권면을 다룬다.

entries.definition: (one who looks forth), daughter of Haran the brother of Abram, and sister of Milcah and of Lot. (Genesis 11:29) In the Jewish traditions she is identified with Sarai. (B.C. about 1920.)
entries.definition_ko: '내다보는 자'라는 뜻으로 아브람의 형제 하란의 딸이며 밀가와 롯의 자매이다(창세기 11:29). 유대 전승에서는 사래와 동일시된다.

entries.definition: (man of Kerioth). [Judas IscariotISCARIOT]
entries.definition_ko: '그리욧 사람'이라는 뜻이다. 유다 가룟(JUDAS ISCARIOT) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: (praising), a man in the line of Judah, commemorated as the “father of Eshtemos.” (1 Chronicles 4:17)
entries.definition_ko: '찬양하는'이라는 뜻으로 유다 계열 인물, '에스드모아의 아버지'로 기록된다(역대상 4:17).

entries.definition: (left behind), a son of Abraham and Keturah, (Genesis 25:2; 1 Chronicles 1:32) and the progenitor of a tribe of northern Arabia. (B.C. after 1856.)
entries.definition_ko: '남겨진'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함과 그두라의 아들이며(창세기 25:2) 북아라비아 한 부족의 시조가 되었다.

entries.definition: (he that dwells at Nobl), son of Rapha, one of the race of Philistine giants, who attacked David in battle, but was slain by Abishai. (2 Samuel 21:16,17) (B.C. 1018.)
entries.definition_ko: '놉에 거하는 자'라는 뜻으로 라파의 아들, 블레셋 거인족 중 하나로 다윗을 전투에서 공격했으나 아비새에게 죽임당했다(사무엘하 21:16).

entries.definition: (man of shame) the youngest of Saul’s four sons, and his legitimate successor. (B.C. 1068.) Ish-bosheth was “forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and though only in name. The wars and negotiations with David were entirely carried on by Abner (2 Samuel 2:12; 3:6,12) The death of Abner deprived the house of Saul of its last remaining support. When Ish-bosheth heard of it, “his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.” He was murdered in his bed.
entries.definition_ko: '수치의 사람'이라는 뜻으로 사울의 네 아들 중 막내이자 합법적 후계자였다. 40세에 이스라엘 왕이 되었으나 명목상일 뿐, 다윗과의 전쟁과 협상은 전적으로 아브넬이 주도했다(사무엘하 2:12). 아브넬이 죽자 사울 가문의 마지막 지지 기반을 잃었고 '그의 손이 약해지고 온 이스라엘이 놀랐다'고 기록되며 결국 침상에서 살해당했다.

entries.definition: (my husband). This word occurs in (Hosea 2:16) It is the Israelite term, in opposition to Baali, the Canaanite term, with the same meaning, though with a significance of its own. (salutary). • A man of the descendants of Judah, son of Appaim, (1 Chronicles 2:31) one of the great house of Hezron. • In a subsequent genealogy of Judah we find another Ishi, with a son Zoheth. (1 Chronicles 4:20) • Head of a family of the tribe of Simeon. (1 Chronicles 4:42) • One of the heads of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan. (1 Chronicles 5:24)
entries.definition_ko: '나의 남편'이라는 뜻으로 호세아 2:16에 나오며 가나안 용어 '바알리'에 대비되는 이스라엘 용어이다. 별도로 '이시'('구원의'라는 뜻)라는 이름의 인물이 여럿 있다: (1) 유다 헤스론 가문 압바임의 아들(역대상 2:31). (2) 조헷이라는 아들을 둔 또 다른 유다 사람(역대상 4:20). (3) 시므온 지파 가문 우두머리(역대상 4:42). (4) 요단 동편 므낫세 반 지파 우두머리 중 하나(역대상 5:24).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah lends), the fifth of the five sons of Izrahiah, one of the heads of the tribe of Issachar in the time of David. (1 Chronicles 7:3) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빌려주신'이라는 뜻으로 다윗 시대 잇사갈 지파 우두머리 중 하나인 이스라히야의 다섯 아들 중 막내이다(역대상 7:3).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah lends), a lay Israelite of the Bene-Harim who had married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:31) (B.C. 459.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빌려주신'이라는 뜻으로 이방인 아내와 결혼한 브네하림 가문의 평신도 이스라엘인이다(에스라 10:31).

entries.definition: (desolation), a name in the genealogy of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:3)
entries.definition_ko: '황폐'라는 뜻으로 유다 족보에 나오는 이름이다(역대상 4:3).

entries.definition: (whom God hears). • The son of Abraham by Hagar the Egyptian his concubine; born when Abraham was fourscore and six years old. (Genesis 16:15,16) (B.C. 1910.) Ishmael was the first-born of his father. He was born in Abraham’s house when he dwelt in the plain of Mamre; and on the institution of the covenant of circumcision, was circumcised, he being then thirteen years old (Genesis 17:26) With the institution of the covenant, God renewed his promise respecting Ishmael. He does not again appear in the narrative until the weaning of Isaac. At the great feast made in celebration of the weaning, “Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, which she had borne unto Abraham, mocking,” and urged Abraham to cast him and his mother out. Comforted by the renewal of God’s promise to make of Ishmael a great nation, Abraham sent them away, and they departed and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba. His mother took Ishmael a wife out of the land of Egypt.” (Genesis 21:9-21) This wife of Ishmael was the mother of the twelve sons and one daughter. Of the later life of Ishmael we know little. He was present with Isaac at the burial of Abraham. He died at the age of 137 years. (Genesis 25:17,18) The sons of Ishmael peopled the north and west of the Arabian peninsula, and eventually formed the chief element of the Arab nation, the wandering Bedouin tribes. They are now mostly Mohammedans who look to him as their spiritual father, as the Jews look to Abraham. Their language, which is generally acknowledged to have been the Arabic community so called, has been adopted with insignificant exceptions throughout Arabia. The term “Ishmaelite” occur on three occasions: (Genesis 37:25,27,28; 39:1; Judges 8:24; Psalms 83:6) • One of the sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul through Meribbaal or Mephibosheth. (1 Chronicles 8:38; 9:44) • A man of Judah, father of Zebadiah. (2 Chronicles 19:11) • Another man of Judah, son of Jehohanan; one of the captains of hundreds who assisted Jehoiada in restoring Joash to the throne. (2 Chronicles 23:1) • A priest of the Bene-Pashur, who was forced by Ezra to relinquish his foreign wife. (Ezra 10:22) • The son of Nethaniah; a perfect marvel of craft and villainy, whose treachery forms one of the chief episodes of the history of the period immediately succeeding the first fall of Jerusalem. His exploits are related in (Jeremiah 40:7; Jeremiah 41:16) with a short summary. During the siege of the city he had fled across the Jordan where he found a refuge at the court of Baalis. After the departure of the Chaldeans, Ishmael made no secret of his intention to kill the superintendent left by the king of Babylon and usurp his position. Of this Zedaliah was warned in express terms by Johanan and his companions, but notwithstanding entertained Ishmael and his followers at a feast, (Jeremiah 41:1) during which Ishmael murdered Gedaliah and all his attendants. The same night he killed all Zedaliah’s establishment, including some Chaldean soldiers who were there. For two days the massacre remained entirely unknown to the people of the town. On the second day eighty devotees were bringing incense and offerings to the ruins of the temple. At his invitation they turned aside to the residence of the superintendent, and there Ishmael and his band butchered nearly the whole number: ten only escaped by offering a heavy ransom for their lives. This done he descended to the town, surprised and carried off the daughters of King Zedekiah, who had been sent there by Nebuchadnezzar for safety, with their eunuchs and their Chaldean guard, (Jeremiah 41:10,16) and all the people of the town, and made off with his prisoners to the country of the Ammonites. The news of the massacre had by this time got abroad, and Ishmael was quickly pursued by Johanan and his companions. He was attacked, two of his bravos slain, the whole of the prey recovered; and Ishmael himself with the remaining eight of his people, escaped to the Ammonites.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 들으신다'는 뜻. (1) 아브라함이 애굽 사람 첩 하갈을 통해 86세에 얻은 아들(창세기 16:15)로 아브라함의 맏아들이었다. 13세에 할례를 받았다(창세기 17:26). 이삭이 젖 뗄 때 사라의 요청으로 하갈과 함께 쫓겨나 브엘세바 광야를 방황했으며 애굽 사람 아내를 통해 열두 아들과 딸 하나를 낳았다. 137세에 죽었다(창세기 25:17). 그 후손이 아라비아 반도 북서부에 퍼져 아랍 민족, 특히 베두인 유목 부족의 주요 구성원이 되었으며 오늘날 대부분 무슬림으로 그를 영적 아버지로 여긴다. (2)~(5) 그 외 여러 동명이인들이 있으며, 그중 느다냐의 아들 이스마엘은 예루살렘 함락 직후 그다랴 총독을 암살하고 유다인들을 학살한 뒤 암몬 땅으로 도망친 악명 높은 인물이다(예레미야 40:7).

entries.definition: (decendant of Ishmael). [Ishmael]
entries.definition_ko: 이스마엘(ISHMAEL)의 후손을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: (Jehovah hears), son of Obadiah; the ruler of the tribe of Zebulun in the time of King David. (1 Chronicles 27:19) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으신다'는 뜻으로 오바댜의 아들, 다윗 시대 스불론 지파 지도자였다(역대상 27:19).

entries.definition: (1 Chronicles 2:17) and Ish’me-elites (descendants of Ishmael), (Genesis 37:25,27,28; 39:1) the form in which the descendants of Ishmael are given in a few places in the Authorized Version.
entries.definition_ko: 이스마엘 자손을 가리키는 흠정역의 다른 표기이다(역대상 2:17).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah keeps), a Benjamite, one of the family of Elpaal. (1 Chronicles 8:18) (B.C. before 538.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지키시는'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 사람, 엘바알 가문이다(역대상 8:18).

entries.definition: (man of glory), one of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan, son of Hammoleketh. (1 Chronicles 7:18) (B.C. 1491.)
entries.definition_ko: '영광의 사람'이라는 뜻으로 요단 동편 므낫세 지파, 함몰레겟의 아들이다(역대상 7:18).

entries.definition: (bald), a Benjamite, one of the family of Shashak. (1 Chronicles 8:22) (B.C. before 588.)
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람, 사삭 가문이다(역대상 8:22).

entries.definition: (men of Tob), apparently one of the small kingdoms or states which formed part of the general country of Aram, named with Zobah, Rehob and Maacah. (2 Samuel 10:6,8)
entries.definition_ko: '돕 사람들'이라는 뜻으로 소바·르홉·마아가와 함께 언급되는 아람 소국 중 하나로 보인다(사무엘하 10:6).

entries.definition: (quiet), the second son of Asher. (Genesis 46:17) (B.C. 1706.)
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 둘째 아들이다(창세기 46:17).

entries.definition: (quiet), the third son of Asher, (1 Chronicles 7:30) founder of a family bearing his name. (Numbers 26:44) Authorized Version “Jesuites.” (B.C. 1706.)
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 셋째 아들이며 그 이름을 딴 가문의 시조이다(역대상 7:30).

entries.definition: (quiet), the second son of Saul by his wife Ahinoam (1 Samuel 14:4) comp. 1Sam 14:50(Died B.C. 1053.)
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 사울과 아히노암 사이의 둘째 아들이다(사무엘상 14:4).

entries.definition: The radical sense of the Hebrew word seems to be “habitable places,” as opposed to water, and in this sense it occurs in (Isaiah 42:15) Hence it means secondarily any maritime district, whether belonging to a continent or to an island; thus it is used of the shore of the Mediterranean, (Isaiah 20:6; 23:2,6) and of the coasts of Elishah, (Ezekiel 27:7) i.e. of Greece and Asia Minor.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 원어의 근본 의미는 물에 대비되는 '거주 가능한 땅'이며(이사야 42:15) 이후 대륙이든 섬이든 해안 지역 전체를 뜻하는 것으로 확장되어 지중해 연안(이사야 20:6)이나 엘리사(헬라·소아시아) 해안을 가리키는 데도 쓰인다(에스겔 27:7).

entries.definition: (Jehovah hears), a Gibeonite, one of the chiefs of those warriors, who joined David at Ziklag. (1 Chronicles 12:4). (B.C. 1064.) (whom Jehovah upholds), a Levite who was one of the overseers of offerings during the revival under King Hezekiah. (2 Chronicles 31:13) (B.C. 776.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으신다'는 뜻으로 다윗에게 시글락에서 합류한 기브온 용사 지도자 중 하나였다(역대상 12:4). 별도로 '여호와께서 붙드시는 자'라는 뜻의 동명이인은 히스기야 시대 헌물 감독 레위인 중 하나였다(역대하 31:13).

entries.definition: (bald), a Benjamite of the family of Beriah; one of the heads of his tribe. (1 Chronicles 8:16) (B.C. before 588.)
entries.definition_ko: '대머리'라는 뜻으로 브리아 가문 베냐민 사람, 지파 우두머리 중 하나이다(역대상 8:16).

entries.definition: (the prince that prevails with God). • The name given, (Genesis 32:28) to Jacob after his wrestling with the angel, (Hosea 12:4) at Peniel. Gesenius interprets Israel “soldier of God.” • It became the national name of the twelve tribes collectively. They are so called in (Exodus 3:16) and afterward. • It is used in a narrower sense, excluding Judah, in (1 Samuel 11:8; 2 Samuel 20:1; 1 Kings 12:16) Thenceforth it was assumed and accepted as the name of the northern kingdom. • After the Babylonian captivity, the returned exiles resumed the name Israel as the designation of their nation. The name Israel is also used to denote lay-men, as distinguished from priests, Levites and other ministers. (Ezra 6:16; 9:1; 10:25; Nehemiah 11:3) etc.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님과 겨루어 이긴 왕자'라는 뜻. (1) 브니엘에서 천사와 씨름한 후 야곱에게 주어진 이름(창세기 32:28). 게제니우스는 '하나님의 군사'로 해석한다. (2) 열두 지파 전체를 가리키는 민족명이 되었다(출애굽기 3:16). (3) 유다를 제외한 좁은 의미로도 쓰여(사무엘상 11:8) 이후 북이스라엘 왕국의 명칭으로 굳어졌다. (4) 바벨론 포로 귀환 후 귀환자들이 다시 자기 민족을 '이스라엘'이라 불렀다. (5) 제사장·레위인 등 성직자와 구별되는 평신도를 가리키는 데도 쓰인다(에스라 6:16).

entries.definition: I. the kingdom.—The prophet Ahijah of Shiloh, who was commissioned in the latter days of Solomon to announce the division of the kingdom, left one tribe (Judah) to the house of David, and assigned ten to Jeroboam. (1 Kings 11:31,35) These were probably Joseph (Ephraim and Manasseh), Issachar, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali, Benjamin, Dan, Simeon, Gad and Reuben; Levi being intentionally omitted. Eventually the greater part of Benjamin, and probably the whole of Simeon and Dan, were included as if by common consent in the kingdom of Judah. With respect to the conquests of David, Moab appears to have been attached to the kingdom of Israel. (2 Kings 3:4) so much of Syria as remained subject to Solomon, see (1 Kings 11:24) would probably be claimed by his successor in the northern kingdom; and Ammon was at one time allied (2 Chronicles 20:1) we know not how closely or how early, with Moab. The seacoast between Accho and Japho remained in the possession of Israel. The whole population may perhaps have amounted to at least three and a half millions. II. the capitals .—Shechem was the first capital of the new kingdom. (1 Kings 12:25) Subsequently Tirzah became the royal residence, if not the capital, of Jeroboam (1 Kings 14:17) and of his successors. cf. (1 Kings 15:33; 16:8,17,23) Samaria was chosen by Omri. (1 Kings 16:24) Jezreel was probably only a royal residence of some of the Israelitish kings. III. History .—The kingdom of Israel lasted 254 years, from B.C. 975 to B.C. 721. The detailed history of the kingdom will be found under the names of its nineteen kings. See chart of the kings of Judah and Israel, at the end of the work. A summary view may be taken in four periods: (a) B.C. 975-929. Jeroboam had not sufficient force of character in himself to make a lasting impression on his people. A king, but not a founder of a dynasty, he aimed at nothing beyond securing his present elevation. Baasha, in the midst of the army at Gibbethon, slew the son and successor of Jeroboam; Zimri, a captain of chariots, slew the son and successor of Baasha; Omri, the captain of the host, was chosen to punish Zimri; and after a civil war of four years he prevailed over Tibni, the choice of half the people. (b) B.C. 929-884. For forty-five years Israel wag governed by the house of Omri. The princes of his house cultivated an alliance with the king of Judah which was cemented by the marriage of Jehoram and Athaliah. The adoption of Baal-worship led to a reaction in the nation, to the moral triumph of the prophets in the person of Elijah, and to extinction of the house of Ahab in obedience to the bidding of Elisha. (c) B.C. 884-772. Unparalleled triumphs, but deeper humiliation, awaited the kingdom of Israel under the dynasty of Jehu. Hazael, the ablest king of Damascus, reduced Jehoahaz to the condition of a vassal, and triumphed for a time over both the disunited Hebrew kingdoms. Almost the first sign of the restoration of their strength was a war between them; and Jehoash, the grandson of Jehu, entered Jerusalem as the conqueror of Amaziah. Jehoash also turned the tide of war against the Syrians; and Jeroboam II., the most powerful of all the kings of of Israel, captured Damascus, and recovered the whole ancient frontier from Hamath to the Dead Sea. This short-lived greatness expired with the last king of Jehu’s line. (d) B.C. 772-721. Military violence, it would seem, broke off the hereditary succession after the obscure and probably convulsed reign of Zachariah. An unsuccessful usurper, Shallum, is followed by the cruel Menahem, who, being unable to make head against the first attack of Assyria under Pul, became the agent of that monarch for the oppressive taxation of his subjects. Yet his power at home was sufficient to insure for his son and successor Pekahiah a ten-years reign, cut short by a bold usurper, Pekah. Abandoning the northern and transjordanic regions to the encroaching power of Assyria under Tiglathpileser, he was very near subjugating Judah, with the help of Damascus, now the coequal ally of Israel. But Assyria interposing summarily put an end to the independence of Damascus, and perhaps was the indirect cause of the assassination of the baffled Pekah. The irresolute Hoshea, the next and last usurper, became tributary to his invaders Shalmaneser, betrayed the Assyrian to the rival monarchy of Egypt, and was punished by the loss of his liberty, and by the capture, after a three-years siege, of his strong capital, Samaria. Some gleanings of the ten tribes yet remained in the land after so many years of religious decline, moral debasement, national degradation, anarchy, bloodshed and deportation. Even these were gathered up by the conqueror and carried to Assyria, never again, as a distinct people, to occupy their portion of that goodly and pleasant land which their forefathers won under Joshua from the heathen. (Schaff Bib. Dic.) adds to this summary that “after the destruction of the kingdom of Israel, B.C. 721, the name ’Israel’ began to be applied to the whole surviving people. No doubt many of the kingdom of Israel joined the later kingdom of the Jews after the captivity, and became part of that kingdom.—ED.)
entries.definition_ko: 선지자 실로 사람 아히야가 솔로몬 말년에 왕국 분열을 선포하며 한 지파(유다)는 다윗 가문에, 열 지파는 여로보암에게 배정했다(열왕기상 11:31). 세겜이 첫 수도였다가(열왕기상 12:25) 디르사, 이후 오므리가 세운 사마리아가 수도가 되었다. 이스르엘은 일부 왕들의 별궁이었을 것이다. 왕국은 주전 975년부터 721년까지 254년간 존속했으며 19명의 왕을 거쳤다. 여로보암 왕조(주전 975~929), 오므리 왕조(929~884, 바알 숭배 도입과 엘리야·엘리사를 통한 반동), 예후 왕조(884~772, 여로보암 2세 때 최대 영토 회복 후 급속 쇠퇴), 마지막 시기(772~721, 잦은 찬탈과 앗수르의 압박 끝에 살만에셀에게 사마리아 함락, 3년 포위 후 열 지파가 앗수르로 사로잡혀 감)로 나뉜다.

entries.definition: (descendant of Israel). In (2 Samuel 17:25) Ithra, the father of Amasa, is called “an Israelite,” while in (1 Chronicles 2:17) he appears as “Jether the Ishmaelite.” The latter is undoubtedly the true reading.
entries.definition_ko: '이스라엘의 후손'이라는 뜻이다. 사무엘하 17:25에서는 아마사의 아버지 이드라를 '이스라엘 사람'이라 부르나 역대상 2:17에서는 '이스마엘 사람 예델'로 나오는데 후자가 옳은 표기로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: (reward). I. The ninth son of Jacob and the fifth of Leah. (Genesis 30:17,18) (B.C. 1753-45) At the descent into Egypt four sons are ascribed to him, who founded the four chief families of the tribes. (Genesis 46:13; Numbers 26:23,25; 1 Chronicles 7:1) The number of the fighting men of Issachar, when taken in the census at Sinai, was 54,400. During the journey they seem to have steadily increased. The allotment of Issachar lay above that of Manasseh. (Joshua 19:17-23) In the words of Josephus, “it extended in length from Carmel to the Jordan, in breadth to Mount Tabor.” This territory was, as it still is, among the richest land in Palestine. It is this aspect of the territory of Issachar which appears to be alluded to in the blessing of Jacob. • A Korhite Levite, one of the door-keepers of the house of Jehovah, seventh son of Obed-edom. (1 Chronicles 26:5)
entries.definition_ko: '보상'이라는 뜻. (1) 야곱의 아홉째 아들이자 레아의 다섯째 아들(창세기 30:17). 애굽로 내려갈 때 네 아들이 있어 잇사갈 지파의 네 주요 가문을 이루었다. 시내 인구조사 때 전투 가능 인원은 54,400명이었다. 잇사갈의 몫은 므낫세 위쪽에 위치했으며(여호수아 19:17) 요세푸스에 따르면 '길이는 갈멜에서 요단강까지, 너비는 다볼산까지' 뻗었다. 팔레스타인에서 가장 비옥한 땅 중 하나였으며 이는 야곱의 축복에 반영된 것으로 보인다. (2) 고라 가문 레위인, 오벧에돔의 일곱째 아들, 성전 문지기(역대상 26:5).

entries.definition: (whom Jehovah lends). • A descendant of Moses by his younger son Eliezer. (1 Chronicles 24:21) comp. 1Chr 23:17; 26:25(B.C. after 1451.) • A Levite of the house of Kohath and family of Uzziel. (1 Chronicles 24:26) (Uncertain date.)
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빌려주신'이라는 뜻. (1) 모세의 둘째 아들 엘리에셀의 후손(역대상 24:21). (2) 고핫 가문 웃시엘 족속의 레위인(역대상 24:26).

entries.definition: (Leviticus 15:2,3; 22:4; Numbers 5:2; 2 Samuel 3:29) In (Leviticus 15:3) a distinction is introduced, which merely means that the cessation of the actual flux does not constitute ceremonial cleanness, but that the patient must abide the legal time, seven days, ver 13, and perform the prescribed purifications and sacrifice. ver. 14.
entries.definition_ko: 레위기 15:2 등에 나오는 유출병 관련 규정으로 실제 유출이 멈춘 것만으로 의식적 정결이 되는 것이 아니라 정해진 기간(7일)을 지키고 규정된 정결 의식과 제사를 드려야 함을 구분해 설명한다.

entries.definition: (quiet), second son of Asher. (1 Chronicles 7:30) (B.C. 1706.)
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 둘째 아들이다(역대상 7:30).

entries.definition: (quiet), third son of Asher, (Genesis 46:17) founder of a family called after him, though in the Authorized Version appearing as THE Jesuites. (Numbers 26:44) (B.C. 1706.)
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 셋째 아들이며 그 이름을 딴 가문의 시조이다(창세기 46:17).

entries.definition: [Army]
entries.definition_ko: 군대(ARMY) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: This word is used in the New Testament, (Acts 18:2; 27:1; Hebrews 13:24) in the usual sense of the period, i.e. in its true geographical sense, as denoting the whole natural peninsula between the Alps and the Straits of Messina.
entries.definition_ko: 신약에서 당대의 일반적 의미, 곧 알프스와 메시나 해협 사이의 이탈리아 반도 전체를 지리적으로 가리키는 데 쓰인다(사도행전 18:2).

entries.definition: (with the Lord), a Benjamite, son of Ribai of Gibeah, one of the heroes of David’s guard. (1 Chronicles 11:31) (B.C. 1046.)
entries.definition_ko: '주와 함께'라는 뜻으로 기브아 사람 리배의 아들, 베냐민 사람, 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나이다(역대상 11:31).

entries.definition: (land of palms), the youngest son of Aaron. (Exodus 6:23) (B.C. 1491.) After the death of Nadab and Abihu, (Leviticus 10:1) Eleazar and Ithamar were appointed to succeed to their places in the priestly office. (Exodus 28:1,40,43; Numbers 3:3,4; 1 Chronicles 24:2) In the distribution of services belonging to the tabernacle, and its transport on the march of the Israelites, the Gershonites and the Merarites were placed under the superintendence of Ithamar. (Exodus 38:21; Numbers 4:21-33) The high priesthood passed into the family of Ithamar in the person of Eli, but for what reason we are not informed.
entries.definition_ko: '종려나무의 땅'이라는 뜻으로 아론의 막내아들이다(출애굽기 6:23). 나답과 아비후가 죽은 후 엘르아살과 함께 제사장직을 이어받았다(레위기 10:1). 성막 봉사와 이동 시 게르손·므라리 자손이 그의 감독 아래 있었다(출애굽기 38:21). 훗날 대제사장직이 엘리를 통해 이다말 가문으로 넘어갔으나 그 이유는 알려지지 않았다.
