entries.definition: the last book of the New Testament. It is often called the Apocalypse, which is its title in Greek, signifying “Revelation,” • Canonical authority and authorship.—The inquiry as to the canonical authority of the Revelation resolves itself into a question of authorship. Was St. John the apostle and evangelist the writer of the Revelation? The evidence adduced in support of his being the author consists of (1) the assertions of the author and (2) historical tradition. (1) The author’s description of himself in the 1st and 22d chapters is certainly equivalent to an assertion that he is the apostle. He names himself simply John, without prefix or addition. is also described as a servant of Christ, one who had borne testimony as an eye-witness of the word of God and of the testimony of Christ. He is in Patmos for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ. He is also a fellow sufferer with those whom he addresses, and the authorized channel of the most direct and important communication that was ever made to the Seven Churches of Asia, of which churches John the apostle was at that time the spiritual governor and teacher. Lastly, the writer was a fellow servant of angels and a brother of prophets. All these marks are found united in the apostle John, and in him alone of all historical persons. (2) A long series of writers testify to St. John’s authorship: Justin Martyr (cir. 150 A.D.), Eusebius, Irenaeus (A.D. 195), Clement of Alexandria (about 200), Tertullian (207), Origen (233). All the foregoing writers, testifying that the book came from an apostle, believed that it was a part of Holy Scripture. The book was admitted into the list of the Third Council of Carthage, A.D. 397. • Time and place of writing.—The date of the Revelation is given by the great majority of critics as A.D. 95-97. Irenaeus says: “It (i.e. the Revelation) was seen no very long time ago, but almost in our own generation, at the close of Domitian’s reign. Eusebius also records that, in the persecution under Domitian, John the apostle and evangelist was banished to the Island Patmos for his testimony of the divine word. There is no mention in any writer of the first three centuries of any other time or place, and the style in which the messages to the Seven Churches are delivered rather suggests the notion that the book was written in Patmos. • Interpretation .—Modern interpreters are generally placed in three great divisions: (a) The Historical or Continuous exposition, in whose opinion the Revelation is a progressive history of the fortunes of the Church from the first century to the end been almost or altogether fulfilled in the time which has passed since it was written; that it refers principally to the triumph of Christianity over Judaism and Paganism, signalized in the downfall of Jerusalem and of Rome. (c) The Futurist expositors, whose views show a strong reaction against some extravagances of the two preceding schools. They believe that the whole book, excepting perhaps the first three chapters, refers principally, if not exclusively, to events which are yet-to come. Dr.Arnold in his sermons “On the Interpretation of Prophecy” suggests that we should bear in mind that predictions have a lower historical sense as well as a higher spiritual sense; that there may be one or more than one typical, imperfect, historical fulfillment of the prophecy, in each of which the higher spiritual fulfillment is shadowed forth more or less distinctly.
entries.definition_ko: 신약의 마지막 책으로 헬라어 원제 '아포칼립시스'(계시)에서 이름이 유래했다. 저자는 사도 요한으로 널리 인정되며 도미티아누스 박해 말기(주후 95-97년경) 밧모섬에서 기록된 것으로 여겨진다. 해석의 관점은 크게 역사적 해석(교회사 전체를 다룬다는 견해), 예비적 해석(주로 예루살렘과 로마의 멸망 등 이미 성취된 사건을 다룬다는 견해), 미래적 해석(대부분 미래에 성취될 사건을 다룬다는 견해)으로 나뉜다.

entries.definition: (a hot stone), one of the places which Sennacherib mentions, in his taunting message to Hezekiah, as having been destroyed by his predecessor. (2 Kings 19:12; Isaiah 37:12)
entries.definition_ko: 산헤립이 히스기야를 조롱하며 자신의 선왕이 정복했다고 언급한 지명 중 하나다(열왕기하 19:12).

entries.definition: (delight), an Asherite, of the sons of Ulla. (1 Chronicles 7:39) (B.C. 1444.)
entries.definition_ko: 아셀 지파 울라의 아들이다(역대상 7:39).

entries.definition: (firm). • King of Damascus. He attacked Jotham during the latter part of his reign, (2 Kings 15:37) but his chief war was with Ahaz, whose territories he invaded, in conjunction with Pekah about B.C. 741. Though unsuccessful is his siege of Jerusalem, (2 Kings 16:5; Isaiah 7:1) he “recovered Elath to Syria.” (2 Kings 16:6) Soon after this he was attacked defeated and slain by Tiglath-pileser II, king of Assyria. (2 Kings 16:9) • One of the families of the Nethinim. (Ezra 2:48; Nehemiah 7:50) (B.C. before 536.)
entries.definition_ko: 다메섹 왕으로 요담 말기를 공격했고 이후 베가와 연합해 아하스를 침공했다(주전 741년경). 예루살렘 포위에는 실패했으나 엘랏을 되찾았고 이후 앗수르 왕 디글랏빌레셋에게 패해 죽임을 당했다(열왕기하 15:37, 16:5-9). 또한 느디님 가문 중 하나도 이 이름이다(에스라 2:48).

entries.definition: (prince), son of Eliadah, a Syrian, who when David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, put himself at the head of a band of freebooters and set up a petty kingdom at Damascus. (1 Kings 11:23) He harassed the kingdom of Solomon during his whole reign. (B.C. 1043-975.)
entries.definition_ko: 다윗이 소바 왕 하닷에셀을 무찔렀을 때 도적떼를 모아 다메섹에 작은 왕국을 세운 아람 사람으로 솔로몬 통치 내내 그를 괴롭혔다(열왕기상 11:23).

entries.definition: (breach), an Italian town situated on the Bruttian coast, just at the southern entrance of the Straits of Messina. The name occurs in the account of St. Paul’s voyage from Syracuse to Puteoli, after the shipwreck at Malta. (Acts 28:13) By a curious coincidence, the figures on its coin are the very “twin brothers” which gave the name to St. Paul’s ship. It was originally a Greek colony; it was miserably destroyed by Dionysius of Syracuse. From Augustus it received advantages which combined with its geographical position in making it important throughout the duration of the Roman empire. The modern Reggio is a town of 10,000 inhabitants. Its distance across the straits from Messina is only about six miles.
entries.definition_ko: 이탈리아 브루티움 해안, 메시나 해협 남쪽 입구에 위치한 도시로 바울이 말타 파선 후 시라쿠사에서 보디올로 가는 항해 중 들른 곳이다(사도행전 28:13).

entries.definition: (head), son of Zorobabel in the genealogy of Christ. (Luke 3:27) It is conjectured that Rhesa is no person, but merely a title.
entries.definition_ko: 그리스도의 족보에서 스룹바벨의 아들로 나오나 실제로는 인물이 아니라 칭호일 가능성이 제기된다(누가복음 3:27).

entries.definition: (rose), the name of a maid who announced Peter’s arrival at the door of Mary’s house after his miraculous release from prison. (Acts 12:13) (A.D. 44.)
entries.definition_ko: 베드로가 옥에서 기적적으로 풀려난 후 찾아왔을 때 문에서 그를 맞이한 마리아의 집 여종이다(사도행전 12:13).

entries.definition: (rosy), a celebrated island in the Mediterranean Sea. (It is triangular in form, 60 miles long from north to south, and about 18 wide. It is noted now, as in ancient times, for its delightful climate and the fertility of its soil. The city of Rhodes, its capital, was famous for its huge brazen statue of Apollo called the Colossus of Rhodes. It stood at the entrance of the harbor, and was so large that ships in full sail could pass between its legs. ED.) Rhodes is immediately opposite the high Carian and Lycian headlands at the southwest extremity of the peninsula of Asia Minor. Its position had much to do with its history. Its real eminence began about 400 B.C. with the founding of the city of Rhodes, at the northeast extremity of the island, which still continues to be the capital. After Alexander’s death it entered on a glorious period, its material prosperity being largely developed, and its institutions deserving and obtaining general esteem. We have notice of the Jewish residents in Rhodes in 1 Macc. 15:23. The Romans, after the defeat of Antiochus, assigned, during some time, to Rhodes certain districts on the mainland. Its Byzantine, history is again eminent. Under Constantine If was the metropolis of the “Province of the Islands,” It was the last place where the Christians of the East held out against the advancing Seracens; and subsequently it was once more famous as the home and fortress of the Knights of St. John. (It is now reduced to abject poverty. There are two cities—Rhodes the capital and Lindus—and forty or fifty villages. The population, according to Turner is 20,000, of whom 6000 are Turks and the rest Greeks, together with a few Jews.)
entries.definition_ko: 지중해의 유명한 섬으로 소아시아 반도 남서쪽 카리아와 리키아 곶 맞은편에 위치했다. 거대한 청동상 '로도스의 거상'으로 유명했으며 바울의 3차 전도여행 항로에 언급된다(사도행전 21:1).

entries.definition: (pleader with Jehovah), the father of Ittai the Benjamite, of Gibeah. (2 Samuel 23:29; 1 Chronicles 11:31) (B.C. before 1020.)
entries.definition_ko: 기브아 사람 베냐민 지파 잇대의 아버지다(사무엘하 23:29).

entries.definition: (fertility), One of the landmarks on the eastern boundary of the land of Israel, as specified by Moses. (Numbers 34:11) It seems hardly possible, without entirely disarranging the specification or the boundary, that the Riblah in question can be the same with the following. • Riblah in the land of Hamath, a place on the great road between Palestine and Babylonia, at which the kings of Babylonia were accustomed to remain while directing the operations of their armies in Palestine and Phoenicia. Here Nebuchadnezzer waited while the sieges of Jerusalem and of Tyre were being conducted by his lieutenants. (Jeremiah 39:5,6; 62:9,10,26,27; 2 Kings 25:6,20,21) In like manner Pharaohnecho after his victory over the Babylonians at Carchemish, returned to Riblah and summoned Jehoahaz from Jerusalem before him. (2 Kings 23:33) This Riblah still retains its ancient name, on the right (east) bank of the el-Asy (Orontes) upon the great road which connects Baalbek and Hums, about 36 miles northeast of the former end 20 miles southwest of the latter place.
entries.definition_ko: 모세가 명시한 이스라엘 동쪽 경계의 표지 중 하나, 또는 팔레스타인과 바벨론을 잇는 대로에 위치한 하맛 땅의 립나로 바벨론 왕들이 군사 작전을 지휘하며 머물던 곳이다. 느부갓네살이 예루살렘과 두로 포위 동안 이곳에 머물렀다(예레미야 39:5,6; 열왕기하 25:6).

entries.definition: It is known that all ancient nations, and especially Orientals, were fond of riddles. The riddles which the queen of Sheba came to ask of Solomon, (1 Kings 10:1; 2 Chronicles 9:1) were rather “hard questions” referring to profound inquiries. Solomon is said, however, to have been very fond of riddles. Riddles were generally proposed in verse, like the celebrated riddle of Samson. (Judges 14:14-19)
entries.definition_ko: 고대 민족, 특히 동방인들은 수수께끼를 즐겼다. 스바 여왕이 솔로몬에게 낸 것은 깊은 질문에 가까웠으며 삼손의 유명한 수수께끼처럼 대개 시 형태로 제시되었다(사사기 14:14-19; 열왕기상 10:1).

entries.definition: a deity worshipped by the Syrians of Damascus, where there was a temple or house of Rimmon. (2 Kings 5:18) Rimmon is perhaps the abbreviated form of Hadad-rimmon, Hadad being the sun-god of the Syrians. Combining this with the pomegranate which was his symbol, Hadad-rimmon would then he the sun-god of the late summer, who ripens the pomegranate and other fruits. (pomegranate) the name of several towns. • A city of Zebulun (1 Chronicles 6:77; Nehemiah 11:29) a Levitical city, the present Rummaneh, six miles north of Nazareth. • A town in the southern portion of Judah, (Joshua 15:3) allotted to Simeon, (Joshua 19:7; 1 Chronicles 4:32) probably 13 miles southwest of Hebron. • Rimmon-parez (pomegranate of the breach), the name of a march-station in the wilderness. (Numbers 33:19,20) No place now known has been identified with it. • Rimmon the Rock, a cliff or inaccessible natural fastness, in which the six hundred Benjamites who escaped the slaughter of Gibeah took refuge. (Judges 20:45,47; 21:13) In the wild country which lies on the east of the central highlands of Benjamin the name is still found attached to a village perched on the summit of a conical chalky hill, visible in all directions, and commanding the whole country. • A Benjamite of Beeroth, the father of Rechab and Baanah, the murderers of Ishbosheth. (2 Samuel 4:2,5,9)
entries.definition_ko: 다메섹의 수리아인들이 숭배한 신으로 그 신전이 있었다(열왕기하 5:18). 또한 스불론 지파 레위 성읍, 유다·시므온 지파 남부 성읍, 광야의 진영 이름, 베냐민 사람들이 도피한 바위 요새, 이스보셋을 죽인 레갑과 바아나의 아버지 등 여러 지명·인명으로도 쓰인다(여호수아 15:32, 19:7; 사사기 20:45).

entries.definition: The ring was regarded as an indispensable article of a Hebrew’s attire, inasmuch as it contained his signet. It was hence the symbol of authority. (Genesis 41:42; Esther 3:10) Rings were worn not only by men, but by women. (Isaiah 3:21) We may conclude from (Exodus 28:11) that the rings contained a stone engraven with a device or with the owner’s name. The custom appears also to have prevailed among the Jews of the apostolic age. (James 2:2)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인의 필수 복식으로 인장을 담고 있어 권위의 상징으로 쓰였다. 남녀 모두 착용했으며 반지에는 문양이나 소유자의 이름이 새겨진 보석이 박혀 있었다(창세기 41:42; 에스더 3:10; 야고보서 2:2).

entries.definition: (a shout), one of the descendants of Judah. (1 Chronicles 4:20) (B.C. 1300.)
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 후손이다(역대상 4:20).

entries.definition: (spoken), the second son of Gomer. (Genesis 10:3) The name may be identified with the Rhipaean mountains, i.e. the Carpathian range in the northeast of Dacia.
entries.definition_ko: 고멜의 둘째 아들로 카르파티아 산맥 지역과 연관된 것으로 추정된다(창세기 10:3).

entries.definition: (heath), a march-station in the wilderness, (Numbers 33:18,19) Probably northeast of Hazeroth.
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘 광야 진영 중 하나로 하스롯 동북쪽에 위치했던 것으로 추정된다(민수기 33:18,19).

entries.definition: (a ruin), a march-station in the wilderness. (Numbers 33:21,22)
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘 광야 진영 중 하나다(민수기 33:21,22).

entries.definition: In the sense in which we employ the word viz. for a perennial stream of considerable size, a river is a much rarer object in the East than in the West. With the exception of the Jordan and the Litany, the streams of the holy land are either entirely dried up in the summer months converted into hot lanes of glaring stones, or else reduced to very small streamlets, deeply sunk in a narrow bed, and concealed from view by a dense growth of shrubs. The perennial river is called nahar by the Hebrews. With the definite article, “the river,” it signifies invariably the Euphrates. (Genesis 31:21; Exodus 23:31; Numbers 24:6; 2 Samuel 10:16) etc. It is never applied to the fleeting fugitive torrents of Palestine. The term for these is nachal, for which our translators have used promiscuously, and sometimes almost alternately, “valley” “brook” and “river.” No one of these words expresses the thing intended; but the term “brook” is peculiarly unhappy. Many of the wadys of Palestine are deep, abrupt chasms or rents in the solid rock of-the hills, and have a savage, gloomy aspect, far removed from that of an English brook. Unfortunately our language does not contain any single word which has both the meanings of the Hebrew nachal and its Arabic equivalent wady which can be used at once for a dry valley and for the stream which occasionally flows through it.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '나하르'는 요단강과 리타니강을 제외하면 대개 유브라데강을 가리키며, 팔레스타인의 계절적 급류는 '나할'(와디)이라는 별도의 단어로 표현되어 영어 성경에서는 '골짜기', '시내', '강' 등으로 다양하게 번역된다.

entries.definition: • The Nile. (Genesis 15:18) [Nile] • A desert stream on the border of Egypt, still occasionally flowing in the valley called Wadi-l-’Areesh . The centre of the valley is occupied by the bed of this torrent, which only flows after rains, as is usual in the desert valleys. This stream is first mentioned as the point where the southern border of the promised land touched the Mediterranean, which formed its western border. (Numbers 34:3-6) In the latter history we find Solomon’s kingdom extending from the “entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt,” (1 Kings 8:65) and Egypt limited in the same manner where the loss of the eastern provinces is mentioned. (2 Kings 24:7)
entries.definition_ko: 나일강(창세기 15:18)을 가리키거나, 애굽 국경 사막의 계절 하천으로 현재의 와디 엘아리쉬를 가리킨다. 후자는 약속의 땅 남쪽 경계이자 솔로몬 왕국의 남서 경계로 언급된다(민수기 34:3-6; 열왕기상 8:65).

entries.definition: concubine to King Saul, and mother of his two sons Armoni and Mephibosheth. (B.C. 1080.) The tragic story of the love and endurance with which she watched over the bodies of her two sons, who were killed by the Gibeonites, (2 Samuel 21:8-11) has made Rizpah one of the most familiar objects in the whole Bible.
entries.definition_ko: 사울 왕의 첩으로 두 아들 알모니와 므비보셋의 어머니다. 기브온 사람들에게 죽임당한 두 아들의 시신을 지킨 애절한 이야기로 유명하다(사무엘하 21:8-11).

entries.definition: This word occurs but once in the Authorized Version of the Bible, viz. in (1 Samuel 37:10) where it is used in the sense of “raid” or “inroad.” Where a travelled road is meant “path” or “way” is used, since the eastern roads are more like our paths.
entries.definition_ko: 흠정역에서 단 한 번 '습격'이라는 뜻으로 쓰인다(사무엘상 27:10).

entries.definition: Robbery has ever been one of the principal employments of the nomad tribes of the East. From the time of Ishmael to the present day the Bedouin has been a “wild man,” and a robber by trade. (Genesis 16:12) The Mosaic law on the subject of theft is contained in (Exodus 2:2) There seems no reason to suppose that the law underwent any alteration in Solomon’s time. Man-stealing was punishable with death. (Exodus 21:16; 24:7) Invasion of right in land was strictly forbidden. (27:17; Isaiah 5:8; Micah 2:2)
entries.definition_ko: 고대 동방 유목 민족의 주요 생업 중 하나였다. 모세 율법은 도둑질을 엄히 다스렸고 사람을 납치하는 것은 사형에 처해졌으며 토지의 권리 침해도 엄격히 금지되었다(출애굽기 21:16, 22장; 이사야 5:8).

entries.definition: The Hebrew words thus translated denote some species of antelope, probably the Gazella arabica of Syria and Arabia. The gazelle was allowed as food, (12:15,22) etc.; it is mentioned as very fleet of foot, (2 Samuel 2:18; 1 Chronicles 12:8) it was hunted, (Isaiah 13:14; Proverbs 6:5) it was celebrated for its loveliness. (Song of Solomon 2:9,17; 8:14)
entries.definition_ko: 일종의 영양(가젤)을 가리키는 히브리어로 발이 빠르고 사냥의 대상이었으며 아름다움으로도 유명했다(신명기 12:15; 사무엘하 2:18; 아가 2:9).

entries.definition: (fullers) the residence of Barzillai the Gileadite, (2 Samuel 17:27; 19:31) in the highlands east of the Jordan.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 동편 고지대에 위치한 길르앗 사람 바르실래의 거주지다(사무엘하 17:27, 19:31).

entries.definition: (clamor), an Asherite, of the sons of Shamer. (1 Chronicles 7:34) (B.C. about 1490.)
entries.definition_ko: 아셀 지파 세멜의 아들이다(역대상 7:34).

entries.definition: A book in ancient times consisted of a single long strip of paper or parchment, which was usually kept rolled upon a stick, and was unrolled when a person wished to read it. The roll was usually written on one side only, and hence the particular notice of one that was “written within and without.” (Ezekiel 2:10) The writing was arranged in columns.
entries.definition_ko: 고대의 책은 종이나 양피지를 긴 띠 모양으로 이어 막대에 감은 형태였으며 대개 한쪽 면에만 글을 썼다. 에스겔서에서는 '안팎에 쓰인' 특별한 경우가 언급된다(에스겔 2:10).

entries.definition: one of the fourteen sons of Heman. (1 Chronicles 25:4,31) (B.C. about 1014.)
entries.definition_ko: 헤만의 열넷 아들 중 하나다(역대상 25:4,31).

entries.definition: • The first historic mention of Rome in the Bible is in 1 Macc. 1:10, about the year 161 B.C. in the year 65 B.C., when Syria was made a Roman province by Pompey, the Jews were still governed by one of the Asmonaean princes. The next year Pompey himself marched an army into Judea and took Jerusalem. From this time the Jews were practically under the government of Rome. Finally, Antipater’s son Herod the Great was made king by Antony’s interest, B.C. 40, and confirmed in the kingdom by Augustus, B.C. 30. The Jews, however, were all this time tributaries of Rome, and their princes in reality were Roman procurators, On the banishment of Archelaus, A.D. 6, Judea became a mere appendage of the province of Syria, and was governed by a Roman procurator, who resided at Caesarea. Such were the relations of the Jewish people to the Roman government at the time when the New Testament history begins. • Extent of the empire .—Cicero’s description of the Greek states and colonies as a “fringe on the skirts of barbarism” has been well applied to the Roman dominions before the conquests of Pompey and Caesar. The Roman empire was still confined to a narrow strip encircling the Mediterranean Sea. Pompey added Asia Minor and Syria. Caesar added Gaul. The generals of Augustus overran the northwest Portion of Spain and the country between the Alps and the Danube. The boundaries of the empire were now the Atlantic on the west, the Euphrates on the east, the deserts of Africa, the cataracts of the Nile and the Arabian deserts on the south, the British Channel, the Rhine, the Danube and the Black Sea on the north. The only subsequent conquests of importance were those of Britain by Claudius and of Dacia by Trajan. The only independent powers of importance were the Parthians on the east and the Germans on the north. The population of the empire in the time of Augustus has been calculated at 85,000,000. • The provinces .—The usual fate of a country conquered by Rome was to be come a subject province, governed directly from Rome by officers sent out for that purpose. Sometimes, however, petty sovereigns were left in possession of a nominal independence on the borders or within the natural limits of the province. Augustus divided the provinces into two classes— (1) Imperial; (2) Senatorial; retaining in his own hands, for obvious reasons, those provinces where the presence of a large military force was necessary, and committing the peaceful and unarmed provinces to the senate. The New Testament writers invariably designate the governors of senatorial provinces by the correct title anthupatoi, proconsuls. (Acts 13:7; 18:12; 19:38) For the governor of an imperial province, properly styled “legatus Caesaris,” the word hegemon (governor) is used in the New Testament. The provinces were heavily taxed for the benefit of Rome and her citizens. They are said to have been better governed under the empire than under the commonwealth, and those of the emperor better than those of the senate. • The condition of the Roman empire at the time when Christianity appeared has often been dwelt upon as affording obvious illustrations of St. Paul’s expression that the “fullness of time had come.” (Galatians 4:4) The general peace within the limits of the empire the formation of military roads, the suppression of piracy, the march of the legions, the voyages of the corn fleets, the general in crease of traffic, the spread of the Latin language in the West as Greek had already spread in the East, the external unity of the empire, offered facilities hitherto unknown for the spread of a world-wide religion. The tendency, too, of despotism like that of the Roman empire to reduce all its subjects to a dead level was a powerful instrument in breaking down the pride of privileged races and national religious, and familiarizing men with the truth that “God had made of one blood all nations on the face of the earth.” (Acts 17:24,26) Put still more striking than this outward preparation for the diffusion of the gospel was the appearance of a deep and wide-spread corruption, which seemed to defy any human remedy.
entries.definition_ko:
• 성경에서 로마가 역사적으로 처음 언급된 것은 주전 161년경 마카베오상 1:10에서다. 주전 65년 폼페이우스가 수리아를 로마의 속주로 삼았을 때에도 유대인은 여전히 하스몬 왕가의 한 사람이 다스리고 있었다. 이듬해 폼페이우스가 몸소 군대를 이끌고 유대로 들어와 예루살렘을 취했다. 이때부터 유대인은 사실상 로마의 통치 아래 있었다. 마침내 안티파터의 아들 헤롯 대왕이 안토니우스의 주선으로 왕이 되었고(주전 40년) 아구스도에게 그 왕위를 확인받았다(주전 30년). 그러나 유대인은 이 기간 내내 로마에 조공을 바쳤고 그 통치자들은 실제로는 로마의 총독이었다. 주후 6년 아켈라오가 유배되자 유대는 수리아 속주의 부속지에 지나지 않게 되어, 가이사랴에 거하는 로마 총독이 다스렸다. 신약의 역사가 시작될 때 유대 백성과 로마 정부의 관계는 이러했다.

• 제국의 판도 — 키케로가 헬라의 여러 도시국가와 식민지를 '야만의 옷자락에 두른 가장자리 장식'이라 한 말은 폼페이우스와 카이사르의 정복 이전 로마의 영토에 잘 들어맞는다. 그때까지 로마 제국은 지중해를 두른 좁은 띠에 국한되어 있었다. 폼페이우스가 소아시아와 수리아를 더했고 카이사르가 갈리아를 더했다. 아구스도의 장군들은 서바나 서북부와 알프스와 도나우 사이의 지역을 휩쓸었다. 이제 제국의 경계는 서로 대서양, 동으로 유브라데, 남으로 아프리카의 사막과 나일의 폭포와 아라비아 사막, 북으로 영국 해협과 라인과 도나우와 흑해였다. 그 뒤로 중요한 정복은 클라우디우스의 브리타니아 정복과 트라야누스의 다키아 정복뿐이었다. 중요한 독립 세력은 동쪽의 파르티아와 북쪽의 게르만뿐이었다. 아구스도 때 제국의 인구는 팔천오백만으로 헤아려진다.

• 속주 — 로마에 정복된 나라의 통상적 운명은 속주가 되어 그 목적으로 파견된 관리를 통해 로마에서 직접 통치받는 것이었다. 그러나 때로는 속주의 변두리나 그 자연적 경계 안에 작은 군주들을 남겨 두어 명목상의 독립을 누리게 하기도 했다. 아구스도는 속주를 두 부류로 나누어 (1) 황제 속주와 (2) 원로원 속주로 삼았으니, 뚜렷한 이유로 큰 군대가 있어야 하는 속주는 자기 손에 두고 평온하여 무장이 필요 없는 속주는 원로원에 맡겼다. 신약 기자들은 원로원 속주의 총독을 언제나 '안뒤파토스', 곧 총독의 정확한 칭호로 표기한다(사도행전 13:7; 18:12; 19:38). 황제 속주의 통치자는 본래 '레가투스 카이사리스'라 불리는데, 신약에서는 '헤게몬'(총독)이라는 말이 쓰인다. 속주는 로마와 그 시민의 이익을 위해 무거운 세금을 물었다. 공화정 때보다 제정 아래서 더 잘 다스려졌고, 원로원 속주보다 황제 속주가 더 잘 다스려졌다고 한다.

• 그리스도교가 나타났을 때 로마 제국의 형편은 '때가 차매'라는 바울의 말을 뚜렷이 예증하는 것으로 자주 이야기되어 왔다(갈라디아서 4:4). 제국의 경계 안에 두루 퍼진 평화, 군용 도로의 건설, 해적의 소탕, 군단의 행군, 곡물 선단의 항해, 왕래의 전반적 증가, 동방에 이미 헬라어가 퍼진 것처럼 서방에 라틴어가 퍼진 일, 제국의 외적 통일은 세계적 종교가 퍼지는 데 이전에 없던 편의를 제공했다. 또한 로마 제국 같은 전제 정치가 그 모든 신민을 한 수준으로 낮추려는 경향은, 특권을 지닌 민족의 교만과 민족 종교를 허무는 강력한 도구가 되었고, '하나님이 인류의 모든 족속을 한 혈통으로 만드사'라는 진리에 사람들을 익숙하게 했다(사도행전 17:24,26). 그러나 복음의 확산을 위한 이 외적 준비보다 더 두드러진 것은, 사람의 어떤 처방으로도 고칠 수 없어 보이는 깊고 널리 퍼진 부패가 나타난 일이었다.

entries.definition: • The date of this epistle is fixed at the time of the visit recorded in Acts 20:3during the winter and spring following the apostle’s long residence at Ephesus A.D. 58. On this visit he remained in Greece three months. • The place of writing was Corinth. • The occasion which prompted it, and the circumstances attending its writing, were as follows:—St. Paul had long purposed visiting Rome, and still retained this purpose, wishing also to extend his journey to Spain. Etom. 1:9-13; 15:22-29. For the time, however, he was prevented from carrying out his design, as he was bound for Jerusalem with the alms of the Gentile Christians, and meanwhile he addressed this letter to the Romans, to supply the lack of his personal teaching. Phoebe, a deaconess of the neighboring church of Cenchreae, was on the point of starting for Rome, ch. (Romans 16:1,2) and probably conveyed the letter. The body of the epistle was written at the apostle’s dictation by Tertius, ch. (Romans 16:22) but perhaps we may infer, from the abruptness of the final doxology, that it was added by the apostle himself. • The origin of the Roman church is involved in obscurity. If it had been founded by St. Peter according to a later tradition, the absence of any allusion to him both in this epistle and in the letters written by St. Paul from Rome would admit of no explanation. It is equally clear that no other apostle was like founder. The statement in the Clementines—that the first tidings of the gospel reached Rome during the lifetime of our Lord is evidently a fiction for the purposes of the romance. On the other hand, it is clear that the foundation of this church dates very far back. It may be that some of these Romans, “both Jews and proselytes,” present. On the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:10) carried back the earliest tidings of the new doctrine; or the gospel may have first reached the imperial city through those who were scattered abroad to escape the persecution which followed on the death of Stephen. (Acts 8:4; 11:10) At first we may suppose that the gospel had preached there in a confused and imperfect form, scarcely more than a phase of Judaism, as in the case of Apollos at Corinth, (Acts 18:25) or the disciples at Ephesus. (Acts 19:1-3) As time advanced and better-instructed teachers arrived the clouds would gradually clear away, fill at length the presence of the great apostle himself at Rome dispersed the mists of Judaism which still hung about the Roman church. • A question next arises as to the composition of the Roman church at the time when St. Paul wrote. It is more probable that St. Paul addressed a mixed church of Jews and Gentiles, the latter perhaps being the more numerous. These Gentile converts, however, were not for the most part native Romans. Strange as the: paradox appears, nothing is more certain than that the church of Rome was at this time a Greek and not a Latin church. All the literature of the early Roman church was written in the Greek tongue. • The heterogeneous composition of this church explains the general character of the the exclusive predominance of a single form of error, but the coincidence of different and opposing forms. It was: therefore the business of the Christian teacher to reconcile the opposing difficulties and to hold out a meeting-point in the gospel. This is exactly what St. Paul does in the Epistle to the Romans. • In describing the purport of this epistle we may start from St. Paul’s own words, which, standing at the beginning of the doctrinal portion, may be taken as giving a summary of the contents. ch. (Romans 1:16,17) Accordingly the epistle has been described as comprising “the religious philosophy of the world’s history “The atonement of Christ is the centre of religious history. The epistle, from its general character, lends itself more readily to an analysis than is often the case with St. Paul’s epistles. While this epistle contains the fullest and most systematic exposition of the apostle’s teaching, it is at the same time a very striking expression of his character . Nowhere do his earnest and affectionate nature and his tact and delicacy in handling unwelcome topics appear more strongly than when he is dealing with the rejection of his fellow country men the Jews. Internal evidence is so strongly in favor of the genuineness of the Epistle to the Romans that it has never been seriously questioned.
entries.definition_ko:
• 이 서신의 기록 시기는 사도행전 20:3에 기록된 방문 때, 곧 바울이 에베소에 오래 머문 다음 해 겨울과 봄으로 잡히니 주후 58년이다. 이 방문 때 그는 헬라에 석 달을 머물렀다.

• 기록한 곳은 고린도였다.

• 기록의 계기와 정황은 이러하다. 바울은 오래전부터 로마를 방문하려 했고 그 뜻을 여전히 품고 있었으며 그 여정을 서바나까지 넓히기를 바랐다(로마서 1:9-13; 15:22-29). 그러나 당시에는 이방인 그리스도인의 구제금을 가지고 예루살렘으로 가야 했으므로 그 계획을 이룰 수 없었고, 그동안 자기가 직접 가르치지 못하는 부족함을 채우려고 이 편지를 로마인들에게 보냈다. 이웃한 겐그레아 교회의 여집사 뵈뵈가 마침 로마로 떠나려던 참이었으므로(로마서 16:1,2) 아마 그가 편지를 전했을 것이다. 서신의 본문은 사도가 부르는 대로 더디오가 받아썼으나(로마서 16:22), 마지막 송영이 갑작스레 붙은 것으로 보아 그 부분은 사도 자신이 덧붙였다고 짐작할 수 있다.

• 로마 교회의 기원은 불분명하다. 후대의 전승대로 베드로가 세운 것이라면, 이 서신에서나 바울이 로마에서 쓴 편지들에서나 그에 대한 언급이 전혀 없다는 사실은 설명할 길이 없다. 다른 어떤 사도도 그 설립자가 아니었음 또한 분명하다. 주님이 살아 계실 때 복음의 첫 소식이 로마에 이르렀다는 클레멘스 위서의 진술은 명백히 그 이야기를 위한 허구다. 반면 이 교회의 설립이 매우 이른 시기로 거슬러 올라감은 분명하다. 오순절 날 함께 있던 '유대인과 유대교에 들어온 사람들' 가운데 로마 사람 몇이(사도행전 2:10) 새 교훈의 최초 소식을 가지고 돌아갔을 수도 있고, 스데반의 죽음에 뒤이은 박해를 피해 흩어진 이들을 통해 복음이 처음 제국의 수도에 이르렀을 수도 있다(사도행전 8:4; 11:19). 처음에는 복음이 거기서 혼란스럽고 불완전한 형태로, 고린도의 아볼로(사도행전 18:25)나 에베소의 제자들(사도행전 19:1-3)의 경우처럼 유대교의 한 국면에 지나지 않게 전해졌으리라 짐작할 수 있다. 시간이 흐르고 더 잘 배운 교사들이 이르면서 구름이 차츰 걷혔고, 마침내 위대한 사도 자신이 로마에 있게 되자 로마 교회에 아직 드리워 있던 유대주의의 안개가 흩어졌다.

• 다음으로 바울이 편지를 쓸 당시 로마 교회의 구성에 대한 물음이 일어난다. 바울은 유대인과 이방인이 섞인 교회에 편지했고 아마 이방인이 더 많았으리라고 보는 편이 개연성이 높다. 그러나 이 이방인 개종자들은 대부분 로마 태생이 아니었다. 역설처럼 보이지만, 이 무렵 로마 교회가 라틴 교회가 아니라 헬라 교회였다는 것보다 더 확실한 사실은 없다. 초기 로마 교회의 문헌은 모두 헬라어로 쓰였다.

• 이 교회의 이질적인 구성은 이 서신의 전반적 성격을 설명해 준다. 한 가지 오류만이 홀로 지배한 것이 아니라 서로 다르고 맞서는 여러 형태의 오류가 함께 있었다. 그러므로 그리스도의 교사가 할 일은 맞서는 난점들을 화해시키고 복음 안에서 만나는 자리를 내미는 것이었다. 바로 이것이 바울이 로마서에서 하는 일이다.

• 이 서신의 취지를 말하자면 바울 자신의 말에서 출발할 수 있으니, 교리 부분의 첫머리에 놓인 그 말은 내용의 요약으로 볼 수 있다(로마서 1:16,17). 그리하여 이 서신은 '세계 역사의 종교 철학'을 담았다고 일컬어져 왔다. 그리스도의 속죄가 종교 역사의 중심이다. 이 서신은 그 전반적 성격 때문에 바울의 다른 서신들보다 분석하기가 한결 쉽다.

이 서신은 사도의 가르침을 가장 충실하고 체계적으로 펼쳐 놓은 동시에, 그의 인격을 매우 인상 깊게 드러낸다. 동족 유대인의 버림받음을 다룰 때만큼 그의 진지하고 애정 어린 성품과, 달갑지 않은 주제를 다루는 기지와 섬세함이 강하게 드러나는 곳은 없다. 로마서의 진정성에 대한 내적 증거가 매우 강력하여 이는 한 번도 진지하게 의심된 적이 없다.

entries.definition: the famous capital of the ancient world, is situated on the Tiber at a distance of about 15 miles from its mouth. The “seven hills,” (Revelation 17:9) which formed the nucleus of the ancient city stand on the left bank. On the opposite side of the river rises the far higher side of the Janiculum. Here from very early times was a fortress with a suburb beneath it extending to the river. Modern Rome lies to the north of the ancient city, covering with its principal portion the plain to the north of the seven hills, once known as the Campus Martius, and on the opposite bank extending over the low ground beneath the Vatican to the north of the ancient Janiculum. Rome is not mentioned in the Bible except in the books of Maccabees and in three books of the New Testament, viz., the Acts, the Epistle to the Romans and the Second Epistle to Timothy. • Jewish inhabitants. the conquests of Pompey seem to have given rise to the first settlement of Jews at Rome. The Jewish king Aristobulus and his son formed part of Pompey’s triumph, and many Jewish captives and immigrants were brought to Rome at that time. A special district was assigned to them, not on the site of the modern Ghetto, between the Capitol and the island of the Tiber, but across the Tiber. Many of these Jews were made freedmen. Julius Caesar showed them some kindness; they were favored also by Augustus, and by Tiberius during the latter part of his reign. It is chiefly in connection with St. Paul’s history that Rome comes before us in the Bible. In illustration of that history it may be useful to give some account of Rome in the time of Nero, the “Caesar” to whom St. Paul appealed, and in whose reign he suffered martyrdom. • The city in Paul’s time.—The city at that time must be imagined as a large and irregular mass of buildings unprotected by an outer wall. It had long outgrown the old Servian wall; but the limits of the suburbs cannot be exactly defined. Neither the nature of the buildings nor the configuration of the ground was such as to give a striking appearance to the city viewed from without. “Ancient Rome had neither cupola nor camyanile,” and the hills, never lofty or imposing, would present, when covered with the buildings and streets of a huge city, a confused appearance like the hills of modern London, to which they have sometimes been compared. The visit of St. Paul lies between two famous epochs in the history of the city, viz, its restoration by Augustus and its restoration by Nero. The boast of Augustus is well known, “that he found the city of brick, and left it of marble.” Some parts of the city, especially the Forum and Campus Martius, must have presented a magnificent appearance, of which Niebur’s “Lectures on Roman History,” ii. 177, will give a general idea; but many of the principal buildings which attract the attention of modern travellers in ancient Rome were not yet built. The streets were generally narrow and winding, flanked by densely crowded lodging-houses (insulae) of enormous height. Augustus found it necessary to limit their height to 70 feet. St, Paul’s first visit to Rome took place before the Neronian conflagration but even after the restoration of the city which followed upon that event, many of the old evils continued. The population of the city has been variously estimated. Probably Gibbon’s estimate of 1,200,000 is nearest to the truth. One half of the population consisted, in all probability, of slaves. The larger part of the remainder consisted of pauper citizens supported in idleness by the miserable system of public gratuities. There appears to have been no middle class, and no free industrial population. Side by side with the wretched classes just mentioned was the comparatively small body of the wealthy nobility, of whose luxury and profligacy we learn so much from the heathen writers of the time, Such was the population which St. Paul would find at Rome at the time of his visit. We learn from the Acts of the Apostles that he was detained at Rome for “two whole years,” “dwelling in his own hired house with a soldier that kept him,” (Acts 28:16; 30) to whom apparently, according to Roman custom, he was hound with a chain. (Acts 28:20; Ephesians 6:20; Philemon 1:13) Here he preached to all that came to him, no man forbidding him. (Acts 28:30,31) It is generally believed that on his “appeal to Caesar” he was acquitted, and after some time spent in freedom, was a second time imprisoned at Rome. Five of his epistles, viz., those to the Colossians, Ephesians, Philippians, that to Philemon, and the Second Epistle to Timothy, were in all probability written from Rome, the latter shortly before his death (2 Timothy 4:6) the others during his first imprisonment. It is universally believed that he suffered martyrdom at Rome. • The localities in and about Rome especially connected with the life of Paul are— (1) The Appian Way, by which he approached Rome. (Acts 28:15) [Appii Forum FORUM] (2) “The palace,” Or “Caesar’s court” (praetorium,) (Philemon 1:13) This may mean either the great camp of the Praetorian guards which Tiberius established outside the walls on the northeast of the city, or, as seems more probable, a barrack attached to the imperial residence on the Palatine. There is no sufficient proof that the word “praetorium” was ever used to designate the emperors palace, though it is used for the official residence of a Roman governor. (John 18:28; Acts 23:35) the mention of “Caesar’s household,” (Philemon 4:22) confirms the notion that St. Paul’s residence was in the immediate neighborhood of the emperor’s house on the Palatine. (3) The connection of other localities at home with St. Paul’s name rests only on traditions of more or less probability. We may mention especially— (4) The Mamertine prison, of Tullianum, built by Ancus Martius near the Forum. It still exists beneath the church of St. Giuseppe dei Falegnami. It is said that St. Peter and St. Paul were fellow prisoners here for nine months. This is not the place to discuss the question whether St. Peter was ever at Rome. It may be sufficient to state that though there is no evidence of such a visit in the New Testament, unless Babylon in (1 Peter 5:13) is a mystical name for Rome yet early testimony and the universal belief of the early Church seems sufficient to establish the fact of his having suffered martyrdom there. [Peter] The story, however, of the imprisonment in the Mamertine prison seems inconsistent with (2 Timothy 4:11) (5) The chapel on the Ostian road which marks the spot where the two apostles are said to, have separated on their way to martyrdom. (6)The supposed scene of St. Paul’s martyrdom, viz., the church of St. Paolo alle tre fontane on the Ostian road. To these may be added— (7) The supposed scene of St. Peter’s martyrdom, viz., the church of St. Pietro in Montorio, on the Janiculum. (8) The chapel Domine que Vadis, on the Aypian road, the scene of the beautiful legend of our Lord’s appearance to St. Peter as he was escaping from martyrdom. (9) The places where the bodies of the two apostles, after having been deposited first in the catacombs, are supposed to have been finally buried—that of St. Paul by the Ostian road, that of St. Peter beneath the dome of the famous Basilica which bears his name. We may add, as sites unquestionably connected with the Roman Christians of the apostolic age— (10) The gardens of Nero in the Vatican. Not far from the spot where St. Peter’s now stands. Here Christians, wrapped in the skins of beasts, were torn to pieces by dogs, or, clothed in inflammable robes, were burnt to serve as torches during the midnight games. Others were crucified. (11) The Catacombs. These subterranean galleries, commonly from 8 to 10 feet in height and from 4 to 6 in width, and extending for miles, especially in the neighborhood of the old Appian and Nomentan Ways, were unquestionably used as places of refuge, of worship and of burial by the early Christians. The earliest dated inscription in the catacombs is A.D. 71. Nothing is known of the first founder of the Christian Church at Rome. Christianity may, perhaps, have been introduced into the city not long after the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost by the “strangers of Rome, who were then at Jerusalem, (Acts 2:10) It is clear that there were many Christians at Rome before St. Paul visited the city. (Romans 1:8,13,15; 15:20) The names of twenty-four Christians at Rome are given in the salutations at the end of the Epistle to the Romans. Linus, who is mentioned (2 Timothy 4:21) and Clement, Phil 4:3Are supposed to have succeeded St. Peter as bishops of Rome.
entries.definition_ko:
옛 세계의 이름난 수도로 티베르 강가, 하구에서 약 15마일 되는 곳에 있다. 옛 성읍의 중심을 이룬 '일곱 산'(요한계시록 17:9)은 왼쪽 기슭에 있고, 강 건너편에는 훨씬 높은 야니쿨룸 비탈이 솟아 아주 이른 시대부터 요새와 그 아래 강까지 뻗은 변두리 마을이 있었다. 오늘날의 로마는 옛 성읍 북쪽에 있어 주요 부분이 일곱 산 북쪽 평지 곧 옛 캄푸스 마르티우스를 덮고, 건너편으로는 옛 야니쿨룸 북쪽 바티칸 아래 낮은 땅까지 뻗는다. 성경에서 로마는 마카베오서와 신약 세 책 곧 사도행전과 로마서와 디모데후서에만 언급된다.
유대인 주민. 로마에 유대인이 처음 정착한 것은 폼페이우스의 정복에서 비롯된 듯하다. 유대 왕 아리스토불루스와 그 아들이 폼페이우스의 개선 행렬에 끼었고 그때 많은 유대인 포로와 이주민이 로마로 왔다. 그들에게 따로 구역이 주어졌는데, 카피톨과 티베르 섬 사이의 오늘날 게토 자리가 아니라 티베르 건너편이었다. 이 유대인 가운데 다수가 자유민이 되었다. 율리우스 카이사르가 그들에게 얼마쯤 호의를 보였고 아구스도도, 또 디베료도 치세 후반에 그들을 우대하였다. 로마가 성경에 나오는 것은 주로 바울의 역사와 관련해서이므로, 바울이 상소한 '가이사'요 그 치세에 바울이 순교한 네로 때의 로마를 살펴보는 것이 그 역사를 밝히는 데 도움이 된다.
바울 때의 성읍. 그때 성읍은 바깥 성벽으로 보호되지 않은 크고 고르지 않은 건물 덩어리로 그려야 한다. 옛 세르비우스 성벽을 벗어난 지 오래였으나 변두리의 경계를 정확히 그을 수는 없다. 건물의 성격도 지형도 밖에서 보아 인상적인 모습을 주지는 못하였으니, '옛 로마에는 둥근 지붕도 종탑도 없었고' 결코 높거나 웅장하지 않은 언덕들은 거대한 성읍의 건물과 거리로 덮여 오늘날 런던의 언덕처럼 어수선하게 보였을 것이다. 바울의 방문은 아구스도의 재건과 네로의 재건이라는 두 유명한 시기 사이에 놓인다. '벽돌의 성읍을 발견하여 대리석의 성읍으로 남겼다'는 아구스도의 자랑은 잘 알려져 있다. 포룸과 캄푸스 마르티우스 같은 몇몇 곳은 웅장하였겠으나, 오늘날 옛 로마를 찾는 이들의 눈길을 끄는 주요 건물 다수는 아직 지어지지 않았다. 거리는 대개 좁고 굽었으며 엄청나게 높은 셋집(인술라)이 빽빽이 늘어섰으므로 아구스도가 그 높이를 70피트로 제한하여야 하였다. 바울의 첫 방문은 네로의 대화재 이전이었으나 그 뒤의 재건 뒤에도 옛 폐단이 많이 남았다. 인구는 여러 가지로 헤아려졌는데 기번의 백이십만이 아마도 진실에 가장 가까울 것이다. 그 절반은 거의 틀림없이 노예였고, 나머지의 큰 몫은 공공 배급이라는 비참한 제도로 놀며 부양되는 빈민 시민이었다. 중간 계층도, 자유로운 산업 인구도 없었던 것으로 보인다. 이 가련한 무리와 나란히, 당대 이방 저술가들에게서 그 사치와 방탕을 많이 듣게 되는 비교적 적은 수의 부유한 귀족이 있었다. 바울이 로마에서 만난 것이 이런 인구였다. 사도행전에서 우리는 그가 로마에서 '온 이태를' 갇혀 '자기 셋집에 지키는 군사 한 사람과 함께' 지냈고(사도행전 28:16,30), 로마의 관례대로 그와 사슬로 매여 있었음을 안다(사도행전 28:20; 에베소서 6:20; 빌레몬서 1:13). 여기서 그는 찾아오는 모든 사람에게 전하되 아무도 금하지 않았다(사도행전 28:30,31). 대체로 '가이사에게 상소'한 그가 무죄로 풀려나 얼마 동안 자유로이 지낸 뒤 로마에서 두 번째로 갇혔다고 여겨진다. 그의 서신 다섯 곧 골로새서, 에베소서, 빌립보서, 빌레몬서, 디모데후서가 거의 틀림없이 로마에서 쓰였으니, 마지막 것은 죽기 직전에(디모데후서 4:6), 나머지는 첫 갇힘 동안에 쓰였다. 그가 로마에서 순교하였다는 데는 이견이 없다.
바울의 생애와 특별히 이어진 로마 안팎의 장소는 이러하다. (1) 그가 로마로 다가간 아피아 가도(사도행전 28:15). (2) '궁' 곧 '가이사의 집'(프라이토리움, 빌립보서 1:13). 이는 디베료가 성 밖 북동쪽에 세운 근위대의 큰 병영을 뜻하거나, 더 그럴듯하게는 팔라티누스의 황제 거처에 딸린 병사를 뜻할 수 있다. '프라이토리움'이 황제의 궁을 가리키는 데 쓰였다는 넉넉한 증거는 없으나 로마 총독의 공관에는 쓰인다(요한복음 18:28; 사도행전 23:35). '가이사의 집 사람들'을 언급한 것은(빌립보서 4:22) 바울의 거처가 팔라티누스의 황제 저택 바로 근처였다는 생각을 뒷받침한다. (3) 그 밖의 장소가 바울의 이름과 이어진 것은 신빙성이 다양한 전승에 기댈 뿐이다. 특히 (4) 앙쿠스 마르티우스가 포룸 가까이 세운 마메르티누스 감옥 곧 툴리아눔이 있으니 지금도 성 주세페 데이 팔레냐미 교회 아래 남아 있는데, 베드로와 바울이 여기서 아홉 달 동안 함께 갇혔다고 한다. 베드로가 로마에 온 적이 있는가를 여기서 논할 것은 아니나, 베드로전서 5:13의 바벨론이 로마의 신비한 이름이 아니라면 신약에는 그런 방문의 증거가 없되 초기의 증언과 초대 교회의 보편적 믿음이 그가 거기서 순교하였다는 사실을 세우기에 넉넉하다고만 말해 둔다. 다만 마메르티누스 감옥에 갇혔다는 이야기는 디모데후서 4:11과 맞지 않아 보인다. (5) 두 사도가 순교하러 가는 길에 갈라섰다고 하는 자리를 표시하는 오스티아 가도의 예배당. (6) 바울의 순교 자리라는 오스티아 가도의 성 파올로 알레 트레 폰타네 교회. 여기에 (7) 베드로의 순교 자리라는 야니쿨룸의 성 피에트로 인 몬토리오 교회, (8) 베드로가 순교를 피하여 달아날 때 주님이 나타나셨다는 아름다운 전설의 자리인 아피아 가도의 도미네 쿠오 바디스 예배당, (9) 두 사도의 유해가 처음에 카타콤에 두어졌다가 마침내 묻혔다는 곳 곧 바울은 오스티아 가도에, 베드로는 그 이름을 지닌 이름난 대성당의 돔 아래를 더할 수 있다. 사도 시대 로마 그리스도인과 틀림없이 이어진 자리로는 (10) 바티칸의 네로의 정원이 있으니, 지금 성 베드로 대성당이 선 자리에서 멀지 않다. 여기서 그리스도인들이 짐승 가죽에 싸여 개에게 찢겼고, 불붙는 옷을 입고 한밤 경기의 횃불 노릇을 하며 탔으며, 또 다른 이들은 십자가에 못 박혔다. (11) 카타콤. 대개 높이 8에서 10피트, 너비 4에서 6피트로 여러 마일 뻗은 이 지하 회랑은, 특히 옛 아피아 가도와 노멘타나 가도 부근에 있어 초기 그리스도인이 피난과 예배와 매장의 자리로 쓴 것이 틀림없다. 카타콤에서 연대가 있는 가장 이른 명문은 주후 71년의 것이다.
로마에 그리스도인 교회를 처음 세운 이에 대해서는 알려진 바가 없다. 오순절 날 성령이 부어진 뒤 오래지 않아, 그때 예루살렘에 있던 '로마로부터 온 나그네'들이(사도행전 2:10) 그리스도교를 이 성읍에 들여왔을 수 있다. 바울이 이 성읍을 찾기 전에 이미 많은 그리스도인이 로마에 있었음은 분명하다(로마서 1:8,13,15; 15:20). 로마서 끝의 문안에 로마의 그리스도인 스물네 사람의 이름이 나온다. 디모데후서 4:21에 언급된 리노와 빌립보서 4:3의 글레멘드가 베드로를 이어 로마의 감독이 되었다고 여겨진다.

entries.definition: [House]
entries.definition_ko: 집(House) 항목을 보라.

entries.definition: The references to “room” in (Matthew 23:6; Mark 12:39; Luke 14:7,8; 20:46) signify the highest place on the highest couch round the dinner or supper table—the “uppermost seat”, as it is more accurately rendered in (Luke 11:43)
entries.definition_ko: 잔치 자리에서 가장 높은 자리를 가리키는 표현이다(마태복음 23:6; 누가복음 14:7,8, 11:43).

entries.definition: occurs twice only, viz. in (Song of Solomon 2:1; Isaiah 35:1) There is much difference of opinion as to what particular flower is here denoted; but it appears to us most probable that the narcissus is intended. Chateaubriand mentions the narcissus as growing in the Plain of Sharon. Roses are greatly prized in the East, more especially for the sake of the rose-water, which is much request. Dr. Hooker observed seven species of wild roses in Syria.
entries.definition_ko: 아가서와 이사야서에 각각 한 번씩 나오며 정확한 꽃의 정체에는 이견이 있으나 수선화일 가능성이 제기된다(아가 2:1; 이사야 35:1).

entries.definition: (Ezekiel 38:2,3; 39:1) probably a proper name, referring to the first of the three great Scythian tribes of which Magog was the head. (head). In the genealogy of (Genesis 46:21) Rosh is reckoned among the sons of Benjamin.
entries.definition_ko: 에스겔서에서 마곡을 우두머리로 한 세 스키타이 부족 중 하나를 가리키는 고유명사로 추정되며(에스겔 38:2,3), 창세기 족보에서는 베냐민의 아들 중 하나로 나온다(창세기 46:21).

entries.definition: Properly “naphtha,” as it is both in the LXX. and the Vulgate, as well as in the Peshito-Syriac. Pliny mentions naphtha as a product of Babylonia, similar in appearance to liquid bitumen, and having a remarkable affinity to fire.
entries.definition_ko: 실제로는 '나프타'를 가리키는 것으로 보이며 칠십인역과 불가타에도 그렇게 나온다. 바벨론에서 산출되는 물질로 불에 잘 타는 성질이 있다.

entries.definition: Concerning the meaning of the Hebrew words translated “rubies” there is much difference of opinion. (Job 28:18) see also Prov 3:15; 8:11; 31:10Some suppose “coral” to be in tended; others “pearl,” supposing that the original word signifies merely “bright in color,” or “color of a reddish tinge.” (The real ruby is a red sapphire, next in value to the diamond. The finest rubies are brought chiefly from Ceylon and Burmah.)
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 원어의 정확한 의미에는 이견이 있으며 산호나 진주를 가리킨다는 견해도 있다. 지혜와 값진 것을 비유하는 데 쓰인다(욥기 28:18; 잠언 3:15, 31:10).

entries.definition: occurs only in (Luke 11:42) The rue here spoken of is doubtless the common Ruta graveolens a shrubby plant about two feet high, of strong medicinal virtues. It is a native of the Mediterranean coasts, and has been found by Hasselquist on Mount Tabor. The Talmud enumerates rue amongst kitchen herbs, and regards it as free of tithe as being a plant not cultivated in gardens. In our Lord’s time however rue was doubtless a garden plant, and therefore tithable.
entries.definition_ko: 강한 약효를 지닌 관목으로 지중해 연안이 원산지이며 예수 시대에는 정원 재배 작물로 십일조 대상이었다(누가복음 11:42).

entries.definition: (red) is mentioned in (Mark 15:21) as a son of Simon the Cyrenian. (Luke 23:26) (A.D. 29.) Again, in (Romans 16:13) the apostle Paul salutes a Rufus whom he designates as “elect in the Lord.” This Rufus was probably identical with the one to whom Mark refers.
entries.definition_ko: 구레네 사람 시몬의 아들(마가복음 15:21), 또는 바울이 로마서에서 '주 안에서 택하심을 입은 자'로 문안한 루포를 가리키며 두 사람이 동일 인물일 가능성이 있다(로마서 16:13).

entries.definition: (having obtained mercy). (Hosea 2:1) The name if name it be, is symbolical, and is addressed to the DAUGHTERS of the people, to denote that they were still the objects of love and tender compassion.
entries.definition_ko: '긍휼히 여김을 받은 자'라는 뜻으로 호세아서에서 백성이 여전히 하나님의 사랑과 긍휼의 대상임을 나타내는 상징적 이름이다(호세아 2:1).

entries.definition: (high), mentioned once only— (2 Kings 23:36) It has been conjectured to be the same place as Arumah. (Judges 9:41) which was apparently near Shechem. It is more probable that it is identical with Dumah. (Joshua 15:52)
entries.definition_ko: 여호야김의 어머니 스비다의 고향으로 세겜 인근 아루마 또는 두마와 동일시하는 견해가 있다(열왕기하 23:36).

entries.definition: (a female friend) a Moabitish woman, the wife, first of Mahlon, second of Boaz, the ancestress of David and Christ, and one of the four women who are named by St. Matthew in the genealogy of Christ. A severe famine in the land of Judah induced Elimelech, a native of Bethlehem—ephratah, to emigrate into the land of Moab, with his wife Naomi, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion. This was probably about the time of Gideon, B.C. 1250. At the end of ten years Naomi now left a widow and childless, having heard that there was plenty again in Judah, resolved to return to Bethlehem, and her daughter-in-law Ruth returned with her. They arrived at Bethlehem just at the beginning of barley harvest, and Ruth, going out to glean, chanced to go into the field of wheat, a wealthy man and a near kinsman of her father-in-law, Elimelech. Upon learning who the stranger was, Boaz treated her with the utmost kindness and respect, and sent her home laden with corn which she had gleaned. Encouraged by this incident, Naomi instructed Ruth to claim at the hand of Boaz that he should perform the part of her husband’s near kinsman, by purchasing the inheritance of Elimelech and taking her to be his wife. With all due solemnity, Boaz took Ruth to be his wife, amidst the blessings and congratulations of their neighbors. Their son, Obed, was ’the father of Jesse, who was the father of David.
entries.definition_ko: 모압 여인으로 처음에는 말론의 아내였다가 이후 보아스의 아내가 되어 다윗과 그리스도의 조상이 되었다. 시어머니 나오미와 함께 베들레헴으로 돌아와 보아스의 밭에서 이삭을 줍다가 그의 은혜를 입었고, 기업 무를 자의 법에 따라 보아스와 결혼해 아들 오벳을 낳았다. 오벳은 이새의 아버지, 이새는 다윗의 아버지다(룻기).

entries.definition: contains the history of Ruth, as narrated in the preceding article. The main object of the writer is evidently to give an account of David’s ancestors; and the book was avowedly composed long after the time of the heroine. See (Ruth 1:1; 4:7,17) Its date and author are quite uncertain. Tradition is in favor of Samuel. It is probable that the books of Judges, Ruth, Samuel and Kings originally formed but one work. The book of Ruth clearly forms part of the books of Samuel, supplying as it does the essential point of David’s genealogy and early family history, and is no less clearly connected with the book of Judges by its opening verse and the epoch to which the whole book relates.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 조상 계보를 설명하려는 목적으로 기록된 것으로 보이며 저자는 불확실하나 전통적으로 사무엘로 여겨진다. 사사기, 룻기, 사무엘서, 열왕기가 원래 한 작품이었을 가능성이 있으며 룻기는 사사 시대를 배경으로 다윗의 족보와 초기 가족사를 보완하는 역할을 한다.

entries.definition: (Heb. cussemeth) occurs in (Exodus 9:32; Isaiah 28:25) in the latter the margin reads “spelt.” In (Ezekiel 4:9) the text has “fitches“ and the margin “rie.” It is probable that by cussemeth “spelt” is intended. Spelt (Triticum spelta) is grown in some parts of the south of Germany; it differs but slightly from our common wheat (T. vulgare).
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '쿠세메트'로 흠정역에서는 '스펠트밀'로도 표기되며 일반 밀과 큰 차이가 없는 곡물이다(출애굽기 9:32; 이사야 28:25).

entries.definition: (why hast thou forsaken me?), part of Christ’s fourth cry on the cross. (Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34) This, with the other words uttered with it, as given in Mark, is Aramaic (Syro-Chaldaic), the common dialect of the people of palestine in Christ’s time and the whole is a translation of the Hebrew (given in Matthew) of the first words of the 22d Psalm.—ED.
entries.definition_ko: '어찌하여 나를 버리셨나이까'라는 뜻으로 십자가 위 예수의 네 번째 외침 중 일부이며 아람어(시로칼대아 방언)로 시편 22편 첫 구절의 히브리어를 옮긴 것이다(마태복음 27:46; 마가복음 15:34).

entries.definition: occurs in (Romans 9:29; James 5:4) but is more familiar through its occurrence in the Sanctus of Te Deum—“Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth.” Sabaoth is the Greek form of the Hebrew word tsebaoth “armies,” and is translated in the Authorized Version of the Old Testament by “Lord of hosts,” “Lord God of hosts.” In the mouth and the mind of an ancient Hebrew, Jehovah-tsebaoth was the leader and commander of the armies of the nation, who “went forth with them” (Psalms 44:9) and led them to certain victory over the worshippers of Baal Chemosh. Molech, Ashtaroth and other false gods.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어 '체바오트'(군대들)의 헬라식 표기로 흠정역에서는 '만군의 여호와'로 번역된다. 이스라엘 군대를 이끄시고 바알과 그모스 등 거짓 신 숭배자들에게 승리를 주시는 하나님을 가리킨다(로마서 9:29; 야고보서 5:4).

entries.definition: (shabbath), “a day of rest,” from shabath “to cease to do to,” “to rest”). The name is applied to divers great festivals, but principally and usually to the seventh day of the week, the strict observance of which is enforced not merely in the general Mosaic code, but in the Decalogue itself. The consecration of the Sabbath was coeval with the creation. The first scriptural notice of it, though it is not mentioned by name, is to be found in (Genesis 2:3) at the close of the record of the six-days creation. There are not wanting indirect evidences of its observance, as the intervals between Noah’s sending forth the birds out of the ark, an act naturally associated with the weekly service, (Genesis 8:7-12) and in the week of a wedding celebration, (Genesis 29:27,28) but when a special occasion arises, in connection with the prohibition against gathering manna on the Sabbath, the institution is mentioned as one already known. (Exodus 16:22-30) And that this (All this is confirmed by the great antiquity of the division of time into weeks, and the naming the days after the sun, moon and planets.) was especially one of the institutions adopted by Moses from the ancient patriarchal usage is implied in the very words of the law “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.” But even if such evidence were wanting, the reason of the institution would be a sufficient proof. It was to be a joyful celebration of God’s completion of his creation. It has indeed been said that Moses gives quite a different reason for the institution of the Sabbath, as a memorial of the deliverance front Egyptian bondage. (5:15) The words added in Deuteronomy are a special motive for the joy with which the Sabbath should be celebrated and for the kindness which extended its blessings to the slave and the beast of burden as well as to the master: “that thy man servant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thought. (5:14) These attempts to limit the ordinance proceed from an entire misconception of its spirit, as if it were a season of stern privation rather than of special privilege. But in truth, the prohibition of work is only subsidiary to the positive idea of joyful rest and recreation in communion with Jehovah, who himself “rested and was refreshed.” (Exodus 31:17) comp. (Exodus 23:12) It is in (Exodus 16:23-29) that we find the first incontrovertible institution of the day, as one given to and to be kept by the children of Israel. Shortly afterward it was re-enacted in the Fourth Commandment. This beneficent character of the Fourth Commandment is very apparent in the version of it which we find in Deuteronomy. (5:12-15) The law and the Sabbath are placed upon the same ground, and to give rights to classes that would otherwise have been without such—to the bondman and bondmaid may, to the beast of the field-is viewed here as their main end. “The stranger,” too is comprehended in the benefit. But the original proclamation of it in Exodus places it on a ground which, closely connected no doubt with these others is yet higher and more comprehensive. The divine method of working and rest is there propose to work and to rest. Time then to man as the model after which presented a perfect whole it is most important to remember that the Fourth Commandment is not limited to a mere enactment respecting one day, but prescribes the due distribution of a week, and enforces the six days’ work as much as the seventh day’s rest. This higher ground of observance was felt to invest the Sabbath with a theological character, and rendered if the great witness for faith in a personal and creating God. It was to be a sacred pause in the ordinary labor which man earns his bread the curse the fall was to be suspended for one and, having spent that day in joyful remembrance of God’s mercies, man had a fresh start in his course of labor. A great snare, too, has always been hidden in the word work, as if the commandment forbade occupation and imposed idleness. The terms in the commandment show plainly enough the sort of work which is contemplated-servile work and business. The Pentateuch presents us with but three applications of the general principle— (Exodus 16:29; 35:3; Numbers 15:32-36) The reference of Isaiah to the Sabbath gives us no details. The references in Jeremiah and Nehemiah show that carrying goods for sale, and buying such, were equally profanations of the day. A consideration of the spirit of the law and of Christ’s comments on it will show that it is work for worldly gain that was to be suspended; and hence the restrictive clause is prefaced with the restrictive command. “Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work;” for so only could the sabbatic rest be fairly earned. Hence, too, the stress constantly laid on permitting the servant and beast of burden to share the rest which selfishness would grudge to them. Thus the spirit of the Sabbath was joy, refreshment and mercy, arising from remembrance of God’s goodness as Creator and as the Deliverer from bondage. The Sabbath was a perpetual sign and covenant, and the holiness of the day is collected with the holiness of the people; “that ye may know that I am Jehovah that doth sanctify you.” (Exodus 31:12-17; Ezekiel 20:12) Joy was the key-note Of their service. Nehemiah commanded the people, on a day holy to Jehovah “Mourn not, nor weep: eat the fat, and drink: the sweet, and send portions to them for whom nothing is prepared.” (Nehemiah 8:9-13) The Sabbath is named as a day of special worship in the sanctuary. (Leviticus 19:30; 26:2) It was proclaimed as a holy convocation. (Leviticus 23:3) In later times the worship of the sanctuary was enlivened by sacred music. (Psalms 68:25-27; 150:1)... etc. On this day the people were accustomed to consult their prophets, (2 Kings 4:23) and to give to their children that instruction in the truths recalled to memory by the day which is so repeatedly enjoined as the duty of parents; it was “the Sabbath of Jehovah” not only in the sanctuary, but “in all their dwellings.” (Leviticus 23:3) When we come to the New Testament we find the most marked stress laid on the Sabbath. In whatever ways the Jew might err respecting it, he had altogether ceased to neglect it. On the contrary wherever he went its observance became the most visible badge of his nationality. Our Lord’s mode of observing the Sabbath was one of the main features of his life, which his Pharisaic adversaries meet eagerly watched and criticized. They had invented many prohibitions respecting the Sabbath of which we find nothing in the original institution. Some of these prohibitions were fantastic and arbitrary, in the number of those “heavy burdens and grievous to be borne” while the latter expounders of the law “laid on men’s shoulders.” Comp. (Matthew 12:1-13; John 5:10) That this perversion of the Sabbath had become very general in our Saviour’s time is apparent both from the recorded objections to acts of his on that day and from his marked conduct on occasions to which those objections were sure to be urged. (Matthew 12:1-16; Mark 3:2; Luke 6:1-5; 13:10-17; John 6:2-18; 7:23; 9:1-34) Christ’s words do not remit the duty of keeping the Sabbath, but only deliver it from the false methods of keeping which prevented it from bestowing upon men the spiritual blessings it was ordained to confer.
entries.definition_ko:
(히브리어 '샵바트'는 '그치다', '쉬다'를 뜻하는 '샤바트'에서 온 '쉬는 날'이라는 뜻) 이 이름은 여러 큰 절기에 쓰이나 주로, 또 보통은 한 주의 일곱째 날을 가리키며, 이를 엄히 지키라는 명령은 모세 율법 전반뿐 아니라 십계명 자체에 담겨 있다.
안식일의 거룩한 구별은 창조와 함께 시작되었다. 이름이 나오지는 않으나 성경의 첫 언급은 엿새 창조 기록의 끝인 창세기 2:3에 있다. 그것이 지켜졌음을 간접으로 보여 주는 것이 없지 않으니, 노아가 방주에서 새를 내보낸 간격(창세기 8:7-12)과 혼인 잔치의 한 주(창세기 29:27,28)가 그러하다. 그러다가 안식일에 만나를 거두지 말라는 금령과 관련하여 특별한 계기가 생겼을 때, 이 제도는 이미 알려진 것으로 언급된다(출애굽기 16:22-30). 이것이 모세가 옛 족장의 관습에서 받아들인 제도 가운데 하나임은 '안식일을 기억하여 거룩하게 지키라'는 율법의 말 자체가 뜻한다. 그런 증거가 없더라도 제정의 이유만으로 넉넉한 증명이 될 것이니, 그것은 하나님이 창조를 마치심을 기뻐 기념하는 날이어야 하였다. 모세가 애굽 종살이에서 건짐받은 일을 기념하는 것이라는 다른 이유를 든다고들 말한다(신명기 5:15). 그러나 신명기에 더해진 말은 안식일을 기뻐 지켜야 할 특별한 동기요, 그 복을 종과 짐승에게까지 미치게 하는 친절의 근거이니 '네 남종과 네 여종에게 너같이 안식하게 할지니라' 하였다. 이 규례를 제약으로만 보려는 시도는 그 정신을 온전히 잘못 안 데서 나오니, 마치 안식일이 특별한 특권의 때가 아니라 모진 결핍의 때인 것처럼 여기는 것이다. 실은 일을 금하는 것은 '쉬시며 평안하셨던'(출애굽기 31:17) 여호와와 사귀며 기쁘게 쉬고 회복한다는 적극적 관념에 딸린 것일 뿐이다.
이 날이 이스라엘 자손에게 주어져 지켜야 할 날로 처음 뚜렷이 제정된 것은 출애굽기 16:23-29이며, 곧이어 넷째 계명에서 다시 규정되었다. 넷째 계명의 이 은혜로운 성격은 신명기의 표현에 매우 뚜렷하니(신명기 5:12-15), 율법과 안식일이 같은 바탕에 놓이고, 그렇지 않으면 아무 권리도 없을 계층 곧 남종과 여종과 나아가 들의 짐승에게까지 권리를 주는 것이 여기서 그 주된 목적으로 여겨지며 '나그네'도 그 유익에 든다. 그러나 출애굽기의 본래 선포는 이보다 더 높고 포괄적인 근거에 둔다. 하나님께서 일하시고 쉬신 방식이 사람이 일하고 쉬는 본으로 제시된다. 넷째 계명이 한 날에 관한 규정에 그치지 않고 한 주의 마땅한 배분을 정하여, 일곱째 날의 쉼 못지않게 엿새의 일도 명한다는 점을 기억하는 것이 매우 중요하다. 이 더 높은 근거가 안식일에 신학적 성격을 입혀, 인격적이시며 창조하시는 하나님을 믿는 믿음의 큰 증거가 되게 하였다. 그것은 사람이 타락의 저주로 땀 흘려 양식을 얻는 여느 수고 가운데 놓인 거룩한 멈춤이어서 하루 동안 저주가 유예되었고, 그날을 하나님의 긍휼을 기뻐 기억하며 보낸 사람은 새로 수고의 길에 나섰다. '일'이라는 말에 늘 큰 올무가 숨어 있었으니, 마치 계명이 모든 활동을 금하고 게으름을 지우는 것처럼 여기는 것이다. 계명의 표현은 여기서 뜻하는 일이 어떤 것인지 곧 종의 일과 생업임을 넉넉히 보여 준다. 오경은 이 일반 원리의 적용을 셋만 보여 준다(출애굽기 16:29; 35:3; 민수기 15:32-36). 이사야의 언급은 자세하지 않으나, 예레미야와 느헤미야의 언급은 팔 물건을 나르는 것과 그것을 사는 것이 똑같이 이 날을 더럽히는 일이었음을 보여 준다. 율법의 정신과 그리스도의 논평을 헤아리면 멈추어야 할 것은 세상의 이익을 위한 일이었음이 드러나며, 그래서 제한하는 조항 앞에 '엿새 동안은 힘써 네 모든 일을 행할 것이나'라는 명령이 놓이니 그래야만 안식의 쉼을 정당히 얻기 때문이다. 그러므로 이기심이라면 아까워할 그 쉼을 종과 짐승도 함께 누리게 하라는 데 늘 힘이 실린다. 이처럼 안식일의 정신은 창조주요 종살이에서 건지신 이이신 하나님의 선하심을 기억하는 데서 나오는 기쁨과 회복과 긍휼이었다. 안식일은 영원한 표징이요 언약이며, 이 날의 거룩함은 백성의 거룩함과 이어져 '나는 너희를 거룩하게 하는 여호와인 줄 너희가 알게 함이라' 하셨다(출애굽기 31:12-17; 에스겔 20:12). 기쁨이 그 섬김의 기조였으니, 느헤미야는 여호와께 거룩한 날에 백성에게 명하기를 '슬퍼하지 말며 울지 말라 살진 것을 먹고 단 것을 마시되 준비하지 못한 자에게는 나누어 주라' 하였다(느헤미야 8:9-12). 안식일은 성소에서 특별히 예배하는 날로 이름이 나오며(레위기 19:30; 26:2) 거룩한 성회로 선포되었다(레위기 23:3). 후대에는 성소의 예배가 거룩한 음악으로 활기를 얻었다(시편 68:25-27; 150편 등). 이 날에 백성은 선지자에게 묻는 것이 관례였고(열왕기하 4:23), 부모의 본분으로 거듭 명령된 대로 이 날이 일깨우는 진리를 자녀에게 가르쳤다. 그것은 성소에서만이 아니라 '너희 거하는 모든 곳에서' '여호와의 안식일'이었다(레위기 23:3).
신약에 이르면 안식일이 더없이 뚜렷하게 강조된다. 유대인이 그것에 관하여 어떤 그릇된 길로 갔든 소홀히 여기는 일은 아주 그쳤고, 도리어 어디를 가든 그 준수가 민족성의 가장 눈에 띄는 표가 되었다. 주님께서 안식일을 지키신 방식은 바리새인 대적들이 가장 열심히 지켜보고 비판한 그 생애의 주요 특징 가운데 하나였다. 그들은 본래의 제정에는 전혀 없는 금령을 많이 만들어 내었으니, 그 가운데 어떤 것은 기괴하고 제멋대로여서 후대의 율법 해설자들이 '사람의 어깨에 지운' '무겁고 지기 어려운 짐'에 들었다(마태복음 12:1-13; 요한복음 5:10 비교). 안식일을 이렇게 비뚤어지게 만든 일이 구주 때에 매우 널리 퍼져 있었음은, 그날에 하신 일에 제기된 반대와 그런 반대가 나올 것이 뻔한 자리에서 보이신 그의 뚜렷한 행동에서 다 드러난다(마태복음 12:1-16; 마가복음 3:2; 누가복음 6:1-5; 13:10-17; 요한복음 5:2-18; 7:23; 9:1-34). 그리스도의 말씀은 안식일을 지킬 본분을 면제하시는 것이 아니라, 그 날이 사람에게 주도록 정해진 영적 복을 베풀지 못하게 막던 그릇된 지킴의 방식에서 그것을 건지실 뿐이다.

entries.definition: (Acts 1:12) The law as regards travel on the Sabbath is found in (Exodus 16:29) As some departure from a man’s own place was unavoidable, it was thought necessary to determine the allowable amount, which was fixed at 2000 paces, or about six furlongs from the wall of the city. The permitted distance seems to have been grounded on the space to he kept between the ark and the people, (Joshua 3:4) in the wilderness, which tradition said was that between the ark and the tents. We find the same distance given as the circumference outside the walls of the Levitical cities to be counted as their suburbs. (Numbers 33:5) The terminus a quo was thus not a man’s own house, but the wall of the city where he dwelt.
entries.definition_ko: 안식일에 이동할 수 있도록 허용된 거리로 성벽에서 약 2천 걸음(6훌롱)이었다(사도행전 1:12).

entries.definition: Each seventh year, by the Mosaic code, was to be kept holy. (Exodus 23:10,11) The commandment is to sow and reap for six years, and to let the land rest on the seventh, “that the poor of thy people may eat; and what they leave the beasts of the held shall eat. It is added in (15:1) ... that the seventh Year should also be one of release to debtors. (15:1-11) Neither tillage nor cultivation of any sort was to be practiced. The sabbatical year opened in the sabbatical month, and the whole law was to be read every such year, during the feast of Tabernacles, to the assembled people. At the completion of a week of sabbatical years, the sabbatical scale received its completion in the year of jubilee. [Jubilee, The Year Of] The constant neglect of this law from the very first was one of the national sins that were punished by the Babylonian captivity. Of the observance of the sabbatical year after the captivity we have a proof in 1 Macc. 6:49.
entries.definition_ko: 모세 율법에 따라 일곱째 해마다 땅을 쉬게 하고 채무를 탕감하는 해였다. 경작을 금하고 저절로 자란 소출은 가난한 자와 짐승이 먹도록 했으며, 초막절에 온 백성 앞에서 율법 전체를 낭독했다. 이 규례를 지속적으로 소홀히 한 것이 바벨론 포로의 원인 중 하나로 여겨진다(출애굽기 23:10,11; 신명기 15:1-11).
